explanation: L0/N1049- is a layer-0 token-embedding readout keyed to the diet/diagnosis word stems, not to nutrition as a topic: its strength is fixed almost entirely by the current token (97% token identity, 0% position) and the pole fires hardest at 2.0-4.0 on whichever single Qwen BPE piece spells the diet stem in that tokenisation - ' diet'/'diet'/' Diet' (2.5 alone, 2.9-4.0 in sentence context), ' diets' (2.1-2.4), ' dieta', and the 'iet' piece of a line-initial 'Diet' (3.2) - with a mid band of 0.6-1.6 on ' diag'/' diagnose'/' diagnosis'/' diagnoses'/' diagnostic(s)'/' DIAG'/'_diag', 'agnosis', ' Dietary'/' dietary' (0.9-1.9), ' nutrition'/' Nutrition' (0.8-1.3), ' budget' (1.2-1.4) and 'Di' (0.5-0.7). It is lexical and piece-level rather than semantic or topical: ' diet' fires just as hard in the political sense ('the Japanese diet debated the bill', 3.2) as in the food sense, health/food/disease words without those stems (' health', ' food', ' meal', ' disease', ' obesity', ' medical', ' doctor') and 'die'-initial near-misses (' die', ' diesel', ' dinner', ' digital', ' dialogue') stay at or below 0.25 in context, and the same word fires or not depending on Qwen's split - ' dietitian' (' diet'+'itian') reaches 3.5 while the spelling ' dietician' (' di'+'etic'+'ian') reaches only 0.34, and ' diets' reaches 2.4 while ' Diets' (' Di'+'ets') reaches only 0.5.

Layer-0 unigram (token-identity) detector: the current token alone sets the pole (token identity explains 91% of activation variance, 82% of the input attribution sits on the peak token itself, position ~1%), and it fires on a fixed, graded lexicon of specific vocabulary entries rather than on a topic - strongest on ' vit- ' forms (' vitamins' 1.12, ' Vitamin' 0.76, ' vitamin' 0.71, the pieces 'vit' 0.64 / 'itamin' 0.57), on Chinese health/importance/positive-affect words (维生素 1.35, 重视 0.95, 兴奋 0.81, 自信 0.72, 重要 0.72, 营养 0.71, 乐观 0.65), and at 0.35-0.75 on the Latinate stems ' important/importance', 'etermin/determin(ation/ant)', 'optim(ism/istic/ization)', 'abil/abilit/stabil/instability/rehabilitation' and the word-internal piece 'ital' (vital, revitalisation, hopital), plus camelCase identifiers built from them (legalArgumentException 0.94, .dropout 0.70, addPreferredGap 0.64, ToggleButton 0.50). It is lexical, not conceptual or orthographic: near-synonyms spelled as different tokens stay at the 0.00-0.16 baseline ('significant' 0.06, 'crucial' 0.16, 'health' 0.16, 'nutrient' 0.15, 'hope' 0.07, 'ability' 0.00 while the piece 'abilit' gives 0.46, 'optimal' 0.05 while 'optimization' gives 0.45) and the same letters inside another token never fire ('gravity' 0.01, 'activity' 0.01, 'hospital' 0.00 versus the piece 'ital' 0.40), while a trigger token fires from any sentence and any position (' important' gives 0.44-0.72 across frames, ' vitamins' 1.12-1.17); only about 0.5% of the tokens of ordinary mixed web text cross the 0.25-of-max threshold, so the mechanism is retrospective, not lookahead (its Jacobian-lens list is incoherent, kurtosis 3.4).

Layer-0 subword bigram detector: fires on a word-internal continuation token (no leading space) such as 'ley', 'PE', 'uk', 'RA', 'w', 'rie', 'ry', 'pose', 'aler', 'ale', 'rah', 'to', 'TE', '4' when the immediately preceding token is a short word-start fragment ending in P/p or h/H (' P', 'P', ' Ch', 'ch', ' Sch', ' H', ' Ph', ' Sh', ' AP', ' MP', ' EP', 'Sup', ' Rip', ' Ash'); it stays near zero when the same continuation follows any other fragment or whole word (' K'+'rie', ' Kings'+'ley', ' Prop'+'ose', 'Q'+'450'), when the continuation carries a leading space (' P'+' w'), on the prefix token itself, and on continuations outside the set ('ola', 'ina', 'ett', 'ford'), independent of wider context.

The pole is a retrospective detector for a rare, out-of-place word-piece: it fires when the current token is an uncommon piece of vocabulary - a non-English or accented letter/word (İşte, جبل, いち, bonne, kan), a code or technical literal (bootstrap, override, usr, .nav, cdnjs, GV), an all-caps identifier (LOUD, BOOL, ÜN), a rare proper noun (Kuwait, Massachusetts, Vermont) or low-frequency open-class vocabulary (chemotherapy, transplantation, conference, interview) - and reads ~0 on the highest-frequency English words (' the', ' of', ' a', ' and', ' is', ' can', ' people', ' home'), on digits, and on whitespace/newline-only tokens. The preceding token gates this rather than causing it: the very same literal is strong after a boundary ('print(bootstrap)' 0.82, 'print(aced)' 1.04, 'print( override)' 0.55, 'Q:\n\n override' 0.93) but near zero after an ordinary word or a closing bracket ('the function bootstrap(x)' 0.00, 'print)bootstrap)' 0.07), while merely uncommon English words such as ' actually' and ' support' form a weaker 0.2-0.3 band that fires after any word (0.31 / 0.22) and is silent after a comma (0.00); the ragged edge I cannot yet predict is a minority of mid-frequency function words that do fire (' when' 0.16, ' whether' 0.14) and common content words that do not (' because' 0.02, ' very' 0.00), and the neuron's opposite (positive) pole peaks on the most frequent function words, digits and the closers ')', ']' and '}'.

Layer-0 single-token (unigram) detector for a fixed, semantically unrelated lexicon: it fires on the current token alone when that token is one of a specific set, strongest on 'monary' (the tail of cardiopulmonary/extrapulmonary, ~1.0), 'Classic' (no leading space), 'Jean', ' favorite'/' favourite', 'la' (S-la-ughters), 'StringRef', 'ties' (Six-ties), 'yth' (Fors-yth), 'au' (Nass-au), 'egade', ' NEGLIGENCE', ' steady', ' pulmonary', ' console', ' mening', 'oph' (es-oph-agitis), ' Manhattan', ' BOOST', and stays near zero on close synonyms or same-domain neighbours ('Modern', ' passion', ' stable', ' terminal', ' renal', ' hepatitis', ' gastr', 'Jan' only ~0.3). Surrounding context barely matters (the preceding token shifts strength by at most ~0.1-0.3 of max, e.g. ' JS' before 'StringRef' raises it), so the same trigger token fires in any sentence, register or language.

Retrospective layer-0 token detector: the negative pole reads the current token's own embedding and fires in proportion to how close that token sits to the 'method / technique / management' noun cluster - method(s), technique(s), methodology/ies, management, treatment(s) and business(es) at 1.1-2.2 of its 2.22 max, with practice(s), strategy/ies, approach, procedure, therapy, software, enterprise, company, style(s), algorithm and firm at 0.35-0.85 - including plural, capitalised, camelCase/identifier and translated forms ('Method' in makeNativeMethod, '_methods', 'метод', '方法', 'método', 'méthode'), at any position and largely regardless of the surrounding words. It stays near zero on near-synonyms that name a plan or a bare process rather than a practised way of doing something (process 0.02, plan 0.01, way 0.00, mode 0.00, framework 0.00, protocol 0.01) and on adjectival derivatives of the same stems (strategic 0.06, practical 0.09, procedural 0.12), and 'administration' (0.00) does not stand in for 'management' (1.64), so the pole tracks this specific embedding cluster rather than the general concept of a procedure or a technical/business register.

Layer-0 grapheme detector for the letter h in the token currently being read: the pole fires on any token whose surface string starts with h/H, whether it is a bare or short piece or a hyphen/space/punctuation-prefixed one ('-H' 4.02, '-h' 3.91, 'HP' 3.63, 'H' 3.53, ' H' 3.48, 'h' 2.52, 'hl' 3.12, ' Harvard' 2.26) or the word-initial h that BPE leaves inside a longer word ('historic' 1.60 in 'prehistoric', 'hood' 0.93 in 'boyhood'), reaching 1.1-4.4 of the 4.4 scan max for all but its ~9% most frequent h-words (' have' 0.24, ' his' 0.19, ' here' 0.30, ' how' 0.12, ' however' 0.03), while tokens whose h is not leading stay at the floor (medians 0.11 for h-after-one-letter pieces like ' sh', 'ch', 0.00-0.01 for ' the', 'this', 'which', and 0.000 for tokens with no h at all), with only a weak residual band when h ends a short piece (' unh' 1.5, ' pH' 1.35, 'oh' 0.53). It is retrospective and context-invariant (token identity explains 99.7% of variance, position 0%, 91% of the input attribution on the peak token, and the same token gives the same strength in any sentence), orthographic rather than lexical (the invented word 'hox' fires at 3.17 against 'glorx' 0.06), and zero-ablating it costs the model the continuation of the h-word just read ('oo' after 'Boo-H', 'od' after 'non-H', 'ick' after 'oak-h') rather than any fixed upcoming token, so it is not lookahead.

This pole is a retrospective unigram detector for a capitalized word-onset token: it fires when the current token starts a word with an uppercase letter and belongs to an idiosyncratic embedding-defined set concentrated on past-tense/past-participle and modal verb forms (Made, Taken, Fell, Slept, Caught, Known, Established, Received, Filed, Submitted, Bought, Sent, Had, Saw, Should, May) plus scattered capitalized members (March, Unemployment, Gate, Dawn, Offer, and Sadd-/Fle-/Conf-/Dep-/Arr- onsets). The same stems lowercased (made, should, may, saddler), subword continuations (ler, ositions), and out-of-set capitalized tokens (The, He, Dogs, Monday, Zebra, Quantum, Eaten, Landed) stay at the near-zero floor (~0.03).

Fires retrospectively when the current Latin-script token is target/Target/targets/-target heading a referential phrase for a selected, attacked, expected or configured concrete entity, goal or code-target argument in running prose or code (target server/position/shape/employer/compounds/audience, our/2050 target, target of/for-PP, target= / data-target / target_link / target.value, or verb to target), or is value/CellValue naming a code property being assigned. It stays inactive when the same goal meaning is rendered as Chinese 目标, when targets appears only as an isolated markdown-table cell without clausal government, and when target merely premodifies a measure noun to specify a numeric threshold (target weight/mass/amount/quantity).

Layer-0 lexical key, not a meaning detector: the pole's strength on a text is the max over its tokens of a fixed per-token-type key, so the peak sits on that token, a long passage is active as soon as one key token appears anywhere in it, about 2% of the vocabulary is above the 0.32 activity threshold, and ordinary prose with no key token stays at or below ~0.2 (20 such sentences measured <=0.17). The interpretable head of the key is amount/degree vocabulary (' handful' 1.45 in a sentence, ' plenty' 0.98, ' plethora' 0.74, ' myriad' 0.77, ' quota' 0.71, ' minority' 0.51, ' majority' 0.49, ' few' 0.39, ' subtly' 1.11, ' passionate' 0.86, ' incapable' 0.69, ' capable' 0.59, ' questionable' 0.64, ' potentially' 0.97), with a semantically unrelated tail of individual tokens and word pieces firing just as hard (' pot' 1.04, ' potato' 0.49, ' mosquito' 0.55, 'caret' 1.14, ' tasty' 1.21, ' dorm' 0.89, 'expire' 0.55, 'epad' inside ' Notepad' 1.00, 'ika' inside ' Troika' 0.63, and scattered code or control identifiers such as 'TODO', 'getArguments' and 'ObjectId' near the threshold). Because the key belongs to the token type and not to the sense, ' handful' fires in 'a handful of them' (1.45) and in 'a handful at bedtime' (1.43), ' potential' fires in 'potential energy' and ' minority' in 'the minority party', while near-synonyms that are different tokens stay silent (' modicum' 0.00, ' dash' 0.02, ' pinch' 0.20, ' numerous' 0.08, ' abundance' 0.21, ' quantity' 0.13, ' many'/' much'/' several'/' number'/' amount' <=0.12, ' meticulous' 0.05, ' esoteric' 0.02); words fire only when the Qwen tokenizer emits a high-key piece for them - the mid-sentence space-prefixed ' handful' fires, a sentence-initial capitalised ' Handful' (tokenised 'Hand'+'ful') does not, and ' Notepad' fires through 'epad' while 'capability' 0.06, 'questionably' 0.05 and 'expires' 0.19 do not. Its negative pole is the mirror contrast: directional '-ward/-orth' tokens (' forward' -3.8, ' onward' -1.5, ' clockwise' -1.0) suppress the unit and so sit at 0 on this pole.

This pole is a retrospective unigram detector for grammatical glue/boundary tokens that hand off to the next constituent: it peaks on the token itself, strongest for the lexically specific verb form ' prescribed', strong for the infinitive/preposition ' to', the indefinite article ' a', and the standalone space token that separates a head from a following number, and moderate for ' at'/' in'/' of', comma, quote, '>' and ' and'. It is silent on content words and on matched function tokens ' the', ' on', ' for', ' with', sentence-final '.', and other past participles such as ' described' or ' given', with surrounding words contributing almost nothing (single-token probes replicate in-context strengths).

Pole N3347+ is a layer-0 retrospective token-identity detector: it fires when the current token is an uncommon, low-frequency vocabulary item - a rare proper noun or place name, a Latin/Greek technical, legal or medical word, a loanword, a code identifier, or a mid-word suffix piece of such a word ('ogen' in pathogen 0.62, 'ication' in adjudication 0.38, 'ination' 0.21 averaged over its 14 scan occurrences) - and reads 0.00-0.001 on frequent vocabulary, function words and everyday content words alike, whatever the position, syntax or preceding token; the negative pole is a separate g+u- regime whose extreme tokens are other-script and framework-code strings, not the mirror of this set. Strength is graded with rarity (mean 0.020 for tokens seen 3-4 times per 200k-token scan versus 0.004 for the 1000+ group; nothing seen 500+ times reaches 5% of max) and is token-specific rather than class-complete, so many rare words fire ('sediment', 'watershed', 'Kashmir', 'trombone', 'Meanwhile') while others of the same kind stay at zero ('jurisdiction', 'proclamation', 'Madagascar', 'repository'), and a token's own corpus mean, not its context, predicts its activation.

A layer-0 token detector for short runs of 3 to 6 hash marks used as Markdown heading or banner markers ('###', '####', '#####', '######'; strongest for 4-5 hashes, about 4-5.2 when the token begins a line after a blank line or the document, and weaker, about 2.2-3.8, for the space-prefixed variants ' ###'/' ####' used inline or in code comments). It fires only weakly (about 0.2-0.35 of max) on '##', a single '#', hash runs of 8 or more, and the bullet '•', and is essentially silent on other list or emphasis markers ('-', '*', '****') and on the heading text that follows.

Layer-0 lexical detector: fires on the current token itself (about 70-95% of the drive; the preceding token adds at most ~0.15 of max) when it is one of a fixed set of word-forms, strongest (>=0.7 of max) for history/History, approach, work/Working, Architecture, problems, args, a closing brace '}', and Chinese 工作/这样做/历史, medium (0.3-0.6) for process, research, interface, probably, problem, arguments, running, type, function, and weak (<0.3) for modal/hedge words such as would/could/usually. It is not a concept detector: close synonyms that are different tokens (heritage, tradition, tackle, method, procedure, labor, issues, params, Platform) stay near zero, and the words around a trigger barely change its activation.

Retrospective layer-0 token-identity lookup, not a concept detector: strength is a fixed per-token value carried by the current token alone (token id explains 95.5% of the variance, position 0.3%; the peak token carries 0.84-1.00 of the integrated-gradient attribution, and a word scores the same in unrelated documents - ' clock' 1.21-1.34 over five occurrences, ' cash' 0.88-1.05 over nine, ' money' 0.66-0.83 over eleven, ' funds' 0.31-0.38 over six). A prompt is predicted ACTIVE only if it contains one of a closed set of word-forms - ' clock' (1.26) > ' cash' (0.96) ~ ' thrust' (0.94) ~ ' fauc' (0.83) ~ ' grounding' (0.81) > ' money' (0.71) > ' deficit' (0.60) > ' imperative' / ' Carmen' / ' Mon' / ' hunger' / ' brushing' / ' Ruby' / ' Rod' / ' Burg' / ' Pend' / ' conflict' / ' Cambridge' / ' mon' / ' Grammar' / ' conservative' / ' Monday' / ' fever' / ' revenue' / ' debt' / ' crisis' / ' Harvard' / ' funding' / ' dollars' / ' mill' / ' grammar' / ' military' / ' calcium' / ' muscular' / ' cough' / ' curves' / ' cavity' / ' strikes' / ' funds' / ' groundwater' (0.34-0.56, the 0.33 activity line is fuzzy by about +/-0.02) - and predicted INACTIVE for every other token, however close in meaning: 'water' 0.01 over 27 occurrences, 'time' 0.09, 'minute' 0.11, '$' 0.04, 'percent' 0.00, 'business' 0.12, 'company' 0.15, 'income' 0.15, 'spending' 0.17, 'dollar' 0.22, 'penny' 0.25, 'capital' 0.27, 'budget' 0.27. The lookup is on the surface form, so capital ' Pend' fires at 0.47 while the lowercase 'pend' inside 'pendulum' stays at 0.26, ' cashews' (tokenised ' cash'+'ews') fires at 0.88 while the single token ' cashier' stays at 0.16, and the opposite pole's vocabulary (' parts', ' group', ' whole', ' &', the bullet '·') is silent here.

The pole fires on a detached separator glyph: a single token that begins with a space and is made only of punctuation, detached from the word before it. Its strength is graded by glyph, strongest (0.5-1.0 of max) for the dash/slash/joiner family ' -', ' –', ' —', ' /', ' ·', ' |', ' >', ' --', ' +', ' •', ' :', ' ||', ' //' (and rarer forms such as ' ›', ' ―', ' ..', ' ---'), moderate (about 0.25-0.5 of max, sometimes just under the active threshold) for a detached ampersand, question or exclamation mark, semicolon, asterisk, equals sign, ellipsis or period, and at or below the active threshold for a detached comma, close paren, open bracket, quote, dollar sign, hash or backtick; the same glyph without its leading space (bare '-', '–', '/', as in 'well-known', '1925–2013', 'http://', 'Key:') is not detected at all. It is retrospective: the peak lands on the separator itself (76% of the input attribution is on that token), the token that follows it has no effect, the Jacobian-lens write just mirrors the same detached-glyph family (' >', ' ►', ' ..', ' ›', ' =>', ' :') and the measured ablation profile is unconcentrated (KL 0.006) - and it is about three times weaker when the separator starts a line after a newline (0.3-0.6) or about 40% weaker after another space-prefixed punctuation token (~1.0-1.2) than when it follows the last letter or digit of the left-hand item (1.4-2.0), which drops the weaker glyphs below the active threshold at a line start.

The pole is a layer-0 unigram (token-identity) detector: its strength is set by which token is being read, not by context or position (token identity explains 90% of the variance, position 1%), and it never fires on the frequent core of the vocabulary, staying at zero for function words, common content words and common names ('the', 'people', 'time', 'white', 'John', 'Paris' all measure <=0.06, and in the scan no token appearing 100+ times reaches the active threshold). It fires only on a sparse, idiosyncratic subset of the low-frequency long tail - rare words ('picnic', 'apartment', 'purple', 'blond', 'notebook'), proper names and places ('Sarah', 'Barbara', 'Rwanda'), technical and code/markup identifiers ('Npgsql', 'DataTable', 'dataGridView', '.md', '.rs') and unusual word pieces ('elix', 'oton', 'ologist') - and because many equally low-frequency words ('canyon', 'automobile', 'cuisine') stay at zero, predict active only when a marked long-tail token of these kinds is present, and inactive when every token is frequent core vocabulary.

Layer-0 lexical detector keyed on the current token's identity, with a small boost from the token just before it. It fires on a fixed set of whole words: ' Baseball'/' baseball', ' football', ' college'/' university', ' engineer(ing)', ' crane', ' army', ' soldier', ' surgeon', ' eye', ' ear', ' jumped'. Close neighbours outside the set stay low (' basketball', ' hockey', ' school', ' doctor', ' pilot', ' police', ' tree', ' arm', ' leg', single-token ' Josh'). It also fires on word-internal fragments ('osh', 'anth', 'ourn', 'ockey', 'oust', 'onaut', 'ene'), and these are much stronger when the previous token is the j-onset piece ' j'/' Jay' (j|osh, j|ockey, j|ournald, Jay|anthi) than when another onset precedes them (b|osh, t|ournald, r|ock|ey); a bare ' j' token gives only a weak ~0.27.

The pole reads the identity of the current token through a fixed layer-0 key centred on markup and code identifiers: '<X' angle-bracket tokens and '>' fire up to 3.5-4.1 on code (4-5x the 0.82 maximum anywhere in the web scan), and on plain prose the firing inventory is that same token-id set and its nearest surface forms - CamelCase continuations ('Locker' in 'BitLocker', 'Discover' in 'OutreachDiscovering', 'Ball' in 'Pendulum Ball'), '>' after a tag-name piece, ' &', bare capitalised title words (0.82 as the first token of a text), and the word-internal pieces 'able'/'ination'/'occus'/'iers'/'ians' - plus a residual set of ordinary polysyllabic words (' must', ' through', ' proper', ' related', ' during', about 0.2) that share the same embedding region with no obvious semantic link; each token's strength is fixed by its id, so context and position move it by at most about 0.1 apart from the first-token boost. Explicit exclusions a detector must apply: the space-initial spelling of the same string is a different token id and is inert (' able' 0.00 vs 'able' 0.46; ' <T' 0.00 vs '<T' 4.1; ' Test' 0.08 vs 'Test' 0.82), the stems are inert ('market', 'Discrim', 'row', 'Bit' all about 0), other derivational suffixes are inert ('ology', 'ance', 'ment', 'ness', 'ity', 'ation' all < 0.1), and common function words (' the', ' of', ' and', ' is', ' to') are inert.

Layer-0 unigram detector: the pole's strength is fixed by the identity of the single token at that position and essentially not by its context (the same token peaks at 1.23-1.29 for ' river' and 0.53-0.57 for ' market' across four unrelated sentences), so it fires wherever the current token is one of its key word-forms, led by ' ocean' (about 2.8, twice anything else) and then ' Forest'/' forest', ' circuit', ' river'/' River', ' abyss', ' cemetery', ' Amazon', ' Jackson', ' Pacific', ' Arctic', ' reef', ' cavern', ' desert', ' market', ' interval', ' revision', ' survey', ' review', ' discord', ' Instagram'; capitalised variants and other pieces of the same word (' Ocean', ' oceans', ' cean', ' rivers') fire as well. The key set is a specific, heterogeneous list of word-forms rather than a semantic class - equally concrete nouns and near-synonyms of its members stay inactive (' sea', ' lake', ' water', ' mountain', ' island', ' beach', ' church', ' hotel', ' table', ' book', ' cathedral', ' lighthouse', ' peninsula', ' glacier', ' volcano' all peak below the 0.39 active threshold), and so do unrelated proper names (' Nile', ' Everest', ' Europe', ' Tokyo'), so predict active only when the current token is one of the listed forms or a case/spelling variant of one.

Fires on a word-internal continuation subword (a token with no leading space, e.g. 'ster', 'mit', 'ux', 'CG', 'ther') whose immediately preceding token is a short word-initial vowel fragment, by far most strongly the letter E in any form ('E', ' E', '-E', '(E', "'e"), at about half strength after 'A'/'O'/'Wa'/'e', weakly after 'I'/'U', and near zero after consonant fragments ('K', 'T', 'Ad', 'Em', 'Al') or on the same subword at word start or after a full word. The pole is silent when the token after 'E' starts a new word (' coli', '.'), so it is driven by the previous-token fragment combined with being mid-word, not by the identity of the continuation token alone.

A layer-1 bigram detector that fires on the second token of a few specific two-token pairs: most often the host token 'www' right after a URL scheme 'http://' or 'https://' (weak for a bare 'www', a missing scheme or most other subdomains such as 'docs' or 'mail'); also ' in'/' inside' right after a form of 'look' ('look in', 'looking in'; weak for ' at', ' into', or ' in' after other verbs); and 'L' right after 'OR' (as in 'ORL1'). The same tokens elsewhere, and the tokens before or after them, stay near zero.

A layer-1 spelling-fragment detector: the negative pole fires when the current token is one of a learned set of unusual letter fragments that occur as non-final pieces of names, acronyms and technical or foreign words - 'US' after 'V' (VUS), 'PT' after 'F' (FPTCs), 'MT' after 'E' (EMT), 'OP' after 'C' (COPD), 'AY' after 'H' (HAYNE), 'orm' after 'c' (cormorant), 'ank' after 'K' (Kankakee), 'uv' after 'ma' (mauvaises), 'æ' after 'hj' (hjælpe) - and on the name-onset tokens ' Hay'/'Hay' (Hayne, Hayao), ' Tay' (Tayyip), ' Bog' (Bogut) and ' Anderson', plus a smaller glue family of hyphen pieces ('-free' after 'risk'/'gun', '-engine' after 'reverse', '-' in 'X-Plane', the minus in '3*a - 7'). The trigger is the specific fragment, not the word's rarity or meaning: equally rare names and technical words with ordinary spellings (Kowalski, Nakamura, apoptosis, cholangitis), the same letters inside common words (bay, dorm, bank, corner, corn, GTP, 'haystack' as a single token) and ordinary prose all stay near zero, while the positive pole of the same SwiGLU unit fires on a disjoint fragment set ('ao' in Hayao, 'ot' in luaotfload).

N1675− fires on the lowercase function-word slots of Title Case spans: a lowercase function word (of, on, in, a, the, and, for, to, &, by, from, about) preceded within about four tokens by capitalized content words, peaking (2.2/2.31) on the prepositions, articles and conjunctions inside document titles, headlines, section headings, legal captions and quoted titles ('The Effects of Event Rate on a Cognitive Vigilance Task', 'The People of the State of Colorado', 'Eat & Drink Like a Local'), and more weakly on lowercase continuations inside capitalized names ('cci' in Carlucci 0.68, 'd' in P.3d 0.71, '.com' in ESPN.com 0.93); one capitalized word immediately before gives 0.88 of the full peak, a lowercase word immediately before cuts it to 0.29, and no capitalized word at all leaves 0.01. It is the case contrast that drives it rather than capital density or title position: the same words in ordinary lowercase prose sit at the floor (mean 0.001 and 0.02% active where no nearby content word is capitalized), a title embedded mid-sentence in prose still fires (2.28), while capitalizing the peak word itself (' Of' 0.11), every word (0.39) or ALL CAPS (0.04) goes quiet, no capitalized token anywhere reaches the active threshold (0/25,702), and the case of the tokens after the peak is irrelevant (a title-case prefix with a lowercase tail still fires at 1.67) - so the pole is retrospective on the capitalized run before it; its positive pole is the mirror, peaking (0.27-0.31 versus at most 0.15 in lowercase controls) on the blank line that ends a title-case heading line and on the first lowercase prose word after such a span.

This is a retrospective layer-1 detector for the preposition/adverbial particle that directly follows a noun or verb naming a hostile or damaging event (fight/fought, war, battle, attack, strike, hit, assault, bombing, raid, siege, shooting, crash, blow, wound, damage, threat, struggle, and the setback words fall/fell, failure/failed, loss, drop, slump); one word of separation still fires at roughly a third of the strength, and the event word alone, at the end of the sentence, does not fire. It peaks on the particle itself and only for target/direction particles (on, to, at, for, against, upon, over, back, down, between, into), not for in/with/from or a non-preposition (the, a, and, was, punctuation), and it stays near zero after a benign head (walk, plan, profit, cost, key, access, decision, answer), so it tracks the adversative-collocation shape rather than the particle token alone (a weaker secondary mode, under 60% of max, also fires on the second token of rare capitalized/continuation pairs such as 'Dwar|ves', 'Bruce| N' and 'Die|-Namics', which this axis does not explain).

This pole fires retrospectively on the current token when it is an informative, content-bearing word (mid-frequency nouns, verbs, and meaning-carrying function words such as 'from', 'because', 'are'), driven mostly by that token's own embedding; it stays near zero on the highest-frequency filler tokens ('the', 'a', 'and') and punctuation in the same positions, regardless of surrounding context.

The negative pole fires on a standalone operator glyph that is being used as an operator inside a symbolic expression: strongest on the space-prefixed plus ' +' and its LaTeX form '+\' (e.g. $a + b$, \kappa_{\mathrm{ex}}+\kappa_{\mathrm{in}}, 3 + 4, x = 42; y = x + 1;, f(a) + g(b)), then on ' -' and ' ='/'=\' at roughly a third to a half of that strength, with strength graded by how formulaic the immediate context is (highest inside $...$ math and backslash-command neighbourhoods, lower when the same expression is embedded in ordinary prose). It stays near zero when the glyph is not an operator of an expression: fused into a word, identifier, e-mail or URL ('C++', 'a+b', 'john+tag@example.com', 'h=315'), replaced by non-operator punctuation (a comma between the same operands), a lone LaTeX command or backslash, narrative or programming-discussion prose ('The story a + b is here.', 'In Python, a + b works.'), or another operator glyph (*, /, <, >, ^, ==, !=), which fire at most weakly (peak <= ~0.75, below the active range); it is a formula-operator detector, not a general symbol, punctuation or LaTeX detector.

Retrospective (unigram-family) detector for Greek-letter material: it fires on tokens spelling Greek letter names in any casing or gluing - full names ('Omega', ' Gamma', ' kappa', 'Sigma'), name tails ('appa', 'elta', 'amma', 'psilon', 'mega'), hyphen/dot/underscore-glued forms ('-beta', '-alpha', '.psi', '_tau') - and on Greek Unicode characters, either as merged single tokens (Ω, Σ, Γ, κ, μ, λ) or as UTF-8 byte-fallback fragments, where the continuation byte fires only after its Greek lead byte (the scan's top peak 6.6 is the second byte of Ω in '141 Ω'; that byte is ≈0 standalone). Firing is graded by how close the token sits on the neuron's key ('Omega' 6.60, 'appa' 4.44, ' kappa' 2.54, ' delta' 1.65 standalone; the tail 'igma' and lookalikes Latin k/O/um, 'é', ' html' are ≈0), and I acknowledge two unexplained leftovers: a context-driven offshoot at 15-23% of max on a specific word set ('Thorne', 'refractory', 'ligament', 'gait', 'quintiles', 'nanotube', 'unibody', 'bivalent', 'text/html', 'd’/l’+vowel') whose fragments are ≈0 standalone and which is word-specific ('Phorne' 0.24, 'olfactory' 0.06, 'turniles' 0.03 do not fire), and a weak standalone tail ≤1.6 on a few non-Greek tokens ('我院', '-HT', 'ptide', ' Silicon', 'fty'); the negative pole fires on generic non-Greek word-continuation fragments ('io', 'elle', 'ethylene', 'Part'), the complement this pole excludes.

Retrospective word-piece detector: the positive pole fires on a token that is a non-initial piece of a multi-token word — a token with no leading space that continues the orthographic word begun in the previous token — and peaks (~0.9-1.0) on the continuation piece, usually the first one, of an uncommon name, identifier or loan/technical word (C|orm|orant, J|op|lin, proper|Id, Ab|und|ant, eag|erness, Upps|ala, J|alan); the same string starting a fresh word after a space (property Id 0.39, property id 0.27) or a word-initial token fires far less, and word-specific rare fragments (Reykjavik's 'jav'/'ik', Kubernetes) do not fire at all. A second, distinct SwiGLU double-negative regime (gate<0 and up<0) fires on 'by' as the passive agent after a past participle (measured by, generated by), while every other 'by' variant is the pole's most-suppressed token in the vocabulary (negative pole = a 'by' detector); a weak whole-word component also fires on a few common words when they are the second element of a tight compound/collocation (student| pilot, right| now, to| have).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a frequent local chunk: a common bigram or collocation (next+year, quarterly+revenue, pinch+of, guilty+to, second+half, water+boils, the+door, return+true), a fixed phrase (according+to, at+least+eight), a word-internal subword continuation (ochond+ria), or a sentence-initial content word after BOS (Add, Water, SELECT). The preceding 1-2 tokens do most of the causal work (single-token ablation effect ~1.0), so the identical peak token after an unrelated word stays near zero.

Predicted active when the current token completes a specific locally-licensed chunk: a content word strongly constrained by its immediate predecessor, such as final→note, quarterly→revenue, senator→announced, year→went, or determiner/adjective→noun (the/cold→wind); the same peak token with a non-licensing predecessor, or a different peak token in the same frame, goes quiet, while edits to distant words change almost nothing. The pole is retrospective (about 78% of attribution sits on the peak plus previous token with mean distance 1.2, and the Jacobian lens promotes no coherent token set at kurtosis about 3.2); its strong examples divide between the SwiGLU g+u+ regime (final note, quarterly revenue) and the g-u- regime (cold wind, river flooded), two sub-detectors implementing the same chunk-completion job.

L1/N3692- fires on the token that names physical merchandise or the retail/wholesale trade that moves it: the goods and paperwork words goods, products, merchandise, inventory, shipment, parcel, catalog, invoice, receipt, discount, sale, and the store, outlet, mall, shelf, supplier, wholesaler they pass through, in a selling frame ('They sell goods online.' 1.11; 'The receipt is in the bag.' 0.70) and in a plain one ('The catalog arrived in the mail.' 0.29; 'They need more inventory.' 0.27; 'The supplier failed to deliver.' 0.25), and its output direction independently promotes the same concept (Jacobian lens: goods/commodities/supplier/goods). Predicted inactive: text whose content words are money or finance held as such (money, cash, bank, loan, budget, salary, profit, fund), abstract nouns (question, idea, reason, method), or unrelated concrete nouns (door, letter, train, garden, film, bike); the token before a merchandise word is inert (' goods' 0.62 on the token itself vs 0.002 on the token before), and other isolated content words can only reach a low tail of about a fifth of the merchandise amplitude.

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a highly predictable local unit begun by the preceding 1-3 tokens: a subword continuation (Elect-rons, Mit-ochondria, the final 0 in 100), a contraction or clitic piece (can-'t, j-'), or the second half of a fixed whole-word collocation (second-half, greater-than, on-average, quarterly-revenue, triangle-inequality, are-you-going). The same surface token outside its cueing context activates it weakly or not at all.

N4001+ is a technical-register detector that fires on a plain-English content word (accounts, instructions, diagram, list, table, risk, guide, edit, switch) when the same phrase or clause carries a computing/network referent (server, client, host, ssh, password, email, Internet, network, certificate, router, gateway, login, https URL) a few tokens earlier; the identical word in a non-technical frame (dog, garden, book, teacher) or in a neutral sentence sits near zero, and the network nouns themselves (client, server, internet, password, certificate, host) do not fire this pole - they fire the negative pole. The response is contextual, not lexical: freezing each token alone gives a flat near-zero activation (max 0.91, mean 0.017) and the input rows projected through the embedding matrix are flat, so it cannot be predicted from the peak token's identity.

Fires on the token that completes a stereotyped, memorized local chunk: the predictable second half of a frequent collocation or idiom (negative charge, crowd erupted, dark energy, in March), a code/SQL idiom (as np, SELECT name), a word-final subword finishing a distinctive multi-subword word (amoxicillin, </body>), or a conventional memorized sentence opener right after BOS (She, Tokyo, SELECT). It stays near zero on the same tokens in isolation (bank, energy, greater, sits, erupted all ~0 alone) or inside novel combinations (meeting erupted, solar energy, in theory, is older).

The positive pole is a retrospective, current-token detector for the space that separates or relates two things: it fires when the token under it names an interval, gap, spacing, span, partition or ratio between two anchors - ' interval' 1.79/1.60/1.55/1.43/1.35 in '95% confidence interval' and '30-millisecond interval', ' spaced' 1.48, ' spacing' 1.16 and 1.00, ' span' 0.60-0.64, ' pitch' 0.51, ' window' 0.38-0.62, ' boundary' 0.40, ' divider' 0.38, ' margin' 0.34, ' ratio' 0.35, ' gap' 0.21-0.24 - and stays at the floor for words that measure a property of a single object in the identical frame (' distance' 0.04, ' clearance' 0.04, ' width' 0.07, ' depth' 0.05, ' radius' 0.05, ' length' 0.08, ' offset' 0.07, ' angle' 0.03). The word itself is the cause and it is not lookahead (replacing the peak token removes 1.00 of the activation, the token before at most 0.19, and editing anything after the peak gives delta 0.00), the sense built up in front of the word gates it (' window' as an opening or a time interval 0.38-0.62 versus the JavaScript global 0.09-0.14; a rail or protein ' loop' 0.44-0.68 versus a 'foreach loop' 0.07-0.15), and I acknowledge a memorized tail that does not share this meaning - ' Guinness' 0.82-0.85, ' switch' 0.77-1.19 in every sense including a C switch statement, and specific mid-word fragments ('apse' in rel-apse 0.67-0.71, 'isen' in He-isenberg 0.53, 'arr' in Chap-arr-al 0.52) - while the fragments of names the scan never saw stay low (Kowalski 0.17, Nakamura 0.08, apoptosis 0.06, cholangitis 0.07).

The pole fires on the word-final piece of a content word that the tokenizer happened to split: a token with no leading space that continues the word begun by the previous token, when that piece is a lexical chunk (str|aws 'straws', Con|dit 'Condit', dro|oling 'drooling', H|oles 'Holes', -ad|ult 'sub-adult', lace|w|ings 'lacewings', sys|root 'sysroot', hammer|head 'hammerhead', war|heads, well|head, Aqu|atic 'Aquatic', Expl|ode 'Explode', rep|resents 'represents', str|add|led 'straddled', Sp|ine 'Spine'), i.e. it tracks word-internal composition rather than the word: both pieces matter, so str+aws gives 2.5 of max while p+aws, m+oles and ch+root stay near zero. The identical word delivered as one whole token ('strips', 'holes', 'adult', 'pooling', 'lacewing', 'ahead', 'overhead', 'string', 'aquatic'), or as two spaced words ('sys root' 0.49, 'lace wings' 0.16), peaks below 0.25 of max, as do split tails that are productive grammatical suffixes ('ing', 'tion', 'ness', 'ent(s)'); 'head'/'heads' are the one piece that also fires as a spaced token after a content-word modifier ('hammer head' 1.05, 'long head' 0.88, 'the head of' only 0.32).

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a locally highly constrained chunk: a frequent bigram or collocation (greater->than, are->often, went->by), a determiner/preposition/verb plus its expected noun or function word (the->sunrise/report, of->France/flour, opened/flooded->the), or a subword, digit, punctuation or code fragment finishing a word, year, number or call (Tok->yo, 196->9, 1->0, np->.zeros, j->'). The same token without that constraining left context stays low.

Layer-1 word-identity detector for the English lexeme REACH: the pole is strongly active (peak 2.6-5.7 against a 1.12 activity line) at any position that spells the word - ' reach', ' Reach', ' reaches', ' reached', ' reaching', ' Reached', the same word split across a token boundary ('Re'+'aches' about 9.2, 'RE'+'ACH' about 11.2), and compounds that leave 'reach' as its own token (overreach about 6.0-9.6, outreach about 2.0-2.4) - whatever the sense (motion verb, noun of extent or influence, the idioms 'within reach' and 'out of reach', and a bare mention of the word all peak alike), while words that merely contain 'reach' as a substring (reachable about 1.1-1.8, unreachable about 2.1) stay above the line but far weaker. It is neither a semantic nor an orthographic detector: the spelling neighbours 'each', 'teach', 'beach', 'speech', 'catch' and the extent synonyms 'extent', 'range', 'span', 'scope', 'breadth', 'attain', 'achieve' stay in the 0.1-0.5 background, only 'stretch'/'extend'/'extension' form a weak 0.5-1.9 ring that straddles the activity line, and a preceding extent modifier ('long', 'wide', 'broad', 'far', 'extended') raises the peak by about 1-1.5 but never drops it below about 2.5.

This pole is a retrospective detector for the second token of a locally predictable two-token chunk: it peaks on the current token when it completes a dotted-path class segment (java.util to .List/.HashSet high ~1.0+, to .HashMap mid ~0.57, to .Iterator weak ~0.15), a doc-comment marker (/// to @, * to @ ~0.39-0.69) with tag-word completion only for memorized words (return ~1.15; throws/brief themselves ~0.0-0.09 stay low), a clause/code line-end (October to ; ~0.22, short return-line to newline ~0.34, capital to of ~0.27, def to add ~0.59), or a memorized subword completion (key to gen ~0.64, fund to us ~0.63, am to oxic ~0.19, Tok to yo ~0.12). It stays near floor on the same characters as one token or space-separated (boot+gen ~0.01, spaced fund us ~0.25 versus glued ~0.63), on unmemorized splits (boot to gen ~0.01 versus key to gen ~0.64), and on ordinary content words regardless of identity (server/daemon ~0.06, France/Spain after of identical 0.27), so the (previous, current) pair predicts it better than either token alone.

This pole fires when the current token is strongly licensed by the immediately preceding local context, i.e. it completes a conventional multi-token chunk: a collocation ('so fast', 'cups of', 'According to', 'Please remember', 'carry a'), a name/compound/number/subword completion ('Neil Armstrong', 're-election', 'Seine', '3.9', 'barks'), and at sequence start it fires on a few unigram keywords (SELECT, FAST, TABLE). Replacing either the peak token or its one-token licensor with an unlicensed word collapses activity, while substituting another licensed completion preserves it.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a productive local unit with its immediately preceding context: a word (subword continuation, contraction), a noun phrase (determiner/adjective/possessive plus nominal), a clause core (subject plus verb, auxiliary/modal plus verb or negation), a code frame (function name plus paren, import alias), or a clause-closing period. Open content slots generalize across fillers while breaking the frame's function-word skeleton silences the identical surface token, which beats the token-identity confound; post-peak edits leave firing exactly unchanged and the Jacobian lens is Gaussian noise (kurtosis 3.7) whose promoted tokens never follow the peaks, ruling out lookahead.

The negative pole fires on the token that names a piece of geographic territory used as the location/scope of a phrase: either a region noun (area, region, province, state, city, county, district, borough, municipality) or a place name (England, Britain, Europe, Australia, Tanzania, California, San Francisco, the UK, the EC), typically as the object of a containment preposition (in, across, within, around) or as the head of 'the <place-name> area/region'. Its strength tracks how much of a set the territory delimits - quantified or generic phrases about things spread over the territory ('every hotel in the province', 'the museums in the city', 'buildings in the Ottawa area', 'endemic fauna of Tanzania', 'sportspeople from Presov') reach 0.4-1.9 on this neuron's 1.69 scale - and it falls to 0.00-0.20 for a definite-singular individual merely located in a country ('the hotel in England is expensive', 'the man in England was arrested'), for concrete object containers ('found in the office', 'in the drawer'), and when the place name is the clause subject ('England has many hotels') or a predicate-final adjunct ('Hotels are expensive in England').

The pole fires where a formal value is supplied rather than where the word 'true' happens to occur: it peaks on the 'true'/'false' (and 0/1) literal that a function, check or expression returns, evaluates to, yields, or is set to, on the literal operand of an ==/!= test, on the value slot of a 'has value X' predicate, and on literal operands inside code expressions (c(1, 5, 7, 12), [1, 2, 3], 0xffff00); a weaker rise (about 0.4 of max) sits on 'presence' when it names what an examination looks for ('examined for the presence of X'). The same words as ordinary adjectives or narrative predicates ('a true copy', 'it is true that the plan worked', 'the story is true'), non-literal results ('returns its result', 'returns an integer'), plain assignment or variable-to-variable comparison ('x = 5', 'flag = true', 'n > 5'), and 'the presence of X was confirmed' stay at or below 0.2 of the 1.39 max.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token completing a stock procedural or document-structure formula of formal institutional prose: appellate disposition and filing language (this court reverses, briefs of the parties, appeals from a judgment, filed a motion, affirms the conviction, Petition for Certification), patent-specification boilerplate (The present invention following a Field-of-Invention header, Description of the Related Art, Provided herein), and analogous license, publication, and code scaffolding (copy of the License, published in / issue of the journal, method=POST, super.viewDidLoad). It needs both the selecting preceding word and the wider formulaic document context, so swapping the cue word or the genre framing collapses activation on the identical peak token, while edits after the peak change nothing.

The positive pole fires while the model is assembling or re-reading a distinctive multi-piece word - a proper name, acronym, camelCase/snake_case identifier, slash- or hyphen-joined compound, or scientific/technical term - peaking on one of the word's internal pieces (e.g. 'ar' in 'laparotomy', '.PRO'/'JECT' in 'PROJECT_ROOTS', 'gary' in '"Calgary') and dropping on the word's final piece. Its strength rises about 1.8x when the same item has already appeared earlier in the passage, is essentially zero on ordinary lowercase prose and on single-token function words, and its negative pole instead peaks on short common function words and boilerplate scaffolding (comment headers, 'Category:' labels, bylines).

Fires on the preposition or determiner that opens the interlocutor slot right after a word naming an act of interviewing, telling or reporting, questioning, surveying or recording: 'interview with', 'confirmed to', 'statement to', 'speaking to', 'told [the]', 'interviewed/questioned/photographed/surveyed by', 'phone call with', '(return) phone calls'. The peak is usually on 'with/to/by' (or 'the' / the outlet name just after it), whoever the interlocutor turns out to be, and activity is weak (<0.2 of max) when the same preposition follows a non-communicative head ('partnership with', 'returned to', 'funded by', 'walking to'). A weaker secondary activity (about 0.3-0.6 of max) appears on the digits of four-digit years that date a reported or studied event ('in 2004', 'June 2018').

The pole fires retrospectively on a word that locates something already displayed rather than introducing new content: the second of two complementary positional labels that divide a figure, screenshot, table or page into parts ('Right' after 'Left: ...', 'Below' after 'Above: ...', 'Bottom' after 'Top: ...', 'on the right' after 'on the left'), or a pointer to a place in the page or document ('shown below', 'the previous post', 'at the bottom of', 'FIG.', 'click on the image to enlarge', 'enclosed in square brackets'). The same positional words used for physical space (turn left at the corner and then right at the lights; she sat on the left and he sat on the right), a lone unpaired label ('Left: the harbour view.'), and ordinary declarative prose stay at the 0.04-0.05 baseline, and the negative pole of the same neuron instead peaks on running technical/methods prose ('conventional', 'prophylaxis', 'treatment', 'methods').

Retrospectively fires on a qualifier that sits inside a phrase or relative clause restricting what a noun phrase picks out (or how far a claim holds): the negator of a reduced relative ('a service not listed', 'reactions not previously observed'), an epistemic or comparison adjective in a modifier ('variants of unknown significance', 'changes of unclear importance', 'with comparable/equivalent effects', 'with known effects'), a selective degree adverb ('particularly'/'especially', but not plain 'very'/'extremely'/'quite'), a partitive relative ('one of which'), and, in structured text, the value that fills a labelled slot ('Category:1903 births', a method's parameter list, an array-selector assignment). It is near zero on the same words used as a bare main-clause predicate ('the service is not listed', 'the changes have known effects', 'the subjects were particularly poor scorers') and on absolute magnitude or normality adjectives in the same slot ('beneficial', 'harmful', 'severe', 'major', 'typical', 'normal').

N2977+ fires on formulaic, reused web phrasing - the strings a site, publisher or marketer recycles rather than the article's own prose. Its peaks sit inside page furniture (datelines, e.g. the comma of 'Friday, October 12, 2012' 1.90 or 'Wednesday, January 26, 2011' 1.74; publication metadata 'Volume 51 // Number 4' 0.99, 'September 2004' 1.15, 'Issue: November 2, 2002' 1.14; form fields '|Name: ___|Period: ___|' 1.39; breadcrumbs and counters 'Home > Preview' 0.92, 'Page 1 of 4 | Next page' 1.00), navigation, read-more links and calls to action ('Continue Reading' 1.04, 'More Articles' 1.09, 'Table of Contents' 1.20, 'Download PDF' 0.96, 'Sign up for our newsletter' 0.88, 'Ask a question' 1.26, 'Click here to read the rest of the story' 1.14, 'Share this page with your friends' 1.14, 'Want to learn more? Check out our other articles' 1.22), and canned reader-directed idioms ('Why not try...' 1.76, 'everything you need to know' 2.15, 'How about...' 2.30, 'Here are the ten things you need to know about sleep' 0.75). It stays at baseline on the article's own sentences that carry the same words ('The meeting is on Friday, October 12, 2012' 0.42; 'Friday, October 12, 2012' embedded mid-sentence 0.28; 'All you need is in the box' 0.55 vs 'Everything you need is in the box' 1.53; 'Would you like a cup of tea?' 0.71 vs 'How about a cup of tea?' 2.30) and on short declarative site metadata ('This website uses cookies...' 0.06, 'Comments are closed.' 0.24, 'Powered by WordPress.' 0.30), so the trigger is the canned phrasing itself, not the token, the topic or second-person address. The negative pole draws the opposite contrast, firing on lively spoken-register second-person prose ('now's the time to get up and start moving' -3.07, 'We look forward to hearing from you' -2.44, 'Pleased to meet you' -1.88).

This pole is a formal-institutional-prose detector: it peaks on ordinary function words (the article, prepositions, ' to', ' the', ' of', ' on', ' into') when the enclosing 50+ tokens are third-person institutional or legal writing - court opinions, filings, encyclopedic biographies, official/reportorial news, and the formal parts of technical documentation - and stays near zero in casual, conversational or marketing prose that contains the same function words. Inside that register its strongest single lever is legal-proceeding vocabulary in the same clause (defendant, plaintiff, appellant, motion, appeal, jurisdiction, record, error), not any particular entity, and it does not act as a next-token predictor.

This pole fires retrospectively on the first token of a required complement immediately after a complement-selecting head: a preposition or particle (on, off, by), a transitive verb or deverbal participle (led, lead, placed, governing, headed), or an arithmetic or joining operator (+, -, hyphen, backslash). Removing or replacing the selecting head while keeping the peak token collapses activity; changing distant content does not.

Fires on the content tokens of a hand-written literal data value in code, config, connection strings, paths or command lines: the sample or placeholder string a programmer typed in, such as a person's name, password, username, hostname, sheet or folder name, or the words demo/test. It is strongest on the first one or two subword tokens after the opening quote, '=', ':\\' or '-l' that begins the value, and on arbitrary or idiosyncratic values ("Maria", "demo", tecmint, students, C:\\BE). It is weak on conventional system or default values (Windows, Sheet1, Sales, localhost, 127.0.0.1) and near zero on keywords, variable references (null, None, $other, getpass()) and ordinary prose, even when the prose contains the same word.

This pole fires retrospectively on explicit scalar-quantity and measured-exchange constructions: equative frames (as much as), lower-bound thresholds (at least), tradeoff/exchange frames (at the expense of, sacrifice X for Y), sameness of amount, and precise measurements or dimensions with units. It peaks on the connective or measure token ('of', second 'as', 'for', 'least', digits) and stays quiet when the same function words appear in non-quantitative roles or when quantities are vague.

The negative pole fires on a token that designates a place or a position inside a structured space: most strongly on sub-national/administrative place nouns used locatively ('in a county', 'north-eastern Poland', 'the U.S. state of Illinois', 'in a village', 'several parts of the country') and on the locator/index tokens of a numbered address or lookup (the '[' and index of array accesses such as row[0], 'at index 5', 'page 42', 'chapter 7', 'Patent No. 11-325849', 'ZIP code 55089'). It is retrospective (truncating the text immediately after the peak leaves the peak unchanged, and ablating the pole at the peak leaves next-token probabilities unchanged) and is much weaker or silent on concrete object nouns in the same slot ('a house'), temporal references ('in 1998'), plain numerals in prose ('the total is 5') and place nouns in subject position ('The county is large' ~0.3 vs ~0.9 locatively); the same neuron's positive pole instead peaks on generic, vaguely enumerative prose ('a list of handy shortcuts for hosts, presenters, and attendees' = 1.2).

The pole fires on text that states a concrete route or step for reaching a goal - purpose and how-to infinitives ('how to <verb>', 'To <verb> ..., <step>'), locating steps ('First, find X in Y by Z'), navigation paths ('Go to A / B / C', 'Click ...') and method statements ('X can be done by Y') - building up over the surrounding how-to/troubleshooting context and peaking on the token that opens or closes such a clause (the purpose verb, the segment before a colon, the sentence-final period). It stays near zero when the same subject matter is narrated, described, or speculated about, and for bare recipe-style imperatives that carry no goal or route structure.

The positive pole is a weak, low-amplitude unit whose only reliable positive signal is animacy in subject position - animate subject pronouns (I/we/he/she/they/you) sit 3-4x above the ~0.03 floor (mean 0.08, median 0.07, present within-document in 92% of 203 documents, carried by the SwiGLU g<0,u<0 regime) - together with rare, unexplained large spikes (max 1.18; only 0.36% of tokens clear 0.25xmax) that ride short 2-5-token local configurations such as 'Kremlin under Misha' or 'third party social media', which collapse when the configuration is broken (under->and: 0.75->0.22; third->first: 0.58->0.24) but survive a synonym swap inside it (to->on: 0.88->0.96; by->from: 0.53->0.53). Everything else stays at the floor: 'it' (0.024), articles (0.026), ordinary nouns and verbs, code and legal citations, and any text without such a configuration; no single feature predicts the spikes (token identity explains 19% of variance, token frequency, embedding and residual-stream norm, next-token entropy and surprisal and position all |r| < 0.2, and the best contextual predictor, being the first token of a new line or sentence, covers only ~15% of spikes at a 4x lift), so this should be read as a weak conjunction gate rather than a feature detector.

Retrospective clause-closure detector: the pole fires on the token that completes a semantically self-contained unit — typically the sentence-final period ending a complete declarative proposition, or mid-sentence the particle/noun that completes an idiomatic verb phrase or noun phrase (e.g. went by, next year). It stays low on the same tokens when the preceding span is left incomplete or fragmentary.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token closes a conventionalized local frame opened by its head word: a relational preposition after its head (open to from, capital to of, landed to on, percent to in), a pronoun after a speech verb (announced to she), a determiner in a naming frame (called to the), or a degree head or noun completing its modifier (so to fast, scored to twice, at to noon, heavy to rain). Peak strength is set by the head-plus-closer bigram rather than either token alone: swapping the head (open to closed, capital to mayor, called to painted, announced to denied) or the closer (from to near, fast to slowly, noon to midnight) collapses the peak, while changing the word after the peak (of France to of soup, the powerhouse to the library, in March to in theory) leaves it unchanged.

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a highly familiar local chunk — a frozen bigram or collocation (there->lived, went->by, Hello->world, routine->patrol, triangle->inequality) or a split word or number (hab->ite, 16->0, extra->ordinary) — driven mostly by the immediately preceding 1-2 tokens, so a later extraordinary continuation does not suppress it and the same word in an unfamiliar slot (routine after 'and' before 'database') drives it only weakly.

Retrospective detector for a conventionalized local continuation: the pole peaks on a token that completes a frequent multi-word formula opened within the previous ~4 tokens (verb+particle/preposition collocation, existential there+verb, determiner+noun, clause/procedure continuation, HTML/code idiom), with strength scaling with the conventionality of the opener; the same token in swapped, boundary-broken, or uncommon-collocate order stays near baseline, while equally conventional lexical substitutions preserve it.

This pole is a weak retrospective detector of phrase-internal continuation: it fires (ceiling 0.215) on a token that extends an already-opened phrase given the preceding 1-3 tokens — list separators, a preposition or particle completing a verb phrase, the second half of a fixed collocation ('at least', 'not guilty', 'sea level'), a modal after a subject pronoun, or a content word completing a noun phrase — and stays silent at text onsets (position-0 mean 0.0) where no left context exists. It prepares no specific upcoming token: the Jacobian lens is near-Gaussian (kurtosis 4.0) with incoherent promoted tokens and 0% lens agreement, and input attribution sits mostly on the peak token itself (61%, mean distance 1.1).

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a locally highly constrained chunk: a quantity or measure phrase (array dimension, dosage digits, 'after three days', 'calls for two'), a fixed collocation ('sea level', 'log n', 'range(10'), a verb-selected preposition or next recipe step ('stared at', 'twice in', 'and fry'), or the sentence-final period closing a formulaic factual report. The same token fires weakly when its preceding 1-3 tokens do not predict it, so activity is set by local contextual constraint, not by token identity; it carries no specific upcoming-token prediction (Jacobian kurtosis ~3.4, incoherent promoted lists).

The pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a familiar 2-4-token cue inside a well-formed declarative sentence: an adjective/noun/verb plus noun collocation ('light energy', 'on the Moon', 'of the cell'), a quantity ('100', 'two cups', '3.9 percent'), or a fixed function frame ('at least', 'FROM users WHERE', 'x =', 'in range'). Scrambling the cue word order, swapping in an anomalous or nonce completion, or removing the sentence context collapses the peak, while paraphrases that preserve the frame or edits after the peak leave it unchanged. This beats the token-identity confound (72% variance): the same token fires after its familiar cue and goes quiet elsewhere (e.g. 'energy' peaks after 'light' but not after 'chemical' or 'banana').

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a frequent local phrase or frame -- a preposition closing an adverbial ('twice in'), 'and' closing a list, a digit completing a round number, or a comma/period closing a formulaic clause -- with strength graded by how familiar the preceding 1-3 tokens are; incongruous or rare fillers collapse the peak, while changing tokens after the peak leaves it unchanged.

This pole fires when a singular individual is picked out of a plural or group background: activation peaks on the finite third-person-singular predicate that follows the singular subject noun phrase ('the transfer arm is designed', 'Spider-Man has grossed', 'the song has sold') or on an appositive/comma attached to that NP, and it is strongest when a plural mention of the same kind sits in the preceding sentence ('several films ... The film has', 'two engines ... The engine was'). It is near zero for plural subjects with plural predicates ('the films have', 'the transfer arms are'), for bare non-referential pronouns ('it is', 'they are'), and for a lone singular clause with no plural or group context (single sentences such as 'The film has grossed $864 million' peak at 0.03-0.28, well below the 0.25 x max threshold); a 3sg form under a plural subject ('the films has') is intermediate, and the pole's output suppresses plural third-person pronouns ('they/their', 他们/她们/它们, 各自) while promoting singular possessives ('his', 'himself').

The negative pole is the non-human side of a person-referent feature: it fires retrospectively on a token that carries no human reference, and its peak in a snippet is the most strongly non-human content word there - a concrete object, substance, plant, animal or natural phenomenon ('pan', 'clouds', 'rain', 'nature', 'rates', 'mould', 'water'), or, when the snippet has none, a numeral or punctuation mark ('=', '0', '1', sentence-final '.'). It sits at the floor, with the positive pole firing instead, when the current token names a person or a group of people - above all kinship, social-role and collective nouns ('family', 'friend', 'colleague', 'neighbour', 'teacher', 'patient', 'child', 'children', 'students') - so a snippet whose content words are all person nouns is predicted inactive (measured: 'for the family' +1.9, 'the neighbour' +1.4, 'the friend' +1.5, 'the teacher' +0.8, 'the patient' +0.7, versus 'the table' +0.0 and 'the river' +0.0), while swapping a non-human subject or object for a person in an otherwise identical frame lowers the pole (in an otherwise identical frame, 'The workshop repaired...' peaks at 0.34 and 'Her brother repaired...' at 0.11, against a scan scale of 1.19).

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that closes a syntactic slot opened by the immediately preceding words (typically within ~4 tokens): a determiner or complement after a preposition (over the, on the, by Friday), the particle after an auxiliary (did not), the second half of a fixed collocation (ORDER BY), a unit/date noun after a numeral or temporal anchor (three days of, next/last year, in March, eight characters), the finite main verb after its subject (market fell, violinist played, orchestra tuned), or sentence-final punctuation closing the clause. The same surface token fires weakly or not at all when it does not close such a slot (e.g. 'the' after a verb, 'of' after 'ideas', 'year' replaced by 'idea').

L11/N4169- fires at the word that completes an ending or leave-taking expression, not on the topic of endings: the preposition or particle directly after a departure or close-of-period verb ('left/leaves/departed/quit' + with, without, behind, after, in; 'ended/closed' + with, without), the leave-taking word 'goodbye', and 'last'/'final' inside a definite or possessive noun phrase that names the final instance of something ('his last game', 'the last of the firewood', 'for the last time', 'in his last moments'), together with the head noun that such a phrase modifies ('their last game', 'final moments'). It stays near zero in the identically shaped beginnings and continuations ('first', 'initial', 'next', 'latest', 'began/started with', 'stayed with', 'left the building at eleven'), for 'last' meaning most-recent ('last week's meeting', 'the previous summer') and for bare ending vocabulary ('finished with a win', 'over', 'until', 'the final report'), so the trigger is the closing construction rather than the token or the concept alone.

Fires on the connective that hands a just-named plural category noun over to a list of its members: most reliably ', including' after a plural noun naming a class of entities (countries, cities, species, universities, artists, dishes; 0.4-1.0 of max, above threshold in >90% of 'several <class>, including' cases with ~500 tokens of prior text), and less reliably ', such as' / ', like' / ', notably' in the same slot (0.3-0.8, stronger in long documents, weak when there is no comma before them). It stays below 25% of max on 'including' that adds a component to an amount, price or duration ('the invoice/rent/fee, including tax', 'ten euros, including a drink', 'four hours, including stops', 'All costs, including tax'), after generic artifact categories (tools, instruments, materials), and on 'for example', 'for instance' and usually ', e.g.'; known leftovers predicted active are '<nationality adjective> state/province/canton of <Name>' ('the German state of Bavaria', not 'the state of Bavaria' or 'the city of Paris'), the WordPress footer 'This entry was posted ... and is filed under <Tag>', a clause-final ':' that opens an elaboration ('single-handedly: with ...', 'visible at once: the ...'; not reported speech 'He answered: ...'), LaTeX/code operators (' +', ' =', '\frac'), and a diffuse background (~0.6% of ordinary tokens reach 0.29-0.5) that makes most texts longer than ~150 tokens active, so only short texts without these triggers are predicted inactive.

Retrospective detector for a clause-internal token that is the locally predictable continuation of the preceding 1-3 tokens (idiomatic collocations such as stared at+the and boils+at, and productive frames such as For i+in, quarterly+revenue, Add the+food-noun, would not+seek, list+FROM, it+'s). The same surface token evokes little activity sentence-initially, after a non-selecting predecessor, or in scrambled order.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a locally predictable 2-3 token construction licensed by the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens (e.g. a preposition selected by the prior noun/verb, 'than' after a comparative, a verb after its subject, a function name after 'def', a noun after a determiner/possessive), and stays low when the same token appears without that licensing left context.

N546+ is a long-range discourse-topic detector: it fires on a content word (noun or verb) whose meaning fits the topic established by the preceding passage, and its strength grows with how much topical context has accumulated (the word 'debt' in a finance passage reads 0.01 with no context, then 0.15 / 0.20 / 0.30 after 1 / 2 / 3 finance sentences). The same word in an unrelated passage falls to ~0, a related word that was never mentioned (loan, borrowing) still fires (~0.29), and function words, formulaic or idiomatic content words and locally well-formed but off-topic words stay near zero, so the trigger is semantic topical fit with the long context, not the token's identity, frequency or local predictability.

Fires retrospectively when the text has just stated that a person ends or is forced to end an affiliation with a team, employer, office, tenancy or held possession (resigning, stepping down from a role, being forced to leave or forced out, being sold or transferred to another club, quitting, retiring, a tenure ending with until plus a year, absence, or something being lost), peaking on the severance word or the function word right after it, with a separate weaker trigger for the colon after a language name in an etymology gloss such as (Greek:. It stays near zero for spatial direction or posture change with no affiliation loss (turn left, walk down, sat down), object removal without affiliation loss (took the letter out of her bag), preservation or retention (saved the house, kept everything), tenure start or continuation (welcomed the new chair, a long and stable tenure, since, presence), scheduled transport departures (the train will leave from platform 4), and noun leave (annual leave).

This pole fires when the current token completes a unit already pinned down by earlier context: a later fragment of an uncommon proper-name spelling (Mba|eyi, Bramblecl|aw), the expected word of a memorized boilerplate or template (additional |information, for |the specific), or the resolving word of a rigid multi-token frame (what he |was, the image will |appear). It stays near zero on equally predictable local bigrams outside such long constructions (peanut |butter, rock and |roll), on fragments of common words (hippopotamus), on common names in the same frames (Johnson), and when the expected continuation is replaced by an incongruous word.

This pole fires on tokens inside a run of symbolic mathematical notation: an expression in which digits, single-letter variables and arithmetic operators or exponents are combined without intervening words (e.g. '3x + 7 = 22', 'x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0', 'x^4/2 + x', '4a + 3b - 2a + 7b'), peaking on the operator, exponent or coefficient digit in the densest part of the expression, and growing stronger the more symbolic material precedes. It stays near zero in ordinary prose, and also in arithmetic or measurements written out in words ('three x plus seven equals twenty-two', 'twelve feet long', 'two cups of flour'), which is why the same content in words rather than symbols drops the activation.

This pole is a retrospective detector for text that is written in a fixed documentary format rather than free prose: it peaks on the token that fills a conventional slot of that format - a licence or copyright restriction clause ('without the express written permission of the publisher', 'the specific language governing permissions and limitations'), a patent preamble ('the [present] invention relates generally/broadly to'), a biographical parenthetical ('(born 28 July 1992)', '(b. 1992)'), a bibliographic citation line ('et al.'), a legal case caption ('..., a Corporation Not For Profit'), a URL path ('/post/2010/09/'), or a code import/annotation/HTML class name. It is the slot and not the token - 'permissions' to 'rights', 'generally' to 'broadly' and 'born' to 'b' all keep the peak where it is, while the identical clause in a plain sentence, in ordinary legal prose, or behind a narrative lead-in stays at or below 0.35, well under the 0.48 active threshold on the 1.91 scale; known leftovers are the rare political adverb 'legislatively', which fires on its own (judicially/statutorily/ministerially do not), and the code-notation family, which only reaches threshold inside a real code block.

The positive pole fires when the current token completes a familiar local multi-token chunk: a verb-selected preposition/particle (stared->at, contain->at), a preposition or determiner plus its content word (at->the/sea, carry->a, pinch of->salt), a greeting plus punctuation (Bonjour->comma), a category-matching list item (Nairobi and->Lima), or a character inside a rigid markup run (<h->1). Activation grades on how strongly the specific prefix items select that token, so the identical surface token in a non-selecting prefix (admired->at, conceal->at, saw->the) stays near zero. The scan-top HTML/tag responses use the canonical g+u+ SwiGLU regime while the graded 0.2-0.46 chunk responses are g-u- double-negative; both implement the same completion function.

This retrospective neuron fires on clause-terminating punctuation (chiefly periods and commas) that summarizes a preceding statement of computational runtime or algorithmic complexity, especially when qualified by distribution conditions such as 'on average' or 'worst case'. In the true gated SwiGLU positive regime (g > 0, u > 0), it reaches its highest activations at these boundaries, whereas widespread sub-threshold activations on common tokens reflect the double-negative (g < 0, u < 0) regime.

The pole fires retrospectively on the digit token that opens a numeral inside a terse reference or notation run: the page/volume/docket/year/index value that a label, abbreviation or bracket points to ('477 F.2d 598', 'pp 143-167', 'No. 12-3842', '16-1 BCA 36,569 at 178,110', '1916: 139', 'October 25, 2004', 'January 17, 2018', 'DocReq 001013b', '[@Rempe2015a', 'for (i in 1:ncol(pval))'), peaking on the first one or two digits of that numeral and decaying over its remaining digits ('598' -> 0.97/0.81/0.25, '1040' -> 0.96/0.89/0.58/0.02). It stays near the floor on the same numerals embedded in ordinary words ('477 days, 598 pages' 0.35 vs 0.97 in the reporter slot), on spelled-out numbers, and in plain prose, while code label/value boundaries (' => $', ' =', ' public') form a weaker secondary family that the numeral reading does not cover.

The negative pole is a clause-completion detector for running expository prose: it fires on the token where a sentence that has just made a specific statement ends, either the sentence-final period or the comma that opens an exemplifying continuation of the noun phrase just read ('such as Gouda, Parmesan, or goat cheese', ', at 22 percent', ', including ...'). It stays near zero on punctuation internal to a phrase (list commas, decimal points, abbreviations), on the periods of one- and two-word fragments ('Table. Chair. Lamp.'), and on plain short sentences that state nothing specific ('The cat sat quietly on the old wooden mat', 'Bananas are yellow'); the material after the junction never changes it.

This pole fires where a document reproduces or identifies a string instead of composing new prose: at the onset of a direct quotation (the opening quote mark " " / " “ " / " ' " / " ‘ ", or a mis-typed " ” ", and the first one or two words inside it, strongest when that first word is a dialogue opener such as Yes, Yeah, No, Oh, Sure or Hello) regardless of which verb or phrase introduces it (said, replied, declared, whispered, 'saying things like', 'phrases such as', 'the word', 'the phrase', 'the message', 'Best Line:', or a colon), and on the all-caps licence/file constants LICENSE, COPYING and COPYRIGHT (strongly) and AUTHORS, CONTRIBUTORS and NOTICE (more weakly) when the text points the reader at that file, plus the same identifying job for people in reference frames (the abbreviation period of a personal initial like 'W.C.' or 'Rosemary C.', and a personal name in the predicate of a kinship list like 'His parents were William (d.1784) and Agnes'). It stays below the active threshold on ordinary narrative and descriptive prose, on the same utterance reported without quotation marks ('said that the car was here', 'said hello'), on other file names and lower-case spellings (README, MIT, GPL, manual, documentation, 'license'), on ordinary proper nouns in plain sentences ('Prince William visited the school', 'The team included John Smith, Mary Jones and Peter Brown', 'The cities were Boston and Chicago'), on a bare year inside a prose sentence, and on a quotation that starts a text with no preceding narration; its strength is graded with the lead-in, needing roughly an attributive clause (raw strength 0.63 for 'Maria looked at the mayor and said "hello"', versus 0.27 for the five-word 'He said "hello".', against an active threshold near 0.33).

The negative pole is a retrospective detector of the typographic line boundary of an informational article: it peaks on the newline token that closes a standalone label line - a heading, sub-headline, caption, pull-quote, case-citation line, date header or one-word section label ('Background', 'Personal history', 'Alternatives') - and, as a graded secondary family, on the temporal adjunct that anchors a paragraph or clause ('On Thursday,', 'That afternoon,', 'on Saturday'), the spike landing on the day name or adverb and its closing comma. It stays at the floor for those same heading words folded into a running sentence, for paragraph breaks between ordinary sentences, for the same temporal words in a parenthetical aside or used non-temporally ('2007 people'), and in fiction, dialogue, instructional and persuasive text; amplitude is graded by how much the surrounding document reads like a scraped article, so clean synthetic expository prose reproduces only part of the heading response (a leftover this class acknowledges).

This pole is a copy / verbatim-repetition detector: it fires while the model reads a span of text that has already appeared earlier in the same context, so a first occurrence is near 0.0 while the second and later occurrences rise (higher with more repeats and with a closer word-for-word match, and strongest on the shared wording itself), and deleting, rewording or merely paraphrasing the earlier occurrence collapses it. It is relational, not lexical: swapping the repeated content (Monday to Sunday throughout a repeated holiday list) leaves peak strength unchanged, and a repeated nonsense string activates it as well as repeated prose.

The pole fires on the linking function word of a specific, name- or term-like nominal: overwhelmingly ' of' (and the ' the' that immediately follows it), plus ' per', ' in', ' by', ' below', ' than', ' about' in dates, rates and measured quantities, and digits/operators inside numbers and formulas, at the point where the left context has already built a definite noun phrase denoting a particular institution, document, body part, rule or quantity ('the local chapter of', 'the Wisconsin chapter of', 'the Civil Rights Act of', 'the long head of', 'the law of', 'the 22nd day of', 'the History of the County of'). It stays at zero, and its negative pole instead fires, when the same preposition only joins a bare generic or quantitative head to its complement ('the number of', 'the importance of', 'the use of', 'the first chapter of the book', 'The Battle of Hastings') or sits in a heading ('Overview of', 'Table of Contents'); the peak sits on the function word and collapses on the following content word, so the reading is retrospective, fixed by the left context and insensitive to which designation actually follows.
