Fires on the opening tokens of a conjunct that follows a bare comma (or a line break) with no conjunction, i.e. the second or later member of an asyndetic list or parallel series ("dimers, trim[ers]", "word processor, office [suite]", "easier to read, [more]", "six physicians, [six]", "1. ..., [2].", comma-spliced parallel clauses "shape, responses [were]"). It peaks on the token that completes the new conjunct's head (often the second token after the comma). It stays near zero when the conjunct is introduced by 'and'/'or', a semicolon or a full stop, and after non-coordinating commas (introductory adverbials, subordinate clauses, appositives, vocatives); single-token items in plain noun lists fire only weakly.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a locally licensed continuation of a frame set up by the preceding ~1-8 tokens: the second half of a parallel contrast (Electrons... while protons), a list (egg, and a), a conditional consequent (if..., then the), or a head-noun/preposition complement (capital of, into the). The same surface token without its licensing frame (isolated 'the'/'a'/'of', or 'protons' after 'Bananas') stays near zero, and equivalent frame-preserving swaps (and/but) change nothing.

This pole is a town-list (gazetteer) separator detector: it fires on the punctuation token that closes one entry - the comma first, then full stop, colon or semicolon - inside a run of at least two short one-per-line list entries whose head is a town or city name, i.e. the travel-guide contents format '#### Woodstock ... #### Lyndhurst,' (2.0-2.7 there). It stays at the floor for the identical word and comma in running prose (0.00), for the same scaffold when the entry head is a country (0.22), a person's name (0.27-0.76), a brand or a common noun (0.00-0.15), and when only one prior list entry has established the shape (0.04).

The pole fires on the token that completes a nominal compound: the head (final) token of a noun whose subtype/kind is fixed by an immediately preceding attributive noun or relational, kind-denoting adjective ('threat risk assessments', 'water method', 'coronary function', 'produce section', 'child genius'), and it peaks on the last sub-token of a multi-token head word ('lar|vic|ides', 'dash|boards'). The same head noun standing alone ('a method', 0.06 of max), after only a gradable adjective ('a new/simple method', 0.2-0.3) or with a PP complement instead of a compound ('the method of the lab', 0.12) stays low, activation sits on the head rather than on the modifying noun, and a per-word preference for technical/abstract nominals modulates amplitude without changing which positions fire.

Fires on the interior pieces (second through second-to-last) of a rare, recognisable string that the tokenizer splits into several subword, letter or digit pieces: brand and place names (Coldwell| Bank|er, Daler|-R|owney, Ilfrac|om|be, Eyjafjallajokull), Latin set phrases (res ipsa lo|quit|ur, incertae| sed|is), code identifiers (execute_from|_command|_line, frozen|_string|_literal, s|.r|.o) and model or error codes (HMC58|8|3L, V6|1|7F, C20|6|1, ed255|1|9). It peaks once the earlier pieces have identified the string and more pieces must follow. It stays near zero on the first piece, on the final completing piece, on common words and phrases, on unfamiliar gibberish (Qorvexlandipur), and when an earlier piece is changed so the string is no longer recognisable (Coldwater Banker, Dalek-Rowney, 'error at2061').

The negative pole fires, retrospectively, on a section-label line in structured text: the words that name a block at the head of a line ('Personal history', 'Background', 'Overview', 'Goal and content', 'How to Use the Tool', 'Patients - Methods', 'Field of the Invention', 'Plan Your Trip', 'References', 'Draw'), with the response building across the label and peaking on its last token or on the newline that closes the label line. The same words lose about 40% of the response when folded into a running sentence (1.40 -> 0.85, 1.16 -> 0.77), a label with no line of text above it is nearly silent (0.04 for a text-initial 'Overview' vs 0.85 for the same label after any preceding line), and deleting the setext underline under 'Goal and content' changes nothing (1.309 -> 1.309), so the pole reads a label that has already been written rather than preparing the underline or the body that follows it.

Fires at the seam where an element of an already-established repeated text format ends and the next slot of that format begins — the import slot after a Java package header, later entries of a JSON/INI/SQL/email-header/comment/diff/citation/table/numbered-list block — and, in prose, at the quote-close+attribution or the comma/dash that closes a long parenthetical insertion whose embedded clause has a lexical verb and its complement. The trigger is the structural boundary rather than the surface token: the same `import`, `,"`, comma or newline in free prose, as a lone or first occurrence, or after a short or verbless/copular quotation stays below threshold.

This pole fires on the first token of an optional circumstantial extension -- a causal/temporal/manner/locative adjunct, source preposition, approximator, or second conjunct -- at the point where the preceding clause is already grammatically complete without it; the same function word (because/after/from/around/and) with no complete clause before it, e.g. fronted or in a scrambled fragment, stays weak. It is retrospective over the 1-4 preceding tokens, not a predictor of a specific next token: the Jacobian lens is flat (kurtosis 3.2, incoherent guess/failed/wrong list matching nothing after the peaks), and scrambling only the left context collapses the peak.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a stereotyped two-to-three-token frame set up by the immediately preceding context: weekday-plus-comma datelines (Friday/Thursday,), authorship 'written by', license boilerplate ('Licensed', 'license statement'), copular/passive auxiliaries ('was', 'wasn', 'Is'), prepositional and determiner links ('of', 'in', 'the', 'by', 'or', 'he'), and code/markup/subword completions ('[](', ']]', 'items', 'ced'). Activation is driven by the preceding cue word(s) together with the completing token, not by the peak token in isolation.

The negative pole fires on the opening word of a noun phrase that is the complement of a preceding relational head: an abstract or nominalised noun taking an 'of'/'in' complement ('the assessment of lower limb strength', 'a decrease in lower limb strength', 'basic knowledge of both systems', 'the news of the remastering', 'the mainstay of COPD treatment') or the complement of 'due to' ('Faults can occur due to database connectors'). The peak lands on the complement's opening modifier or determiner rather than on its head noun (the head sits about five times lower, and a bare, non-classifying noun in the modifier slot, 'of limb strength' or 'of muscle strength', stays at the floor), while the same words placed in a subject or in a verb's direct object ('We measured lower limb strength', 'The database connectors caused the fault') stay at the floor; dense technical paragraphs sometimes lift the same modifier inside a subject phrase to a third of the peak (e.g. 'the recent audit failures' after a paragraph about audits), which this rule does not cover.

The pole fires on a run of like records recited in a recurring frame - a series of numeric question/answer pairs, discography or bibliography entries, citation and name lists, caption/timestamp lines - where the activation climbs across the run (near baseline on one or two entries, elevated by the fourth or fifth, strongest after eight or more) and stays elevated over most of the run's tokens instead of one word. The same facts written as connected prose, bulleted prose about a single topic, code, and explanatory scientific or technical writing keep it at baseline, and one lone number, name or compound noun in an otherwise expository sentence does not fire it.

N910's negative pole is a sparse retrospective detector of the abstract informational content of technical or expository prose: it peaks on a bare content noun naming what a text, dataset or analysis consists of (strongest on 'data' and 'content', then 'information', 'text', 'evidence', 'details', 'measures', 'quality') where that noun heads a nominal compound or a coordinated nominal ('study selection and data extraction', 'content analysis', 'ablation strategies', 'SSH port number'), and only when the preceding ten to thirty tokens are themselves expository/technical text. It is predicted inactive on nouns for people, objects or events ('patients', 'images', 'files', 'authors', 'meetings') in the same frames, on the same information nouns used as ordinary clausal subjects or objects ('the data were extracted', 'we examined the quality of the evidence'), and on the same phrases after a non-expository lead-in, though roughly a quarter of its weaker peaks fall on predicate words in narrative text ('it sounded like', 'two of them were'), which this class does not yet explain.

This pole fires on the token that continues or completes the currently open clause or phrase: the grammatically expected next piece such as a noun completing a possessive or attributive phrase, a relativizer after its head noun, a verb or copula completing the predicate, an infinitive 'to' after its trigger, or a comma resuming the main clause after a fronted adjunct. It stays quieter at sentence onsets, after sentence-final breaks, or when the expected continuation is replaced by a token that cannot fill the slot.

This pole fires on the token that completes a familiar, high-frequency local collocation (e.g. 'algorithm runs', 'greater than', 'by Friday', 'often called', 'chemical energy', 'compared with last year') or a conventional name/date/number/code completion ('Apollo 11', 'year 1600', '(3, 3)', 'ORDER BY name'), reading the peak token together with the preceding 1-3 tokens; the same surface token in an incongruous or non-idiomatic pairing ('purple than', 'and Friday', 'algorithm grows', 'blue year') activates weakly.

Peaks retrospectively on the token that completes a highly constrained conventional 2-4 word collocation or factual-specification template (e.g. contain-at(-least), returns-true, pleaded-not-guilty, from-9, fry-until); the same peak token in an open-ended context without the 1-3 token licensing prefix activates less.

The negative pole fires at clause-internal relational link words that import external task content into an ongoing clause: consultative 'see' (', see problem 6', '; see it'), source 'from' plus a task noun ('from problem 6', 'from the problem'), and comparative 'same as', peaking on the link word or head noun ('see' 2.1-2.6, 'problem' 1.4-2.0, 'as' 1.8). It stays near zero on sentence-initial document-structuring pointers ('See Figure 3 for ...' 0.07, 'According to Table 4 ...' 0.19, 'After completing Step 3 ...' 0.33), on document-internal caption nouns (Figure/Table/Step/line) in plain instructional prose, and in narration with no such link.

The pole retrospectively detects a locally licensed continuation: it fires on the current token when that token is the filler selected or obliged by the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens (the variable slot after 'If', the complement after a selecting verb such as 'believe' or 'calls', the unit after a quantity such as '500 mg' or 'billion light', the article continuing a parallel definite-NP chain such as 'and the', or the period closing a complete clause), with strength graded by how tightly the local frame constrains that filler. The same token in a non-licensing frame collapses (' x' 0.394 to 0.000; ' calls' 0.144 to 0.000) while distant edits leave firing intact; the Jacobian lens shows no coherent promoted set (kurtosis 3.1, 10% lens agreement) and attribution is 76% within one token, so it reacts to what was read rather than preparing a prediction.

Fires retrospectively on a token that is a conventional, lexically fitting continuation completing the immediately preceding multi-token frame (a copula after a conjoined plural subject, 'of' after a complement-taking noun, a particle after its verb, a characteristic predicate after its subject, or a speech verb closing quoted dialogue); the same syntactic slot with an unfitting word, or the same function token without its licensing frame, stays low.

Retrospective: the pole peaks on the clause-linking word itself - concessive subordinators (although, while, whereas), result connectives (therefore, thus, consequently, meanwhile), the relative/comparative functors which, than and like, and the constative relational predicates (is called, uses, contains, involves, located, means) - when that word opens a clause after a full stop or a comma. It stays near zero on the additive/contrastive adverbials however, moreover, furthermore, nevertheless and nonetheless, on the causal subordinators because and since, on plain sentence openers (In, For, Some, These, The) and on concrete content nouns.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a short local stem: a whole content noun after a determiner, quantifier or adjective (telescope, report, capital, cat, dog, summit, witness, library, orchestra), a subword completion after its word-initial piece (lescope after Te, phony after sym, board after white), or a code operand inside an open call (3). Peak strength is set by the current token's identity: microscope, rumor, and notion read near zero in the identical frames where telescope, report and capital peak while the licenser (The) and surrounding verbs (captured, sat) sit near zero, and edits to tokens after the peak leave the peak unchanged.

This pole fires on the open-class content word that carries a specific technical detail - typically the modifier or head that makes a technical noun phrase specific ('traditional sequencing methodologies', 'pancreatic retroperitoneal position', 'the required high sensitivity') - inside scientific/technical exposition; it goes near zero on a determiner in the same slot and on the same sentence when the preceding passage is narrative, news or boilerplate prose. Strength is set by how much technical content the passage carries rather than by the peak token's identity (a synonym, or even an unrelated open-class word such as 'purple', still spikes at 0.96-1.66 of the base) and not by position, so it behaves as a diffuse 'technical content in progress' detector rather than a word detector.

The negative pole of Qwen2.5-0.5B L13/N1963 fires on the punctuation token that opens a parenthetical/aside interpolation inside a running sentence: strongest on an em dash or spaced double hyphen (scan means 0.45-0.53, peaks 1.6-1.9), weaker on an en dash, and weakly but reliably on an opening parenthesis (mean 0.19 across the scan's 804 ' (' tokens versus 0.03 for an arbitrary token; usually below the 0.25 x max active threshold, but up to 1.2 when the parenthesis holds a heavy apposition or citation). It is retrospective - it peaks on the delimiter itself, with no rise at the preceding token (0.02-0.03) and only 0.02-0.04 on the next token - and is silent on the matching closing dash or bracket (all 403 scanned ')' tokens and the second dash of a dash-opened aside score ~0), on commas, colons and semicolons, on dashes at the start of a list line, and on en dashes inside numeric ranges; its Jacobian-lens write promotes opening-paren tokens (' (', ' ("', ' ([', ' (<'), the canonical spelling of that same 'parenthesis open' state.

This pole fires when the current token completes a frequent, strongly predicted local collocation set up by the immediately preceding one or two tokens (e.g. modal plus main verb as in 'must contain', verb or preposition plus 'the', 'because' or 'capital' plus 'of', subject plus its characteristic verb as in 'Water boils', determiner plus noun as in 'The cat', or 'ORDER BY' plus a column name). It responds to the (trigger, completion) pair just read rather than to either token alone, fires across unrelated topics whenever such a pair occurs, and is unaffected by tokens after the peak.

The negative pole of L13/N2052 is a Wikipedia category-markup detector: it fires when the text contains a wiki category declaration ('Category:<term>', and even more strongly '[[Category:<term>]]'), ramping through 'Category' and ':' to a peak on the opening tokens of the category term, and it fires hardest when that term begins with a 4-digit year ('Category:1903 births/films', peak ~2.0 locally and 3.4 in full articles), less for word terms ('Category:Italian cyclists' ~1.4) and single words ('Category:Physics' ~0.9). The trigger is the wiki category syntax plus a year-like value, not the tokens or the year itself: running prose ('He was born in 1903', 0.2), ordinary label lines ('Name: John Smith' 0.07, 'Year: 1903 births' 0.46), CSV rows and infobox fields stay near zero, and a minority of strong activations (5 of the 20 scan examples, in non-wiki prose) are not explained by this hypothesis.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is a locally highly predictable continuation of the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens, completing a strong collocation, enumerative list, formulaic phrase, multi-digit number, markup tag, or sentence close; the same token in an unpredictable local frame activates it much less.

L13/N2763+ is a near-floor, non-selective unit rather than a feature detector: its 0.71 scan maximum is only the 2.2nd percentile of layer 13's 4,864 positive-pole maxima, 61% of tokens lie in the SwiGLU double-negative mode (g<0, u<0) where the gate is shut and the strength is just the size of the up-projection (r=0.97 with |u|, r=-0.04 with |g|), and 9.9% of all 200k scanned tokens already exceed a quarter of the maximum, so any 100+ token passage of running prose should be labelled active (peak ~0.35-0.5 of scale) and only short or non-prose text inactive. Its maximum lands on whichever rare or punctuation-heavy token projects largest ('.../', ',', ' etc', ']', ')'), so substituting one ordinary word for another - a noun for a noun, a date/clock string for words, or 'rather than' for 'and not' - is predicted to leave the peak within 0.05 of scale, and the digit peaks of the scan (dates, clock times, copyright years, which come from a separate gate-open g>0,u>0 mode on only 0.3% of tokens) do not reproduce in fresh short contexts (they peak at 0.17-0.31 raw, 0.24-0.44 of scale, on ':' or a space, not on the date).

The positive pole fires on the classifying, domain-specifying vocabulary of written expository prose - the word that states what kind of thing, or in what field or respect, the text is talking about: relational adjectives and noun classifiers such as medical, clinical, surgical, hospital, patient, official, academic, scientific, industrial, biological, brain, molecular, viral, prior (art), in vivo, state-of-the-art, and domain adverbs of respect such as internally or technically. It is near zero on qualitative adjectives (old, heavy, happy), generic determiners and pronouns, and on conversational, narrative, lyric or list-like text, and the same classifying word fires roughly twice as strongly when the surrounding passage is technical/expository than when it is casual.

The negative pole detects a reference to a historical period - a year, decade or century expression - and fires while that period is being read: it climbs from the leading '1' and peaks on the second or third digit once the century is fixed ('19' in 19th/1900s/1950s/1990s is the strongest form, 3.6-4.5 against the audit's 4.17 maximum, with 18xx ~2.2-2.9 and 1600s/1700s/20xx ~1.3-1.9 in the same frame, and all 19xx decades are indistinguishable), stays high on the trailing 'th'/'s'/'century', and fires moderately (1.0-1.5) on era-defining terms of the modern past (Soviet, World War II, Cold War, Victorian era); on this audit's 200k-token scan 1.8% of tokens lie inside a date/period expression, yet they hold 98% of the tokens above 2.0 (mean strength 0.51 there versus 0.03 elsewhere). It stays near zero when the same digits are quantities, codes, ordinals or addresses ('1876 dollars' 0.50, '1876 units' 0.12, '19th street' 0.12, 'Her phone number was 1876' 0.02), on antiquity (Roman 0.25, pharaoh 0.19, 'ancient' 0.09), on vague past talk ('in the past' 0.31) and on present-day prose; its transported output direction (TV/television/Sony/broadcast promoted, ancient/Romans/parchment suppressed) is diffuse with next-token KL about 8e-4, so the mechanism is retrospective and the weak positive pole (max 2.32 on the same scan) does not carry this feature.

N3451- is a retrospective 'frame-led word' detector: it puts a single sharp spike (up to 1.14, against a 1.18 scan maximum and a median of 0.002) on one word token when the words before it form a well-formed, conventional clause leading into that word, and the size of the spike is set by that left context rather than by the token itself - holding the peak token and its entire right context identical, scrambling the same preceding words ('The reason we continue to read/watch...' -> 'continue we reason The to read/watch...') drops ' read' from 1.14 to 0.03 (prompt peak 1.14 -> 0.61), replacing one frame word ('reason' -> 'point') drops the peak to 0.34, and the same word inside a plain progressive clause ('She was wearing headbands in the yard today.') peaks at only 0.14. Predict inactive when the same word's left context is scrambled, is degenerate filler ('ok ok ok...', 'the and of to in a...'), or is a bare list/label fragment, and predict active for a content word that closes a conventional clause - the pole is not a token detector (token identity explains 20% of variance, and ' wearing'/'reading' 1.11/1.09 both fire while 'carrying' 0.33 does not in the identical slot) and its Jacobian-lens direction names no target token (kurtosis 3.4, 0% logit/Jacobian overlap, zero-ablating the peaks shifts next-token KL by ~1e-5), so it reacts to what has been read rather than preparing a specific upcoming token.

The positive pole fires on the sub-word fragments of an unfamiliar, non-lexical letter string - an unseen acronym or ticker, a mixed letter-digit identifier, an e-mail local part, handle, hash or citation key - that the model cannot resolve to a dictionary word: activation is spread over the whole string ('RR' 0.7 then 'V' 2.5 inside 'RRV', 0.5-2.4 across 'X','K','Z') with the peak on one of its fragments, while the same letters inside ordinary words, familiar single-token acronyms (IBM, NASA, LLC, ABC), misspellings and non-English text leave it near zero. It is strongest when the unknown string is introduced as the label of a named entity ('The company Rentz (RRV)...' 3.8 vs 'Rentz (RRV)...' 1.7), so it is a retrospective detector of label/identifier strings being read out character by character rather than a next-token predictor.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token caps a conventional 2-4 word collocational frame built with the immediately preceding tokens (e.g. 'because of', 'energy into', 'characters and one', 'central bank raised', 'according to the report,'), with strength graded by how conventional the frame is; the identical surface token outside such a frame drives little activity, while clause-final punctuation fires on any complete preceding clause regardless of word choice.

The negative pole fires on the word-pieces of program identifiers (class, type, function, variable and package names) inside source code, peaking on the identifier's leading piece - ' Weather' in WeatherTodayModel, ' V'/'pn'/'Sites' in VpnSitesClient, ' aut' in autorest, ' graphics' in 'var graphics' - and staying elevated across the rest of the name, equally for declared and referenced names. It is near zero on language keywords, punctuation, operators, numbers and string text, and falls to roughly a tenth of peak when the very same words appear in ordinary prose (a code comment is intermediate); strength does vary between names (' Module', 'Sites', 'Sampling', 'Multi' fire several times harder than 'Client', 'Model', 'Foo'), which is the residual token-identity confound.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventional, locally predictable multi-token construction: a fixed idiom (Once upon), a quantity+unit or number+magnitude pairing (two cups, 13 billion, 3.9), a modal/negation+verb chunk (would not seek), a verb+preposition collocation (stored in), a determiner/adjective+noun phrase (the function, a positive one), or boilerplate code and syntax (second function parameter, SELECT-list FROM, range(10):, <html><), firing strongest for the most stereotyped completions. The identical surface token in a broken or non-conventional frame stays near-silent while open slots generalize (purple one), so the claim beats the token-identity confound; post-peak edits leave firing exactly unchanged and the Jacobian lens is Gaussian noise (kurtosis 3.38) whose promoted tokens never follow the peaks, ruling out lookahead.

The positive pole fires inside a span that reproduces wording already seen earlier in the same document - a paragraph duplicated two or three times, a question echoed from a page's question list as a section heading, a paper title re-quoted in a later citation, a term re-glossed in another language, a long sentence re-used verbatim - with strength growing both with how much of the current span is duplicated and with how many restatements the document carries (a duplicated paragraph or a four-question list reaches ~0.5-0.9 of scale, heavily duplicated passages 1.2-2.0). It stays near its floor (~0.1-0.25) on the first occurrence of exactly the same wording, on a single short sentence repeated only once, on new prose that merely continues the topic, on a repeated single word or ordinary short phrase, and on a quotation that is not recycled from earlier in the document.

Fires retrospectively when the current token continues an already-established repeated formatting template, i.e. the third-or-later same-format item such as successive quoted utterances, forum comments, markdown headings, JSON key lines, dated diary entries, filmography/config entries or code methods, with strength growing as more same-format items accumulate; stays weak on an isolated first heading, entry or quote and on ordinary prose paragraph or sentence breaks with no repeating template.

This pole fires retrospectively at a token that continues a coherent clause or fixed phrase, with strength graded by the length and fit of its left context: strong firing (about 0.15-0.32) requires at least four preceding tokens forming an intact clause whose final one or two tokens directly license the peak (for example stared at leading to dog, by 12 leading to percent, would not leading to seek). The same content word fires only weakly (about 0.00-0.12) when its licensing bigram is replaced (zebra for at sends dog from 0.32 to 0.09; late for 12 sends percent from 0.22 to 0.09), when word order is scrambled (rates falls to about 0.12), when the context is random words (peak about 0.12 or less), or when three or fewer tokens precede it (At the dog gives 0.00; isolated Dog gives 0.00); isolated, sentence-initial, and clause-truncating function-word tokens sit near zero. Because activation ramps up over the intact prefix, corrupting a late token leaves earlier tokens still firing (stared stays near 0.25; friend in an intact prefix reaches 0.21 while a trailing truncating the is 0.00), so this claim applies per token at the manipulated position, not to the whole-text maximum.

Retrospective chunk-completion detector: the pole peaks on the word that completes a conventional local chunk opened by the preceding token(s) -- canonically a sentence- or phrase-initial common noun after a determiner/article (The/A orchestra, recipe, senator, museum), and as offshoots the expected token after a code keyword (numpy to as, FROM to users), a verb licensing a preposition (hiked to to), a comma licensing 'and', a digit continuing a number, or the second half of a fixed collocation (central to bank, golden to brown). The same word without its conventional opener (as after 'served', orchestra after 'His', senator mid-sentence) or an unfamiliar word in the same slot (mat to xyz, brown to xyz) activates weakly or not at all, while changes after the peak leave the peak unchanged.

This pole fires where a document's or record's metadata block - a run of short label-plus-value fragments such as a title, byline, date, price, score, or attribute fields like 'Price: 12', 'Weight: 3 kg', 'Material: cotton' - closes and running body prose begins. It peaks on the block's closing token (a newline, period or bracketed title end) and on the body's first word, its strength grows with the number of fields already read (one bare label is usually sub-threshold, three or more attribute fields are strong), and it stays quiet when the same facts are written as sentences, at a paragraph break between two prose sentences, after a bare value-less heading such as 'Note' or 'Chapter One', and after dialogue speaker labels.

The negative pole of L13/N439 fires when the text sets a second, alternative referent against the one already in focus: it peaks on contrastive/substitutive phrases ('in favour of', 'instead of', 'in place of', 'rather than', 'as opposed to', 'compared to/with', 'in contrast to', 'unlike') and on the later members of an enumeration or alternative list ('X, Y and Z', 'X or Y', especially after 'like/such as/including'), the strength scaling with how explicitly the alternative is marked. It stays near the floor for proposition-level negation ('not', 'never'), for clause-linking contrast ('but', 'although', 'however', 'whereas', 'while'), for 'and' that merely sequences two clauses, and for 'between X and Y'; it is retrospective (zero-ablating the pole on its top examples leaves next-token probabilities essentially unchanged, KL 2e-5).

N4610- is a retrospective detector for the read-out of a low-frequency, domain-specific word: it fires on the token at which a rare content word becomes identified - usually the second BPE piece of a multi-token rare word (K|iv|u, Stone|h|enge, Hir|anyak|ashyapu, super|abs|orbent, Mach|-Z|ehnder, cata|le|psy, io.gitlab.art|urb|osch) and otherwise the distinctive word inside a specialised fixed phrase (coronal 'mass' ejections, institutional 'review' board, burden 'of' proof, ineffective assistance 'of' counsel). It scales with word rarity and with how established the word already is - a rare word's first mention is weak (0.0-0.3) while a re-mention or a strongly predicting frame raises it to 0.6-2.3 - whereas ordinary common words, common multi-piece words (somebody, nevertheless, understand), common phrases (peer review, cup of tea, state of the art), word-initial function words and never-seen nonsense strings (Blubberhouse, Xylophonia) stay near zero.

The negative pole fires on the token that is a word-internal fragment of an unfamiliar proper name: the interior or final subword piece of a rare surname, place name or coined/foreign-looking name that the model has no familiar lexical item or known entity for (Lovell 'ell' 2.4 of max 3.8, Standish 'ish' 2.2, Jodrell 'rell' 2.2, Amundsen 'sen' 3.2, Plesetsk 'etsk' 1.6, Menzies 'ies' 1.6, Schulich 'ich' 1.9, coined 'Zarvoski' 'ki' 2.3), with activation growing along the name so that the first piece stays near zero (' Lov' 0.25, ' Menz' 0.09, ' Zar' 0.41) and the last piece is strongest; on the held-out scan windows this is the only thing that reaches the 0.25x-max (about 0.94) active threshold in 5% of 32-token windows. It stays below that threshold on the identical fragments when the word is familiar English even if multi-piece and capitalized (internationalization 'ization' 0.0, multidisciplinary 0.09, Polytechnic 0.6, Pleistocene 0.6, telescope 0.02), when the earlier piece of the name is missing from the prompt ('elson-MIT' 0.3 vs 'Lemelson-MIT' 3.5, 'Menz ies' 0.35, bare 'ies' 0.02), and for names the model already holds as known entities or single familiar tokens (Churchill 1.4, Manchester 0.9, Shakespeare 0.65, 'Roald Amundsen' 0.5 against bare 'Amundsen' 3.2); the only non-name tokens seen at threshold are single commas or digits inside dense citation lists, at about 1.0.

Fires retrospectively on the specifying word inside a definite noun phrase that picks out one unique institution, titled office, law, work, or previously named place or person: the ordinal numbering a court, circuit, district or wing (Fourth, Eighth, Second, 3rd), the distinguishing word of a formal state or agency title (United, Republic, Associated), a title noun (prime, invention, act), or an anaphoric definite standing in for a just-named entity (the country for China, the latter for Vajpayee, the archipelago for Hawaii). Stays near floor on the same words used as predicative adjectives (remained united), indefinites (an economist), bare generics (Ancient giants), seasons (in the spring), or an ordinal with an ordinary time noun (19th year).

The pole fires on the token that opens or completes a time, quantity, or measure phrase, most strongly the bare space or word right before a number or unit (e.g. 'boils at [ ]100', 'prescribed [ ]500 mg', 'galaxy [ ]13 billion') or a time-completing word such as 'next [year]' or 'second [half]'. It stays near zero on the same position when the quantity or time slot is removed, and on ordinary non-quantity content words.

Fires on the leading digit or quantity word of a reported share, count or margin (percentages, vote tallies, patient/subject breakdowns, poll margins such as five points or ninety-five) when long prior context establishes empirical or technical reporting such as a clinical trial, survey, or election; the same numerals without that reporting frame do not activate it.

This pole fires retrospectively on the linking word (for, from, by, the, this) or status word (listed, rated, official, Score) that completes a formal provenance-or-status assertion about an item: a clause stating the item's source, authorship, listing, rating, or disposition in catalogue, legal, listing, review, or editorial-boilerplate register. Activation is driven by the preceding noun/verb phrase naming the assertion (e.g. 'catalogue record', 'Warranty', 'currently listed', 'Opinion', 'rated'), not by the linking word alone, so the same function word in casual text evokes little response.

This pole is a sparse retrospective detector (near-zero bulk over ~200k tokens, max 1.84) that fires on the function-word or evaluative-word joints of clauses stating a precaution, requirement, maintenance condition, or damage/malfunction contingency (e.g. 'avoids any nasty accidents with', 'be careful when handling', 'must contain', 'are dropped ... may'); the same surface tokens stay near zero in neutral reporting, bare punctual imperatives, direct harm statements without precautionary framing, and at sentence or piece onsets. Single sentences give weak-to-moderate activation; the top tail needs a longer cautionary passage. Acknowledged leftovers: neutral project-credit ('initial direction') and spec-conditional ('may be parsed') peaks are not covered.

Fires retrospectively on descriptions of movement along a path — journeys, travel, tours, deployments, treks, flights, and named routes, lines, and ways (railway lines, highways, rivers, parallels) — typically peaking on the preposition, destination, or route noun that completes the motion description, and staying quiet on matched static frames. A narrow offshoot also responds to dense coordinate-like reference strings such as multi-part legal citations with volume, page, and year numbers.

Fires at the onset of a numeral that states a cardinal quantity (a count or amount of things: subjects, people, hours, fans, donations, dollars, points, votes), peaking on the space token, '$', 'n =' or first digit just before the digits, and strongest when the frame sets up a sizable quantity ('a combined total of', 'over', 'about', 'more than $', '(n =', 'needs', 'population of'). It stays near zero when the same digits are an identifier or date (years, 'in 1960', page/room/ward/form numbers, 'Fig.', postal codes, coordinates) and when no number follows, so it encodes 'a quantity count is starting here', not digit tokens per se.

Fires on tokens inside spans that continue character-for-character, i.e. verbatim memorized strings: OSS license-header sentences ('This Source Code Form is subject to the terms of the ... License', the AS-IS disclaimer), court-caption formulas ('PER CURIAM' under 'UNITED STATES COURT OF APPEALS', '... CIRCUIT'), tool-output and template spans (netstat rows, docker info lines, '(ABSTRACT TRUNCATED AT 250 WORDS)', docfx/javadoc markup like '<!--[if IE]><![endif]-->'), box-drawn comment headers, Windows GAC strong-name paths (v4.0_4.0.0.0__b03f5f7f11d50a3a), and other fixed runs such as hex digits, aligned whitespace columns and rare word fragments (' abs|ou|lt|ely'); activation rises along such a span and peaks where the upcoming token is most certain (measured Spearman +0.63 between pole strength and next-token certainty, -0.63 with next-token surprise), which is why the very same fragments (' subject', 'f', ' C', 'RED') are inert in ordinary prose. Retrospective: the fixed span is already on the page, and the pole's output promotes its literal continuation (identifier/path/format fragments like 'f', '0', '_MS', ' terms', ' tcp', whitespace runs) while suppressing generic word continuations (' to', ' and', ' a', ','); ablation moves probability off exactly those continuation tokens.

Fires on text about cultivating crops or plants (agronomy/horticulture: fields, soil, fertilizer or pesticide application, irrigation, weeds competing with crops, plants grown under given conditions, harvests, drought, lawns): activation switches on at the first crop/plant-cultivation word and stays high over the following tokens of that clause, usually peaking on the verbs, prepositions, conjunctions and punctuation after the topic word (e.g. 'applied', 'for', 'under', 'during', 'and', '.') rather than on the topic noun itself; one short sentence is enough, no long context is required. It is weak (under about 30% of max) for livestock/animal husbandry and forestry/logging, and near zero for the same sentence frames about non-agricultural subjects (finance, plumbing, cell culture, computers, cooking, code).

This pole fires on the reference apparatus of formal, templated text rather than on what that text says: metadata field labels and their colons in a paper header ('author:', 'address:', 'bibliography:'), citation and numbered cross-reference markers ('[12, 13]', '([@bib26]', 'section 4', 'problem 6', 'Aim 3', '10.1002/mrm.27594'), section headings with their underline rules, and formulaic openers such as 'To identify ... we studied' or 'The purpose of this study was to'. Running narrative prose, plain bullet lists, config YAML, JSON and code stay far below it (peak under 0.2 of max), and the peak at a metadata label rises with how much front matter has already been read (deleting the abstract or the address fields drops 'author:' from 2.58 to 2.04 and 2.26).

Retrospective detector for the token that completes a locally conventionalized chunk given the preceding 1-3 tokens: a list-final conjunction ('Nairobi and'), a definite description ('The capital/river', 'the Moon', 'sea level'), an idiom or collocation ('fell silent', 'calls for', 'follows directly', 'he asked' after quoted speech), a code alias ('as np'), or a subword/digit completion ('Photosynthesis', '1600'). The same surface token is weak in an open compositional context ('A capital', 'each level', 'as module'), so local constraint predicts strength better than token identity alone.

This pole fires retrospectively on a token that continues an already-opened local construction: a decimal point inside a multi-digit number, an expected clause keyword (WHERE) inside a SQL statement, a tag inside a markup element, a mid-word subword, or a phrase-internal function word (preposition, particle, subordinator, article) extending the current phrase. It goes quiet when the same slot holds a token that breaks the construction, while a different word filling the same slot, or a change to a distant content word, leaves it essentially unchanged.

The negative pole fires, retrospectively, on the vocabulary of material livelihood: money and price terms (wage, salary, pay, compensated, cost, price, fee, expense, funding, income, profit, budget, cheap/expensive), work and its conditions (employees, workers, occupations, occupational, employment, injuries, safety), and the demographic and food/health conditions of everyday life (population, farmers, crops, yields, nutrients, deficiency, hunger, poverty, availability of a necessity). The response is semantic and register-independent rather than token-level: a money or welfare synonym in the same slot fires as strongly, while a physical or descriptive attribute in that slot (weight, hue, temperature, length, machinery, weather) leaves it near zero, and the same words fire inside narrative fiction; a phrase like 'the overall cost of the system' stays elevated across the next few tokens (cost 1.66, of 1.06, the 0.81, system 0.64), and quantities used as amounts that are converted, consumed or doubled ('0.032 atomic mass units of mass', 'the speed of his intel chips will double') also fire, unlike static attributes.

Fires on the final token that completes a multi-token proper name (software/framework, product, organisation, league, place) when that name is the topic label of a heading-like slot: the opening words of a title (e.g. a StackExchange 'Q:\n\n' title, a tournament/page title), an item in a 'Category:' list at the end of a wiki article, or a name the document has already established as its recurring subject. The same name inside ordinary running prose on first mention, a name broken by a function word, or a plain common noun stays near zero (< 0.2).

This negative pole fires on a clause that restates content already present in the same context: it peaks on the answer, heading-repeat, definition or summary that re-uses the distinctive content words of an earlier question, heading or claim (the FAQ/definition pattern), and its strength grows with the number of echoed content words (none shared ~0.1-0.3 of the 1.386 max, three or four shared ~0.9-1.3), saturating around three. It falls back to baseline when the clause introduces new vocabulary even on the same topic, and its output direction barely moves the next-token distribution (Jacobian kurtosis 3.4, lens agreement 0%, measure_lookahead KL 7e-5), so it is retrospective rather than predictive.

The pole fires on promotional web-marketing prose: copy that promises or explains how to improve a website's or a business's online results, including SEO / search-engine-optimisation vocabulary (keywords, links, rankings, traffic, visitors, banners, logos, e-commerce) and benefit claims such as 'we can help you boost your sales' or 'we offer a full range of SEO services including ...'. It stays inactive on descriptive and narrative prose, news reports, technical documentation, service pages that merely state what an offline business offers, and short calls to action with no improvement claim.

The pole fires retrospectively on the short run of grammatical scaffold words that carries a clause's copula/auxiliary, typically a relativizer or light subject followed by is/was/will/'s/to ('...a LEGO Dimensions announcement which is supposed to...', '...; your first post wasn't...', '...a file was...', '...is expected to...', '...astronomers expect it to...'), and drops to ~0 one token later on the clause's lexical verb or on an adjacent rare content word ('happen', 'modified', 'peak', ' LEGO', ' Dimensions'). The run is only scored when 20-50 tokens of preceding text have already fixed the clause's content: the same words alone give 0.06, after an unrelated sentence 0.5-0.6, inside their own passage 2.6-2.9, and the same clause with 'that' instead of 'which', or with a coordinated instead of a relativized clause, drops to 1.3-1.7 -- so it tracks how tightly the passage constrains the current grammatical run, not the identity of the token; the opposite pole is the numeric counterpart, peaking on digit continuations of numbers ('1[6].00', '7[0] months', '5[0]0th').

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is the conventional, highly constrained continuation of the preceding one to three tokens — the verb licensed by its subject (Shakespeare->wrote), the function word completing a fixed frame (sits on->the, Tuesday through->Sunday, converts energy->into), or the noun completing a stock phrase (triangle->inequality) — and stays low when the identical token follows an incongruous prefix. Changing only the following token leaves the peak unchanged, so it reacts to the licensing prefix, not to any upcoming token.

Fires on the last element of a coordinated series of three or more parallel items, usually the content word right after the final 'and'/'or' (e.g. 'hot, hard, dirty and [dangerous]', 'foods, fuels, and [medicines]', 'advice, diagnosis, or [treatment]', '..., Glasgow and [Hull]'). The final item must be a plausible member of the same category, though it need not be predictable. A secondary trigger is the volume/number slot that closes the journal-name part of a bibliographic citation ('Genome [ ]47', 'Naturalist, [ ]152', 'Vol[.] 9'). Activity is weak or absent when the same word stands alone, ends only a two-item pair, follows repeated intensifiers, or does not fit the list's category.

Fires on website cookie/tracking-consent notice boilerplate, i.e. a site telling its visitor that it uses cookies (or analytics/tracking) to give them the best experience and that continuing to browse/use the site means they agree (English, French and other languages). Activity builds across the notice clause and peaks on the sentence-ending punctuation (or the following 'By'/'This') right after a 'we use cookies to ... experience/website' or 'this site uses cookies' clause; it is near zero when cookies are a topic rather than a notice (browser cookie how-tos, studies about cookie banners) or food (bake/eat cookies, jar of cookies), and weak (~0.15-0.45 of max) on adjacent legal boilerplate like reCAPTCHA notices, newsletter sign-up privacy lines and GPL licence headers.

The negative pole fires at the token that completes a NAMED HUMAN SOURCE OR ACTOR inside a passage that reports what people said or did - the last subword of a person's surname ('Shull', 'Susler', 'Schneider', 'Bohr', 'Trachtenberg', 'Bush'), or the comma or first predicate token right after it, staying high over the first words of the predicate (' had' 1.06, ' this' 0.72, ' said' 1.03) - and across the scan its active tokens sit immediately before a reported-speech verb (' reported' 9.7% active, ' told' 6.3%, ' said' 3.6%, against 0.09% of all tokens). It is an attribution detector, not a name-hole or trigger-token detector: the same name in object or by-phrase position (0.23-0.34), a person already named in the immediately preceding clause (0.26), a role description of the same referent ('the beat writer', 'the man': 0.15-0.34), an indefinite description, a place name and an inanimate subject (0.05-0.45) all stay low (named organisations and collective source nouns are a weaker, unreliable extension, 0.3-1.2), and because the response is passage-gated a bare one-clause prompt containing a full name reaches only 0.10-0.67 while the same clause reaches 1.6-2.0 once the preceding sentence reports another named person's statement ('Jordan Raanan reported the visit first.').

In its g+/u- sign regime this negative pole fires on a '.' token that terminates a grammatically complete declarative clause, acting as a retrospective clause-closure signal (single-token ablation of the final content word or the period removes ~0.5-1.2 of strength; integrated-gradients mass sits on the period plus the preceding ~5 tokens, mean distance 3.2). The same '.' fires weakly or not at all when it ends a fragment ('before the.' 0.02 vs complete 0.24), when the terminal is '?'/'!' (0.73->0.14), on abbreviation-internal periods, on decimal points whose prefix is not a complete clause ('I have 3.' ~0.0 vs 'The value is 3.' 0.46), or in very short clauses ('She arrived yesterday.' 0.0); strength scales with clause weight (0.24 at 6-12 tokens up to 0.73+ at 13). A separate g-/u+ regime firing mid-sentence on famous-name tokens (Moon, Seine, Neil, world) is a distinct mechanism outside this claim.

The pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a conventional time reference used as a clause-level time adjunct: the '.m' piece of an a.m./p.m. clock time ('The shop shuts at 5 p.m.', 'open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.'), a weekday or schedule word that fixes a recurring time or a deadline ('on weekdays', 'Tuesday through Sunday', 'by Friday'), or a period word inside an explicit comparison ('compared with last month', 'than the previous quarter'). It is not a fixed-collocation or number+unit detector: the same time word stays near baseline in attributive use ('the 6 p.m. train was cancelled', 'the 11 a.m. train'), as do vague time words ('noon', 'later'), bare durations that are the object of a verb ('lasted 45 minutes'), full numeric dates ('on 12 June 2019') and non-temporal measures ('weighed 3 kg', '1200 metres long').

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token continues or completes the local phrase set up by the preceding one to two tokens (list noun plus comma, 'def' plus name, verb plus particle/negation/complement, formula opener plus continuation), with strength scaling with how constraining that local context is. It stays near zero at sentence and phrase onsets and after breaks, so the same peak token (comma, 'not', 'out', 'and') is active as a continuation but inactive as a fresh start.

The pole is a dial for plain everyday human-life prose: it accumulates over a passage of ordinary narrative or description of people and their surroundings (children, family, neighbours, homes, gardens, schools, shops, streets, food, errands) and sits near zero or below on text whose referents are technical, abstract, numeric or institutional (buffers and semaphores, enzymes and substrates, committee reports and statutes, citation strings, arithmetic drills, code). Inside such a passage it peaks on the short grammatical word that hands over to the next common noun - 'the', 'a', 'of', 'in', 'to', 'and', 'or', 'with', 'at', 'by', 'including' or a list comma - and collapses on the noun itself, and the build-up is slow, so one everyday phrase is weak while a paragraph of it is strong.

L15/N1229- is a register detector for text written in an institution's own voice: it rises over a whole passage of corporate, administrative or technical self-description - mission and values statements, product and press-release claims, business reporting, official notices, reference entries, and code or markup - and peaks on whichever token in that passage carries most of the register (an abstract evaluative word such as 'excellence' 1.54, 'innovation' 1.40, 'seamless' 0.85 or 'integrity' 0.77; a formally specified value such as the year in 'The bridge was built in 1893' 0.30 or the times in 'from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.' 0.23; or the closing bracket or tag of a code entry, ')' 0.31 and '></' 0.24). The same content in plain speech or personal narration falls to the floor - 'We deliver excellence across every engagement' 1.54 vs 'We do good work for our clients' 0.08, 'Our team values integrity above all' 0.77 vs 'He questioned her integrity' 0.01, 'The committee reviewed the documents' 0.29 vs 'The children found the documents' 0.16, and a three-sentence personal passage peaks at 0.19-0.25 against 1.46-1.66 for a corporate one - and the mechanism is retrospective: the Jacobian-lens output is flat (kurtosis 3.17, 0 of 10 tokens shared with the logit lens) and zero-ablating the pole moves next-token probabilities by KL 1.7e-5.

L15/N1365+ is a retrospective detector of specific, information-bearing content: it is strongly active when the text carries rare or specialized vocabulary (technical/taxonomic terms, terms of art, names, precise quantities) or states a definition or specification, is near zero on boilerplate, UI strings, list fragments and generic non-topical text, and sits in between on plain narrative prose. Its response is integrated over roughly the preceding ten tokens, so it builds across the sub-word pieces of a rare word and stays elevated over the short phrase that carries it, and it falls back to zero when the same content is merely repeated from the preceding context.

Fires retrospectively on the content token that completes a locally initiated two-word chunk (determiner/adjective/preposition/verb plus its expected noun, comparative adjective plus 'than', verb plus particle, or fixed phrase such as 'sea level'), driven jointly by the peak token and the 1-2 tokens immediately before it; the same content word without its constraining lead-in, or with the lead-in broken, activates weakly or not at all.

L15/N1572+ marks the opening of a new specific reference inside enumerative or attributive text: it fires on the boundary token that introduces a proper title, name, cited source, byline, credit or URL - the determiner (' The'/' A'), the preposition ('according to', 'in', 'for', 'by'), the opening quote or the citation bracket when one is present, otherwise the first token of the name itself - and the firing is weak on a list's first item, builds over the next two or three items, and is near zero for the same tokens in ordinary prose, for lowercased or common-noun items, and for an item repeated verbatim. It is retrospective rather than lookahead: the Jacobian lens is flat (kurtosis 3.2, lens agreement 0%) and zero-ablating the pole changes next-token probabilities by about 2e-5 KL, so it integrates the enumerative context already read instead of preparing a particular upcoming token.

Activates when the current token completes a high-frequency local bigram or fixed collocation with its immediate neighbours (e.g. 'over the', 'at the', 'called the', 'sea level', 'as np', 'Tokyo'), i.e. a fluent formulaic continuation; the same word in a rare local pairing does not drive it.

Retrospective detector that peaks on the connective token inside a formal locator/attribution string -- the @, dot-piece, slash, colon, by/for, or identifier digit of a URL, email, file path, contact number, document/trial ID, citation, or institutional committee/document name -- that tells where to find, contact, or credit something after a named project, organization, or work. Removing the locator/attribution frame while keeping the same surface token sharply reduces activity.

The positive pole is a retrospective detector of author- and document-facing discourse: it fires on stretches where the writer's own voice is speaking (first person or possessive 'I/we/my' in a question or statement of the writer's situation, e.g. 'Q:\n\n... I was trying to...', 'I have a small...', 'We give...') or where a text or discussion is the thing being described or pointed at ('The article explains...', 'See also this article ... for more information'). The same content attributed to a third party leaves it near zero ('He was trying to shoot a group of people' 1.16 vs 'I was trying...' 3.07; 'She has a small dog' 0.21 vs 'I have a small dog' 1.29; 'The teacher explains' 0.03 vs 'The article explains' 0.98), as does ordinary third-person narration (<=0.1), and the pole's output direction promotes the vocabulary of explanation and discussion (explain, discuss, understand, inform, details).

This pole fires retrospectively on the onset token of an exact formal payload — the leading digit of a number, a single-letter variable, or a compact symbolic chunk ('=', '(n', '(a', '(i') — when the preceding clause has opened a slot requiring a specific value, bound variable, assignment, or function argument (a measurement/quantity frame, year, dose, or code/math expression). The same digit or letter outside such a slot, or a spelled-out quantity word or plain word substituted into the same position, drives it weakly or not at all.

L15/N3118+ tracks a legal/regulatory framing of a transfer or holding of goods: it is active over the nominal naming the transaction (sale, selling, possession, distribution, trafficking, smuggling, transport, import, supply, manufacture, purchase, carrying) plus its linking function word, peaking on that word (' of'/' for'/' the') and returning to zero on the object NP; the object itself is irrelevant (knife, car, table, dog, person all give the identical 3.24). It is near zero when the same nominal is ordinary commerce with no legal frame ('the recent sale of a knife' 0.15, 'he was praised for the sale of a knife' 0.36) and for offences against persons in the identical 'charged with the X of' frame (murder 0.00, assault 0.00, robbery 0.00, theft 0.69), matching the scan peaks 'possession of heroin', 'distributing an image of a nude minor', 'the sale of counterfeit goods', 'illegal logging' and Dutch 'verkoop van' (sale of) under a ban.

Fires most on the token that continues a highly stereotyped multi-token collocation or boilerplate frame (e.g. from-9-a.m.-to, called-the, after-three-days, around-the-year, to-the-pan, import-X-as, SELECT-THEN-FROM), driven by the preceding 2-3 tokens; the same function or content tokens in novel or anomalous frames activate it weakly or not at all.

L15/N3431- fires where the text specifies units of productive labour or of the compute that performs it: a counted or measured work-role (sixty engineers 1.75, two engineers 1.09, sixty developers 2.21, sixty labourers 2.00, hundreds of our nation's top scientists 1.64, upwards of 60 members of staff 3.86) or the machines doing that work (an 8-core processor 3.30, sixteen cores 3.30, the number of worker threads 3.79, sixty processors 2.47, sixty CPUs 2.05, sixty servers 1.61, sixty robots 1.13); the count/measure is what lifts it, since the same work-role without one stays low (engineers designed the bridge 0.07, the engineers at NASA 0.12). It stays near zero when the identical counting frame names performers, consumers, professional services or ordinary objects (sixty musicians/actors/dancers/tourists/lawyers/paintings 0.26-0.54, two musicians 0.39) and on figurative or performative work (the works of Shakespeare 0.02, she works as a musician 0.04), while a passage that already establishes a project's workforce, machinery or compute keeps it mildly elevated (0.7-1.5) on ordinary tokens there; the mechanism is retrospective.

The positive pole fires where a clause predicates something of a person or a group of people: it peaks on the modal or auxiliary that states what those people can, will, want to, are expected to or are allowed to do ('a consumer can' 2.7, 'millions of voters are expected to' 3.2, 'users searching', 'a woman wants'), and on the people-noun phrase itself when the group is quantified ('millions of voters', 'thousands of devotees'). The same frame with an inanimate or organizational subject stays near zero ('the machines can' 0.27, 'millions of tonnes are expected to' 0.18, 'the buildings can' 0.24), and a plain past-tense verb after a people-subject is also near zero ('the customers returned', 0.00 on 'returned'), so the pole tracks people as the agent of a modal or expected action rather than the modal itself or the tense.

The pole fires on the formal record of a patent or a scientific publication: patent front-matter and prior-art formulae and numbers ('This application is based upon and claims the benefit of priority ...', 'as disclosed in Japanese Patent Laid-Open No. 11-325849', 'U.S. Pat. No. 4,205,780'), journal citation strings and reference lists (volume:page, DOI, 'Angew. Chem., Int. Ed. 46:5779-5782, 2007'), and funding/grant acknowledgements. It falls to zero as soon as the same documents turn to their content (technical description, patent claim bodies, argument) and stays there on ordinary prose, book bibliographies and commercial or personal identifiers (invoice, model or phone numbers), with a bare topical mention of a patent in narrative sitting near the activity line rather than high; the positive pole, by contrast, picks up statute-style citations such as 'Rule 26(c)' and 'ORS 192.640'.

Fires at the token that advances a specific, situated event or addressee-anchored frame given its left context: the verb completing a fitting agent-action onset (She opened, the river flooded), the determiner or object completing a caused-action phrase (played the, Take the, drank the water, close the door), or the head of a directive or interrogative frame (Please + verb, Where are + dynamic verb, then, According to), with strength graded by semantic fit (river 0.87 > lake 0.43 > idea 0.01; water 0.86 versus door 0.05 after drank). It stays near zero for selectional violations, abstract subjects, mental-state verbs (believed 0.00), static noun completions (keys 0.13), generic statements, and repeated or late-clause function words. The output direction promotes proximal deictics (this/here, Jacobian kurtosis 16.8), consistent with grounding a just-established situation, but peaks never precede those tokens and right-context edits leave peak strength unchanged (opened 0.49, are 0.61, stirred 0.67 regardless of continuation), so the unit is retrospective, not predictive.

This pole fires retrospectively on the slot-filler token that completes a short functional frame: the noun completing a determiner or prepositional phrase (The algorithm, a kingdom, the pan), the verb completing a subject or 'to' frame (She opened, to submit), the alias after 'as' (as np), or the variable after a lead-in (If x) — i.e. the word that names the entity or action the clause is about. Replacing a valid filler with a word that cannot satisfy the frame collapses activation, while swapping one valid filler for another preserves it; its output direction promotes naming tokens (called, termed, 称为), consistent with marking the definiendum.

The positive pole fires on the possibility/ability auxiliaries 'can' and 'could' when the clause's subject is the writer or the reader — 'I can …', 'you can …', 'I could …' — peaking on the auxiliary itself (or on the pronoun immediately before it), and it is strongest in running prose where at least one earlier sentence precedes the construction. It reads near zero for the same auxiliaries under a third-person or impersonal subject ('they can', 'it can', 'that can', 'the machine can', 'the setting can be removed'), for the other modals with I/you ('will', 'would', 'should', 'must', 'may', 'might'), and when the construction opens a text.

The pole fires while the model spells out the identity of a software artifact: it is active across a dotted software version number in a software/computing context (the digits and periods of 'django 1.2.3', 'Ubuntu 20.04', 'v2.4.1', 'firmware 15.2', peaking at or just before the first separator after the major number), and more weakly on the tokens of software product/framework/OS names themselves (' django', ' nginx', 'oa' in Modoboa, 'jango' in Django). The computing context can be a software name anywhere in the recent text ('I use django. The fix landed in 1.2.3' fires on the version) or plain engineering register ('the bug was fixed in 1.2.3' fires; 'the car was fixed in 1.2.3' does not), while the same surface forms outside software stay near zero: decimals in ordinary prose ('1.2.3 cups', '3.5 percent', '1.5 mg'), sentence-final periods, and hardware model numbers or proper nouns (Toyota Corolla 2014, iPhone 12, Xeon E5-2690, Mary in London).

This pole fires retrospectively on the current token when it is a semantically salient open-class word (concrete noun, proper name, descriptive adjective, or distinctive verb, including stressed subword pieces) that fits its local phrasal context, and stays near zero on high-frequency function words, digits, and punctuation; it is driven mostly by the peak token itself with gating from 1-3 preceding tokens, and promotes no coherent upcoming-token set.

The pole fires when the text already read describes a change of state applied to something that exists - a replacement, renovation, restoration, repair, removal, relocation, renaming, or, in code, an assignment or UPDATE that sets a field to a new value - and it writes change/repair vocabulary (change, new, fix, remove, restoration) into the residual. It is retrospective and local: the peak sits on the auxiliary or function word that introduces the change predicate ('to', 'can', 'will', 'must be', 'were', 'être', 'for', 'name') and its height is fixed by the preceding text, so swapping the following word ('can do' -> 'can see' -> 'can keep', 'rénové' -> 'vérifié') leaves the peak identical to three decimals.

The negative pole fires at the start of a prenominal modifier that stands between a quantifier and the head noun it modifies: an adjective, adverb or measure-word such as 'square' in '4,000 square feet', 'consecutive' in '42nd consecutive week', 'glorious' in 'five glorious victories', 'additional' in '30 additional years', or the ordinal/unit suffix token when it is fused to the numeral ('nd' in '42nd', '-b' in '137-bp'). It stays near zero when the quantifier is followed directly by its head noun ('three hours', 'five victories', '4,000 feet', '25 years'), when the same modifier follows an article or possessive ('the glorious victories', 'my glorious victories'), and on the head noun itself, which the neuron's positive pole picks up instead (0.5-0.9); strength is graded by how quantitative the determiner is (numerals 2.0-4.5 > few/many/some/dozens of/countless 1.1-1.6 > demonstratives ~1.0 > articles and possessives 0.1-0.5) and, within the construction, by modifier gradability (evaluative adjectives above classifying ones).

L15/N980- is the negative side of a contract-and-terms neuron: its positive pole fires on the token that states a contract, deal, term or its renewal/termination ('four-year deal', 'signed a contract', 'the lease was renewed', 're-elected to a term'), while this pole fires on ordinary prose tokens that state or report the terms of an agreement, payment or obligation rather than asserting one - commercial and financial reporting of deals, acquisitions, mergers, dividends, earnings, pensions, salaries, fees and loans, the transfer/salary vocabulary of sports news, and licence or legal fine print that conditions, restricts or disclaims an obligation ('unless required by applicable law', 'may not', 'in no event ... liable', 'without warranty'). It sits at its floor on neutral narration, description, science and code, and on the agreement word itself, where the neuron fires on its positive pole instead.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a frequent local bigram or trigram collocation (ORDER BY, O(n, import numpy as, greater than, seek re-, are all), with peak strength graded by how frozen the collocation is: breaking the first half collapses the peak while the peak token alone elsewhere fires weakly. Outside these frozen completions it fires weakly and diffusely on ordinary predictable words with no shared syntactic or semantic feature: token identity explains 80% of variance and both vocabulary lenses are near-Gaussian (kurtosis 3.2, 20% agreement), so the crisp claim covers only the collocation-completion peaks.

This pole is a retrospective detector for length/composition specifications of an account or identity credential field: it ramps up through clauses like 'password/PIN/username/passphrase must/should/needs/has (contain | have | be) (at least | exactly) N ...' and peaks on the quantity or complement token (eight, four, least, characters, number). Identical requirement wording with a non-credential subject (recipe, story, meal, contract, committee) evokes only weak activity, and the specific quantity word does not matter. Its output direction strongly suppresses name-related tokens, consistent with firing in credential-field contexts while suppressing name prediction; weak responses on other specifying complements (guilty, light, WHERE) are acknowledged offshoots.

The pole is a retrospective detector of words that name a relation of equality/equivalence or quantitative comparison: it takes its strongest scan values on ' relationship' (5.13, 'a curve-fit to determine the polynomial relationship'), ' equal' (4.53 in 'power-demanding equalisers', and roughly 0.3-1.0 of max in every sense, from 'equal to 44 per cent' and 'equal rights' to 'equalisers'), ' exponential' (4.13), ' equality' (3.53), the 'qu' piece of tokenizer-split inequity/inequitable (0.45-0.67 of max), and 0.1-0.6 of max on the relation nouns of quantitative analysis (correlation, relation, difference, comparison, similarity, metric, causal, correspond, proportional, dependence) plus ' unequal'. It is not a spelling or fairness detector: it stays at or below 0.1 of max on other 'equ' words (equipment, equation, equilibrium, adequate, sequel), on 'qu' inside non-equ words ('earthquake' 0.09, 'vanquished' 0.00), on the fairness/justice lexicon (fair, fairness, justice, discrimination, bias, parity), on generic comparison words (link, gap, pattern), on ' independence' in its political/personal sense ('financial independence' 0.00 against 2.48 for statistical independence assumptions), and on ' equality' as the head of a social-identity compound (gender/racial/marital/gay equality 0.02-0.4 of max against 0.4-1.0 for the bare noun); within-word variation remains only partly explained ('created equal' 0.00), with unexplained leftovers on evolutionary/ecological and the keep/kept/holding tokens.

Qwen2.5-0.5B L16/N1584- fires on the lecture/talk schema: a scheduled occasion at which someone speaks to an audience. It peaks on the word that names such an occasion (lecture, talk, keynote, seminar, symposium, colloquium, webinar, presentation, speech, sermon, briefing, conference, session, classroom), on the person who speaks at or attends one (speaker, presenter, lecturer, panelist, attendee, participant), and on the participation verbs attend / speak at / present at / headline when their object is such an occasion; it fires for unseen synonyms, in past, scheduled and announcement frames, and in other languages (French conference 3.85, Chinese 讲座 3.66 and 演讲 2.57). It stays below the activity line for other kinds of scheduled happening (party, wedding, funeral, protest, rally, election, exam, interview, exhibition, screening, recital, play, gig; a bare 'concert' is the one partial exception I could not explain), for venue and equipment words (auditorium, podium, microphone), and for non-talk senses of its words (the speaker on my phone, the speaker of the parliament, the class struggle, talk about the budget, attend to a patient).

The positive pole is a retrospective, graded detector of clauses that fix how something is to be done, measured, provided or constrained: formal method, parameter, standard and paradigm specifications drive it hardest (peaks 2-3.5, e.g. post hoc Tukey, incubated at 37 C for 30 min, visual search paradigm with 12 distractors), legal and schedule rules moderately (~1), and everyday imperative procedures with measured parameters (recipes, dosages, build commands) plus specification sentences buried in long narrative only weakly (0.25-0.65) yet still above baseline. It stays at incidental-mention levels when the same words are merely reported, remembered or narrated without enacting a specification -- past-tense news, memoir and meta-mention such as Temperatures hit 37 C across the region, post hoc which he had learned in a statistics course, or version 1.0 had sold badly -- so everyday procedures count as weak in-scope positives while reported measurements and mentioned terms count as negatives.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a locally projected phrase: the head noun after a determiner or adjective, the result-state adjective or boolean after a light verb or copula, the identifier after def, or the second half of a conventionalized compound or collocation. The same word outside its licensing frame, or a non-canonical substitution in the same slot, drives it to baseline, while a canonical alternative in the same slot (false for true) preserves it.

Retrospective: fires on a whole content word (noun, adjective, gerund, adverb, a sentence- or line-opening word, or the last piece that completes a tokenizer-split title word such as Cer|emony, Butter|flies, Sur|prising) whose identity the PRECEDING words did not predict, most strongly for abstract, institutional, collective or quantity/size words (knowledge, support, record, history, evidence, army, government, world, market, training, number, large, small) sitting right after an article, preposition, possessive or a sentence/line start; whether the word fits what comes after is irrelevant, so 'A large number of...', 'The world watched', 'the training program', 'after years of wrestling' and 'caused by number of' are all active. It stays near zero when the left context nearly forces the word ('for all of your support', 'Second World War', 'world record', 'basic training', 'stock market', 'in the history of'), on function words, pronouns, digits, punctuation, code keywords and the very first token of a text, and is usually weak (under ~0.3 of max) on a noun that follows an adjective and on mundane concrete nouns (chair, dog, car, park, shop, shirt, snow) even when they are surprising.

Fires on a word-initial 'dis'-family subword fragment (' disc', 'Disc', ' dis', ' diss', ' dist', ' disb', ' DIS', 'D|IS', and the next piece such as 'j' in ' dis|j|unct') when that token is an unfinished word stem that the tokenizer split off from a longer dis- word (discarding, discloses, Discography, Disciplining, disallowed, disorganized, disarming, discredited, dissimilarity), strongest for ' disc'/'Disc' (0.5-1.1 of max) and moderate for ' dis'/' diss'/' dist' (0.3-0.7). It stays near zero (< 0.1 of max) on dis- words that are a single whole-word token (' discussing', ' dismissing', ' disclaimer', ' display', ' disease', ' dispute', ' Disney', ' Discovery') and on the same stems with another prefix (encloses, rearming, reorganized, unallowed), so it tracks 'inside an unfinished dis- word' rather than the letters d-i-s or the negation meaning.

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a stereotyped, highly predictable local frame: a canonical collocation or construction (The stock market, Photosynthesis converts, follows directly, contract was void, eight characters and one, increased by 12, are all, For i) or a subword completion (viol-inist, Mit-ochond). The same token outside its frame (soup stock, engine converts, two numbers, some capitals, mid-sentence telescope) fires weakly or not at all.

The pole fires on the linking or metalinguistic token that introduces a specific named expression: inside Title-Case (or quoted/italicised) work titles and name phrases it peaks on the lowercase connective (' of' in "The Picture of the Day", ' a' in "To Kill a Mockingbird", ' to' in "A Farewell to Arms", ' on' in "Attack on Titan"), and in term/label constructions it peaks on the word or field label that introduces the expression (' term', ' word', ' phrase', 'Terms like', 'Quote:', 'Keywords:', 'See also', 'abstract:'). The same words in ordinary lower-case prose, as isolated tokens, or in non-naming headings such as 'Notes:'/'Warning:' stay near zero, so the trigger is the name/term-mention frame rather than token identity.

This pole fires on a prenominal modifier that identifies which instance, value or version of the head noun is meant - the determinative adjectives certain, specific, particular, given, specified, designated, predetermined, preset, predefined, fixed, default, desired, intended, requested, chosen, selected, arbitrary, same, different, respective - and not on the article, on demonstratives/quantifiers/ordinals (every 0.07, each 0.07, first 0.07, only 0.07, this 0.72, that 1.23, against 4.84 for 'a certain' in the same frame) or on ordinary descriptive adjectives in the identical slot (a large number 0.18, a blue car 0.02, a central angle 0.06, a long letter 0.06). It tracks that sense rather than the surface word or what follows it: 'a certain amount of time' peaks 9.48 on ' certain' but 'I am certain the ...' only 0.23, 'a fixed price' 2.55 but 'they fixed a price' 0.41, 'a given day' 5.32 but 'given the circumstances' 0.25, the negated 'unspecified' keeps only half (2.34 against 5.06), the token after the modifier is always at the floor (amount 0.00, direction 0.00, genre 0.00), and the negative pole never leaves zero, so the pole marks the identifying modifier itself and nothing downstream.

The negative pole is a ball-game-play detector: it fires on passages where a ball or puck is being played in a sporting contest - kicked, thrown, passed, hit, shot, crossed, cleared, headed, putted or carried into or past a target, or to a teammate - and on the scoring plays, points, records and match statistics that report such play, in English or Chinese. Its activity spreads over the whole passage (most input attribution sits more than 16 tokens back, mean distance 46) and peaks on whichever token carries the play or the statistic ('-point' in '800 3-pointers', 'tries' in a try-scoring line, ' hit' in 'he hit .200', 'passing' in '577 passing yards', the 'the'/' into' of 'crossed the ball into the box'), while ball-less sport (400 m running, swimming, chess, esports), ball-sport administration and business news (fixtures, transfers, kit), ordinary motion of non-ball objects and non-sporting numbers stay near zero; outside a formal game it still fires on the same ball-propulsion schema ('kicked the ball into the hedge' 6.3 vs 'kicked the stone into the hedge' 1.2).

The negative pole responds to a field of a biology/medicine literature record, peaking on the separator or whitespace that opens its next field - the ':' in 'Magn Reson Med. 2019;81[:]2551-2565', the space before the pages when the same citation is written out as prose ('...in Magnetic Resonance in Medicine in 2019, volume 81, pages[ ]2551'), the space after '=' in an abstract's statistics ('95% CI =[ ]2.35-15.88'), and the ') (' that closes a long typed parameter list and opens the result list of a signature. Identically formatted citations carrying a physics/engineering/computing venue ('Phys Rev B. 2019;81:2551-2565', 'Adv Neural Inf Process Syst. 2017;30:5998-6008'), the same numbers in running prose, and ordinary narrative text stay near zero.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is the locally licensed continuation or closure of a frame opened within the previous few tokens: a delimiter or keyword completing a code, SQL, or markup construct (comma inside a function signature, '):' closing a loop header, FROM after a select list, '=' after a variable), or a function word extending an open clause in prose (relative 'which', contrastive 'but', reported-speech pronoun 'she', determiner 'your', quantifier 'all'). The same surface token (',', 'and') is silent when the preceding tokens open no such frame, so activity depends on the local frame, not on token identity alone.
