This pole fires retrospectively on reader- or platform-directed gating and payoff lines in human-authored threaded help, forum, and site-administration pages: registration requirements, signup redirects, compliance pledges, placement rules, regeneration warnings, and the answer-boundary markers (bullets, A:, You) that deliver them, once a multi-step setup such as a question, code block, or site boilerplate has accumulated behind them. The same payoff words standalone, restated as flat exposition without a modal consequence, or inside terse machine-generated status logs, standalone legal-licence bodies, and topical Q&A exposition do not drive it; earlier licence-text and answer-header scan hits fired only where they sat inside such threaded instructional scaffolding, not as licence bodies themselves.

This pole fires retrospectively on definite noun phrases: it peaks on the definite article 'the'/'The' when the next word is a common noun, and on a singular count noun when the immediately preceding token is the definite article; the same nouns with indefinite articles, bare forms, or demonstratives fire it less. Its output direction suppresses competing determiner and relativizer forms ('those', 'that', 'whose').

Fires when the text conventionally designates something — an individual, place, kind or title is said to be called / known as / termed / described as / dubbed / nicknamed / referred to as ['the'] Y (Chinese 被称为 / 称为 / 俗称) — with the peak on the naming predicate (' called', ' known', '被称为') and/or on the determiner that opens the designation (' the Y'). It stays near zero on the phone/summon sense of 'call', on one-off naming of a particular person, on plain taxonomic labelling of an ordinary object ('My friend is called John', 'The teacher called the student a genius', 'The student was called a genius', 'The tool is called a hammer', 'The function is called the sigmoid function' — all ≤ 0.15 of the scan max), and on ordinary declaratives or plain copulas with no naming predicate; inside the frame the strength is graded, with habitual adverbs, definite designations and place/kind subjects reaching 0.5-1.4x the scan max.

This negative pole is a war / armed-conflict detector: it fires on prose that describes organized fighting between armed forces - wars, invasions, battles, sieges, bombings, ambushes, offensives, conquests and troop actions, in English or Chinese - and within such a passage its activity is spread over the surrounding tokens and peaks on whichever token most carries the conflict, sometimes a war noun ('battle', 'enemy', 'Allies'), often a function word introducing a war noun phrase ('the Battle of', 'a battle', 'going to war') and often a digit of the year anchoring the event (1918, 1942, 1870), although those same function words and dates are inert outside a war setting. It is near zero on civilian prose and dates (a company founded in 1870, a birth in September 1939, a count of 1942, a sports or political contest), on individual crime, on atrocity reports (massacre, genocide, the Holocaust) and on war metaphors ('war on drugs', 'battling cancer', 'attack the market'), and weak on war or military mentions that do not describe fighting ('the war museum', 'after the war he returned home', a military budget, soldiers on parade), with partial activation without described fighting mainly for bare world-war-era years (1910s-1940s, strongest in the 1940s), named wars such as the Second World War and Cold-War conflict events such as the Cuban Missile Crisis; because zero-ablating the pole shifts several war words and year digits rather than one specific upcoming token (KL 0.010, top-10 concentration 0.33), the mechanism claim is retrospective.

The negative pole encodes plant natural-product (phytochemical) content: it fires on names of plant natural-product classes (flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, saponins, tannins, glycosides, glucosinolates, polyphenols, carotenoids, essential oils, polysaccharides) and of specific phytochemicals (quercetin, catechin, luteolin, kaempferol, genistein, resveratrol, curcumin, limonene, ginsenoside), on statements about their content or antioxidant activity ('total flavonoid content', 'rich in polyphenols'), and on phytochemical-rich plant foods that set up such a statement ('Green tea is rich in', 'Red wine is rich in', 10.4 of the 15.9 max before any compound is named); it stays elevated across an enumeration of such constituents and generalises to Chinese ('该产品的主要成分是黄酮类、皂苷和挥发油' 9.3 vs '水、盐和糖' 1.1 in the same frame). In the same sentence frames, non-plant chemistry stays far lower - elements/ions, water/salt/sugar, gases, simple sugars, synthetic solvents and reagents (ethanol/acetone 2.6, fluorobenzene 0.7, dichloromethane 0.5) and common drug names (aspirin 0.2, caffeine 0.7, penicillin 0.4, streptomycin 0.2) - as does non-chemical prose (0.1-0.3), and ablating the pole moves next-token probability diffusely over phytochemical vocabulary (top-10 concentration 0.31), so this is a content feature rather than preparation of one specific upcoming token.

Fires retrospectively on predicate verbs and event tokens (such as 'runs', 'opened', 'returns', 'works', 'went', 'rushed', 'flooded') when the grammatical subject is inanimate, computational, or non-agentive, rather than an animate agent. It distinguishes non-agentive operations, inchoative transitions, and operational execution from intentional human or animal actions.

This pole fires where a sentence places a person or an institution inside the larger organization, field, or place it belongs to: it peaks on the of/in/at/for that attaches a role, office, membership or part noun to that whole ('professor of chemistry', 'director of the company', 'member of the department', 'researcher in Adcock's lab', 'Department of Medicine', 'contents of which'), and more weakly on the passive predicates that state such a fact of origin or placement ('was founded/established in 1892', 'was born in', 'worked at', 'joined', 'located in'). It stays near zero when the same prepositions and role words carry no such affiliation: ownership, authorship and quantity genitives ('owner of the company', 'size of the company', 'author of the report', 'cost of the repairs'), the role word used attributively ('the university president', 'the company's director'), and plain event narrative ('the committee approved the merger', 'the cat sat on the mat').

L16/N4681+ fires on the interior of a word the tokenizer has had to spell out in pieces, when that word is a name, a Latin/Greek technical term or a code identifier rather than ordinary English vocabulary: the current token has no leading space and continues the previous token's word, and the peak sits on the fragment that carries the word's distinctive spelling ('opt' in Hymenoptera 2.8, 'onal' in clonal 2.5, 'inement' in bx_refinement 2.4, 'Parent' in m_pParentNode 1.5, 'ological' in Histological 2.0, the '9' of x509 3.0). Strength is graded by how name-like or technical the word is - capitalised name forms fire 1.3-2x the same word in lowercase ('Histological' 2.01 vs 'histological' 1.29, 'Hymenopteran' 2.76 vs 'hymenopteran' 1.40) - and it falls to the floor on any token that starts a word (the identical string: ' Instance' 0.06 vs 'Instance' 1.55), on pieces of ordinary vocabulary and of compounds of ordinary English words (the 'ization' of institutionalization 0.32, the 'Timeout' of RequestTimeout 0.60, the 'conf' of nginx.conf (peak 0.31)), and on technical terms that the tokenizer splits into ordinary fragments inside plain lowercase prose (the 'alan' of acanthocephalan 0.19).

This pole fires when the current token closes a well-formed, expected constituent in a sentence that continues: the comma or semicolon sealing a coherent fronted temporal or clausal adjunct ('In 1969,', 'According to the report,', 'Once upon a time,'), or a noun that coherently fills an anticipated slot — a same-category enumeration member ('flour, one egg', 'Tokyo, Berlin', 'eight characters and one number'), a valid SELECT column ('SELECT name'), a range endpoint ('through Sunday'), or a selectionally fitting object ('the onions ... pan'). It stays near-silent when the same slot holds a semantically anomalous filler ('second garage,', 'Tokyo, apple', 'the rocks ... pan', 'SELECT table') or when the boundary punctuation is removed, and its output direction promotes ',' as the continuation marker.

The negative pole fires at the point where a clause ties something to a hazard: the 'from'/'against' that introduces the source a defence predicate holds off ('protects the rider from injury', 'hardening federal buildings against threats', 'guards the village against floods', 'shields the heart from damage'), the 'by'/'with' that introduces the agent of a harmful state ('endangered by hunting', 'threatened by habitat loss', 'damaged by frost', 'breached by attackers', 'tampered with'), 'to' after 'vulnerable', and the negating element of an elaborated permission/prohibition notice ('may be reproduced ... without the prior written permission', the non-exclusive copyright grant). It stays near zero when the same prepositions carry a plain source, place or agent ('came from the city', 'a letter from my brother', 'played against the champions', 'leaned against the wall', 'monitors the network from the office', 'studied by researchers', 'designed by an architect', 'opened by the mayor') and on harm reported in the active voice with no such slot ('the storm damaged the roof', 'the frost killed the crops'); the hazard noun itself makes no difference ('against threats' and 'against weather' both peak at 2.68, 'damaged by the flood' and 'damaged by the workers' both at 0.67).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventional, stereotyped multi-token construction: an idiom or collocation (pinch/bag of salt, at sea), a memorized proper name or fact (Neil after Moon-and, Seine, sea level in the boiling-point sentence), or a boilerplate measure, legal, or technical slot (greater-than five, times-a-day, from-9-a.m.-to, raised interest, negative charge, pleaded not guilty), with strength scaling with canonicality (salt 7.7-13.6 after of-phrases vs pepper 0.3-0.8; runs 0.29 vs eats 0.06). The identical surface token in a novel or compositional frame stays near silent (guilty 0.50 vs 0.00, charge 0.64 vs 0.01, Neil 1.20 with Apollo context vs 0.04 without), so the claim beats the token-identity confound (R2 82%). The effect is detection of the just-completed frame, not preparation of the next token: the Jacobian lens is Gaussian noise (kurtosis 3.3) whose promoted tokens never follow the peaks, and swapping the word after the peak (Neil Armstrong/ate, sea level/food, hall fell silent/apart) leaves the peak unchanged.

The pole fires on the token that carries a stored, non-compositional string rather than a composed phrase: the opening word-piece of a person or organisation name (' McC' in John McCracken, ' Car' in David Carlucci, ' Co' in Peter Cooley, ' Writers' plus its possessive apostrophe in "Baseball Writers' Association of America"), a domain or file-path fragment ('bo' in boingboing.net, '.do' in docs.doctrine-project.org), or a fixed boilerplate/technical phrase (' entry' in 'any responses to this entry', ' Application' in 'Japanese Patent Application'), often on two or three consecutive tokens of the same string. Strength tracks how firmly the string is stored -- 'Baseball Writers'' 5.7 > 'Football Writers'' 2.5 > 'Martian Writers'' 0.35, 'Peter Cooley' 2.1 > 'Peter Nordland' 0.5 -- while the same surface token inside composed or lower-case prose ('writers'' association', 'the senator John', 'John Smith') stays at the ~0.2 baseline; the numerous weak 0.4-0.9 firings on common words (' get', ' just', ' the', ' if') sit in the opposite SwiGLU sign regime (gate negative, up positive) and are a different, diffuse mechanism.

Retrospective detector for the onset of reported/quoted material in a reportive frame: activation climbs through the attribution clause ('she said,', 'greeted her with', 'I thought:'), peaks on the opening quotation mark that follows it (' "', ' “', ' ‘'), stays elevated across the quoted words, and collapses at the closing quote; the frame carries most of the response (deleting the two quote glyphs costs only ~0.12 of max, and bare quoted dialogue lines still give ~0.5), while the same string in a machine-log frame, config/identifier string literals (JSON keys, #include headers), line-initial quotes after a newline, and impersonal news-register scare quotes sit near zero, and a moderate secondary trigger (~0.25-0.4 of max) fires on numerals ('4 years ago', '2019', '100%') and a few technical-term onsets (' mult'ithreading, ' Bio'hazard) in running prose. The response is gated by document register rather than context length (a 16-token prompt reaches 0.98 of scan max; dialogue-dense or voiced-personal documents lift the whole span with median up to ~0.6 of max, and the same quoted tail gains ~+0.33 of max after a personal-narrative vs technical prefix); the Jacobian promoted list is incoherent (kurtosis 4.6 but 10% lens agreement, CJK/formatting tokens with no overlap with quoted-speech continuations), so this is not lookahead for specific quoted tokens, and the negative pole owns the opposite material - the author's own interpolated voice in parenthetical asides ('(Nooo kidding, John!)', ', of all places,').

Fires on a transitive verb (or the perfect auxiliary 'have/has' right before it) whose direct object has already been supplied to its left, so no object is expected after it: the verb of an object-gap relative clause with or without 'that' ('the table I found', 'the house Jack built', 'the option people have had', 'everything you need'), or a participle whose subject is its patient ('a method has been developed', 'has been known'). It stays near zero on the same verb when an agentive subject precedes it and an object is still to come ('I found the table', 'engineers have developed a system', 'when it released the cables'); it reads only left context, and is strongest when the fronted head is an inanimate thing rather than a person.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a locally expected multi-token construction set up by the preceding 1-4 tokens: 'after' closing a completed event clause, 'than' closing a 'greater' comparative, 'in' closing a stored-energy locative, 'silent' resolving 'fell ___', a past-tense predicate resolving a subject ('crowd erupted'), or 'the' resuming an established scene after 'and'. The same token without its licensing left context fires weakly while a fitting substitute in the same frame still fires, so firing tracks frame completion rather than the token alone.

The pole responds primarily to typographic layout rather than to content: it fires hardest on the token that closes or terminates a markup element (‘</’, ‘ </’, ‘></’, ‘>\n’, ‘">\r\n’) and on the capitalised first word of a paragraph opened by a blank line — headings and section starts such as ‘Copy’, ‘Two’, ‘Long’, ‘Over’, ‘Print’, ‘Execute’ (8% of paragraph-initial capitals reach the protocol's active threshold, versus 2% of all tokens). Running lowercase prose and sub-word continuations stay near zero, and the response falls by roughly two thirds when the same heading word is lowercased or pulled into the running line; headings whose opener is not a label-like word (‘Move’) fire far less, a lexical residual the layout account does not explain.

The negative pole fires on the token that closes a slot in laid-out text - the ':' ending an aligned 'Label:' field, the final character of a padded identifier, citation, docket number or filename, the tail of a Markdown underline or ASCII rule, a table cell, or a sentence-final period before a wide gap - i.e. on the token immediately before a whitespace-only token (padding spaces or a blank line), with the peak on that closing token rather than on the whitespace. It requires the layout to be established earlier in the document: the same words with single spaces between fields stay near baseline (0.44 of 11.56), a lone padded line reaches only 0.09, and one earlier padded line lifts the next field's ':' from 0.09 to 4.53; its output direction promotes exactly those padding whitespace tokens, but the zero-ablation KL averaged over the base prompts is 3.1e-4, below the lookahead threshold, because the pole is active on fewer than 0.1% of scan tokens, so the mechanism is claimed retrospective.

The negative pole tracks a bounded amount being fully consumed or taken up: it peaks on a totality or portion word ('all', 'whole', 'entire', 'completely', 'half', 'most', a percentage) that quantifies a definite mass in the object of a consumption/processing verb ('she had eaten all of the cake', 'eaten the entire cake', 'read the whole book', 'covers the whole disk', 'enough to fill the bookshelf'), and it peaks on the verb instead when the portion phrase comes first ('the whole cake was eaten', '60 percent of the cake was eaten', 'half of the cake was eaten', 'the whole book was read'), i.e. the peak lands on whichever of the two elements is read second, and activation needs both (bare 'the cake was eaten' reaches only 0.28 of the scan max, bare 'they ate pasta' 0.22). It stays near zero when the same words carry no consumed amount: idioms ('all of a sudden' 0.04, 'after all' 0.10, 'on the whole' 0.04, 'the whole point' 0.03), stative or attributive predication ('the entire city was dark/flooded/destroyed' 0.06), non-consuming predicates over the same definite object ('all of the cake was seen 0.03 / burned 0.03 / sold 0.02 / moved 0.03', 'the whole floor was washed 0.01', 'the whole wall was painted 0.05'), and vague quantity words when no such verb is present ('some'/'several'/'a lot' in object position stay at 0.04-0.18).

The negative pole fires retrospectively at a link token or light verb inside a fixed frame, not at content words: the ' or' of the gendered-pronoun formula ('he or she', 'his or her', 'she or he'), the link word inside fixed names (' del' in 'Tierra del Fuego/Norte', ' of' in 'House of Representatives/Lords/Commons'), the separator or second endpoint of a numeral range ('ages 12-17', 'grades 11 and 12', 'June 14 - 16'), the compound 'high school', and the light verbs hold/take/get/raise in change-of-state or quantified predicates ('holds 90%', 'takes around 1,000 years', 'took a heavy toll', 'got worse', 'getting late'). It stays at its floor for the same surface words outside those frames - ' and'/' or'/' of' joining ordinary nouns or other names ('bread and milk', 'the lid of the jar', 'University of Michigan', 'Antigua and Barbuda'), lone unpaired numbers, other 'school' compounds, and synonymous or plain-complement verbs ('contains 90%', 'caused a heavy toll', 'the trip took 5 hours') - and the same neuron's positive pole fires on build/building/built (up to 19.9), so this pole is the weak opposite-sign side of a construction/relational feature.

L17/N2593+ fires on the connector that closes a formally-named designation, above all the ' of' (and its equivalents ' van'/' de'/' la') that attaches a named legal or official instrument to its qualifier: 'the Statute of limitations' 10.7, 'the Ordinance of 1787' 12.0, 'the Decree of the committee' 10.1, 'the Act of God' 12.9, 'the Civil Rights Act of 1964' 11.0, 'the Treaty of Paris' 7.1, 'Apache License, Version 2.0' 6.6, weakening through other title-cased names (Council/Committee/Court/House/Order/Medal/League/Battle/Gulf/Revolution, 1.7-5.0) and through the 2-3 band of ' of' inside institutional and encyclopedic titles ('Court of Appeals', 'Medal of Honor', 'Forest of Dean'). It is near zero on the same connector after abstract, mass, partitive or generic-role nouns ('the idea of justice' 0.0, 'the use of force' 0.0, 'the regulation of the market' 0.04, 'the Ministry of Defence' 0.25, 'the University of Oxford' 0.7), on the lowercase common-noun use of an instrument word ('the act of God' 1.4 vs 'the Act of God' 12.9), on every other preposition after the same nouns ('the Statute on limitations' 0.9, 'the Decree by the committee' 1.8) and on bare dates with no designation ('He graduated from college in 1998' 0.4). The response reads only words already present - a year or a common noun after the same ' of' leaves it bit-identical ('the Ordinance of 1787' 11.99 = 'the Ordinance of the committee' 11.99) - while its output direction promotes the calendar months (13 of its top-13 raw-unembedding promotions, 9 of the top-10 Jacobian-lens tokens), so it writes a date bias rather than predicting a specific upcoming token, and the protocol's lookahead probe returns retrospective.

Lexical detector that fires on the token itself for spatial-orientation/geometric-axis adjectives (' vertical', ' horizontal', ' perpendicular', ' parallel', ' vertically', ' flat', 'ob|lique') and on the word-initial prefix piece ' hyper' (hyperlinks, hyperactive, hyperchromatic, hyperparathyroidism), with weaker firing on ' flex' (flexor), ' virtual' and the ':\n' after an 'address'/'author' key in arXiv-style YAML metadata; near-orientation synonyms (' upright', ' diagonal', ' cross') and the following noun stay near zero.

Retrospective detector for the token that advances or closes a rigid document-scaffold or boilerplate template: the final year digit completing a full weekday-day-month-year date line, a dot inside a version triple, the #/@ marker inside a markdown anchor or bracketed citation/bib-link, a ==== heading underline after a title, the ) closing a code signature, or the modal in a license-header formula. It fires only when distant scaffold context (date words, Introduction/frontmatter, license, CDN, or citation markup) is present; the same tokens in ordinary prose do not drive it.

The positive pole fires on tokens inside a phrase that specifies a quantity: a number bound to a unit or measure word ('100 degrees', '40 liters', 'two cups', '3 meters', 'eight characters', '500 mg', '3.9 percent'), the amount nouns themselves ('amount', 'quantity'), and the markers that pin an amount to an exact value or a required level ('exactly', 'at least', 'sufficient', 'necessary', 'needed'). Vague degree wording ('quite wide', 'a high temperature', 'about 40 liters') or the same frames carrying no quantity ('add the sugar to the batter') activate it far less.

Fires retrospectively when the token year completes the definite phrase the year referring to a calendar year as an elapsed or dated interval; it stays near baseline on year with other premodifiers such as next, last, that, a, or plural years.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a locally stereotyped multi-token construction licensed by the preceding 1-2 tokens: the keyword closing a loop header ('For i in'), a negation after a modal ('would not', 'can not'), the second half of a fixed collocation ('not guilty'), or a time/quantity word pinned by its frame ('Friday at', 'at 100'). Breaking the construction's first half collapses the peak even when the peak token itself is unchanged, so activity tracks the predictability of the chunk, not just peak-token identity.

This pole fires retrospectively on the second half of a canonical, locally licensed head-complement bigram: a verb, predicative adjective, preposition, or complement word that is the idiomatic continuation of the immediately preceding head (museum is->open, revenue->increased, calls->for, proper-noun->wrote). Breaking or removing the licensing head, or swapping the peak token for a non-collocate, collapses the peak even when the peak token is unchanged; changing the subject's identity or downstream tokens leaves it unchanged.

The negative pole fires at the seam of a stacked technical modifier phrase: on the coordinator or punctuation token that follows a technical content word inside a modifier list (' and' after 'surgical' / 'prevention' / 'pharmacological', ',' after 'clinical'), and on the internal hyphen/formant seam of a prefixed technical compound (' non' and '-ph' inside 'non-pharmacological', '-in' inside 'non-invasive', ' north' and '-east' inside 'north-eastern'). The strength of a junction is set by the preceding technical word rather than by what follows it ('prevention and rehabilitation' = 'prevention and recovery' = 'prevention and cats' = 2.02 of a 3.09 max), while the same connectives joining short common words or whole clauses stay low ('old and new' 0.12, 'cats and dogs' 0.22, a clause-level 'and' 0.16), bare negation without a prefixed stem drops it to zero ('an invasive technique' 0.00), and it tracks neither position (R2 0.003) nor next-token uncertainty (r = -0.01 with entropy), so it is a retrospective detector of technical modifier-list and compound-seam structure, not of the connective token, of negation, or of surprisal.

The pole fires on a token that is the strongly predicted completion of a formulaic multi-token construction given the preceding 1-3 tokens (e.g. 'return' closing a def header, the head noun of a fixed verb phrase like 'remove your shoes', the comparative in 'is __ than', the preposition in a day-range), with graded strength tracking conditional predictability; the same token in a neutral context, or an unpredictable substitute in the same slot, stays near zero. Its removal-family output direction shows no causal next-token effect (zero-ablation KL ~6e-5, far below the 1e-3 lookahead threshold; near-zero activation on 'remove'/'removal' themselves), so the unit reacts retrospectively to a confirmed prediction rather than preparing any upcoming token.

The positive pole fires on the possessive 'at' phrase of terms and prerogative - 'at' + your/its/their + (own/sole) + a noun naming what is left to a party or at stake for it ('at your option' 14.5, 'at its sole discretion' 25.7, 'at their option' 16.2, 'at your own risk' 23.3, 'at your earliest convenience' 8.1, and the modal permission 'you may use the software at your home' 15.1) - and on the copyright-licence formula 'Use of this/these <thing> is ...' ('Use of this source code is governed by ...' 11.3). It peaks on the possessive determiner itself or on the 'at' immediately before it and its output finishes the phrase ('at'->'your', 'your'->'own', 'its'->'sole'; ablating it shifts probability onto ' own', ' option', ' risk', ' sole'), while it stays near zero on locative or temporal 'at' without a possessive ('at the station' 0.4, 'at 37 C' 0.0, 'at noon' 0.0, 'at 3 percent' 1.3, 'at 60 mph' 0.1), on 'at + possessive' inside plain event narration ('we stayed at your house' 0.2, 'she looked at your picture' 0.3, 'the parties met at their office' 1.0), on a third-person possessive in a stative location ('the book is at his home' 1.1, 'at its home' 0.4, 'at the home' 0.2), and on licence wording outside those formulae ('Permission is hereby granted' 0.7, 'IN NO EVENT SHALL' 0.4, 'This software is licensed under' 0.5, 'You may not use this file except in compliance' 2.7).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is the lexically specific word that completes the construction set up by the preceding words: manner 'so' after verbs of temporal passage, the sort key after ORDER BY, the proper-noun complement of 'of', 'password' after a determiner, conjunction 'and' continuing a finished clause, or a period closing a complete statement. The same surface token stays near zero when its frame is absent or different, and off-list words in the same slot usually fire weakly or not at all, while a few interchangeable slots (sort key, of-complement) accept any filler.

The pole fires on a document's formatting scaffold rather than on its wording: on the non-lexical characters that structure or delimit fields, items and numerals - HTML/markdown/comment markers (' <!--', '**', '##', '#">'), the period of a line-leading list number ('1.'), the ' /' between parallel names, the thousands ',' inside a number, and the ' and'/space token that closes a multi-digit numeral inside a templated line, with strength growing with the digit count. The same characters used as ordinary prose punctuation (a sentence-final period, a conjunction 'and', 'TCP/IP', 'R&D', or 65000 written without the comma) leave the pole at baseline.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is the head of the clause predicate that completes the preceding subject noun phrase, typically an intransitive or change-of-state verb, predicate adjective, or predicate nominal. It stays quiet on the same surface word used attributively, infinitivally or transitively, or when the noun phrase appears without its predicate head.

Pole fires retrospectively at a low-salience structural continuation token — a CSS/config/diagnostic colon, a digit inside a version/hash/measurement/DOI, a boilerplate boundary (regenerated.

import, LICENSE-file.
package, Reserved.
#include), or a generic word completing an established formal collocation (missing, production, localization, changes, transport, SUCH, a) — but only when embedded in an extended formal structured document (code/stylesheet block, compiler/runtime log with path context, license header, spec/system report, or multi-sentence academic/technical exposition). The same colon, digit, or -tion/-sion nominalization (attenuation, dispersion, polarization, reduction, retention) in an isolated single sentence, short list, or informally framed post yields only weak activation below the active line.

Fires on the word 'single' itself (any case, including the subword 'ingle' in camelCase 'singleLine') when it is used in its plain counting/category sense of 'exactly one unit' or 'one-unit kind' (single-photon, single-center, a single game, single room/ticket, single mother, 'I am single'), at roughly 0.6-1.0 of max; other multiplicity words fire much more weakly (double ~0.35-0.45, multi/dual/sole/mon(o)/one ~0.1-0.3, return/twin/great ~0). The pole is strongly suppressed (<~0.25 of max) when 'single' is the emphatic polarity intensifier after 'every', 'not a', 'not one', 'without a' or 'just a', or the music-release noun after 'released', 'new', 'latest', 'first' or 'lead'; plain predicate negation ('I am not single') does not suppress it, and tokens after 'single' are inactive.

The negative pole of L17/N650 fires on tokens that are pieces of non-prose formal notation rather than words: the '0' inside a 4-digit year in the 2000s ('20xx'), digits and dots inside version/decimal literals ('1.3.1', '2.6.32'), and fragments of URLs, file paths, dotted module names and hyphenated code/class identifiers ('/python', '.views', ' navbar', 'col-sm-3'); prose words and bare quantities (e.g. '2009 items', '4321') do not fire it. The detector is retrospective and context-gated: a literal appearing for the first time in plain narrative prose stays near zero, and activation climbs once the document has already established that notation (an earlier year or date, a code block, or markup), so the same year token runs from ~0.1-0.3 in a story to 4-13 in a dated legal document or a technical Q&A.

In Java/C++/JS-like source, this pole fires on the token opening an integer-count value slot: the '=' of a declaration/assignment whose declared type is an integer type (int, unsigned int) or whose untyped var/bare target is a cardinal count/index noun (total, count/counter, numberOfItems, currentpage), and the 'return' of a predicate-guarded early exit (if-contains/equals ... return true/false) in a boolean- or int-returning method. It stays near zero when the slot's type is floating-point or text/object (double, float, float64, String, Object, collections), when the identifier denotes a non-count aggregate, ratio, duration or generic computed result (average, ratio in a typed declaration, elapsedMillis, Go result float64, computed tax/rate), on non-code '=' analogues (JSON colon values, SQL WHERE, shell assignments, prose 'Let x =', Python object bindings, compound '+=') and on unguarded bare returns (int getter, computed-double return).

The pole fires on tokens that carry specialist, non-everyday technical content: scientific, engineering, medical or computing vocabulary used in its concrete/technical sense (' calcium', 'the coating was applied to the wall', 'Ca2+-ATPase', 'dissolved', 'electrodes were attached to the scalp'), and on pieces of machine notation such as paths, environment-variable assignments, version strings and category/date number strings ('/etc/ssh/ssh_config', 'LD_ASSUME_KERNEL=2.4.1', 'Category:1940'). It sits near zero on ordinary narrative or conversational prose and on abstract or everyday uses of the same words ('a penalty applied to the firm', 'the mineral chelator', 'the ssh settings file', 'nineteen forty', 'the file was attached to the email'), and a preceding passage of metadata, log or specification text raises the peak about 2-3x (why the scan's maxima sit inside documentation, logs, patents and reference pages).

This pole fires at discourse-deictic anchor points where the text refers back to earlier content: the speaker's own prior communications ('as I have mentioned/said in...', 'recall from my previous...'), citations of where something was stated or documented ('mentioned in your edit', 'read in the link', 'as reported by', 'In a related article'), and back-references to prior events ('twenty years previously', 'return to in a minute'). It is driven by the anaphoric construction rather than trigger words or the upcoming token: replacing the communicative verb with a non-communicative one collapses activity, while swapping the following word ('previous' vs 'recent') changes nothing.

Fires on tokens in computer/software/web text - code and command lines, URLs and file paths, config/log/format strings, API doc comments, and interface text or page chrome addressed to the user (open/click/type/press with a digital object such as file, folder, app, page, menu, settings, button; 'leave a comment', 'sign in to continue', '1,325 shares') - peaking on the digital artifact's name or on the technical literal (an identifier or CamelCase piece, UI label, flag, path component, version or id number). It stays near zero in narrative, news, academic and general expository prose, including prose that describes computing systems abstractly (compilers, databases, algorithms), and on physical objects even inside the same imperative frames (door, box, garden, boat).

Fires on the first sub-word piece of a multi-token surname or place name: a short capitalised fragment, mostly W-initial (' We', ' Wo', ' Wa', ' W') and also ' Ra', ' Ke', ' Ka', ' Kl', 'ke', ' dela', that sits in a name slot (after a first name, a title such as Mr./Dr., or 'at'/'in' before an institution or place), so the word is still unfinished (Weisberg, Weill, Inverkeithing, Raanan). It stays silent on the same letters as a complete word (the pronoun 'We' at a clause start, single-token names such as Weber, Goldberg, Johnson, Inverness), on later pieces of the name ('ill', 'isberg'), and on other first pieces such as ' Gins', ' Br' or ' St'. A weaker offshoot fires on a pivot token inside memorised boilerplate, e.g. ' via' in a 'Sun-Sentinel via AP' photo credit and '=' in 'initial-scale=1'.

The negative pole is a licensing/copyright-notice detector: it fires on the standard notice that names who holds a document's copyright and states the terms under which it may be used ('Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License")', 'Permission is hereby granted, free of charge...', 'This program is free software... GNU General Public License', 'All rights reserved', MIT/GPL/Apache/CC-BY header blocks), most strongly when such a multi-line notice heads a source file, and more weakly on other verbatim standard strings of the same files (e.g. the canonical Go 'if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }' check, fixed log/error formats, CDN URLs and version strings). It keys on the stock wording of that notice register rather than on legal meaning: the same licence terms paraphrased in fresh prose, and other legal registers (contracts, EULAs, statutes, court opinions, patent claims), stay near zero, so predict active on licence/copyright notice text in any language and inactive on ordinary prose and on legal prose that is not a licence notice.

The pole fires on the digits of a numeral that is the bound of a comparison: the second number of a range ('between 15 and 20 percent', 'aged 18 to 65', '20 to 30 students') or an age/threshold value in a statement about people ('aged 65', 'older than 55', 'under 15', 'a quarter of the population is over 65'), where it reaches roughly 2-30x the scan's scale. Numerals used as plain values or labels ('in 1999', 'costs 40 dollars', 'page 65', 'about 65 million', '65 percent of the population') and comparators applied to a single object's physical dimension ('the wall is 65 metres', 'the temperature is over 30 degrees') leave it near zero, and a numeral-free sentence gives only a weak few-tenths background (0.2-0.5, near the record's active line) rather than true silence.

L18/N2906- fires where a subject gets back to a state, place or role it held before: it peaks on the return verb or on the possessive/determiner that follows it in spans such as 'went back to her usual routine', 'regained their previous level', 'reverted to his old habits', 'reclaimed its place', 'returned to action', 'took over the position from his predecessor' and 'replacing collagen lost by the natural aging process', and sits at its floor for forward or novel change ('reached their highest level', 'moved to the top of the league'), for bare repetition ('played the same song again', 'reread the letter twice'), for plain possession ('picked up his coat') and for neutral prose. Its weight rows encode the same concept (gate 恢复/重建/修复/重返/recover/lost, up repar/repl/补/rebuild, down 重新/replacement/rebuilt), opposite to the positive pole, which fires on privation and removal ('the losses were serious', 'the storm broke the windows', 'the parts were removed'); isolated single-token spikes on word pieces like 'ash' in rare surnames or ' (' before an abbreviation are a separate, weaker token-identity component.

Fires at the slot where a numeric value is about to be given for a measured attribute that has already been named (age, weight, size, dilation, percentage, warranty length, an Android layout_width/height): the bare space token ' ' before the digits, the '="' after a dimension attribute, or a connective right after such a number that opens a second bound or an approximation (' or', ' to', ' and', ' about': '16 years or more', 'age from 15 to 99', '70 kg or so', '70-80 mesh and smaller'). It stays weak (< 0.25 of max) when the same number or connective appears without a quantity attribute named before it (e.g. 'range in name from 15 to 99', 'was named and found to be 1.8', 'layout_title="', 'smoke or drink'); a minority of top examples on non-numeric words (' videos', ' insured', 'isha') are not covered.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current period token terminates a complete, well-formed declarative sentence (a finished proposition with subject and predicate), drawing on the preceding clause content; it stays low on question-mark closures, on mid-sentence or abbreviation periods, on fragments ending in a period, and when the same sentence lacks terminal punctuation.

N3197+ fires at the token where a progression the preceding context already set going advances one step: the second half of a repeated comparative ('more and more', 'less and less', 'faster and faster'), a predicate reporting movement toward or past a state ('getting closer', 'fast approaching', '2019 is here', 'was disappearing', 'began to decline', 'steadily disappearing'), or each new iteration of a repeated record in formatted text (every '</field>\r\n' closing a repeated field record in an XML schema, every ' }\n' closing a repeated class property, each '{\' of a run of LaTeX math groups). Static prose carrying the same information stays near zero - the same frame with a stative predicate ('was remembered', 'was continuing'), 'more or less' for 'more and more', or the same XML records written as one prose line drop the peak to 0.0-1.4 - and the unit's output direction writes against the 'recently / lately / gradually / later / today' time-adverb family (logit-lens suppression z to -4.0, its negative pole peaking on ' recently'), i.e. it marks ongoing change rather than recency or any single upcoming token.

Fires on the word of (or among/amongst) when it links a superlative, ordinal-extreme, or prototypical-exemplar head to its comparison domain, e.g. biggest win of his life, worst of all, busiest weekend of Christmas, first attack of its kind, Porsche of SUVs, chief among the painters; plain possessive or partitive of without a ranking or extreme head does not drive it.

The pole fires on four specific slots, peaking on that token: (1) the preposition that introduces the weapon or instrument in a scene of violence or crime, set by the scene rather than the verb ('attacked his wife with a screwdriver', 'the gunman met the guard with a rifle', also 'using', and cross-lingually only here: French 'avec' and Spanish 'con' in 'atacó ... con un cuchillo'; about 2.5-4); (2) attributive 'due' and the degree adjective of a manner 'with' phrase ('due process/diligence/respect', 'with great care/confidence', including sentence-initial 'With great care,'; about 2.4-4.7, while clause-final 'due to' is weaker at about 1.1-1.6); (3) a year digit, usually the last, in copyright notices and parenthesised birth-death dates ('Copyright (c) 2016', '(5 July 1914 - 11 April 2009)'; about 1.4-3.1); and (4) more weakly (about 1.0-2.3), has/have right after a chemical, drug, molecule or theory subject that states its property or effect ('the drug has no effect', 'the compound has a melting point'). It is inactive (below about 0.9) on years in running prose ('built in 1940', 'In July 1914'), predicative 'is due', non-violent tool use and comitative, noun-modifying or lexicalised with/avec ('fixed the shelf with', 'helped his wife with', 'the girl with the red hat', 'agree with', 'diagnosed with', 'La chambre avec balcon'), sentence-initial possessive 'With three assistants...', possession HAVE with an ordinary subject (person, organisation, place or building: 'the hotel/museum/committee has', French 'Le musee a une collection', 'I/we/you have'), and modal 'have to', where 'have' and 'to' stay below 0.5 (the one known leftover is 'Visitors have to show a badge', at 1.4 on 'show').

The pole fires on a preposition heading a circumstantial or complement PP that situates an actual event or factual claim in its frame — its time, place, condition, standard of comparison, content, cause, or deadline (in March, at sea level, with last year, of a galaxy, by Friday); the same tokens stay near zero as infinitive markers, particles, or verb-selected idioms, and event clauses with no PP at all stay near zero. Input attribution is left-loaded (mean distance 3.5 tokens back, nothing beyond 16 back) and the Jacobian lens promotes frame nouns (condition/premise/environment/situation), not any specific next token, so the mechanism is retrospective; weak-tail peaks on bare verbs, a code delimiter, and a word fragment are acknowledged leftovers.

The positive pole encodes effortful striving: it fires on the verbs that name the act of trying to reach a goal (try/tries/tried/trying 9.5-16.3, strive/strove 10.0-12.5, struggle 5.0, fought 6.3, battle 2.3, work/works/working/worked 4.3-7.4, aim 6.4, attempt 3.9, endeavour 3.6, toil 6.2, labour 1.7-3.0, slog 1.2, compete 3.9, on a 16.8 peak) and on the degree words that grade that effort ('hard' 9.6 right after 'try', 'hardest' 10.1, 'very' 4.0, 'really' 4.7), while staying near baseline on verbs that take the identical 'to + infinitive' complement but express intention, permission or success (want 0.45, need 0.23, plan 0.07-0.31, decide 0.08, agree 1.16, promise 0.21, refuse 0.07-0.26, seem 0.12-0.20, begin 0.00, manage 0.06), on effort nouns ('The attempt failed' 0.03, 'His effort' 0.03, 'great effort' 0.05) and on 'hard/very/extremely' outside an effort frame ('a hard problem' 0.19, 'hard to say' 0.31, 'extremely cold' 0.42, 'hit the ball hard' 0.00). Its output direction writes exactly those effort intensifiers forward (' hard' +2.4, 'hardest' +2.2, 'very' +1.9, 'harder' +1.9, 'really' +2.1, 'exceptionally' +1.9 logits at the peaks, measured by zero-ablating the pole) while the negative pole never exceeds 0.4 on the same strings, so it is a detector of effort rather than one end of a dial; leftovers it does not explain: possessives after 'try' split oddly ('try our/my best' 14.8/15.5 vs 'try his/their best' 2.0/4.4) and exertion verbs that do not take a to-infinitive goal stay low (persist 0.00, grind 0.02, push 0.71, achieve 0.63, commit 0.31).

The pole fires on the token immediately before a highly predictable 'from' — an adverb completing a source/origin construction ('follows directly', 'graduated directly', 'exported directly') or the last column of a SQL SELECT list — and its output direction exclusively promotes 'from'/FROM variants, preparing that upcoming token; it shuts off once 'from' appears. Weak firing on dates and nouns with no following 'from' (e.g. 'March', 'summit') is an acknowledged leftover.

L19/N1901- fires at the token where the model is mid-way through spelling out a longer word (or word-like string) that the tokenizer split across pieces: a non-final piece whose next token must be the rest of the same word, as in ' att' in attestation, ' appe' in appeasement, 'am' in amalgamation, 'atab' in compatability, 'va' in much-vaunted, 'CAP' in CAPTCHA and '/ap' in an Android URL. It is near zero on the same word delivered as one token (compatibility vs compatability, tourist attractions vs Tourist Attractions), on a split word's last piece ('unted', 'ility', 'actions'), and where the model has already closed the piece and predicts a space ('app' in apprenticeship, 'assert' in assertion); its output pushes the next token toward word-continuation fragments (-unted, -ility, -ologies, -ested, -itude) rather than one particular word.

L19/N2185+ is a lookahead adjective neuron: it peaks on the token at which the next word (or the next word after a determiner, e.g. 'described as " a dark velvet"') is a descriptive, gradable adjective, whichever syntactic slot announces it - copula or linking verb (is/are/was/be, sounded, tasted, looked), degree adverb (so, most, very, extremely, generally), determiner or possessive opening an attributively modified NP ('its expressive...', 'a web-friendly...'), or a coordinator/comma continuing an adjectival series ('ADJ and', 'ADJ,'). Its transported output direction promotes exactly this class ('crisp', 'soft', 'warm', 'sharp', 'bold'), and activation collapses to near zero when the same surface position instead predicts a noun, verb or manner adverb ('wood and', 'ran smoothly', 'Victorian and'), so it tracks the model's expectation of an upcoming adjective rather than the part of speech already read; the negative pole is not a mirror and stays an order of magnitude weaker.

Retrospective: the pole's strong canonical-regime (g+u+) response fires on a noun token that names a channel, bond, agreement, proof, or barrier through which two other things relate (river, bridge, link, treaty, theorem, equation, inequality), graded by how directly the noun denotes such a link (river/treaty/bridge/theorem high; mountain/dog/guess/novel/rumor near zero in identical frames). The weak broad firing on surrounding glue words (prepositions, articles, spaces before numbers, verbs like proved) comes from a separate SwiGLU double-negative (g-u-) background process, and the pole predicts no specific next token (none of the tokens after peaks overlap its connect/separate/linking lens list).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is the highly predictable, syntactically selected continuation of the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens (a memorized collocation such as sat->on, fell->to, pleaded->not, announced she->would, theorem->follows, wind->rushed, Apollo->space+digit, galaxy->space+digit): replacing either the trigger or the completion collapses it, weakening the trigger grades it down, and a longer matching left context boosts it. It does not prepare a specific upcoming token (ablation next-token KL ~3.5e-06; swapping the upcoming digits 11->99 leaves the peak unchanged) despite a Jacobian lens pointing at closing quote/period tokens.

The pole fires on a word that is about to be followed by ' of' — typically the head of an abstract, relational or quantity noun phrase ('amount', 'effect', 'type', 'risk', 'importance', 'structure', 'levels', 'results', 'percent') in contexts where the model itself puts most of its next-token mass on ' of' (mean strength 0.32 where P(next=' of') >= 0.5, versus 0.06 over a 94k-token corpus). Concrete object nouns in the identical frame ('the table of …', 'the cat of …') fire about 2.5x less, and the pole's write shifts the next-token distribution towards ' of' and away from the rival preposition ' in'.

This pole fires retrospectively on a closed-class structural token — a preposition/particle (of, over, on, at, in, for, by), the copula 'is', the coordinator 'and', the article 'a' in fixed frames, '=', the space joining a label to its number, or a constituent-closing token (sentence-final '.', '</body>') — at the moment the immediate left context (1-2 tokens) has set up that head-relation-complement joint; the same surface token stays near-silent when the frame is broken by a content word in the slot, while swapping one structural token for another in the same slot, or swapping the upcoming complement noun, leaves the peak unchanged. Its output direction aligns with 'function'-family vocabulary, consistent with marking function-word-mediated composition rather than any specific upcoming word, so the claim is retrospective.

The positive pole fires at the hinge of a value statement about a definite, measurable attribute of a concrete entity: it peaks on the last token of the attribute phrase, or of the reporting verb that introduces the value ('the stadium's capacity', 'the tower's height', 'the patient's age/gender', 'the male:female ratio', 'the company's beta', 'was recorded as', 'is expected to be'), one token before a form of 'be', 'as', '=', or the opening token of a literal value (a number, an ID or hex string), with strength scaling with how strongly that attribute term fixes the copula/value continuation. It is near zero for direct predication of an entity ('the car is red', 'the boy's mood is happy'), for non-measurable or unanchored attributes ('the arrangement is ready', 'the port number is 8080'), and at predictable non-equative continuations ('New York', 'in terms of'); the value's content never matters, and although the output direction promotes exactly that copula (' as', ' is'; Chinese 为/是) and suppresses relative pronouns ('which/who'), the measured direct ablation effect is small (lookahead KL ~3e-5), so the mechanism claim is retrospective.

This pole fires on a pre-nominal selector, paradigmatically 'elected' (more weakly 'appointed', 'government', 'central'), peaking on the modifier token immediately before a likely institutional or collective noun. It is a lookahead signal: at the peak the model's top next-token predictions are exactly the pole's promoted family (representatives, officials, members, leaders), ablating the pole removes that probability mass (KL ~0.14), and swapping the actual next noun leaves the peak unchanged.

This pole fires when the current token continues the ongoing constituent, i.e. it is directly licensed by the immediately preceding token (determiner/adjective/quantifier/preposition/auxiliary-negation selecting a noun or verb, a stem selecting its completion, an identifier selecting its operator or argument in code), and it stays near zero on constituent onsets such as sentence-initial words, clause-linking conjunctions and nouns starting a new subject. Its output direction promotes no coherent token set (Jacobian kurtosis ~3.4, incoherent promoted list), so it is a retrospective local-continuation detector, not a next-token predictor.

Fires on the highly predictable continuation token of a verbatim-repeated boilerplate template already established in the preceding context: a C/Go brace-plus-indent or tab, an HTML/SVG/JSX tag boundary, a #pragma diagnostic word, a debug-log '/.ssh'-style path piece, or the fixed next word of an ebook-license, email-header, or institutional/collocational formula (may be, Board of, intimate partners). Long-preamble templates (ebook license, C++ signature-plus-brace, log sequence) need tens of preceding template tokens, so the same surface token in a novel, short, or single-sentence context (a fresh Python/YAML indent, an isolated bracket emoticon, everyday of/be/intimate/ssh/clang) stays quiet; a C-style indent fires whether or not its block is closed.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a frequent fixed local chunk with the immediately preceding token(s) — e.g. 'in'+'the', 'Where'+'are', 'The'+'stock', 'the'+'contract', 'can'+"'t", '5'+' p', 'i'+'in', 'return'+'a', or the digits of a canonical year — so activation requires the specific (context, token) conjunction: swapping the preceding token ('in'->'aboard', 'Where'->'They') or the peak token ('stock'->'dusty', 'contract'->'banana', 'converts'->'destroys') collapses it, while changes 3+ tokens back ('He'->'She', 'court'->'judge', '1969'->'1949') leave it unchanged.

This pole fires when the current token grounds the clause in something concrete and specific: most strongly (canonical g+u+ SwiGLU regime, strengths above ~0.9, unbounded) when it completes a numeric quantity with its unit or scale such as the first digit of a round number, a unit like ' mg' after digits, or a time/year marker; and more weakly (double-negative g-u- regime, strengths capped around ~0.6) at the head of the clause predicate, typically a concrete action verb or modal ('opened', 'sat', 'scored', 'stepped', 'must') or a nearby required argument or boundary, with abstract or stative predicates firing less. It reacts to the current and immediately preceding tokens rather than preparing any specific upcoming token.

Retrospective: in its main (g+u+) regime the pole fires on a content token that fills a delimited structural slot — prototypically a table cell right after a ' | ' delimiter (strength 1-4, abolished to ~0 when the pipe is swapped for 'and'/',' at equal token length), and also tag-enclosed, parenthesized, or SQL BY-clause/statement-final content, with extra boost for column-header-like words (name/email/col). Its output direction specifically promotes ' | '-family pipe tokens (Jacobian kurtosis 7.7, z>10), pushing continuations toward pipe-delimited structure. A separate weak SwiGLU double-negative (g-u-) regime fires ~0.3 on common function words ('on','to','the'), explaining the scan's low prose tail and the 59% token-identity variance rather than the strong peaks.

The negative pole fires when the current token is a word-initial subword fragment — the first piece of a longer word that the tokenizer split into several tokens — with a learned per-fragment gain that is large for p-/re- technical-vocabulary onsets (' pem' in pemphigus, ' pe' in peptidase, ' p' in pumice or penguin, ' per' in percutaneous, ' rep'/'rem'/'ref') and small for most other fragments (' ps', ' pl', ' pr', ' punct'); pieces after the first ('ph', 'ig', 'ands') are much weaker. It is near zero for ordinary complete words (even rare or p-initial ones: patients, people, pneumonia, granite) and for nonsense fragments, weakens when the same word already appeared in the context, and also fires on pieces of non-word strings — DOI digit runs after a citation cue, page references ('p. 2'), p-values ('p = .05'), 'P.3d' citations, 'per cent', hyphenated compounds ('air-powder').

Retrospective marker for the current token being (or completing) a content-bearing referential element: a clause-launching pronoun or keyword (He/She/They/SELECT), a proper noun, number, or date word (Nairobi, 1, March, October), or the locally determined continuation of one (Mit->ochond, p->.m, next->year), with rarer, more specific items activating more strongly; it stays near zero on high-frequency structural tokens (the/The, and, of, commas, periods).

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a frequent, highly predictable two-part collocation: the second subword of a common word (granular, nuance, ingrained, recombination) or the second word of a frozen modifier-head or verb-particle pair (fine grain, fine lines, fringe benefits, slow down, teaming up, highly processed). The same peak token without its usual preceding partner activates it weakly or not at all.

The negative pole detects the letter L at a word-piece boundary: it peaks (1.2-1.7 of its 1.76 max) on the token that continues a word whose immediately preceding piece is a short fragment ending in 'l'/'L' - above all the bare L piece (' l', ' L', '-l', '-L', '/l'), as in ' l'+'entic' (lenticular), ' lo'+'quit' (loquitur), '/l'+'ua' (lua), ' l'+'us' (lus) - and it fires more weakly (0.2-0.6) on word-initial tokens that carry a capital L, especially L-abbreviations (LTD, LED, LR, LSM, LGA, LTP) and proper nouns. It stays at the floor on the bare L token itself, on ordinary words that merely contain an l (also, world, album, clinic), and it is much weaker after longer l-final fragments ('al', 'pal', 'loader'), so it is a piece-boundary feature, not a 'contains l' or 'these tokens' feature.

N170+ is a personal-pronoun anaphora detector: it fires on a personal pronoun (I/my, you/your, he/him/his, she/her, we/our, they/them/their, or a reflexive like myself/himself/herself/themselves) when that pronoun agrees in person, number and gender with a person already mentioned in the preceding context, and it stays near zero on the very same pronoun token when the antecedent is absent (sentence-initial), only later (cataphoric), or gender/number-mismatched. The match is evaluated retrospectively against the recent context: repeated names and nouns never fire it, words after the pronoun do not change it, and a competing feminine mention nearby silences masculine pronouns while a salient feminine antecedent licenses she/her even alongside male mentions.

This pole fires on the token that completes a locally predictable two-part chunk: the second subword of a word, the second word of a fixed collocation or function-word phrase (e.g. central bank, second half, According to, pinch of), or a continuation inside a digit or symbolic sequence. Strength is set jointly by the preceding token and the peak token, so the same peak token fires weakly when its chunk partner is replaced.

L2/N202+ fires on the token that completes a two-part compound name: the head (second) element of a nominal compound in prose ('search button', 'shift key', 'settings page', 'author page', 'Patriot Act', 'hand-foot syndrome'), a quoted label placed before such a head ('"red" button' fires, bare 'red button' does not), and, in code, the final CamelCase/snake_case component of an identifier ('...FolderJoinPolicy', '...CertificateRequest', '...VpnSitesClient', 'priceCtrl', 'readRecords'). Predict inactive: the same head token after a determiner, possessive or attributive adjective ('the button', 'his button', 'the red button'), the earlier components of the same compound ('Shared'/'Folder'/'Join' = 0.00), and compounds whose head is an ordinary object noun that rarely heads compound terms ('search dog', 'search chair', 'search door' stay about 0 even after a noun).

Detects the orthographic stem "deci-" in any language or casing, mainly the decide/decision family (decide, decided, deciding, decision(s), decisive, undecided, indecisive, decidir/decisión, décidé/décision, decisões) plus offshoots that share the letters (decimal, deciliter, decibel, deciduous). It fires on the token that completes the stem, and fires hardest when the stem is split across tokens (Dec+ided, Dec+ide, DEC+ISION, DEC+IMAL, inde+cis, decis+ões; roughly 5-9) rather than held in one whole-word token (' decided', ' decision', ' decimal'; roughly 1.5-4). It stays near zero on other "dec-" words (deceive, decorate, December, declare, decree only ~0.9), on look-alikes (divide, division, divisive, precise, concise) and on synonyms (choose, choice, resolved, agreed).

The negative pole fires when a possessive or existential phrase attributes a mental/conceptual entity to a subject: its peak (1.0-3.0, against a ~0.55 determiner floor) lands on the noun of 'have/has/had/gain/give/provide/possess (a|an|the|no|any) N' when N names a content or faculty of mind - idea, insight, understanding, sense, mind, thought, theory, hypothesis, concept, notion, claim, belief, opinion, view, perspective, interpretation, definition, principle, assumption, taste, eyes, ears ('She has an insight' 2.34, 'She has a claim' 2.68, 'She has a theory' 1.00, 'She gained insight' 1.76, 'has a sense of humour' 2.80). The same nouns only predicated or discussed stay silent ('The idea was good' 0.00, 'The theory is wrong' 0.00, 'We discussed the idea' 0.16, 'Their understanding grew' 0.09), a possessive phrase over a physical or non-mental noun reaches only the determiner's 0.5-0.6 ('She has a car' peaks at ' a' 0.57 while 'car' is 0.00), and the leftovers are a few physical tokens that sit in the same embedding region (hammer 1.45, windshield 1.21, skull 0.84, 'eur' inside 'aneurysm' 1.4) plus 'claim', which fires 0.6-1.1 even outside the frame.

L2/N287+ is a two-token unit detector: the current token is only weakly predictive alone, and the pole peaks on the token that completes a word or number whose opening piece was the immediately preceding token, glued with no space at the join. Its dominant, most reproducible case is the digit pair '5' -> '4'/'5'/'6' (the numerals 54/55/56, e.g. '56-year-old', 'Port=5432', and the interior of '5555'), with a lexically narrower second family of word-final pieces (Ġf+'umble', ĠMar+'lon', Ġblue+'prints', Ġvent+'ral', ĠR+'ourke', Ġd+'ags', F+'***'); it is predicted inactive when the same token follows a different partner (Ġm+'umble', Ġrib+'osomal', 5 followed by 0/7/8/9), when the same word is one token or is split by a space ('Mar lon', 'blueprint'), and for any token in isolation.

The pole fires on the token that completes a two-token predicate unit built on a form of 'make' or 'keep' - the particle of a phrasal verb ('make up' 2.1, 'keep up' 3.6-4.6, 'make out' 1.4, 'make with' 1.1-2.1, 'keep with' 2.4), the resultative adjective the verb selects ('make good' 4.5-4.9, 'make ready' 3.3-3.7, 'make better' 2.3-3.1, 'make worse' 1.4) or the light-verb noun ('make peace' 2.3-3.0, 'make time' 1.5-1.6, 'make do' 3.2) - and it is silent on the verb's ordinary object NPs and on grammaticalised continuations: 'make sure' is 0.00 at all 29 occurrences in the 200k-token scan, 'make sense' 0.45, 'make use' 0.39, 'make known' 0.1, 'make careful' 0.1, 'keep track' 0.1, 'keep quiet' 0.2, and determiners or pronouns that open the object ('make the/it/them/him/their/people', 'keep the/it/them') drive the opposite pole to -3.0 to -6.5. Both halves of the pair are necessary: ' good' after feel/look/seem/very/a stays at 0.16 and ' up' after look/hold/pick/set/give/put at 0.11-0.46 ('get up' only 1.20), tokenizer-split compounds are not enough ('over'+'come', 'black'+'board', 'sun'+'light' 0.13; 'zinc electrode' 0.25), and ' of' two tokens after 'make' fires only when the middle token is 'sense' ('make sense of' 2.6-2.8, 'make use of' 0.9; ' of' after a time quantity like 'years of' stays at 0.8-1.4, at or below the 1.21 active threshold).

Retrospective detector for the token that resolves the currently open unit: a subword finishing a rare word (amoxic->illin, Photos->ynthesis), a symbol or collocate completing a fixed frame (as->np, golden->brown), or the predicate, complement, or head noun a clause was waiting for (Lima->are, cat->sat, defendant->pleaded, submit->report), plus a unigram bias for sentence-initial discourse tokens (Please, I, Hello). Lexically incongruous fillers (table for brown/pleaded) and structural function words (the, and, ., on) stay near zero. The subword/symbol completions fire via the standard g+u+ SwiGLU regime while the clause-level resolvers fire via the double-negative g-u- regime, i.e. two related implementations of one resolution job.

Retrospective detector: fires when the current token is the highly predictable local completion of the immediately preceding 1-2 tokens (the second half of a conventional collocation, syntactic frame, or split word, e.g. court->ruled, museum->is, capital of->France, pleaded->not, triangle->inequality, 100->degrees, Elect->rons); the same token after an unrelated word stays quiet.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a strongly-cued local chunk: a subword piece continuing a split (usually rare or technical) word (hy+pos, pron+eness, G+yll, McPh+erson, Ph+on, Ty+len) or the second word of a frozen collocation (public+service, Public+Affairs, Blood+glucose/sugar). Near-misses that stay near zero: the same tail piece after a weakly-cueing prefix (ty+pos 1.08 vs hy+pos 4.12; Gen+etic ~0), the same morpheme merged into one common token (happiness), or a free word combination (public park, sea spray). Graded detector: common words completing the same way fire weakly (typos 1.08) rather than zero.

The negative pole fires on closed-class 'linker' words of two kinds. About 23% of its activation mass is the single token ' to' (the infinitive/complement marker), which reaches strength about 0.4 in nearly any syntactic context, so almost any English sentence containing ' to' peaks just above the scan's active threshold (0.55); far stronger responses (strength 1-4, at or above the scan maximum of 2.2) go to the word that completes a 'for'/'of' name or term phrase - the noun 1-3 tokens after 'for' in a naming frame ('the Institute for Cancer' 3.4, 'for Teachers' 2.7, 'for Class 9' 1.4) or the connective that closes a name head ('Conservation of' 1.7, 'what to expect from' 2.4, 'Polk County Courthouse' 1.1) - while the same nouns outside such a frame stay silent ('the University of Michigan' 0.1, 'for students' 0.04, 'we met Cancer' 0.04). The two modes are separate SwiGLU sign regimes (gate<0,up>0 for ' to'; gate>0,up<0 for the frame completions), and the pole is retrospective: zero-ablating it on a mix of both modes gives KL 3.8e-4 against the next-token distribution, below the 1e-3 lookahead threshold.

Fires retrospectively when the current token completes a locally highly predictable continuation licensed by the preceding 1-2 tokens — the second half of a fixed collocation, conventional phrase, SQL/syntax pattern, or split subword/number form; the same frequent token in an unpredictable bigram context does not drive it.

This positive pole is a retrospective, graded detector of two-token binding: it peaks on a token that completes a unit opened by the token immediately to its left, either the next piece of a word the tokenizer split ('As' after 'PD' in PDAs, 'sons' after 'Daw' in Dawsons, 'ius' after 'Maurit', 'us' after 'sa' in sausages, 'va' after 'Pur') or the second element of a multi-token name or fixed expression ('Britain' after 'Great', 'Alberta' after 'University of', 'Violence' after 'Family', 'China' after 'Greater', 'Lakes' after 'Great', 'recently' after 'until', 'out' after 'grew', 'well' after 'may', 'A' after 'David'). The same word after a determiner, preposition or unrelated modifier ('modern Britain', 'the college in Alberta', 'may still', 'came out', lowercase 'violence') sits at or below zero, so the pole tracks how strongly this model binds the pair rather than the token's identity, frequency or surprisal (correlation with the model's own next-token log-probability is -0.005 over 20k natural-text tokens, with entropy -0.03, with token frequency 0.06); it is selective rather than a general compound detector, since 'New York', 'White House' and 'University of Toronto' are inactive while 'Great Britain', 'Great Lakes' and 'University of Alberta' are active.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a conventional multi-token expression: a verb plus its idiomatic particle or preposition (rushed into, stared at, follows directly from), a fixed adjective-noun phrase (golden brown), or a similarly stereotyped slot (def add, after three), with strength graded by how strongly the preceding one or two tokens license the current one. Same-token context breaks collapse firing while distant meaning changes do not; early-position subword onsets (They h, def xyz) fire via the opposite SwiGLU sign regime (g+u+ vs the dominant g-u-) and are a separate offshoot this claim does not cover.

The negative pole fires on the content word that a group term attributively qualifies: it peaks on the second element of a compound whose first word names a human group or social category (nationality, ethnicity, religion, race, age, gender, kinship, disability or role), strongest on collective/abstract heads (Muslim history 3.6, black history 9.1, gay community 2.2, refugee families 2.2, young person 2.3, trans woman, white power, Japanese Patent), and it generalises to unseen groups and heads (Kurdish, Roma, Sikh, deaf, immigrant, Catholic, migrant all fire at 1.4-2.5 on unseen heads). It stays near zero for the same head noun after a non-group modifier (social/world/medical/music history 0.05-0.09, private schools 0.15, wealthy families 0.24, kitchen table 0.28) and when the group word is not the immediately preceding token (the history of Sikhs 0.26, women who are Muslim 0.71, multi-token group words whose last fragment is what actually precedes the head, e.g. Elderly -> 'ly' 0.21); the leftovers are weak activations on local/jazz history (0.7-1.1) and on the subword 'ch' of Harishchandra (1.6-1.9).

Retrospective negation-scope detector. Its strong, general response (about 0.5-2.7) is to the token that sits inside the scope of a negator earlier in the clause (not, n't, never, no, nobody, nothing, without, hardly, cannot): the pole peaks on the polarity-sensitive or light word the negation licenses (any, ever, anything, anyone, at all, all, way, just) and on the light word that continues the negated predicate (to, the, a, like, want, some), and it falls to the floor (<=0.15) when that negator is replaced by an affirmative word (also, often, one, all, with) or when the peak token is replaced by a non-polarity synonym. In affirmative text the pole only reaches a weaker 0.15-0.5 band, on degree/quantifier modifiers (much, more, far, very, too, even, both, lower) and on scattered single content words that complete a familiar phrase (central, rain, increased, captured, of), so text with no negator and none of those tokens is predicted inactive.

L2/N3729+ is a retrospective, sparse lexical-binding detector: it fires at token t only when the two-token string (token t-1, token t) is a fixed string the model has memorized, and it stays at the floor when the same slot is filled by a semantically equivalent but unmemorized alternative, so the pole tracks the exact pair and never either token alone. The memorized keys cluster on J-initial stems plus a high-frequency continuation ('Journal of' 5.7, 'jug of' 3.0, 'jazz of' 2.0, 'jar of' 1.9, 'junction of' 1.9, 'Justice of' 2.7, 'j'+'ourn' in journald 4.0, 'J'+'.' 3.0, 'jquery'+'-'+'3' 2.2, 'java'+'Script' 1.8), with a minority of non-J keys ('Rio Grande' 1.6, 'Jackie Chan' 1.5, 'should I'/'should he' 1.5, 'Heisen'+'berg' 1.2, 'Index of' 1.3); parallel strings outside the key set sit at the floor ('bottle of' 0.08, 'report of' 0.04, 'blues of' 0.17, 'jacket of' 0.12, 'New York' 0.02, 'United Nations' 0.03, 'M.' 0.15, 'Schwar'+'zen' 0.08), so a labeler should mark text active only for a listed key pair or an exact repetition of one, not for its family.

Retrospective detector for the completion of a locally predictable 2-3 token unit headed by a function word or fixed formula (preposition/determiner/conjunction/pronoun plus content word, e.g. the report, by Friday, to the hallway, Once upon); it peaks on the head content word only when the 1-2 preceding tokens form the licensing context, and drops when that preceding token is replaced even if the peak word is kept.

L2/N409+ is a sparse, retrospective two-token lexical-binding detector: it spikes, one token wide, on the token that fuses with its immediate left neighbour (for a three-token unit such as 'Mother of God', with the token two places back) into a single memorized lexical item, and its members are almost all proper names, foreign/technical terms, coined compounds and a few fixed frames - both the continuing piece of a split name or term (' Roy'+'ce' 1.35, ' Philip'+'son' 1.05, ' str'+'ig'+'atus' 1.08, ' Flor'+'ham' 0.89, ' Pal'+'ad' 0.85, ' Origin'+'ated' 0.94-0.99, 'phy'+'topl' 0.77, ' f'+'loss' 0.75, ' Bess'+'ie' 0.38, 'ah'+'orse' 0.37, 'of'+'sky' in Rosofsky 0.54) and the head element of a fixed two-word unit (' life'+' forms' 1.24, 'Mother of'+' God' 1.09, 'Voice'+'Thread' 0.92-1.02, 'Joseph'+' Smith' 0.63-0.82, 'genital'+' mutil' 0.85, 'civil'+' service' 0.75, 'from'+' being' 0.75, 'Norman'+' S' 0.73, 'Saint'+' John' 0.53, 'S'+'outhern Song' 0.35, 'life'+' support' 0.45, 'family'+' name' 0.33). The identity of the left neighbour, not of the peak token, decides it: the same head token after a free or unmemorized partner stays at the floor ('many forms' 0.03, 'other forms' 0.01, 'government service' 0.09, 'the service' 0.00, 'currently being' 0.00, ' Smith' after 'ie'/'op' 0.00, ' S' after ' in' 0.16), ordinary split common words stay at the floor ('domestic'+'ated' 0.00, 'elong'+'ated' 0.03, 'jug'+'ated' 0.06), the opening fragment and the later pieces of a unit are silent (' Roy' 0.00, ' Sony' 0.00, ' Joseph' 0.00, 'ation' 0.00, 'ank' 0.00, 'ino' 0.03), what follows the peak is unconstrained (',', ' in', ' from', ' have', ' inherited' all at 0.00-0.14), and strength is graded by how hard this model binds the pair (' Sonya' 1.11 vs 'Jorma' 0.40; ' Philipson' 1.05 vs 'Gilson' 0.28; ' Roy'+'ce' 1.19-1.35 vs 'oy'+'ce' inside Rolls-Royce 0.49-0.56). Membership is pair-specific rather than compositional - equally name-like pairs such as 'Pinetop'+' Smith' and 'Bessie'+' Smith' do not fire - so label a position active only when it completes one of these stored items (a name, taxon, technical term, coined compound, or fixed frame) and label inactive the same head word after a determiner, modifier or unrelated partner, free phrases, ordinary inflected forms, and the unit's opening fragment or trailing pieces; the opposite pole takes the complementary class of two-token completions ('s'+'urgery', 'ant'+'ise'+'ptic', ' birth'+' weight'), so the neuron's axis is which kind of pair, not pair-hood itself, and it is retrospective (Jacobian kurtosis 3.42 with no coherent promoted-token set, lens agreement 0.0, unrelated tokens follow every peak).

This pole fires on the completion-side token of a locally highly constrained bigram: most strongly on a single-character separator (the standalone space immediately before a digit, ( right after range, > closing a tag, or the space after = or >) where the preceding token opens a slot with a nearly determined filler such as a number after to, by, at, =, >, range, or a numbered name like Apollo, and at mid strength on the fixed second word of a memorized phrase (than after greater, of after capital, bank after central, noon after at). The same separator or function word in an unconstrained context (a space before a non-number, of after ordinary nouns, than after other comparatives, ( after other verbs) drives little or no activation, which beats a pure token-identity account; weak blips on ordinary content words (announced, he, triangle, began) are acknowledged leftovers near baseline.

The negative pole fires on a token that does not begin a new word but continues the word the previous token started — a sub-word piece of one word split across tokens (Mu|irs, creat|inine, dys|p|nea, Dem|irt, C|1, actinomycet|em|comitans, Mem|rist|ors) — strongest for long, rare, technical or proper words split into several pieces, and near zero when the token starts a new word after a space (measured lift ~5-15x between the two regimes over 300 pile-10k documents). The only space-prefixed firings are a small memorized set of two-token pairs such as 'City of' (0.87-2.40, but 'City in', 'City at', 'Bank of', 'United States', 'Andrew Mellon' all stay below 0.1) and 'Jim Gray', so the right label is 'this token continues/completes a known two-token word-piece or pair', not the trigger-token list; the positive pole fires on the same kind of continuation pieces (Civil|ian, civilis|ations) and on pairs like 'Code Review', so both poles are continuation detectors that differ in sign and in the pairs they key on.

This negative pole fires on a short token that fuses with the token immediately before it into one lexical unit: (i) the particle ' up' after a short, forceful, consonant-final action-verb stem (crack, rack, back, carve, crush, chalk, crank, build, break, patch, shake, shut, hook, mark + up), and (ii) the second, word-internal piece of a word split across tokens (Buch|annon, Phot|acter, arch|ipel, back|g|arden, setProp|ried). It stays at zero after soft/Latinate or vowel-final verbs before the same particle (took/filled/covered/ended/signed/mixed/looked/gave up) and on the same fragment when the word starts at the current token (Cannon, Bacterium), so it tracks the two-token fusion, not the tokens ' up' or the fragments themselves.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that fills a locally constrained phrasal slot, typically a content noun or verb completing a determiner-, possessive-, adjective- or verb-headed phrase (e.g. 'the valley', 'your report', 'central bank', 'the Moon', 'crowd erupted', 'According to the'), with strength graded by contextual fit. Its output direction suppresses generic 'as'-family continuations (' as', ' As', '作为', '作為', ' sebagai'), consistent with marking local phrase closure.

The negative pole fires on the whitespace token that Qwen's tokenizer splits off immediately before a written numeral - the bare ' ' in 'In 1969', 'around the year 1600', 'open from 9', 'on 7 March 1885', 'the spring of 1919' - where it peaks at 0.3-1.2, decaying across the digits themselves (first digit 0.2-0.3, later digits near zero) and losing that spike when the same number is spelled out in words ('from nine', 'at nine', 'the spring of nineteen forty-five'). Text with no written numeral stays much lower, although a weaker 0.2-0.4 lift on some ordinary prose clauses is an acknowledged leftover this hypothesis does not explain.

This pole fires retrospectively on a content token (or word-piece) that is strongly anticipated by its immediate left context: the completion point of a conventionalized verb+complement ('fell sharply', 'are you', 'went by' as particle), determiner+noun ('the door', 'the court'), quantity+unit ('3.9 percent'), or subword sequence ('sym-phony', 're-election'), with strength tracking how constraining the context is.
