Its output direction decodes to demonstratives ('this/these'), consistent with marking a completed constituent available for anaphoric reference, but since peaks sit on the completing token rather than before a demonstrative, the firing condition is retrospective, not next-token lookahead.

Fires where a passage specifies the physical position, extent or surface of something in a concrete scene: at the spatial preposition plus determiner that open a locative phrase ('around the corner', 'off the ground', 'on the floor', 'under the surface', 'across the brook'), at the modifier that gives an object's shape or appearance ('flat surfaces', 'bare soles', 'an open backpack', 'his left shoulder', 'the muddy floor'), and at body-part terms in positional idioms ('neck and neck', 'head and shoulders above'). The same tokens in abstract, evaluative or procedural prose stay silent ('in the long run', 'the bottom line', 'the proposal', 'the theory'), even inside fixed idioms, so the pole tracks the surrounding physical description rather than the peak token: the word after the peak is irrelevant ('off the ground' 7.65 equals 'off the table' 7.65), while replacing the physical phrasing drops it ('neck and neck' 11.4 to 'tied and level' 0.4).

This pole fires on the digits of a numeral that states a quantity - a measure of how large, how far, how heavy, how long, how much, or how many something is (depth, distance, weight, duration, dose, price, or a counted magnitude with a unit or scale word such as metres, km, ug, mg, million, billion) - peaking on the digit that completes the numeral and dropping to ~0 on the token after it. The same digits used as a label or identifier (serial number, product code, store/page number) leave it inactive, and an explicit unit word need not follow: the pole reads the numeral already present in a measure phrase, it does not prepare an upcoming unit token.

Fires on a subword fragment that begins or continues a memorized multi-token word or fixed phrase: surnames after their given names (Ryan+Fredericks, David+Carlucci, Christy after a name-list comma), common words split mid-word (underst+ated, colon+ized, fed+ora, W+ob+urn, hand+-me), and encoded or path or command pieces (%+2F, &#+3, /usr/local+/lib, math+fr), with strength graded by how strongly the preceding words predict that exact completion, so the identical fragment fires several-fold stronger after its predictive prefix than after a neutral one. It stays near floor on whole-word or single-token uses of the same strings (the colon as a noun, Bog of Allen, Christ as an exclamation), on fragments of long technical words with no predictive prefix (sentence-initial Immunohistochemistry, adenocarcinoma after a determiner or adjective), and in passages containing no such fragments.

The pole is a sparse detector of the civic-institutional register: it spikes (1.6-4.6 of a max of 5.1) where formal prose pins down a particular institution, charity or research effort - on the leading token of an uncommon person or organisation name (' Stam' in Stamoulis 4.6, ' Vo' in Voigt 4.2, ' Ky' in Kytle 3.5, 'no' in Yuzhnoye 2.9) and on nonprofit / volunteer / research-staff vocabulary ('nonprofit' 2.9, 'volunteers' 2.1, 'researchers' 1.8, 'all-volunteer' 1.8, 'charity' 1.8, 'committee' 1.6, ' Organisation' 2.8), plus the function word that closes a heavy institutional phrase ('we' at 4.7 in '...and the generous support of the public, we hope', 'have' at 2.8 after 'St. Jude Children's Research Hospital scientists'). It stays near floor (0.1-0.9) on plain narrative, business reporting, generic organization words ('council', 'company', 'foundation', 'institute'), famous or common names ('Einstein', 'Obama', 'Smith', 'Hernandez'), and on the words 'support'/'help'/'funding' themselves, so merely mentioning support, help or funding does not fire it ('support'->'backing' 2.6->2.4; 'Our work was supported by a grant from the foundation' 0.13).

This pole fires retrospectively on the current token through a gate-by-key conjunction: the gate opens when the token is the singular head noun of a sentence-initial 'The/A/Our + NOUN' phrase, the complement noun of the fixed evidential frame 'According to the NOUN', or a noun immediately following a same-field noun (compounds and credential clusters such as 'password manager', 'file manager', 'login credential'), and the key matches a memorized field of representational artifacts -- recorded-information media (record, report, document, book, file, letter, message, photo, account), access credentials (password, login, credential), and observation/communication instruments and storage (telescope, camera, phone, radio, storage) -- with peak strengths from ~0.4 to above the scan maximum realized in the gate-open (g>0) regime with negative up-projection. It fires weakly or not at all on the same nouns used as verbs (record, report), as plurals, after demonstratives, or as mid-sentence verb complements, on animate, natural-kind, building, vehicle and heavy-machine, material and mass, and abstract nouns in identical frames (teacher, manager alone, engineer, dog, sun, moon, house, window, car, machine, device, engine, paper, salt, system, function, truth), and on all other tokens shows only a diffuse gate-closed-regime response at or below 0.45 of scan maximum (prepositions, determiners and complement or measure nouns inside PPs and adjuncts such as by, the, to, of, mat, storm, level, year, mg, and periods).

The negative pole fires, retrospectively, on the token that completes a quantity pinned to an explicit scale: a non-first digit-piece of a multi-token numeral ('aged 73' peaks at '3', 'Excel 2003' mid-numeral, '90 percent' at '0', '20-30' at the final '0') or the %/magnitude word closing it ('90%', '7 billion', 'thirty years'). It requires the numeral to sit inside a scale construction: an age/demographic bracket ('aged N', 'ages A-B', 'her 30s', 'six months and older'), a version/model/rating ('iOS 6', 'Excel 2003', 'gcc 4.4', 'SPF 30'), a hyphenated range or every-N rate ('25-54', 'every 20-30 minutes'), or an N-or-more/threshold/duration frame ('50 or more', 'past thirty years'). Its gain is set by quantity-dense surrounding discourse (mean attribution distance ~84 tokens): the same construction fires weakly isolated and strongly amid other numerals. It stays near zero on opening digit-pieces, on sentence-initial bare numerals, and on numerals in non-scale uses: bare counts/scores ('73 guests', 'men scored 73', 'Thirty guests'), identifiers and calendar dates ('Room 73', 'year 2003', 'TC-3-22.20'), instruction temperatures and single times ('180 degrees', '45 minutes', 'every 45 minutes' at 2.2), and isolated bare percentages ('73% of households', '90 percent of us' sentence-initial). Residual leftovers it does not explain: bare scale nouns firing inside very numeral-dense passages ('decade' at 8.6) and large round magnitudes ('60,000', '100,000'). Its output direction promotes '+'-family continuation tokens, which together with steering (clamping emits enumerations like '100 dollars', '3 books on science, 2 books on history') indicates the pole hands downstream a to-be-continued quantity signal rather than predicting a specific next token.

This retrospective neuron detects the plus sign symbol '+' (or ' +'), firing when it occurs as an addition operator in mathematical/code expressions (e.g., 'calculate a + b', 'return a + b') or as a positive modifier suffix (e.g., academic grades 'A+', blood types 'AB+'). Its output projection strongly suppresses the '+' token and its variants to prevent redundant consecutive operator emission.

This pole fires on tokens that are highly predictable from their left context — conventional collocations ('central' in 'the central bank'), expected function words ('the' after a preposition), number continuations ('9' in '1969'), keyword-licensed slots ('add' after 'def') and subword completions ('ist') — i.e. it marks low-surprisal, informationally redundant tokens. The same token in a less constraining context fires weakly while changing only the following token leaves the peak unchanged, and it prepares no coherent upcoming-token set (Jacobian-lens kurtosis ~3.4 with incoherent promoted fragments), so the mechanism is retrospective.

L20/N3372- is a natural-science/engineering register detector: its strength builds over the preceding words while the model reads technical description of concrete physical subject matter - materials and the parts made from them, chemical and biological substances, organisms, landforms and their measured properties - and it peaks on the technical content word or numeric value at the point where that vocabulary is locally densest ('a predetermined resistance', 'a pressure of', 'greatest common factor', 'U.S. Highway 136'). It keys on the vocabulary and phrasing rather than on sense or truth (technical-sounding nonsense such as 'the quantum resistance of the capacitor was predetermined by the electrical field' fires as strongly as a real patent sentence) and needs a run of it, so narration, dialogue, sport, money, law, administration, statistics/methodology and code - and a single technical word dropped into such prose - stay near zero.

This pole fires retrospectively on a concrete topic-establishing content word, typically the noun or distinctive verb that fixes what an ordinary sentence is about (theorem, lemma, recipe, galaxy, password, capital, fell, tuned, rushed); in the identical sentence frame it stays near zero on organizational or administrative vocabulary (management, manager, administration, governance, control), and its output direction strongly suppresses management/control tokens, so the pole acts as a concrete-subject detector that down-weights organizational continuations.

This pole fires on a token that is a highly predictable continuation of its immediate 1-3 token prefix, i.e. when the prefix plus the current token form a familiar collocation or construction slot (verb/determiner sequences like 'opened the' and 'before the', 'contain at', 'are all capital', 'bank raised', sentence-initial determiner+noun like 'The defendant' or 'Our quarterly'). The same surface token (e.g. ' the', ' at', ' capital', ' heavy') fires after a familiar prefix but not after an unexpected one, and changing the following token leaves firing unchanged; its output direction promotes plural/collective nouns (projects, programs, systems, companies, datasets).

Retrospective graded salience/novelty signal: strongest on the token delivering the clause's least predictable new content (disambiguating piece of a rare word such as sym/ria/illin, an unpredictable name, date, number or unit such as Neil, October, 100, light-years, or a first-mentioned content word such as orchestra, river, remember, dog), moderate on the sentence-final period summarizing such a clause, and low on predictable function words and on repeated/given words even of the same class (second 'cat' 0.115 vs first 0.357; 'meeting' 0.15 vs 'sym' 0.86).

The negative pole fires on the vocabulary of conducting and analysing a quantitative study: extent adverbs that say how completely a manipulation or measurement was carried out when attached to study nouns ('study', 'experiment', 'trial', 'data', 'sample', 'specimens' - e.g. 'a completely randomized design', 'the specimens were randomly divided into three groups') and the names of study designs and statistical procedures ('repeated measures', 'two-way ANOVA', 'multivariate analyses', 'multiple/logistic regression', 'generalized linear mixed model', 'central composite rotatable design', 'three-stage sampling', 'prospective cohort', 'doubly robust', 'orthogonal' moment functions). The same surface words in ordinary narrative or about non-study subjects, and technical vocabulary that names objects rather than quantitative procedures, leave it at baseline ('The building was completely destroyed' 0.3, 'built randomly over the years' 0.0, 'the Krebs cycle'/'the Higgs boson'/'the Golgi apparatus' ~0), and the neuron's positive pole is silent on all of these inputs (<=0.04) while its write direction is the anti-'system' direction.

Fires retrospectively when the current token continues or completes a conventionalized multi-token expression -- a person, character, organism, drug, or media name, a four-digit year or price figure, or license or code boilerplate -- where the preceding tokens (name stem, genus, 'License', 'class NAME(', 'Price') strongly constrain it; the same surface token without that constraining prefix stays inactive.

Retrospective detector that fires on a token strongly predicted by its immediate left context: the completion of a locally constrained collocation, fixed phrase, name-plus-number, or grammatical frame (e.g. 'seek'+re, 'Apollo'+1, 'because'+of, 'cups'+of, 'the year'+1, 'final'+note, plural-subject+'are'). The same surface token after a weakly constraining predecessor, or an unpredictable token in the same slot, stays quiet, and changing only downstream tokens leaves the peak unchanged.

Retrospectively, the pole fires on the token that introduces a specific, narrow lexical value into a slot the preceding words have opened: the first piece of a rare or technical word or proper name (' sym'+'phony', ' am'+'oxic'+'illin', ' Ham'+'let', ' March', ' Celsius') or the bare leading token that Qwen's tokenizer splits off a numeral ('at 100', 'active = 1', 'Apollo 11'). It sits near baseline on high-frequency generic fillers in the same slot ('the concert', 'active = true'), on the words that set the slot up, and on ordinary prose; within the rare-word class the response is selective (penicillin, ibuprofen and xylophone stay at baseline), and a second, much larger response family on the copula after an expletive subject ('it is', 'it's', up to 7.8 in running text) is not explained by this claim.

The pole fires on the function word that opens a definite reference to members of an organised collective - most strongly the article in partitive phrases ('one / two / several / many / some of the X'), also 'all' + plural noun and '<verb> as <designation>' - and its strength roughly doubles when a collective entity (club, firm, team, church) has been named in the preceding ~15 tokens rather than a mere object (ship, rock, tree). It never peaks on the head noun (which it cannot see), stays near zero on demonstratives ('one of those X'), on genitive 'of' ('a member of the X') and on bare definites ('the members'), and ablating it lowers the probability of collective nouns (club, team, church, NFL); the protocol's lookahead gate still returns retrospective (KL 6.3e-4, just under its 1e-3 threshold).

L20/N930- is a Ruby / RubyGems detector: it is strongly active (0.3-1.0 of scale) on Ruby source code (def...end, @ivar, :symbol, #{} interpolation, bare require 'x') and on Ruby's package-manager register - gem/Gemfile/gemspec lines, the gem names rake, rspec, bundler, rubocop, jekyll and rails even inside ordinary prose, rubygems.org URLs and .../lib/ruby2.x/gems/... paths - and it reaches at most ~0.1 of scale on the same content written in Python, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java or PHP. The pole is retrospective, not lookahead: it reads the Ruby topic already present in the context (48% of its input attribution sits more than 16 tokens back; its gate row is closest to the embeddings of 'ruby', ' Rails', 'nil', '.rb', '.erb', '#{' and 'ARGV'), and its output direction raises that same vocabulary (' gem', ' gems', ' ruby', ' rails', ' hash') in the next-token distribution rather than preparing one specific upcoming token.

The pole is a retrospective 'committed completion' detector: it peaks on a token when the model already holds a nearly determined completion for what follows, either a sub-word piece whose remaining letters are forced (del|uded, deb|riefing, tele|fonene, re|arg|ues, cumhur|ba|şkanı, proverb|ial - the fragment set is idiosyncratic: del-, deb-, tele-, tra-, comp-, det-, dec-, def-, rel-, rec- peak while des-, dev-, comm-, tes- do not) or an ordinary function word whose next word is nearly forced (a single next token holding about 90%+ probability: 'that comment is beside the |point' peaks on ' the', 'the comment is beside the |point' does not). It stays near zero on complete single-token words (deleted, delighted, debate, telephone) and on function words with an open continuation (the book is on the |table, it is beside the |point at issue).

Fires on the token that opens the next slot of a count expression the passage has already established: strongest before a repeated 'multiple'/'Multi-' ('... may have multiple X ... may have multiple Y'; 'multiple A, multiple B and multiple C') and before the second word of a numeral range ('one or more', 'zero or more', 'one or two'), landing on the auxiliary or conjunction that opens the slot (' have', ' and', ' or', ' a', ' to', ' the'). A lone first mention of a quantity word, the quantity word itself, ordinary plural nouns and runs of 'several'/'many' stay below the active threshold (a residue of peaks on mid-word fragments of rare words, e.g. '.ro' in 'openapi.roots' or ' BRO' in 'BROOKLYN', is not covered by this rule), and the pole's write suppresses the word it anticipates: the Jacobian lens suppresses 'multiple'/'multi'/'mult' and promotes 'many'/'few'/'许多'/'muchos', and zero-ablating the pole raises p('multiple') by about 0.12 at its peak.

This pole fires on a short non-final piece of a word the tokenizer has split — a word-initial fragment such as ' ke' (keystone), ' ne' (neared, neil), ' Per' (Pervez, Permanently), ' fer' (ferocious), ' Sne' (Sneaker), ' NE' (NEAREST), ' K' (pKiller) or ' P' (Paseo), or a mid-word fragment such as 'ke' (Inverkeithing) and 'ase' (Paseo) — and on the Romance/Turkic preverbal particles 'ne', 'no', 'he', 'Não' and 'NE' that lean on the following verb, with full strength only when licensed by the immediate left context (a determiner, pronoun, title, proper name, or verb frame). It grades with that context (' ke' ~6.6 after 'the'/'a' but ~2.8 after 'mentioned'; ' Per' ~3.1 inside an assassinate-plus-title frame but ~1.6 after a bare year; whole-token 'electrical' only ~2+ inside dense technical prose versus ~1.2-1.6 everyday), and stays near baseline on single-token words with the same letters (keyboard, nearest, never, calm, Usually, john, Tuesday, Permanent, Patio, electric), on the completion tails of split words ('ystone', 'ared', 'vez', 'ocious', 'aker', 'il'), and on quoted non-ke syllables ('pa').

The pole fires on a token that completes a lexically specific, locally constrained sequence: a constraining opener one to three tokens back (a verb, preposition, or idiom start such as 'pleaded', 'calls for', 'boils at', 'import', 'must', 'so', 'range(1') whose idiomatic continuation the current token supplies (e.g. 'not', 'two', '100', 'numpy', 'contain', 'fast', '0'). It stays near silent on phrase-initial tokens and collapses when the opener is replaced by an equally grammatical but non-associating word, while changes to tokens after the peak have no effect.

The pole fires retrospectively on a token that is a subword piece split out of a longer word (the tokenizer's mid-word boundary), and its strength is set mainly by which piece it is: ' fl' (7-8 of the pole's 9.75 max after almost any lead-in), ' sul' (6.4), ' cl' (5.1), ' cav' (4.4), ' pl' (3.5), ' conv'/' sk'/' carb' (2.8) and the space/case variants ' Pl', ' Sk', 'Fl', ' Cl', plus the word-internal 'um' of 'cr|um|pled' (5.2), while the same letters inside one fused token (' flower' 0.2, ' clock' 0.4) and the leading pieces of other rare or technical words (' mitochond' 0.0, ' Elect' 0.1, ' Hyper' 0.2) stay below 0.6, so it is neither a rare-word/technical-register detector nor an air-conditioning neuron (a small residue on ordinary single tokens such as ' system' 4.7 is not covered by this rule). The word ' air' is a weak member of the same family (1.2 after a neutral 'the') that climbs to 4-9.7 only when the lead-in commits the model to a following compound head ('Please turn off the ... air conditioning' 6.5-7.3, 'the hotel air conditioning' 6.9, 'contaminants like air-borne' 5.6) and stays at 0.9-2.2 when ' air' is a plain noun or the continuation is open ('the air in the room' 1.2, 'air quality' 1.2, 'They discussed the air conditioning' 1.6).

This pole detects competitive-contest content: it is strongly active on tokens in a clause that reports a contest, its competitors, stages, standings or outcome - result verbs ('scored', 'won', 'lost', 'beat', 'eliminated', 'qualified', 'defended'), tournament stages ('semifinal', 'quarterfinal', 'playoffs', 'next round', 'final', 'championship', 'league', 'season'), and honours/records ('record', 'medal', 'gold', 'prize', 'champion', 'reigning', 'defending', 'title') - and its peak lands on the function word ('the', 'a', 'of', 'in', 'for', 'his') that follows such a verb or introduces the contest noun rather than on the contest word itself, so the pole is retrospective: the activation at that function word is unchanged by which noun follows ('in the final' and 'in the stadium' both peak at 18.3), but removing the contest frame collapses it ('scored'->'ate': 1.77 -> 0.33). Prose with no contest in it stays near zero, as do the same strings in a non-contest sense or role ('the final chapter' 0.14, 'the title page' 0.33, 'struck a match' 0.22, 'recorded the interview' 0.00, 'quartered the apple' 0.43), whereas contest nouns keep a moderate response even when used figuratively ('the champion of the cause' 4.25, 'the players in the orchestra' 1.72) and the bare modifier 'world' gives a weak ~1-1.5 response outside 'world record'/'world class'; its output direction promotes exactly this vocabulary (Jacobian/logit lens: ' title', ' Quarter', ' SEM', ' final', 'quarter'; ablation shifts probability toward 'final', 'title', 'semifinal', 'championship', 'tournament'), but the effect is too spread to meet the lookahead criteria.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a short, locally constraining grammatical frame set up by the preceding 1-2 tokens, typically determiner plus head noun, preposition plus complement, auxiliary plus negation or main verb, or subject plus main verb or modal; the same word after a frame-breaking predecessor activates weakly, while distant topic changes matter little.

Retrospective detector that peaks on the second token of a conventional local bigram or collocation (determiner-noun like 'the hall/crowd', verb-possessive like 'tuned their', noun-modifier like 'kingdom far'/'sea level', subject-verb like 'cat sat', or subword continuations like 'amoxic-illin'/'16-0'), driven chiefly by the immediately preceding token; replacing either half of the pair with an incongruous token collapses activation while distant or upcoming-token edits do not.

Fires at the juncture of a quantified duration-or-speed expression: on the space between a duration preamble (takes/take, about, for, every, approximately, time of, last) and its number, or on the rate connector (per, /) joining a distance noun (miles, kilometres, km, knots) to its unit. It reacts to the already-read preamble or distance noun rather than the upcoming unit, so swapping the trailing unit (minutes→elephants, hour→person) leaves the peak unchanged while swapping the preamble verb, distance noun, or connector collapses it.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is the leading fragment of a word the tokenizer split across tokens (Se|ine, re|-election, pro|tons, hab|ite, digit-runs like 1|00), i.e. it detects an incomplete word-initial piece whose remainder is still pending. The same stem as one fused token (Second, review, problems) is inactive, and among identical fragments a constraining prior gates strength (boils at 100 fires, spilled at 100 does not).

Retrospectively fires on tokens within spans describing the physical, anatomical, or structural features and components of biological organisms, cells, or mechanical implements. It remains inactive on abstract concepts, organizations, and figurative or non-structural descriptions sharing similar syntax.

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes or continues an entity-anchoring phrase in factual exposition about a named person, work, vehicle, institution, place, event, date or ranked list — e.g. manufacturer+model (Grumman F), title (Ghost of Christmas, Street Scene, Pulp Fiction), role/honorific+name (recording legend Dave, offensive tackle Al), name-and-name pair (Harry and Ramona, Jacob and Mary, Watt & Shand), lifespan/rank parenthesis plus descriptor, or date/event/origin anchor (mid-1960s, since the creation, wake of the 9/11 attacks, built/boarded a + artifact/vehicle) — driven by the preceding proper-name/type words; it fires regardless of past, present or present-perfect tense, declarative or interrogative mood, or whether the anchor is geographic.

The positive pole is a topic detector for a human singing voice: it is high throughout a passage about a singer or about singing — singing-voice types and vocal technique (soprano, coloratura, contralto, baritone, falsetto, bel canto, vibrato, aria, vocals) and a person singing — and once a singer has been introduced it stays elevated for tens of tokens on otherwise neutral words (e.g. ' her' measures 11.8 after 'Maria was a singer...' but 0.0 after 'Maria was a baker...'), so it tracks the vocal-music topic rather than the trigger tokens. Instrumental or composed classical music (composer, symphony, quartet, pianist, Beethoven) keeps the positive pole near zero while driving the negative pole instead, matching an output direction that promotes ' voice'/'voices'/'sing'/'vocals'/'歌声' and suppresses 'composition'/'composed'; passages about performed or recorded sound (audio mixing, actors' performances) give only weak offshoot activation (means 1-2, peaks about 7).

Retrospective grammatical agreement detector: fires in Romance languages (French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian) on plural determiners, quantifiers, and pre-nominal or modifying adjectives (such as 'nouvelles', 'principales', 'las', 'das', 'des', 'as') agreeing with a feminine plural noun. It exhibits much weaker activation on masculine plural counterparts, and drops to near zero on singular forms and in non-agreeing languages like English.

Retrospective subword-fragment detector: the negative pole fires when the current token is a BPE fragment piece — a token that typically appears inside a longer word (prefix pieces like Sub/sub/subs/SUB/Fle/arbe/ery/vir/Pr/Bib/VIS/vy/fle/ple/E; mid-word pieces like ub/ry/é/erv/v) — and it fires on that token even when the word happens to end there ('a sub sandwich', 'vice versa'), while single-token words containing the same stems (obedient, subordinate, submarine, operator, virus, surgery, Troy) stay near zero and the sequence-initial token (position 0) never fires. The peak does not depend on which continuation follows ('Sub' fires ≈9.4 in Sub ordinate, Sub marine and Sub alone), and zero-ablating the pole at a peak removes next-token probability from the word's continuation pieces ('erv' after 'subs', 'ordinate' after 'ub', 'iss' after 'Fle', 'gia' after 'ry'), so its job appears to be marking 'the word is not finished' to support spelling out the rest; pieces of non-English words (arbejde, fleste, plekje, Februar) fire the same way.

This pole fires on a token that continues or completes a locally opened construction: a formulaic bigram or collocation (import numpy, pleaded not, boils at), a subword completion (Se+ine, h+iked, hab+ite), or the expected next slot of a syntactic frame (For+i, If+x, at least+eight, stored+in), with strength scaling with how constrained the slot is; the same surface token outside such a continuation slot (sentence-initial The/Water/She, or quickly after import) stays near zero. It is retrospective: only the current and preceding ~1-2 tokens drive it, and edits after the peak leave the peak unchanged.

Fires retrospectively when the current token is, or sits inside, a non-first member or its separator (comma, or/and/to, determiner, noun fragment) of an explicit multi-item noun-phrase enumeration of items, rooms, names, or alternatives given earlier list members in context; it stays low on single unlisted nouns, first list members alone, or lone determiners without list context.

N3540- fires on the token that carries a learned Greco-Latin specialist term, most strongly biomedical/clinical vocabulary (pulmonary 6-9, cystic, acute, chronic, atherosclerotic, cardiopulmonary, gastric, metabolic, hepatic, splenic, cytokine, tachycardia, hypotension) and, when the tokenizer splits such a word, on the bound root or suffix fragment that carries it ('atic' in hepatic, 'enic' in splenic, 'ic' in cystic, 'monary' in cardiopulmonary, 'osis'/'itis'/'emic' pieces); the same word is about 40% stronger inside a biomedical passage than inside a software one (pulmonary 9.8 vs 6.9). It sits at its floor (usually under 0.4) on everyday English, on function words, on generic academic words (disease, tissue, treatment, study, patient), on plain anatomical vocabulary (heart, kidney, liver, lung, stomach) and on common medical words the model has seen everywhere (cardiac, renal, hepatitis, asthma, pneumonia, anemia), with the gradient running clinical technical >> other technical (chromatographic about 3.8) >> rare everyday nouns (quokka, axolotl about 1.3-1.8) >> ordinary English; zero-ablating its peaks leaves the next-token distribution essentially unchanged (KL 1e-4, no concentration on any token), so it is retrospective, and its positive pole is the opposite end of the same axis, peaking on formatting tokens (spaces, digits, slashes, '::') in license headers, URLs and code rather than on content words.

Retrospective detector for nominal/numeral phrase completion: it peaks on the head noun, proper-noun piece, compound/predicative adjective, or digit/space-before-digit that completes a determiner-, quantifier- or measure-headed entity, measure or time phrase (heavy rain, sea level, last year, the Moon, capital cities, not guilty, chemical energy, triangle inequality, 3.9 percent, 500 mg, from 9, galaxy 13, range(10), zeros((3)), plus the clause-final intransitive verb/adverb that closes a definite-subject clause (symphony began., so fast., bloomed again.); it stays quiet on bare lexical verbs with complements or continuations (fast as 'will fast strictly', began taking an infinitive, to forgive, verb-chain bubbles), on qualitative attributive adjectives in abstract non-measure NPs (religious reasons), on spelled-out number words (thirty, seven, five hundred), and on identifier-glued code numerals outside loop/shape/measure frames (timeout(30), weak ~0.8).

The negative pole detects legal/contractual 'fine print': clauses in agreements, licences, disclaimers, privacy notices, price/refund/tax terms and court filings that state binding obligations, entitlements, fees, liability or governing law (e.g. 'shall indemnify ... against all claims', 'refunds will be issued within thirty days', 'applicable taxes, duties and customs fees', 'waiver of the filing fee', 'this motion is granted'). Activation is graded - it ramps up across a clause as legal-register wording accumulates, is highest inside court filings and dense contract clauses, and stays near zero in narrative, news, business, medical, scientific or technical prose even when that prose is formal or jargon-heavy.

The pole fires on the token where the model retrieves a specific, low-frequency lexical item rather than composing generic text: the distinctive word of a multi-word proper name (the given name after a role or institution word - 'Mayor Michael', 'Senator Marco', 'Sen. Bernie', 'Federal Communications', 'Department of', 'Court of Appeals') or the opening piece of a rare technical, taxonomic or brand word ('glomeruli', 'monopotassium', 'Lamborghini', 'Opuntia'). It sits at the noise floor on generic prose and on the same words used generically ('He met Michael', 'consumer services', 'the cells', 'a car', 'the Federal Trade Commission'); within that class strength is graded by the network's own token preference, so some familiar names in the identical frame (e.g. 'John', 'Grace') fire only weakly.

The pole fires on the token that carries the internal marker of a written clock time: the single-letter meridiem token right after the hour (' a'/' A' of a.m., ' p'/' P' of p.m., as in '3 a.m.', '9:00 p.m.', '8 P.M.'), the ':' or '.' right after the hour number ('3:30', '16.00', '6.45 in the morning'), or the 'o' of "o'clock" (and, more weakly, the 'A' of a dotted era marker after a year, '476 A.D.'), when the preceding number is read as a time of day. It does not fire on a bare hour with no marker ('at 3 tomorrow'), on the merged 'am'/'pm'/'AM'/'PM' tokens, on a meridiem with no hour in front of it ('in the a.m.'), or on the same letters and separators where the number is a ratio, score, price or version ('3:1', '3.14 dollars', 'Version 2.0'), an item label ('item 3 a'), or an ordinary word ('parley', 'Barking', 'Epigraph').

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a locally (~5 preceding tokens) highly constrained construction — a matching HTML closing tag, a SQL clause keyword, a decimal-point/number format, or a frequent collocation or verb-preposition/noun-preposition pairing (e.g. triangle inequality, powerhouse of the cell, sat on, cups of); the same surface token without that constraining left context is predicted inactive.

L21/N4242+ is a retrospective detector of a specific family of Greco-Latin word stems, and it fires on the subword piece that carries the stem when Qwen's tokenizer has split the word: 'throm' in thrombosis (7.2), 'orph'/'morph' in morphological (9.9), 'otyp' in phenotypic (4.0), 'orph' in polymorphisms (6.6), 'phot' in photonic (8.7), ' hom' in homonym (10.4) and homologation (11.4), 'emp' in spatiotemporal (4.5). It stays at baseline on the same word written as one token (' morphology' 0.1, ' phenotype' -0.2, ' orientation' 0.6, ' vulnerability' 0.0, ' voltage' 0.5), on the pieces that follow the stem ('onym', 'osis', 'onic', 'ages' about 0) and on other split technical words that are not in the family ('polymer' -0.1, 'hydro' -0.3, 'capac' 0.3, 'hepat' -0.9), and for stems that also occur as whole words the model's own expectation that the word continues gates it ('The volt is the unit...' with P(next token is a word-piece) 0.73 fires at 12.1 while 'a nine volt battery' at 0.003 sits at -0.3; 'the path through...' 0.56 fires at 3.4 while 'the garden path...' 0.02 is 0.5).

This pole fires retrospectively on a token that fills the expected second slot of a frequent local syntactic frame set by the immediately preceding 1-2 tokens: a finite verb right after its nominal subject, a head noun after a determiner, modifier noun, or quantifier, a quantity word after a number or 'at least', a module/function/column name after its keyword, a subword completing a word, or clause punctuation after a complete phrase. Only breaking the local part-of-speech frame (wrong coarse category in the opener slot) silences it; swapping in a semantically bizarre but same-category filler (waffles/toaster/nonce words) leaves it active with graded strength, and high-baseline subword or function tokens can fire strongly even in gibberish left context, so global semantic plausibility does not gate it.

Fires on the attributive modifier, prefix or word-initial fragment that opens a multi-token noun phrase, compound or name, at the point where that phrase is clearly unfinished and its head is strongly predictable. Examples are ' Public' in 'Public Affairs', 'ile' in 'Fertile Crescent', ' semi' in 'semi-humid', ' powerful'/' essential' in 'a powerful/essential tool', ' equal' in 'equal opportunity', and 'iz' in 'Leibniz-IZW'. It stays near zero on the head noun that completes the phrase, on function words, and on the same content words when they are used as a head or predicate rather than as a modifier waiting for its head.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that continues an already-established technical-or-quantitative exposition: labor and economic statistics (unemployment figures, wages with a change predicate, interest rates), measurements with numbers plus units or percents (fell to 3.9, 7.8 tons, boils at 100 degrees, increased by 12 percent), code, SQL, API or formal-list vocabulary, and subword completions of rare domain terms or names; strength scales with how quantitative and technical the surrounding passage is. The same surface tokens (figures, was, are, commas, spaces, digits) stay weak-to-moderate in everyday narrative or everyday-object enumerations, and swapping technical content words for everyday ones collapses activation while synonym or digit-preserving edits change nothing. Acknowledged leftovers: short labor-statistic bigrams fire strongly without distant licensing, and the at-least/only/the function-word peaks plus the incoherent Jacobian promoted list with value-token suppression are not covered and may be a separate regime.

The pole marks a word-building fragment: it peaks on the leading piece of a long technical/Graeco-Latin word that Qwen's tokenizer splits into several tokens (' dermat'+'ology', ' therm'+'odynamics', ' cardi'+'ologist', ' electr'+'ify', ' pen'+'itenciário', ' democr'+'ático'), and the strength is carried by that fragment token itself - it barely changes with what completes it (dermatology, dermatologist and dermatitis all give ~10.9/12) and the completing pieces stay near 0. Everything the tokenizer keeps whole (psychology, voltage, thermometer, electromagnetic, and every ordinary word) and rare non-technical fragments (tungsten, obelisk, archipelago) stay below ~0.1 of max, and at the fragment the pole's write promotes the pieces that would finish the word (dermat->'ology'/'itis', magnet->'ometer'/'ism'/'ron', therm->'ite'/'os'), so it tracks an unfinished technical word being spelled out of pieces rather than a topic or a specific upcoming token; engagement is stem-specific (e.g. ' pharmac' and ' onc' are weak), so not every technical word engages it.

This negative pole is the tissue/lesion end of a cell-versus-tissue partition: it fires on the token that names a gross tissue, organ, specimen or tumour entity in biomedical prose (biopsy, marrow, spleen, pancreas, synovium, mucosa, tumour/carcinoma/glioma/sarcoma, craniectomy; peaks of 5-14, higher the more clinical the frame), and stays at or near zero on cell- and molecule-level nouns (cell, cells, gene, genome, chromosome, protein, enzyme, receptor, antibody) even inside the same pathology sentence. Its positive pole is the other end of that axis - it promotes 'cell', 'cells', 'division', 'dividing', '细胞', '分裂' and fires at 30+ on cell-division/proliferation statements - so the negative pole marks 'a tissue/lesion-level entity is being named here, not a dividing cell', and at its peaks it measurably pushes down the generic 'cell'/'cells' continuation.

Litigation-procedure neuron: once a court-case context is set up (case caption, opinion or filing naming parties such as the State, the defendant or an appellant), it fires on the token that opens or sets up a party-role or filing term. Examples: the 'Pl' piece of Plaintiff in a caption or at a paragraph start (~10-15), ' a' or ' "' after '[litigant] filed' before motion/notice (~7-10), a litigant subject like 'The State' or 'the Department' before filed/moved (~7-8), and APPELLANT'S before MOTION (~9). The same tokens without legal context, and ordinary legal prose away from such slots, stay weak (<~2). Leftovers it does not explain: German articles and negation after a verb (keine/eine, ~7) and Android XML 'android:layout' (~4-7).

The pole fires on the singular nouns that name an institution's own activities and the things it funds, teaches and delivers - research, training, teaching, learning, curriculum, course, service(s), programme/program, project, placement, study, survey, assessment, evaluation, screening, prevention, intervention, treatment, therapy, development, expansion, delivery, funding, grant, policy - and on the multi-word institutional names built out of them (Strategic Research Action Plan, Family Violence Prevention Services, Tobacco Regulatory Science Program, Office of Naval Research); each such noun carries roughly 1-4 by itself and the whole clause around it rises to 3-11 once several of them fill it, so sustained programme, prospectus, grant-call or service-description prose runs hot over whole clauses including the intervening function words. What changes from the administrative-register reading is that the trigger is this lexical class and not the text's administrative or public-service character: civic and procedural administration is now predicted inactive (minutes, tenders, contracts, invoices, budgets, ballots all measure 0-0.6), as are the generic umbrella nouns scheme, initiative, strategy, provision and management (0.2-1.0 even inside an institution frame), commercial and consumer copy, sport and recipe uses of the same words, financial reporting and narrative fiction (all 0-1.2), and a lone field noun dropped into otherwise unrelated prose reaches only about 1-2.8, below the 2.49 line; the 6-10 spikes on word-internal fragments of rare proper names (' N' in Nooksack, ' En' in Envisat, ' py' in pyrenaica) are a separate token-level effect, not this claim - the same fragment reaches only 2.2 in a stand-alone sentence and needs an already-hot encyclopaedic passage in front of it to reach 10.

The pole fires when the current token is the lexically informative content word that satisfies the syntactic slot set up by the preceding one to three tokens (head noun after a determiner or possessive, main verb after its subject noun or pronoun, copula after a complete subject, second half of a fixed collocation, or token closing a clause or code block), and stays low on function words that leave the phrase incomplete. It therefore predicts which occurrences of common tokens fire (e.g. the clause-boundary comma but not list commas, the copula after a full subject but not auxiliaries mid-phrase), which token identity alone cannot.

This pole fires on the token at which a locally stereotyped multi-token sequence is resolved by the preceding words: the onset or completion of a fixed collocation (triangle inequality, central bank), a number (the 0 in 1600, the 9 in 3.9), a morphological completion (pro-tons, re-election, can't, j'habite), or a formulaic frame (he after a quoted question, Once upon, Please remember, return a, ORDER BY name;). Firing strength scales with how strongly the preceding context constrains the sequence, so the same token fires weakly in an unconstrained context; words after the peak do not affect it.

This pole marks the cultural sector: it fires on words naming the institutions that produce and transmit culture - schools, colleges and universities, teachers; newspapers, magazines, journals and broadcasters; books and publishers; film, cinema, theatre and museums - while the same-sized, same-frequency institutions of other sectors (bank, hospital, army, factory, ministry, court) and concrete objects (building, road, window) leave it at zero in the identical frame. The drive is passage-level as well as lexical: the same word fires several times harder inside an arts/media/education passage than inside a finance or manufacturing one (identical sentence, 3.84 vs 0.95), and the neuron writes the culture concept forward (zero-ablating it removes 1-2.7 nats from 文化/'cultural'/'art' at every peak and the tokens it loses most are library, film, newspapers, Book), which is what the Jacobian lens is reading.

Retrospective particle-physics detector read out at the following low-content token: the pole peaks (2 to 8.5, against a scan maximum of 8.24) on a preposition, article, conjunction, comma or first fragment of an unfamiliar word when the word just before it names a subatomic particle or particle process ('in'/'the' after electrons, protons, neutrons, photons, quarks, gluons, mesons, kaons, bosons, hadrons, leptons, neutrinos, positrons, antiprotons, atoms; 'into' after annihilate; 'on' in 'based on cavity QED'), and it falls back to the floor when the particle word is instead followed by another content word, so 'The mesons in the box were counted' peaks at 6.4 while 'The mesons were counted in the box' peaks at 1.7. In the identical frame everyday, biological and clinical nouns leave it at the floor ('The cats / kidneys / cookies / onions / crayons in the box were counted', 0.2 to 0.6), clinical and abstract-mathematics words are actively suppressed ('coronary' -3.0, 'the' after 'eigenvalues' -2.3), and in addition a handful of rare name-like tokens carries a fixed positive response (' O' 5.6, ' U' 1.4, ' Ar' 3.1, ' Toyota' 3.1, 'silver' 1.8, ' classical', ' non', ' solar', ' optical'), which is why the fragment ' Ar' fires in 'Gregg Araki' (3.1) but the fragment 'Tan' does not fire in 'Gregg Tanaka' (0.0).

Retrospective: Qwen2.5-0.5B L22/N2281+ fires on a token that does not end its word - the next token continues the same orthographic word with no space - so its peaks land on the word-initial or word-medial BPE fragment of a long or rare word ('[[counter]]|int|uitive', 'electro|card|[[i]]|ogram', 'oph|[[thalm]]|oscope', 'gastro|[[enter]]|ology', 'Long|[[le]]|at', 'm’|[[app]]|elle', 'am|[[oxic]]|illin', 'pharmac|ological' peaking on 'pharmac'), and it falls back to the floor on that word's final fragment ('...|ogram', '...|ological', '...|oscope' all read 0.0) and on words the tokenizer keeps whole however rare they are ('notwithstanding' leaves the whole prompt at 0.25 and 'nevertheless' at 0.08), with ordinary prose usually at 0.15-0.4 against a 0.45 active threshold. It prepares no single upcoming token (Jacobian lens flat, kurtosis 3.3, promoted list '_BACKEND'/'=R'/'ruc' incoherent; zero-ablating the pole moves probability toward sibling word-internal fragments such as 'okin' after 'pharmac' and 'ogram' after 'echoc', KL 2e-5, far below the protocol's lookahead threshold), and which long technical words fire is only partly predicted - echocardio-, pharmaco-, gastroentero-, otorhinolaryngo-, cholecyst- and counter- words fire while spectro-, photo-, immuno-, histo- and arteriosclero- words of the same shape do not - that residue, and the fixed ~0.16 the pole reads on a document's first token, are left unexplained.

N2511+ fires on the token that sits inside a literal, format-determined string rather than a composed one: code formatting runs (' {\n', '{\r\n'), markup/URL syntax ('{ref-type=', 'xmlns:', '.com/en-us'), LaTeX or math fragments ('_n', '-P'), numeric/identifier literals introduced by a format label ('7' after 'ISBN:', '3' in 'sha384-'), escape runs ('\u0'), French elision clitics (' d'', 'qu'', 'l'') and memorised patent/legal formulas ('invention relates to', 'incorporated herein by reference', 'more particularly'), and it grows with the amount of such formatted context preceding it. The same tokens in composed prose stay near the floor (plain ' incorporated', 'xmlns', '-P', '/en', ' relates' and 'ref' all < 0.7), plain code without such a literal and Italian/German prose stay <= 1.7, and zero-ablating the pole at its peaks leaves next-token probabilities essentially unchanged (KL 3e-5 to 1e-3), so the pole is retrospective.

Retrospectively detects the current token completing the word interest in any sense and suppresses its logit signal; common tokens such as sentence-initial The produce only weak baseline activity around 0.46.

Fires on the words of a passage that names the medical treatments, procedures or devices given to a patient (lists of therapies, drugs, catheters and interventions). It peaks on the list connectors (',', ' and', ' of', ' using', ' with') and on the sub-word pieces of the treatment terms inside that span (e.g. 'drug therapy, insertion of an implantable', 'intr|avenous', 'permanent vascular access'). The same words in a non-medical frame (holiday options, a guest, a garden hose, a varnished table), or in a list of symptoms, stay weak or near zero. A smaller set of peaks comes from non-English or code sub-word fragments (' ten'|'aient', 'document'|'atie', ' m'|'uffs', 'navbar'), which are token-specific leftovers.

This pole fires retrospectively on the current token when it completes a locally stereotyped frame: a factual or measurement number ('1' in 'boils at 100'), a dosage link ('of' in '500 mg of'), a conditional clause boundary (',' after 'than five'), a code or technical idiom ('numpy' after 'import', 'i' after 'For'), or a fixed collocation ('triangle' in 'triangle inequality', the '11' slot after 'Apollo'); the same tokens outside such frames evoke little activity. Superimposed on this weak frame-gated field is an extreme frame-independent response selective for the subword token ' pro' as in 'protons' (~7, versus ~0 for other pro-words), in the same g+u+ regime as the weak peaks.

N2866+ is a retrospective detector that fires strongly on the first piece of a multi-token word (rem|ands, N|MDA, am|oxicillin, h|iked) only when the immediately preceding 2-6 token collocation frame licenses that specific word (affirms/vacates/and frames remands, influx/via frames NMDA, mg/of frames amoxicillin); the same slot completed by another word (reverses, remarks), the same frame with a different onset (biked), the fragment used as a unit, acronym, or code identifier (3 m, REM, mInput), and single-token words with no pending completion (humming as one token, dissolved ion, red ant) all stay weak, as does sub-threshold activity on frequent function words. Distant topic words beyond the local frame do not gate it: swapping far-away content (in-the-slices/after-the-trial, day/week, a biomedical vs legal preamble) leaves firing unchanged, so it reads a locally licensed word-onset state, not long-range commitment and not a specific upcoming token (Jacobian kurtosis 3.3, no coherent promoted set).

The pole fires on numerals that stand for a recorded or referenced value rather than a narrated count: the digits of identifier and citation strings (patent and application numbers, case citations such as '305 P.3d 420', DOIs, ISBNs, URL ids, volume:page ranges, timestamps) and of prices, dates, clock times, measurements and statistical figures stated in technical, legal, official or instructional prose, together with the fixed boilerplate that frames such documents ('incorporated herein by reference', licence and copyright notices). It stays below a quarter of peak in chat, fiction, dialogue, opinion, simple questions and personal anecdote whose only numerals are plain counts of things, and in any text with no numerals at all.

The pole fires on passages whose subject matter is the mind and the brain: the entities and claims of neuroscience and cognitive psychology (neurons, synapses, hippocampus, cortex, dopamine, memory, attention, perception, emotion, language, psychiatric and neurological disorder). Substantially weaker but still above threshold, it also rises on scholarly discourse about the arts and sciences (universities, departments, professors, disciplines, papers and citations), while matched passages about commerce, finance, law, engineering, machines, plants or everyday events - and the same words in a technical sense, such as a computer's memory or a company's working capital - stay below a quarter of peak. Because the receptive field is a whole phrase of roughly 20-40 tokens, the single highest token is usually a function word (of, the, in, and, or) or a sub-word piece inside such a passage rather than a fixed trigger word.

L22/N4106- is a computing/data-infrastructure term detector: activation is near zero on ordinary English prose but builds through passages that name computer hardware, network links and digital storage (Ethernet, USB, HDMI, SATA, WiFi, cable, wire, port, socket, plug, router, modem, motherboard, drive, RAID, filesystem, folder, file, database), peaking on the technical term itself or on the determiner/numeral/conjunction that introduces the next one (a, single, three, four, and), so the same function words fire inside a technical passage and stay silent in a garden, recipe or sports sentence with identical syntax. Non-English text and a few fixed specialised phrases (e.g. 'Police Act 1996', 'offensive tackle and guard') reach only about half the computing peaks, a weaker secondary offshoot rather than the main job.

The negative pole fires on the token that carries a rare, specific vocabulary item - a proper name (' Vin', ' Joseph', ' Lacock'), a technical term or acronym (' chelator', ' antagonist', ' CLIA'), or an exact alphanumeric value ('1080i25', '(1985)') - and not on ordinary words: the same sentence with a common word in that slot, or with the word lowercased, drops the peak by 2-7 activation units, and common-noun controls never fire. Its strength is also multiplied 3-6x when the term sits in technical/expository prose rather than plain narrative (the identical ' Lacock' peaks 4.45 after a technical sentence and 0.71 after a plain one, and less on a repeat mention), matching its up_proj half being driven negative by specialised vocabulary while its gate half opens on content-word positions; the positive pole is the mirror image, firing on ordinary content words in plain prose.

The pole is a retrospective word-assembly detector: it fires on a token that is one sub-word piece of a word the model must build from several pieces instead of retrieving it whole - the opening piece of a rare, technical, foreign or proper-name word (' fl' in flanked, ' cl' in clapped, ' h' in hedges, ' U' in Uley, 'p' in p70S6K), or an interior piece of such a word ('rop' in neutropenic, 'ap' in extrapulmonary, 'op' in bronchopulmonary). It is near zero on single-token words in ordinary prose and on pieces of common words (' blo' in bloomed, ' uns' in unsolved), and the same fragment fires several times harder inside a stretch of unfamiliar vocabulary - a list or table of contents of proper names ('England, Wales and Northern Ireland', '#### Uley') - than in plain prose; its few whole-word peaks (' deprived' in a deprivation index, 'last'/'before' in one dated news passage) are unexplained leftovers.

Retrospective, passage-level detector of practical consequence: the pole is active over prose that says what something does to people or to what they care about, either harming them (illness, injury, death, debt, hardship, contamination) or protecting them from harm (a filter, a vaccine, an alarm, a safety rule), and it peaks at 2.5-6 against a scan maximum of 5.5 inside the clause that states the consequence, on the token that introduces it (a modal or auxiliary such as 'can', 'may', 'would', 'is', a relative pronoun or conjunction such as 'who' or 'and', or the predicate itself such as 'fall') or on the harmed quantity itself ('kidney', 'deaths'). Prose that asserts no consequence for anyone - definitions, chemical or physical mechanism, plain description of a place, product or company results, and reports of routine meetings - stays near its floor of 0.6-1.8, and the same tokens ('can', 'is', 'and', 'who') sit well below it in those passages, so the pole is not a token detector (token identity explains only 20% of its variance).

The negative pole is a retrospective detector of unfamiliar, non-whole-word material: it fires on the token where the surrounding text has pulled the model out of ordinary English - a sub-word fragment or short word-initial fragment of a long, rare, technical, transliterated or foreign-language word (Dutch, Turkish, French, Japanese, Latin/Greek genus names, chemical names) that has to be assembled from pieces instead of retrieved as one familiar token. It is near zero on ordinary English words in ordinary prose, and the same token fires or not depending on the surrounding language (' transparent' = 4.3 after 'Het bestuur moet more' but 0.0 after 'The board must become more'), with a secondary peak on the first token of a document (1.5-5.3) and on a few English words that head proper-noun phrases (' Foreign', ' Public').

Sparse, retrospective detector of a recognised, low-frequency specialist item: it peaks on the token at which the model identifies a technical/scientific word, place or product name, or international instrument - usually mid-word ('bell|w|ether' 6-8, 'orth|ost|atic' 4, 'Haemophil|us' 5, 'Enceph|al|opathies' 4, 'Castel| Gand|olfo' 5, 'Silver| W|raith' 3, 'www|.w|3' 6) in any carrier sentence, and on the diagnostic word of a multi-word instrument ('17 regional seas conventions', 'this international agreement', 'North American Free Trade Agreement', 'the Nairobi Convention'). It is not a rarity, surprisal or word-shape detector: invented or merely unfamiliar words of the same shape ('Horgsworthy', 'plintholithic', 'pneumothorax', 'radiopharmaceutical'), ordinary multi-token words ('establishment', 'misunderstanding'), everyday proper names and foreign-language text stay at baseline, and the instrument words fire only when the passage has already named a real instrument ('regional' 3.5 after 'The Convention'/'treaty' vs 0.3 after 'The committee'; 'international' 8.9 under an 'Agreement' header vs 3.8 under 'Report'; 'Rotterdam Convention' 4.3 vs 'Navaro Convention' 2.0); low-strength function-word and digit peaks inside those same saturated passages are leftovers this claim does not cover.

This pole fires on text whose subject matter is computing and online services: passages about software interfaces and digital objects (menus, tabs, buttons, settings, accounts, passwords, logins, files, folders, downloads, uploads, links, web pages, app versions) or about Internet/IT topics (mail authentication, disk encryption, e-commerce checkout, on-line resource pages). It stays near zero on narrative prose, physical-action instructions and non-digital exposition (cooking, car repair, gardening, furniture assembly, law, medicine, history, music theory), even when those contain the same function words, connectives and imperative form.

The negative pole is a definite-article feature: it peaks on the token 'the' (' The'/'the') in running prose - roughly 5-9x stronger than 'a', 'that', 'this' or 'one' in the same left context - with its strength set by the preceding span (0 in some documents, up to 11 in content-dense particular-reference passages such as 'from the top of the tower at Pisa' or 'for the war'; it is not explained by the article's own probability, rho = -0.19, or by next-token entropy, rho = 0.04). It additionally fires on a small lexical set of word-initial sub-word tokens that begin long content words (' Her', ' Ple', ' Gre', ' Middle', ' clar', 'am'), which fire on token shape rather than meaning (' Her' scores identically in Herod and in Heron).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token delivers or terminates a conventionally constrained factual detail set up by the preceding 1-3 tokens: a fixed-phrase or collocation completion ('world' after 'Hello,', 'fell' after 'stock market', 'images' after 'captured'), a quantity with its unit or a digit inside a year/code dimension, a name/date/place specification ('Nairobi' in a capital list, 'March', 'sea level'), or the closing punctuation, bracket, or newline of a clause carrying such content. The same surface trigger token stays quiet when the licensing local pattern is absent: generic emotion words or pattern-breaking substitutes ('purple', 'tables', 'joy') in the identical slot collapse the peak.

This pole fires retrospectively on a token that completes a strongly associated local chunk with its immediate left context: an elided pronoun plus ap-initial verb in French (m'/t' + 'app/ap), the second half of an idiomatic English bigram (cat sat, triangle inequality, stock market, cold wind, capital of), or a word-internal completion (ochond, akespeare). Breaking the left half of the chunk (dog sat, cat ran, circle inequality, English translation of m'appelle) silences it, while changing distant or following tokens (Lyon/Paris, inequality/factory) leaves the peak unchanged.

The negative pole fires on the last token of a bracketed insertion - the token immediately followed by the closing ')', ']' or '}' - when an earlier bracketed insertion in the same passage was closed and followed by a comma, i.e. when the insertion is a non-first item of a comma-separated series of parentheticals (the '2' of 'Alpha (1), Beta (2), Gamma (3)'; the '6' of 'Items [4], [5], [6]'). It is inactive on a lone parenthetical in ordinary prose, on the first insertion of a series, on an insertion introduced by 'and' rather than a comma, and on plain text containing no bracketed insertion.

The pole fires on descriptions of strategic competitive interaction between market agents: rival firms entering, undercutting, or waging price wars, and game-theoretic agents bidding, cooperating, or defecting (auctions, Nash equilibrium, repeated games), accumulated over roughly the preceding clause. Activation scales with the density of market-competition vocabulary, so a dense list of economic nouns partly drives it, while an isolated price report, a regulatory prohibition, or a single price mention buried in non-market narrative stays quiet.

Fires retrospectively on a word-initial fragment such as hab, Se, st or sh only when the completed word is used to refer to a concrete physical entity, named place, or dwelling action (habitation, Seine, stegosaurus, shillelagh); the same onset completing to an abstract process, condition, event or authorization term (habilitation, Session, sterilization, scleroderma, shortfall) leaves it near its weak baseline. Its negative-pole output direction coherently promotes the spatial tokens front and behind (Jacobian kurtosis 7.7, full lens overlap), consistent with priming spatial relations after a concrete-entity mention.

L23/N1769+ is a retrospective 'Java-family member declaration' unit: in Java, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, Scala and Java-style C# source it peaks on the token that opens a declared member - a field modifier (private, public, static, final), a method or constructor name just before its '(', a ':' or '->' introducing a type, a ',' or '<' inside a capitalised parameter or generic list, or the indentation that begins the next member or statement line - and its write suppresses the built-in type tokens it expects ('String', 'Math'). Activation is primed by the members already written in the window, so the first field of a class body scores 3-6, the second and later members 8-10, and full Java/Kotlin/Swift class bodies reach 8-17; sparse Java-shaped code still fires at 3-6 (a Rust struct/impl, a C# class written with lowercase 'string', a Java method body containing a for loop and println calls, a JavaScript function of arithmetic assignments, the same class written with lowercase types), while Go, C, C++, PHP, Ruby, Python, TypeScript classes and interfaces, plain JavaScript without a Math call, SQL, shell, HTML, JSON, YAML and prose stay at or below about 2.5.

The pole spikes on the single token immediately preceding a year-unit noun (year, years, -years) -- e.g. ' light' in 'billion light-years', ' the' in 'the year', ' next'/' last' in 'next/last year' -- with strong peaks (>20% of its max) only in that position and a weak generic-determiner baseline (~5-10% of max) elsewhere; its output direction strongly suppresses all year-variant logits, so it fires to damp the imminent year/years token.

Fires on the first subword fragment of a word the tokenizer splits into several pieces, at the fragment itself, before the rest of the word is seen. It is strongest for a small set of word-start prefixes (' Sch' as in Schenectady, ' Ab' as in Abi/Abilene, ' imm' as in imm|édiate, '.b' as in www.bbc, '-m' as in -missile, ' Fox', ' Greg', ' unf'). It is near zero when the same word is a single whole token (' immediately', ' Albany', ' Schmidt', ' Boston') and on most other fragments (' P' in Poughkeepsie, ' Y' in Ypsilanti).

This pole fires on the canonical, highly predictable word filling an open slot: interrogative 'you' after 'Have/Did' (strongest, 14.0/6.5), BOS pronouns like 'I' (1.88), 'never' after 'I/will' (0.8-1.4), and collocational continuations ('boils' after 'Water', 'on' after 'sat', 'golden' after 'until', '9' after 'from', 'If' sentence-initially). Its output subtracts logit mass from 'ever'/'never' variants, suppressing them as next-token candidates; zero-ablating it at 'Have you' raises P(' ever') from 0.72 to 0.995 (KL 0.92).

Fires retrospectively when the current token is strongly licensed as the onset of a unit by its left-hand frame: a sentence-initial animate-pronoun subject or code/document keyword, a quantity or time slot after a reporting or measure phrase, or the first piece of a fixed term or formula. Peak strength scales with how constraining the frame is, so the same token fires weakly or not at all in a weak frame; it does not prepare any specific upcoming token (Jacobian/logit lenses agree, kurtosis ~3.4, promoted list is incoherent rare tokens) and its output direction instead suppresses frequent format tokens.

Fires on a short non-word fragment token, usually one containing h/H/sh or the piece 'unt', that opens or interrupts a common word split into unusual subword pieces, so the word is left unfinished and its completion is strongly determined (Stone|h|enge, Aft|ersh|ock, "|h|undreds, four| H|DMIs, | CH|B, | unt|reatable/oward/amed, fo|resh|adow, | Sh|rink, | wh|istfully). It stays near zero on whole-word tokens, on the completion pieces themselves, on ordinary single-token words containing h, and on name or foreign-word fragments such as Ash-, Kh-, Bh-, Ch-, Hy-.

The pole is a retrospective word-piece (spelling-fragment) detector: it fires when the current token is one of a small family of short subword fragments - the two-letter onsets ' ch', ' st', ' Ch', ' St', ' sh', ' ph' and mid-word pieces such as 'ph' in triphosphatase - i.e. a piece the tokenizer has split out of a longer word rather than a complete word. In a fixed carrier the fragment token alone sets the strength (' ch' 7.2 > ' st' 4.4 > ' sh' 2.0 > ' ph' 1.3 > ' pl' 0.8 > ' br' 0.6, identical across chisel/chive/chasm/chaff), and the pole stays at its floor on words held in one token (cheese, church, station, strong, photon, stanza, child), on longer fused pieces carrying the same letters (' perm' in permanganate, ' Neb' in Nebuchadnezzar, ' chlor', ' chem', ' Chunk' in getChunk), and on function words and punctuation.

Fires wherever the love concept is carrying the residual stream - the word love/loved/loves/loving, a cross-lingual or near-synonym equivalent (爱, 愛, 사랑, amour, 爱情, 喜欢, affection, hates, adore) - so its peaks land on the function word that continues the love phrase (' and' immediately after love, or further on the clause-opening 'I', 'would', 'do', 'people', 'much', 'a' or a comma) while the love token itself sits at about zero, and the peak grows with how much love-talk the passage carries ('Her love and devotion' peaks at 7.9 on ' and' where 'Her kindness and devotion' peaks at 1.9). Its key and value are anti-parallel: it is the most love-aligned input row in the layer (rank 1 of 4864 for ' love' in both gate_proj and up_proj, with 爱/ love/love/愛/loved/loves/Love/LOVE/loving/affection/hates as the top embedding projections) and it writes minus-love, so it removes love/Love/LOVE/loved/loves/loving/lover/lovers/爱/愛/爱情/热爱/喜爱/喜欢/爱你/사랑/amour from the next-token distribution at four times the magnitude of anything it promotes (a flat set of rare tokens) and steers the model's 'I ___' slot towards have/'m/'ve/like/think; it also rises where love is the model's own leading next-token candidate (mean p(' love') 0.091 at its >=0.25-max peaks versus 0.0002 at activation-matched controls with the same peak token, median rank 3 versus 331), which is the same love-in-the-residual quantity rather than any promotion of love.

Fires on a content token (verb, quantifier, noun, or subword completing a content word) when it is the grammatically and semantically congruent continuation of the whole multi-token clause prefix; replacing a distant subject/topic word with an incongruous one collapses activation even when the immediately preceding 1-2 tokens are identical, while changing only the following token leaves it unchanged.

Fires on an opening or boundary token after which a fresh word will start with no leading space: strongest (10-12) when such a non-word token is the very first token of the text ('[', '
', '

', '---
', '{
', '"'), and moderately (3-10) mid-text on a line or paragraph break that ends a title, question or label (':

', '?

', '.
') or on an opening ' (' / ' [' / ' "' that starts a parenthetical or quote. It is near zero on word tokens, including a first token that is a word ('The', 'So'), and on any token followed by a space-prefixed word (e.g. ',' or ' ' in place of the break). Its output promotes spaceless word-start fragments ('sc', 'sm', 'g', 'gl') as a broad class, not specific tokens.

Fires at a position where the model is partway into a proper name or word and must continue it with the next token, strongest (about 0.4 to 1.0 of max) when the continuation is a TV/radio broadcaster name, Japanese or US networks above all. Examples are ' T' before 'BS' in 'Fuji Television and TBS', 'テレビ' before 朝日/東京, '（' before テレビ in Japanese programme credits, ' and' in 'NBC, CBS, and' and ' i' in 'BBC iPlayer'. It is also strong on a lone word-initial letter piece of a tokenizer-split word, mostly p/P/T ('H+-p|umps', ' P|uts', ' p|acted', ' p|21'); complete words, standalone letters ('p < 0.05'), most other initial letters ('b|umps', ' H|ikes') and lists of non-broadcaster companies stay near zero.

The pole fires on tokens that belong to source code rather than natural language: components of whitespace-free identifier, path, URL and markup-name runs - '/db' in django/db/__init__.py, 'js' and '/ajax' in js/ajax/addQuiz.php, ' android' in android:textColor, 'id' in @+id/imageView4, 'load' in luaotfload, 'nonatomic' in @property (nonatomic,) - with strength rising with the length and separator density of the enclosing run (10-34 for long runs containing / _ : = -, mostly under 2 for short or standalone ones). It is near zero on natural-language words even inside the same file (comments, string literals, HTML body text), on separator-only tokens such as '="', '/', ':', ';' and on the same words written out as prose, and its output only weakly promotes generic code continuations (':text', '/image', '/button', '>\n') rather than one specific next token, so the mechanism is retrospective.

Retrospective detector for being mid-way through spelling an infrequent word or fixed phrase (technical, foreign, proper-noun, or symbolic such as Category:M or snake_case codes): it fires on a non-final subword piece (onset or middle) that must fuse with following subwords to complete the word, with strength graded by rarity and boosted by technical context; it stays near zero on word-final or standalone tokens, on pieces of common words, and on the same letters when they form a complete common word.

At the first position of the input this pole is a graded opener detector: code openers (class/import/def) drive 7-9.5, connective or article openers (The/But/Because/Sh) drive 1-3, and pronouns, question words and most other openers drive ~0, while the same tokens placed mid-sentence in plain English prose evoke ~0. Within quoted dialogue and French spans it instead stays active across many tokens and spikes on straight-punctuation-adjacent fragments: the elided pronoun in j'habite (9.7, versus 3.3 for unelided il and 0 for the same elision in an English frame), the auxiliary did after she inside quotes (2.4), and mid-word pieces such as ochond in Mitochondria; its output direction promotes ASCII structural tokens and strongly suppresses curly-quote tokens, consistent with marking spans where straight-ASCII punctuation applies.

The negative pole fires on the token where the context makes a constraint/restriction word the likely continuation (e.g. ' budget'→' constraints', ' impose a'→' barrier/limit', 'self-im|posed', ' keep her mouth'→' shut', ' locked and the windows'→' locked'); restriction vocabulary that does not set up such a continuation (' not allowed to', ' reveals a fundamental') leaves it silent. Its output suppresses ' constraint(s)'/' restrictions' logits (Jacobian lens, kurtosis 9.2), so it acts as a final-layer suppression/calibration neuron for constraint words; zero-ablation moves KL 0.037 but not concentrated on specific tokens, hence claimed retrospective.

This negative pole fires retrospectively on social-media/chat-domain tokens (chat, tweet/tweets, Facebook, Twitter): a lone 'chat' already drives strength ~2.3 and stacks ('chat chat chat', 'Facebook Twitter tweets') drive it to 7-10, far above the scan max of 1.57, so the scan corpus, which contains no social tokens, caught only weak baseline flickers. Its output direction strongly suppresses exactly those trigger tokens (Jacobian and logit lenses agree at overlap 1.0, kurtosis 5.1, suppressed z ~ -9 to -11), i.e. a suppression neuron that detects chat-domain tokens, with a 1-3-token lingering tail, and damps them.

Fires retrospectively on text whose vocabulary is about plants in the garden/botany/produce sense: the peak lands on the tokens of plant-cultivation words and their immediate neighbours (' shr' in 'dwarf shrub tundra' or 'weeding the shrubs', ' tub' in 'potato tubers', ' vegetable' in 'vegetable beds', 'alled' of 'walled garden', 'eding' of 'weeding', ' watered', ' pot' of 'potting shed', the token after 'the seeds of'), growing with how much of the passage is cultivation content, while the same neuron's positive pole promotes and this negative pole's output writes out that garden token family (' garden', ' vegetable', 'leaf', ' planting'; suppressed z = -10.6, kurtosis 7.3) - a Voita-style suppression write, not lookahead, since the promoted side is incoherent noise. It stays inactive (peak below ~3 on this pole's 12.1 scale) on non-botanical senses of the same word forms (decision tree, chemical plant, random seed, seed capital, family tree, square root, table leaf, dog bark, Garden of Eden), on plant-free registers (steppe/glacier terrain, farm work, legal, politics, arithmetic, non-English garden text), and on lone commercial mentions ('vegetable boxes for market', 0.18 of scale).

The pole fires on the final word of a fixed English collocation in news, encyclopedic or everyday prose, where the preceding word or two almost determine it (e.g. 'percent' after 'fell to 3.9', 'fast' after 'went by so', 'silent' after 'the hall fell', 'charges' after 'pleaded not guilty to all', 'away' after 'light-years'). It is near zero on the same position when the collocation is broken ('3.9 points', 'went by so slowly', 'fell asleep'), on the auxiliary 'to' of 'going to', on rare technical or derivational fragments, and on non-English or code text.

L3/N1429- is a token-level template matcher: it fires at the FINAL token of a small set of learned, low-frequency token templates (2-4 BPE tokens long) - technical identifier/API suffixes (',C URLOPT', '.find DOMNode', 'XML StreamReader', '* Factory', 'run_from _argv'), product/font names ('ES Xi', 'Solid Works', 'Semi Bold'), formal labels/names ('About the Publisher', 'World Economic History Congress', 'Hildebrant, Esq.', 'Israeli-Pale stinian', 'Jay anth') and fixed discourse phrases ('That, my', 'Hence, my') - and strength is graded by how much of the template prefix is present (VMware ESXi 2.31 vs ESXi 0.97; About the Publisher 1.34 vs the Publisher 0.04; Using SolidWorks 1.17 vs Using COSMOSWorks 0.12). It is a token-sequence match, not a word, compound, register or memorised-collocation detector: no token fires alone (all 151,936 single-token inputs <= 0.05); high-frequency collocations stay at baseline (New York, United States, Taylor Swift, Microsoft Windows, Joe Biden all <= 0.12); the same word in ordinary running prose stays at baseline (publisher, congress, search, works); the same surface words fail when the context tokenizes them differently (Bernie Sanders reaches 0.87 as Bern+ie+ĠSanders but 0.49-0.54 as ĠBernie+ĠSanders and 0.29 in prose); and changing one template token abolishes it (About the Publisher 1.34 vs About the Editor 0.04; World Economic History Congress 1.15 vs ...Conference 0.05).

This pole fires when the current token extends or completes a familiar, tightly constraining local frame: the canonical tail of a frozen chunk (as after import numpy, time after once upon a, brown after golden), a subword completion (tons, ochond), or a verb after a pronoun subject. The identical token in an open-ended frame fires weakly or not at all (as after known widely, opened after Bob), so same-token strength varies with context and a pure unigram account fails.

The pole encodes the printing concept: it fires on any token whose contextual meaning names a printer or the act/result of printing, in any language or script, including the token that completes such a word across a boundary - English print/prints/printed/printer/printing/printout/printable/print head, Spanish impresora/imprimir/imprima, French imprimante, Portuguese impressora, Italian stampante, German Drucker, Japanese プリンタ, and typesetting terms such as PostScript, pdflatex, PDF and ink-jet. It stays near zero on words that merely contain the letters (sprint, sprinter, fingerprint, blueprint, Nakajima), on authoring/publishing vocabulary (write, publish, newspaper, typewriter), and on the lexicalised 'fine print' / 'out of print' idioms, so it predicts activity from what a token means in context, not from its spelling or identity alone.

The pole detects a locative/state predication headed by a preposition or copula: it fires on ' in'/' at'/' on'/' to be' when that word heads a small-clause complement whose subject is the preceding reflexive pronoun ('find/consider/catch/imagine/place/put oneself in X', 'consider oneself to be X'), on that reflexive pronoun itself, and more weakly (1-3.5) on the preposition of the reduced passive 'X is located/situated/positioned in/at Y'. It is a construction detector, not a token detector: ' herself' fires after 'found' (5.5) but not after 'hurt' (0.0), and ' in' fires after 'found herself' (6.4) but not after 'found the dog' (0.4) or after an event-locative adjunct ('hurt herself in the kitchen', 0.1); a weak separate tail fires on digit continuations of alphanumeric tokens ('P4'+'5', 'sha3'+'8', ~2.0).

This pole fires (weakly, max ~0.9, dial-like smooth histogram) when the current token is the locally predictable completion of the preceding one or two tokens: the second half of a frequent bigram or collocation (far->away, greater->than, ruled->that), a list/code continuation (Tokyo,->Berlin; (3->,), or a subword finishing a common word (h->iked, am->oxic, Se->ine, j'->hab). The identical token in an unpredictable local context evokes little or no activation, so local bigram predictability predicts firing better than the unigram trigger tokens (on, by, 0, comma, of, at) alone.
