Active in running prose about computer programs and their construction - source code, builds, executables, scripts, installers, versions and releases, debugging, and the people and processes around them - and near zero in everyday prose and in non-computing technical prose (medicine, law, physics), with computer-hardware prose transferring only weakly. The peak lands on the software-specific content words of such a passage, even on word-internal pieces (e.g. 'ini' in 'Rubinius', 'asma' in 'Plasma'), so a token fires only when the preceding context has established the software register; most other computing vocabulary (compiler, library, syntax, function, module, server) gives nothing, which marks this as register-driven rather than a plain technical-term detector.

The pole is a gastroenterology feature: it fires when the current token carries clinical content of the gastrointestinal tract and abdominal cavity in medical prose — bowel/intestine/colonic/rectal/peritoneal/retroperitoneal/abdominal/biliary anatomy, GI procedures and investigations (stent, colonoscopy, colectomy, ileostomy, biopsies, stricture, abdominal imaging) and GI pathology (diverticulitis, malabsorption, polyps, diarrhoea, abdominal cramping). Everyday health words, other organ systems (kidney, liver, heart, lung function), lay non-GI symptom talk and non-medical technical jargon leave it near zero, with only a weak (~0.2 of peak) tail on other specialist clinical terms such as imaging or device vocabulary; its negative pole is the complementary stomach/acid-reflux complaint cluster (heartburn, reflux, peptic ulcer), whose tokens the positive pole's output suppresses.

This pole fires on colloquial, online/spoken-register English: internet-slang and meme vocabulary (derp, snark, facepalm, noob, epic fail, meme, shitpost, lol, ugh, meh, lowkey, cringe, dope), internet-culture names (xkcd, Tumblr, 4chan, Homestuck, Boing Boing, Pastafarian, Rainbow Dash) and conversational fillers and hedges (basically, kinda, pretty much, literally, thing, such, whatever, just), while it is near-silent on formal edited prose and on ordinary standard words of similar meaning (bad, rough, cool, party, event, Facebook, embarrassing), so swapping a slang word for its formal synonym is predicted to switch it off. Its peaks land mid-word on the register-carrying word itself (e.g. 'ark' in snark) with nothing unusual following, and its output weights promote the same register (shit, fuck, badass, -ish, bullshit, derp, Tumblr), so it is a style detector, not a next-token predictor.

The negative pole is the model's Olympic Games feature: it fires on text about the Olympics and Olympic-style multi-sport games — summer and winter editions, regional, continental, Paralympic and youth Games — and on the apparatus vocabulary of those events, which raises it even outside an Olympic frame: host city, venues, athletes' village, opening and closing ceremony, torch relay, flame, cauldron, Olympic rings, medal ceremony, athletes parading under national banners, and 'every four years'. It stays near zero on sport as ordinary play (a league match report, a training run, a round of golf), on sport equipment and recreation, and on the same words in plainly non-sport senses ('he took a torch from the shelf', 'she wore two gold rings', 'the children played games', 'the graduation ceremony').

Fires retrospectively when the token ' he' functions as the Spanish first-person singular auxiliary of haber in a present-perfect construction (preceded by items like 'me' or 'no' and followed by a past participle), not when 'he' is the English masculine pronoun or a subword fragment.

This pole fires on explicit present-tense performative speech-act constructions: a first-person (I/we) or formal institutional subject (archives, permission, licensees, a pleased host) directly governing a recommending, requesting, granting, confirming, presenting, or appreciating verb (recommend, suggest, request, insist, confirm, grant, appreciate, present, hereby), typically peaking on the verb or on the following you/that complement. It does not fire on the same syntax with a belief- or observation-report verb (suspect, watch, track, print), nor on the same directive meaning expressed without a performative verb (you should...).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes the name of an organized sports league or competition (League/Liga, Association, Conference, NFL) or a top-tier professional-sports marker (professional, Pro/pro, premier, Major) inside a passage about competitive sports; the same surface words in non-sports contexts (estate agent, nations summit, software, website, hotels) do not activate it.

Retrospective detector that fires when the current token asserts a binary pairing, mirror-image, equivalence, or opposition relation between two items or claims (opposite ends/sides, counterparts, equivalents, mirror/mirroring, duality-double as in double-stranded/double-edged, or discourse inversion such as conversely, vice versa, on the contrary); quantity senses of double and other non-relational words stay near floor.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that continues or completes a conventionalized expression: the predictable second half of a fixed phrase (surface antigen, crime scene, with one hand, actin-positive) or the predictable middle piece of a rare long word (bios-urf-actant, ext-ens-ibility, sc-abb-ard). Strength is graded by how strongly the preceding one or two content words predict it, and the same token after an unpredictable lead-in (notion, rumor, idea, happy) stays near silent.

N7639+ is a sparse retrospective detector of a lexical unit under construction: it peaks at a token when the model is part-way through assembling a multi-token word or compound term, i.e. on the opening or interior piece of a long, usually technical or foreign word that the tokenizer splits (e.g. 'pale-' in paleontology, 'archae-' in archaeology, 'neuro-' in neurosurgery/neurology, 'alb-' in albendazole, 'oped' in orthopedics, 'mult-' in multicolored, 'astr-' in astronomical, 'sub-' in subvalvular, 'uff' in Muffins, 'at' in ratatouille, 'ob-' in obelisk), and on an attributive modifier that heads a compound, product or name term (e.g. 'high' in 'high heels', 'threaded' in 'threaded holes', 'soft' in 'soft drinks', 'Blue' in 'Blue Duiker', 'white' in 'a white patio dining set'). It is near zero on self-contained content words that finish a phrase in ordinary prose ('the cat sat on the mat', 'the price is high', 'the tower is a high building', 'he studies biology'), and the same modifier word fires much more weakly when it is predicative or phrase-final ('the dress in the window was white' vs 'a white dress').

Fires retrospectively on mentions of domestic companion animals, especially dogs, and close-companion bonds: animal nouns (dog, puppy, pet, stray animal, mane, Scooby), animal-associated behaviors (howling, fetch, trained), and companion terms (best friend, bezzie mate) when they frame a loyal human-animal-style companionship.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a highly predictable multi-token chunk: the second half of a fixed collocation or binomial frame (e.g. 'blessing and a [curse]', 'a kind of', 'one of them') or of a compound code identifier (e.g. 'Npgsql DataAdapter', 'add _library'), where the preceding one or two tokens strongly constrain the peak token. Replacing the predictive prefix while keeping the peak token identical collapses activation, so it tracks completion-given-context rather than the peak token's identity; the Jacobian lens is incoherent (kurtosis 3.3) and promoted arrow tokens never match the actual continuations ('curse', 'military', 'wheels'), ruling out lookahead.

Retrospective 'specialist designator' detector: over ordinary prose the pole sits at the floor (corpus mean 0.04, 0.2% of tokens above 0.5), and it fires (0.5-4.4) on tokens inside a specific, lexicalised designator - a technical term or acronym, a product/organisation/proper name, an identifier or unit ('uninterruptible power supply'/'UPS' 4.4, 'electricity supply' 1.8, 'boil water advisory' 3.9, 'Runtimes' 3.0, 'resourceGroupName' 1.3, 'International Development Agency' 1.6, 'Distinguished Flying Cross' 1.1) - with the excitation spread over the term's tokens, peaking on its most distinctive one, and amplified by the 30-100 tokens of specialist context that precede it (the docker 'Runtimes' peak measures 3.0 after 100 tokens of the daemon dump but 0.07 standing alone). Generic compositional description stays below 0.3 even when technical (chemical reactor 0.0, cooling system, irrigation canal, voltage regulators, accounting department), and everyday narration and dialogue stay at the floor, so the same surface word fires only when its span is such a designator ('water' fires at 3.9 inside 'boil water advisory' while the whole 'water supply' sentence peaks at 0.2; 'power' 4.4 in 'power supply' but 0.07 in 'restored power to the region').

The pole fires on the cue that turns a category, quantity or label already read into one of its specific instances or names: the appositive introducers ', including', ', such as', ', especially', ', particularly', ', specifically' and ', notably' when they follow a plural or quantified noun phrase, and the name-introducing frames of technical text ('a NOUN named/called Y', 'No module named X', path and identifier separators such as 'C:\...\Name', '@drawable/name', "selector 'name:'", '{StaticResource Name}'). It stays near zero when the same surface word carries no instantiation ('specifically'/'especially' as plain adverbs, 'named' as a verb, comparative 'like', clause-initial 'including', a colon inside a URL) and drops about sixfold when the preceding noun is a single already-specific referent ('that topic, including' 0.31 vs 'many topics, including' 1.86), so it tracks the construction rather than the tokens themselves.

Fires on words that name a habitual doubting, disbelieving or irreligious stance — skeptic/skeptical, atheist, agnostic, cynic, doubter, unbeliever — peaking on the stance noun or adjective itself, whether applied to a person or a thing. It does not fire on belief-side or neutral identities (believer, Catholic, student, artist), on generic uncertainty verbs/adjectives (questioned, doubtful), or on surrounding science/medicine/history content.

Fires retrospectively when text reports that an agent (I, we, a court, board, or authors) has reached a decision or committed judgment, typically via past-tense decided/determined/chose/concluded/felt/thought or the passive decision was made, followed by a to-infinitive or that/with complement stating the decided content.

This pole detects tokens that name language itself - a unit or property of verbal and written language - peaking at 2-4 of its 3.95 maximum on text, word(s), phrase(s), sentence, letter(s), character(s), alphabet, spelling, grammar, syntax, punctuation, comma, brackets, hyphen, quotation, vocabulary, syllable, vowel, plural and clause, on the token itself in any context (plain prose, CSS 'text-align', HTML 'text=', JS 'text:'). It reads zero on tokens naming non-linguistic content (image, picture, video, sound, song, portrait), on written works and documents (book, page, story, document, manuscript, transcript) and on unrelated code tokens (json, array, class, compiler, css), while naming/meaning words (name, value, format, term, meaning, title, font, digits) sit at partial, context-dependent strength; its output direction promotes the same language-form vocabulary (Unicode, grammar, letters, markup, alphabet, spelling, phrases, notation) and suppresses 3D-graphics/gaming tokens (GPU, Unity, Oculus, VR, AMD).

This layer-0 pole is a high-frequency-token detector: it fires on the current token with strength graded by that token's unigram frequency, strongest on ubiquitous glue punctuation (' (', '-', ','), moderate on frequent function words (' the', ' and', ' to', ' in', ' of'), and near zero on content words and rare fragments; it never fires on the first token of a prompt.

Retrospective unigram detector for consumer-lifestyle web vocabulary: beauty and personal-care terms, price and money-transaction terms, luxury and status-display terms, home-state adjectives, and body/health and celebrity-gossip terms. It fires on the matching token itself with little dependence on surrounding context, and stays quiet on matched generic, literary, or technical vocabulary.

This layer-0 pole is a token-identity detector for the unspaced (no-leading-space) BPE token of frequent English grammatical and discourse words — determiners, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliaries, degree words, clause adverbs and conversational openers such as the, and, with, of, to, this, that, which, you, it, a, in, was, more, such, unless, whereas, despite, whose, might, upon, perhaps, actually, please. That unspaced form is what GPT-2's tokeniser produces when a word is glued to preceding punctuation (an opening parenthesis, quote, em dash, hyphen, slash, underscore or bracket, or a line start) rather than following a space, so its peaks are the first word inside a parenthetical or quotation — 'files (the "Software")', '(with a count)', '(and you)', 'models (which differ)' — and it fires on the token wherever it occurs, including as the first piece of 'theoretical' ('the') or 'however' ('how'). It is inactive on the space-prefixed token of the same word (' the', ' with', ' and' = 0.00) and on the title-case token ('The', 'And', 'With' = 0.00), stays silent on punctuation and digits, and grades with frequency and grammaticality among unspaced words: unspaced function words reach 1.5-3.4 while unspaced content words are weak (water, code, game, table = 0.00; 'people' = 1.26).

This layer-0 pole is a token-identity detector for the Greco-Roman classical and Greco-Latin learned lexicon: it fires on the token currently being read when that token is ' Greek'/'Greece', a Greek-alphabet letter, a classical Greek or Roman name or antiquity (Achilles, Odysseus, Plato, Caesar, legion, gladiator, Rome, Carthage), or a Latin/Greek word-part inside such vocabulary ('us' as in vagus/nucleus/mucus, 'itus' as in emeritus/mellitus, and 'orth-', 'cran-', 'path-', '-onic', '-acter', 'parap-'). It stays at or below baseline on ordinary English words that merely contain the same letter strings (bus, bonus, status, north, iconic, character), on modern Latinate vocabulary (history, democracy, biology, school) and on non-classical ancient cultures (Hindu, Buddhist, Sanskrit, Egyptian), so the trigger is the token's Greco-Latin classical identity rather than its spelling or the surrounding context.

A layer-0 token detector that fires on the token itself, almost independent of context, for the written-out singular street/thoroughfare nouns ' Street' (strongest, ~0.9-1.0 of max with a capitalised space-prefixed form, ~0.6 for lowercase ' street'), ' Drive', ' Court'/'court' (any sense: law court, tennis court, backcourt, the verb 'court'), ' Road'/' road', ' Avenue', ' Boulevard', ' Highway' and 'field'/' field' (~0.45-0.85 of max), with weaker activity on ' Lane', ' Blvd', ' Rd', ' Ave', plurals like ' fields'/' roads'/' courts' and ' file' (~0.3-0.5). It stays at ~0 on every other token (no floor: first tokens and ordinary text read ~0), including other place nouns such as ' Square', ' Place', ' Bridge', ' Park', ' yard', ' river', ' Council', the abbreviation ' St', ' Way', 'streetcar' and 'Streets'.

Fires when the current token is the subword fragment spelling the /ik/ velar coda ('ic' and its case and tokenization variants 'IC', 'ich', 'ico', 'ici', 'ik'), i.e. a token-level detector for the letters i followed by c/k, independent of the word's meaning or surrounding context.

Fires when the current token contains a dollar-sign character ($), whether as a standalone price marker before a number ($50, $294,990) or as the leading character of a code or shell token ($array, $scope, $which), regardless of the surrounding words; replacing the $ with another symbol or removing it collapses activation while changing nearby non-$ words does not.

The pole is a layer-0 token-identity dial: it fires on the current token whenever that token is one of a fixed, broad set of GPT-2 token types whose embeddings share one direction — news/politics/military and press vocabulary (' Pentagon', ' Police', ' Press', ' News', ' Military', ' Putin', ' ISIS', ' Islam'), code identifiers ('filename', 'Cache', 'Check', 'Request', 'load'), capitalised names (' Cheney', ' Wenger', ' Gaddafi', ' Erdogan') and word-final fragments ('ry', 'ops', 'pped', 'asket', 'herry'). The response is graded rather than thresholded and is fixed by the token, not by its context (a fixed neutral frame reproduces the in-corpus token ranking at Spearman 0.82, position explains 0% and no letter pattern, token frequency or WordNet category predicts it better), so a window's peak follows from which of these token types it contains, with context shifting it only modestly (e.g. ' mythology' fires 1.05 after ' Greek' and 0.74 after 'ancient').

Retrospective detector for social-evaluative and appraisal vocabulary: tokens that express or name approval, disapproval, or judgmental assessment of a person, behavior, or performance (e.g. praise, criticism, compliments, insult, apology, judgment, feedback, approval, expectations, rude, disrespectful, inappropriate, immature, superior, inferior, satisfied, embarrassed, tone, attitude, evaluate, improve). It fires on the appraisal word itself regardless of positive or negative valence, and does not fire on generic quality or sentiment adjectives (excellent, superb, great, good, bad, terrible, awful) or on neutral descriptive nouns (description, performance, character, surprise).

This layer-0 pole is a lexical detector of the lower-case English clause-connective / clause-introducer class: it fires on the current token whenever that token opens a dependent (subordinate, relative, participial or adverbial) clause or adjunct phrase attached to the clause already in progress -- ' including' at the top (2.2-2.4 of the 2.35 max, the scan peak), ' except' next (~2.0), then a broad band at ~1.2-1.9 covering the subordinators and relative pronouns (' although', ' whereas', ' while', ' because', ' since', ' though', ' unless', ' until', ' if', ' when', ' whenever', ' albeit', ' lest', ' insofar', ' wherein', ' whereby', ' whilst', ' whether', ' which', ' whose', ' according', ' depending', ' regardless', ' despite', ' during', ' besides', ' namely', ' pursuant', ' irrespective', ' notwithstanding', ' sans', ' amid', ' alongside', ' unlike', ' at', ' with', ' without', ' via') and the participial clause-introducers (' allowing', ' involving', ' considering', ' regarding', ' assuming', ' indicating', ' consisting', ' ranging', ' using', ' stating', ' suggesting', ' comprising', ' barring', ' judging'). It is ~0 on articles, determiners and personal pronouns, on auxiliaries and finite verbs, on punctuation, on content words (the -ing nouns ' building'/'morning' and the ordinary activity participles ' walking'/'working' both fail), on ' and'/'or'/'nor' (~0.3) and on the complement-marking prepositions ' of' (0.25) and ' to' (0.56), sits at only ~0.9-1.2 on the simple locative prepositions, and is mixed on the conjunctive adverbs (' however', ' thus', ' but', ' so' pass; ' moreover', ' furthermore', ' nevertheless', ' therefore' at 0.2-0.7 do not), while the capitalised sentence-initial forms are much weaker (' Including' ~0.6, ' Although'/'While' ~0.0) and the preceding comma, the following word and the source make no difference, so a text is predicted active exactly when a lower-case token of this connective class occurs in mid-sentence.

This layer-0 pole is a lexical detector of the act of naming/designating: it fires on the current token when that token names, labels or confers a title or office — ' named' by far the strongest (~4.6 of 4.9), then name/names/naming, called/calls/calling, renamed/rename, designate(d)/designation, declared, termed, dubbed, christened, proclaimed, nominate(d)/nominating, appoint(ed), appellation, acronym, abbreviation, nickname/nicknamed, surname, refer(red), registry/registered, listed, and the election-to-office register elect/electing/elected/election(s), vote/voted/voting/voter, campaign, ballot, candidate, with the address formulas thank, wish and congratulate/congratulations clearing the line weakly (~1.3–1.9). It is exactly zero on the names and honorifics themselves (Carl, Raleigh, Charlotte, Mr, Dr, Sir, President, Saint, Mount), on ordinary verbs (walked, built, said, made, died), and on 'name' in other senses (namely, username, filename, game, same, title, label); activation is a pure function of the current token — identical across constructions, positions and topics — so a text is predicted active exactly when one of those designation tokens occurs in it.

This pole fires when the current token evokes containment, packaging, or shipment of goods (e.g. pack, box, wrap, contain, enclose, ship, freight, parcel, postage, deliver, cargo, weigh), and stays at or below zero on other words, including semantically nearby ones like truck, mail, send, store, or sack. A weaker offshoot fires on wet-cooking verbs (boil, simmer, stew).

This Layer-0 pole is a retrospective unigram detector for span-opening tokens: it fires when the current token conventionally opens or initiates a new addressed or named span — markup/bracket openers ('<', '{', '[', '@' with or without a leading space; strongest), utterance openers (greetings Hello/hey/Hi and letter-opener Dear), and first elements of multiword names and titles (New, Los, San, El, La, Mr, Ms). It stays near zero on ordinary content words, on closers ('>', '}', ')', '('), and on mid-span name parts (John, York, Angeles, London), with idiosyncratic edges (e.g., Dr does not fire) consistent with a learned token family rather than a clean semantic rule.

Fires retrospectively when the current token itself is an abstract noun denoting a surrounding material, setting, built system/tool, or occupational/activity domain in which content, processes, or people exist or work (e.g. medium, background, platform, framework, application, IDE, SDK, hobby, profession, industries), irrespective of surrounding context.

This layer-0 pole is a retrospective detector of the current token's surface form and lexical register: it fires (0.5-2.0 of its 2.06 maximum) on a space-prefixed, all-lowercase word token, most strongly on code identifiers and keywords (self, if, return, end, new, class, var, const, string, id, value, dispatch, document) and on technical or concrete common nouns (router, floor, car, bank, door, target), and reads near zero on the same words capitalised or in upper case (Floor, Target, FLOOR), on the word when its leading space is dropped (the 'floor' inside 'x(floor'), on pure digit, punctuation and symbol runs, and on sentences built only from high-frequency function words and generic nouns (the, of, and, is, was, time, people, way, fact, thing, idea, world, information, government). Code-formatted context - after indentation, '=', '(', ':' or ';' - roughly doubles the strength of the same word, so a lowercase word inside a code line almost always clears the active line, whereas in running prose only a technical/concrete subset (floor, car, router, bank, mirror, door at 0.5-0.9) reaches it and most ordinary prose vocabulary (woman, book, report, tree, engine, idea, government) stays at 0.0-0.4.

Fires retrospectively when the current token is the standalone single-letter uppercase A (with or without a leading space), as in a sentence-initial article (A typical...), a Q&A answer label (A:), or a name/word initial (T.A., Aghia split as A + gh); it responds weakly to lowercase a and not at all when the position holds another capital, article, or part of a longer token.

Retrospective layer-0 unigram detector: the strength is fixed by which token sits in the current position (97% of the integrated-gradient attribution is on the peak token, token identity explains 96% of scan variance, and a token keeps its strength across carriers), firing at 0.3-2.0 of the 1.46 scan scale on a fixed, idiosyncratic set of English token forms - 'would'/'wouldn' and 'called' (strongest mid-text), the 'roll' stem (roll, rolls, rolled, rolling, roller), 'til'/'till' and weakly 'until', the weekday names Monday-Thursday and Sunday and their truncations (Tues, Mond, Thur, Fri, Sun), the time words tomorrow/tonight/today/noon/midnight/morning, the apostrophe token, the digit tokens 5-9 (strongest on 8-9), and individual capitalised name tokens (Robin, Roy, Joe, Bernie, Hillary, Warren, Cosby) - while staying at or below zero on every month name (January-December), every place name tested (London, Paris, France, China, Italy, Texas), the other modals (will, must, should, may, can, shall, might), the rest of the 'call' paradigm (call, calls, calling), the 'roll' lookalikes (troll, toll, doll, poll, role, rule), most personal names (Robert, James, Kevin, Anna, Sarah) and ordinary or Latinate vocabulary. Independently of token identity a text's first token is boosted by roughly +0.5 to +1.2, so capitalised sentence-openers that read about 0 mid-text (She, They, He, It, We, If, So, That, For, Please, Our, Once) fire at 0.6-1.3 there - which is why most of the scan's top examples peak at index 0 - and the pole prepares no particular upcoming token (Jacobian and logit-lens kurtosis are both ~3.0).

Layer-0 lexical detector for the space-prefixed word ' help' and a small set of near-synonyms for assistance provided by others: strongest on ' help' (~2.3-2.8 in any sense, including 'cannot help it' and 'help desk') and ' services' (~1.9-3.0, highest after ' emergency'/' ambulance'/' rescue', lowest after ' church'), mid on ' assistance', ' attention', ' agencies', ' intervention', ' authorities', ' expertise', ' rescue', ' aid', ' assist' (~1.5-2.4), weaker on inflections ' helping'/' helps'/' helped'/' helpful'/' helper' (~1.2-1.7) and on unspaced or capitalised 'help'/'Help' (~1.0); it is near zero on close synonyms outside this set (' support', ' guidance', ' treatment', ' department', ' police', ' food'). Context changes strength only modestly (about 30%), raising it when an emergency or medical noun comes just before.

This layer-0 pole is a retrospective detector of the token that completes a multi-token word: it fires when the current token is the final piece of a word GPT-2 has split into several tokens, i.e. a bound suffix morpheme such as -al (hippocamp|al, fract|al), -ation/-ations (Activ|ation, approxim|ations), -ions (transcript|ions), -ization/-ized/-izing, -ive, -ally/-ically/-ical, -ular, -ator, -ment, -ated/-ating, -ologies/-ological or -ivity/-ivities, peaking at 0.6-1.0 of max; generic inflectional final pieces (-ing, -ed, -es) fire only in 15-35% of their occurrences and average about 0.1-0.2 of max. Label a text predicted active only when it contains such a split word whose last piece is one of these suffixes, and predicted inactive when the ending is fused into a single token (' collapse', ' approximation', ' cortical', ' practicalities', ' recognitions'), when the token is the word's first or middle piece ('hippocamp', 'approx', 'im', 'crystall', 'transcript'), or when the same letters stand alone as a word (' al', ' ions'); activation is zero on ordinary prose, and a small minority of firings land on whole Latin-derived words in scientific text (' sequence', ' detector', 0.2-0.6 of max) that I could not tie to a single property.

This pole is a retrospective unigram detector: it fires when the current token is a member of a fixed set of content-word tokens (e.g. must, shall, stared, glanced, princess, queen, violin, glucose, apple, pinch), with strength set by the token's embedding alone, and stays near zero on function words, punctuation, common near-synonyms (will, can, saw, looked, person, woman, water, guitar) and subword continuations (ist, ons, phony). The same token fires across carriers and is unaffected by words after it, while same-slot synonyms of different lexical identity silence it.

Retrospective unigram detector: the pole fires on the current token itself, independent of surrounding context or word-vs-proper-name sense, when the token is a word for ordinary standards and averages (normal, average, mean, median, usual, ordinary, regular, typical, plain, alright), recurrent everyday time (everyday, daily, times, day, morning, noon, dawn, dusk, evening, routine, weekday), casual approximation or comparison (almost, around, circa, compared), or small fixed amounts (pinch, eight, twice), plus a fringe of embedding-similar tokens (hey, odd, basement, umpy). It stays near zero on function words and on most other content words, including near-synonyms with different spellings (common, nearly, moon, hay, today, dozen, standard, often) and capitalized proper-name senses (Dawn).

L0/N604+ is a current-token (unigram) detector for one semantic direction: emphatic, inherent presence, i.e. words asserting that a quality is unmistakably, deeply or widely there. The peak is the 'mark' family of defining signs (mark, marked, marks, Mark, hallmark, trademark, stamped, etched, engraved, imprint, emblem), grading down through 'plainly evident' adjectives (plain, clear, obvious, evident, distinct, pronounced, stark, unmistakable, undeniable, indisputable, conspicuous, unequivocal, manifest) and 'inherent/established' adjectives (fundamental, basic, inherent, innate, ingrained, intrinsic, foundational, essential, natural, bedrock, cornerstone, staple, common, commonplace, standard, universal, ubiquitous, prevalent, predominant, paramount, permanent, eternal, timeless, ancient, classic, traditional), with the same behaviour for every sense of a token (noun 'a mark', verb 'to mark', name 'Mark'); words of evaluative importance (important, major, key, crucial), novelty/oddity (new, strange, unusual, novel), neutral category nouns (sign, feature, trait, quality, property, nature, symbol) and plain adjectives (big, small, good, bad) sit at zero.

This layer-0 pole is a retrospective detector of the current token's identity, and the identity it detects is the vocabulary of a weather report or an observing log: it fires on (a) the reported state of the sky, light, atmosphere and time (sunny, rain, rainfall, precipitation, humidity, visibility, temperatures, highs, lows, forecast, outlook, skies, sky, sunrise, sunset, daylight, twilight, dusk, sunshine, sunlight, light, overnight, nightly, daytime, tonight, hours, clock, clocks, times), (b) the quantities, units and geometry those reports are written in (inches, meters, Fahrenheit, Kelvin, watt, ultraviolet, elevation, altitude, height, heights, tall, above, vertical, latitude, extreme, alert), and (c) the acts and instruments of observing, measuring and recording those states (observatory, observe, observed, observing, observer, observers, observation, observations, watch, watched, witness, witnessed, noticed, noted, record, recorded, measure, measured, measuring, measurement, monitored, readings, tallied, gauge, marker, indicator, broadcast, telescopes, eclipse, celestial, heavens, astronomical, Greenwich, GMT, UTC). It reacts to the token alone rather than to the sentence's meaning, so a sentence about the weather that contains only everyday weather nouns (snow, cloud, wind, cold, warm, heat, moon, storm) or media and imaging words (television, radio, camera, lens, film, press) stays below the activity line, while any listed word fires even in an unrelated sentence; the sole exception is the bare BPE pieces ' att' and ' im', which fire wherever the tokenizer splits a word after those letters, whereas the whole words they begin (attention, important) do not.

This pole fires retrospectively whenever the current token is one of a lexical subset of English preposition/particle word-forms denoting location, direction, or time (on, in, at, into, onto, upon, over, under, above, below, behind, across, around, through, along, near, up, down, out, away, off, before, after, during, within, among, between), regardless of syntactic role, including non-spatial idioms ('at least', 'on average') and code keywords ('in range'). It stays silent on other equally frequent function words, including other prepositions (of, to, for, with, by, from, without, despite, except, versus), content words, and punctuation.

In layer 0 the negative pole of N769 is a retrospective current-token dial: it peaks (near its ~0.17 ceiling) on ordinary content words, names, numbers and items like '(' and ',' (e.g. ' must', ' flooded', ' Neil', ' noon', ' prescribed', ' n'), is markedly weaker on high-frequency function words (' the', ' to', ' year', ' not'), and shuts off to ~0 on symbolic operator/markup tokens ('+', '=', '<', '\') and the variable token ' x' where the positive pole spikes instead. It therefore tracks how content-like versus symbol-like the token just read is, and prepares no specific upcoming token (Jacobian and logit lens top-10 lists agree on 0 tokens, kurtosis ~3.0).

This L0 pole is a retrospective detector that fires on the current token when it dates or reports a completed event: strongest on contemporary calendar-year tokens (graded, peaking around 2000-2016 and fading to zero for years before ~1960), and moderately on occurrence/completion/reporting tokens such as ' ended', ' ending', ' posted', ' shared', ' post'/' shares', and weakly ' ago'; it is silent on other numbers, older years, and neutral verbs/nouns. Activity is driven by the current token's embedding (input-key projection ranks years highest; ~95% of attribution sits on the peak token), not by upcoming-token prediction (Jacobian-lens kurtosis is ~3 with no coherent promoted set).

Retrospective current-token detector for a fixed embedding-space cluster: it fires on whole-word tokens marking shared or established standing and transmitted information (common, known, unknown, shared, prevailing, word, lore, knowledge) and intellectual-property status (patent, copyright, trademark, license, intellectual), plus the bound continuation fragment lic (licenses, publica, allelic). It fires on the token form regardless of sense, case, or context (software Word, name Common/Lore, commonplace) and stays near zero on other tokens including close synonyms (flaw, normal, church, eaten, lawsuit, Microsoft) and the whole-word public.

Fires retrospectively on the word that names the outcome or evaluation of a completed narrative event: achievement or change-of-state verbs (save, won, resigned, defeated, consecrated), their outcome nominals (loss, vow), and evaluative or collective complements (such, bravest, essential, range/Reserves), when read after an explicit subject plus event setup; strongest in encyclopedic biographical and historical prose.

This pole fires retrospectively on the current token when it is a lexical marker of quantified population inquiry or hedged generalization: survey/poll/study/research/rate language (including the ' poll' subword even inside semantically unrelated words like 'pollination'), the hedges 'may'/'might', the quantifier 'many', and the paragraph-break newline token that segments multi-paragraph expository text. It does not fire on generic academic nouns (report, data, evidence, findings), other modals/adverbs (could, often), or other quantity words (several, various), so it is narrower than an academic-register or hedging detector.

This pole fires retrospectively on the main verb token of a simple clause, after a subject has been established, regardless of the verb's specific meaning. It peaks on verbs such as loved, grow, talk, hit and spoke, and not on nouns, adjectives or function words in the same position.

Largely a token-identity detector at layer 1: it fires on a small fixed set of tokens. It fires most strongly (about 0.7-1.0 of max) on ' floor' in any sense (room, Senate or dance floor; weaker after 'ocean' or 'dance') and on the word-internal subword 'idd' (Giddens, inmiddels). It fires moderately (about 0.4-0.8) on the subwords 'iler', 'ARD' (RICHARD, AWARD), 'FF' (AFFIRMED) and 'ently', and on ' record', ' engine', ' simple', ' Hart', ' ear' and ' century'. Synonyms and near-neighbours ('ground', 'rug', 'level', 'table', 'report', 'truck') and other tokens stay below about 0.4 of max, whatever the context or meaning.

This pole is the saturated-inhibition readout (GeLU floor ~0.17) of an L1 neuron: it peaks on non-sequence-initial, word-initial tokens whose embedding plus local bigram context do not match the neuron's positive key (e.g. senator, pleaded, boils, at, summit, the cat/dog). It is silent on the sequence-initial token (which drives the positive pole instead), on continuation pieces and veto words with opposing unigram keys (iked, announced, degrees, rose, world, me, defendant), with the same token's strength varying strongly by predecessor (to: 0.17 after According vs 0.03 after hiked).

This pole is the lower (GELU-trough) lobe of a layer-1 neuron and its strength is a positional-plus-token readout with no semantic or lookahead content: the first token of a prompt is always silent (pre-activation about +0.45 whatever it is), the second position sits at or near the trough for nearly any token (mean strength 0.13, all of 40 varied words negative), and from the third position on a token that is an ordinary word, punctuation, whitespace or subword fragment saturates it at 0.16-0.17, whereas a token that repeats one already seen (' for' repeated runs 0.17, 0.06, 0.00, then positive) or that follows a run of positively-reading content words ('Women patients children adults characters the' peaks at 0.010) stays positive and silent. The pole is therefore predicted active (peak at least 0.10) on almost any prompt of two or more ordinary tokens, and predicted inactive only where every token is silent - a lone first token, a repeated silent word ('women women' = 0.036), or a pure content-word run.

Retrospective lexical detector for one family of English relational word-forms: the vocabulary of opposition, bearing/direction, relative position and directed stance, strong on opposite, contrary, opposed/opposition, offense/offensive, defense/defensive, aggressive, hostile, combative, antagonistic, adversarial, positive, negative, plus, favourable, adverse, advantageous, detrimental, beneficial, advantage, front, ahead, forward, toward(s), approach, direction, oriented, incoming, outgoing, anterior, posterior, exterior, superior, prior, relative, comparative, inverse, complementary, perpendicular, adjacent, inclusive, exclusive, attention, attitude, response, initiative, strategy, warning, complaint, objection, behalf, liaison, letter and way (derived forms of a stem fire together, e.g. opposed/opposing/opposition and offense/offenses/offensive, while the bare verb 'oppose' is weak), and also on the bound pieces of the same vocabulary when BPE exposes them as their own token ('-ative' in talk-ative/figur-ative, '-versely' in in-versely, '-wards' in north-wards, '-clusive' in re-clusive). Membership is lexical rather than conceptual: everyday or process words for the same ideas are silent, including behind/back/left/right/top/bottom, war/fight/attack/battle/conflict/rival, dispute/debate/argument/controversy/confrontation, similar/equal/identical/related/relevant, difference/contrast/distinction, due/prone/liable/subject/capable, plan/view/opinion/position and angry/violent/proud/guilty, as are the connectives but/however/although/nevertheless and the negators not/never/no; the peak is on the word itself (74% of input attribution on it, and context shifts it by only about 0.3-0.6), while the negative pole is a near-constant 0.1-0.17 GELU-dip baseline with no token structure, i.e. feature-absent.

The positive pole fires on the concreteness of the current token: it is active when that token names a concrete, physical thing of the everyday, narrative or historical kind - an artefact, animal, person or role, body part, building or place, or natural entity (pen, desk, church, priest, horse, river, station) - and reads zero when the token is abstract, technical or scientific vocabulary (method, system, theory, evidence, value, electrode, sample, tissue), a pronoun, punctuation, or one of the most frequent function words. It also fires on a small set of relational words that are not the most frequent operators (but, while, though, whose, own and the possessive 's), while their frequent counterparts (and, that, which, their, of, the) stay at zero.

This pole emits a brief retrospective novelty transient on the current token when that token is weakly predicted by the immediately preceding token: surprising continuations (far after kingdom, 1 after =, am after of, three after after) spike and decay on the next token, while highly predictable continuations of identical tokens (half after second, phony after sym, are after Where at 0.02 versus after Lima at 0.22) stay near zero.

Ignoring each text's first token, this pole is a retrospective token detector whose strength is set by the current token (94% of the variance of its pre-activation is between tokens, and it reads exactly the same 0.409 of max whatever token follows): it fires at about 0.15-0.7 of max on quantifiers and degree/discourse adverbs (most, much, another, either, every, each, less, almost, only, just, still, nearly, usually, generally, typically, especially, primarily), on relational prepositions and subordinators (under, after, before, between, into, when, if, while, than), on comparatives and superlatives (longest, best, greater, longer) and on abstract or procedural nouns and verbs (solution, role, result, influence, subject, challenge, standard, process, provide, involve, cover, ensure, require, follow, help, paper, said). It stays at the GELU floor (0.00 of max) on concrete everyday vocabulary - physical objects, animals, plants, foods, places and buildings (bed, cup, dog, egg, chair, flower, horse, fish, lake, street, snow), simple scalar adjectives (big, small, high, low, new, old, good, cold, hot, fast, slow, easy), basic everyday verbs (eat, sleep, sit, stand, open, close, buy, sell, pay, hold, keep, stop) - and on the highest-frequency glue plus 'plain' abstract words (that, this, is, about, at, from, by, idea, knowledge, reason, action, system, theory, method, value, social, national, important, really, also, actually), so an everyday sentence built only from those words peaks at or near zero (0.00-0.05 of max); the boundary is lexical rather than semantic and is graded, so a word just inside the firing families can sit anywhere from 0.1 to 0.5.

Retrospective word-identity detector for one specific lexical field: the pole fires on the current token when that token belongs to the light / imaging / audio / apparel / material-and-finish vocabulary - the whole light family in every sense and inflection (light, lights, lighting, Light), imaging and optics (phot, photograph(y), camera(s), lens, optics, optical, image, picture, video, footage, sight), audio (sound(s), music, audio, acoustic, microphone, headphones, horn), apparel and personal gear (wear, wearing, wore, worn, clothing, clothes, shirt, dress, hat, gloves, shoes, socks, jewellery, armour, helmet, gun, weapons, ammunition, gear, equipment, hardware) and materials/finishes (wood, brass, metal, steel, aluminium, glass, copper, silver, titanium, carbon, leather, wool, ceramic, wire, electric(al), electricity, solar, magnetic, colour, texture, brightness). It responds to the lexeme, not to the meaning or the context: 76% of input attribution sits on the peak token, 94% of activation variance is token identity and 0% position, all senses of ' light' fire alike (illumination, 'not heavy', a pale colour, a traffic light, the verb), 'wearing' fires in 'wearing thin', the pole sits at the GELU floor (about -0.17, which is also the whole negative pole) for function words, abstractions, natural kinds, food, animals, places, people, furniture, kitchenware and vehicles (water, table, bread, dog, tree, mountain, car, phone, computer, money), and membership is graded rather than semantic - inside the field, light/phot/camera/music/wearing/brass/wood sit at 1.4-3.0 while dress/hat/silk/cotton sit at 0.3-0.6, and close synonyms outside the field (lamp, glow, gold, velvet, satin, linen, stone) stay at 0.0-0.6.

This pole fires on the current token when it belongs to one lexical family: the 'span and stage' nouns by which a career, history, place or organisation is indexed. In descending strength that family is year/years, season, league, winter, summer, spring, fall, autumn, career, life, decade, month, childhood, youth, adult, age, generation, junior/senior/sophomore/freshman, rookie, semester, grade, college, collegiate, majors, offseason/preseason, NCAA and the league acronyms (NHL, NBA, NFL, CFL, MLB, MLS), sport(s) and the sport names, and then more weakly (0.6-1.5 of peak) the place and sector tiers state, city, county, province, community, nation, country, world, industry, agriculture, labor. It is a retrospective, sense-blind token detector: 80% of the input attribution sits on the peak token itself, following tokens cannot affect it, and zero-ablating the pole moves next-token logits only diffusely (KL ~ 4e-3, no concentrated promoted token), so verb 'state', the verb 'season' in 'Please season the soup' and 'industry' meaning diligence fire as strongly as the noun senses; and its boundary is lexical rather than semantic, so day, week, hour, minute, time, moment, period, era, quarter, term, tenure, stint, spell, division, conference, tier, level, class and school do not fire, nor do the agents, objects or containers of the same domains (team, player, coach, game, match, tournament, championship, club), while season, league and year are the three highest-activating tokens of the entire 50,257-token vocabulary in a plain 'The X' frame.

This pole retrospectively marks the left edge of an embedded, dependent, or non-Latin-script constituent: it fires on opening brackets, sigils and quotes (' [', ' {', ' <', ' ${', ' @', ' #', ' (', including the code peaks), on determiner-like words that project a following noun (strongest on the relative possessive 'whose', weaker on these/those/that/the/this and possessive determiners), and on word-initial fragments of non-Latin text (notably space-joined CJK lead bytes such as Ġì=[0x20,0xEC] and bare spaces between Korean fragments). It stays near zero on the mirror-image closers (']', '}', '>', ')'), on word-internal continuation bytes, and on standalone pronouns ('who', 'they'), verbs and ordinary content words.

Fires retrospectively on the token that closes an already-opened expectation: the second subword piece of a split word, a structural closer such as an HTML close tag, code newline, or SQL clause keyword, or the predictable second half of a frequent collocation or syntactic frame such as far-away, was-void, or plural-subject-are.

This pole fires on a high-frequency clause-linking token (comma or medial period, 'and', 'of', 'that', 'to', or 'the'/'a'/'it') when it directly continues a mid-sentence noun or verb phrase that syntactically licenses it, such as a date or list item before a comma, a transitive verb before its object article, a noun before 'of', or a verb before 'that'/'and'/'to', with strength graded by the specific preceding word. It stays silent on the same tokens at sentence edges, after greetings or other function words, and on content words substituted into the same slot.

This pole fires retrospectively on the second token of a memorized two-token completion: a word-internal BPE continuation finishing a split word (Bl+ogging, Me+asuring, Ch+annels, m+illed, g+mail), the second word of a fixed collocation (cloud after public/private, Poll after opinion, sharing after love), or a fused punctuation pair ("," closing a quotation, ][ bridging brackets). Firing is gated by the specific preceding token as well as the peak token, so the same surface token is silent after a non-member predecessor and ordinary strong bigrams such as peanut butter or New York do not activate it.

N2423+ is a token-identity detector for a small, closed lexical cluster of information-source / news-attribution words: it fires on the word forms ' media/Media', ' net/Net', ' source(s)/Sources', ' press', ' text(s)', ' official(s)', ' main' and ' technical' wherever they occur (surrounding context shifts strength only mildly), and drops to exactly zero on every other token, including close synonyms such as 'newspaper', 'internet', 'journalist', 'website', 'report', 'wire', 'publication' and 'broadcast'. Words that fill the same news-attribution slots ('police', 'authorities', 'chief', 'staff', 'system', 'kernel', 'images', 'graphics', 'web', 'http') give a much weaker response (roughly 0.2-1.1 versus 1.3-3.3), so the pole is a lexical detector for the media/source/attribution vocabulary, not a semantic category detector.

Ignoring the first token, this pole is a token detector for a small set of subwords. They are French 'ien' completing a one-letter stem (' b'/' r'/' l'+'ien' = bien, rien, lien: 0.5-1.0 of max; ' ch'+'ien' about 0.3, English 'Parisien' about 0), 'ét' of 'été' (0.4-0.6), ' steroid' (0.6-0.7), 'ender' of 'attender' (about 0.5), and English transfer or completion verbs such as ' handed', ' made', ' bought' and ' fixed' (0.3-0.7), but the verbs fire only after about 8 or more tokens of context and are near 0 in a sentence's first few tokens. Other words stay below 0.25 of max: everyday English nouns and verbs ('sandwich', 'visitor', 'gave', 'read'), French 'bon', 'lit', 'lieu' and 'fait', code, and numbers. Long English prose can drift to 0.2-0.35 on scattered content words.

The pole fires retrospectively when the current token marks its noun phrase as an earlier, superseded, or ordered-alternative member of a contrast set, canonically prior-status and ordering markers such as former, previous/previously, latter, and later. It does not fire on neighboring present-tense, recency, generic-modifier, or lookalike tokens (current, once, recently, early, letter, formal), and this characterization does not cover additional verified actives (charitable/charity, alumni, Foundation/Organization-family nouns, South, Sign, 191-series numbers, Aut, dart, foisted/hoisted, unexceptional) for which no shared feature survived testing.

At any non-first position, this pole fires on tokens from a memorized lexical set with two lobes: (a) small stinging/biting/swarming pests and close-range interactions with them (bees, ants, mosquitoes, spiders, butterflies, cockroaches, moths, ticks, honey, sting, buzz, bite, sniff, hover, swarm, bug), and (b) agentive/technical role and artifact nouns (agent/agency, model, prototype, bot/robot, client, interface, button, gadget/widget, worker, atom). It is silent on isolated single tokens and on common nouns outside the set (table, dogs, water, device, computer, doctor, teacher), while marginal members (chemical, users, galaxy, pinch, contract, already, zer) fire weakly and only with topically congruent preceding context.

Fires on structural/boundary tokens rather than content: strongest (about 0.85-1.0 of max) on whitespace control characters (\t, \r, \x0c, \n) that follow a sentence- or statement-ending '.' or ';', next on commas and bare '\n' (about 0.55-0.7), weaker on '.', '?' and short function words (the, and, that, is: about 0.2-0.6), and essentially zero on content words (nouns, adjectives, most verbs). Activation is largest near the start of a text and decays somewhat over long contexts.

Fires on the second or later occurrence of a content-word token or word-stem when the same surface string already appeared earlier in the passage; the identical word as a first mention, with no prior occurrence, does not drive it.

GPT-2 L1/N277's negative pole is a positional readout of the GELU floor, not a content detector: its pre-activation sits in the flat basin around GELU's minimum on every token at absolute positions 1-56 of a forward pass (100% active over all 365 scanned documents, mean strength 0.84-0.98 x the scan maximum), whatever the topic, language or token, then decays with position (95% of tokens active at position 70, 53% at 88, 9% at 100) and is entirely off (pre-activation above zero) from about position 116 on, while a text's first token (position 0) is also off for nearly every token (mean strength 0.013; only the bare tokens 'In' and 'On' reach the 0.25 x scale line); the same neuron's positive pole mirrors this, firing only at late positions (37% of tokens at position 100, 96% at 120). Because a prompt is scored by its peak token, every prompt of two or more tokens is predicted active and only a one-token prompt is predicted inactive; a content edit changes only where in the 57-115 band the decay happens, never whether a two-or-more-token prompt fires.

The positive pole detects non-American English orthography and lexis: it fires on British/Commonwealth spellings and vocabulary (colour, organise, analyse, criticise, centre, theatre, programme, learnt, maths, whilst, petrol, lorry, queue, fortnight, crisps) and UK references (BBC, NHS, Labour, Parliament, Manchester), and equally on non-English text (German, French, Greek, accented letters such as ä, ö, ü, é, è, ê, foreign place names such as Goethe or Nagpur). Standard American English - color, organize, center, program, US states, cities and institutions - leaves it at its negative baseline, and its output direction suppresses the British spellings it detects while promoting American spellings and US references.

The positive pole fires on the token carrying a descriptive quality adjective: a mainly derived, polysyllabic word that says what something is like or how good/notable it is (unusual, effective, suitable, reasonable, sensible, important, impressive, useful, necessary, remarkable, aggressive), at any sentence position; it also fires on the bare adjectival suffix piece when such a word is split across tokens ('able', 'ible', 'ful', 'ical', 'itative', 'itable'). It is predicted inactive for nouns, verbs, adverbs and -ness/-ity/-tion abstract nouns, for the basic perceptual/dimensional/valence adjectives (big, long, tall, hot, high, small, old, new, good, bad, great: all zero), and for classifying/relational adjectives (medical, economic, national, social, digital, legal: well under 0.25 of max).

This pole fires on whatever token occupies position 0 of the input and is silent on every later token; the peak height is modulated by token identity but the on/off pattern is purely positional, i.e. a first-token/position-0 detector.

This pole fires on the wordform itself from a historical-warfare lexical set -- naval vessels and forces (frigate, ships, naval, armies, troops), combat nouns (war, battle/battles, invasion, campaigns), and historical-naval fighter and command titles (Knights, admiral, Conqueror, Army, ship's Captain, warrior) -- peaking on the token that completes the word whether its use is military or not, so a red admiral butterfly, squadrons of geese, a chess knight, the Conqueror of retail, or an invasion of privacy still drive it; semantically related words outside the set (gun, rifle, missile, bombing, murder) and civilian text without these wordforms stay near zero.

This pole is a sparse surface-form detector, not a concept neuron: it fires on a fixed ~1-2% of GPT-2 token types whose forms are marked, namely uppercase chunk tokens ('AS', 'AT', 'IE', 'IS', 'IF', 'ME'), capitalized function words ('In', 'To', 'By', 'Of') and word-internal (no-leading-space) fragments ('ase', 'ages', 'ie', 'ures'), which reach 0.6-1.6, while the same strings' canonical space-prefixed lowercase tokens stay near the floor ('Ġas' 0.10, 'Ġto' 0.05, 'Ġie' 0.13, 'Ġthe' -0.16). 'AS' is not special and neither is the acronym/technical register: in matched frames 'AT' in 'MCAT' fires as hard as 'AS' in 'MCAS' (1.55 vs 1.82), '-ase' in 'helicase' fires as hard as 'AS' in 'GWAS' (1.16), yet genuine acronyms ('NBC', 'CBS', 'ASCII') and technical words split into other fragments ('ization', 'ence', 'ography') stay at the GELU floor; a residual 0.35-0.9 response to a few ordinary concrete nouns in canonical form ('Ġice', 'Ġshake', 'Ġblood', 'Ġlife') is not explained by this rule.

Layer-1 lexical (token-identity) detector on the current token: at every position except the first token of the input it activates at about 1.1-1.9 (0.45-0.75 of its 2.49 max) when the current token is one of a fixed set of English content words or word-pieces, whatever the surrounding text and whatever the sense - the note/notice family (note, notes, notice, noticed, noted, noting), coastal-water nouns (water, sea, sand, rain, beach, shore, bay, gulf, swamp, marsh, tide, salt, moisture), money/legal/conflict nouns (tax, law, war, peace, money, bank, loan, debt, mortgage, fund, police, jail), short personal and place names (Tim, Jim, Jay, Dan, Pam, Cam, Jeff, Kim, Ryan, Cole, Jordan, Bush, Miami) and short everyday words or word-pieces (spot, patch, check, tab, counter, buffer, temper, ante, jazz, buff, aj, iff, uff, orm, sur, crim). Inflected and capitalised forms of those words (waters, taxes, spots, patches, checking, bushes, Water) fire like the base form, while the feature is word identity and not meaning: the pole sits at its floor (about -0.1, i.e. pre-activation <= 0) on function words, on generic concrete nouns (dog, cat, tree, house, book, car, lake, river, ocean, mountain, city, country) and on the close synonyms of its firing words (liquid for water, ocean for sea, levy/statute/rule for tax/law, conflict for war, message for note, verify/inspect for check, cache for buffer, mark for spot).

This pole fires retrospectively on the current token when the token is a topically concentrated (bursty, unevenly distributed) word such as mug, velvet, rain, hall, glucose, or unemployment, while ubiquitous evenly spread words such as water, table, car, dog, people, or function words leave it silent. For such words its strength grows with position through the sentence and is higher amid topically coherent surrounding words than amid generic abstract framing.

The pole is a retrospective lexical detector: it fires at whichever token position is currently reading a word from one English word family, namely rising/growing/gaining (' raise/raising/raised/raises' strongest at 3.2-4.0, then ' grow/grew/growth', ' rise/rose/risen', ' gain/gained', ' climb/climbed', ' rally') together with its close relatives meaning draw or gather in (' draw/drew/drawn', ' gather/gathered', ' amassed', ' garnered'), yield or bring forth (' yield/yielded', ' born', ' arise/arose/arisen', ' spring/sprang/sprung', ' emerge/emerged', ' derive', ' generate', ' source'), or stand tall (' height', ' high', ' mount', ' mountain', ' peak', ' crest'); ' fall/fell' is a weaker member (1.3) while near-synonyms outside the family ('increase' 0.8-1.6, 'expanded', 'doubled', 'surged', 'jumped', 'soared', 'boosted', 'improved', and every decline/decrease/drop/shrink/lower/slump/plunge verb, about 0) stay silent, so membership is lexical (word-form) rather than the abstract concept of increase. Strength is fixed by that single token: changing only the following word leaves the peak unchanged ('raised rates' = 'raised concerns' = 'raised the roof' = 3.96), the only context effect is a 0.5-0.8 boost when the word is the clause's main verb after a subject, and its negative pole is a flat ~0.1 baseline with no token structure.

This pole is the negative lobe of a GELU unit, so its strength is a band-pass read of the unit's pre-activation z (w.LN(h1)+b): it reaches the ceiling (0.170, exactly GELU's minimum) only when z lies in the GELU dip around -0.75 (about -0.93 to -0.59 for strength >= 0.164), is at least half-max for z in (-1.62, -0.20), and falls to zero both when z > -0.09 (the positive-pole side: the sequence-initial token, whose z is always positive, typically +0.6 to +0.85, and code/symbol tokens such as '}', '####', '</' or standalone 's') and when z < -2.03 (polysyllabic content words such as ' first', ' best', ' great', ' world', ' million'). Because z is ~92% set by the current token's key, the pole fires on the middle of the token-key axis - punctuation and common function words in ordinary prose, with ~11% of corpus tokens sitting at the exact ceiling - so it is predicted active whenever any token's z falls in (-2.03, -0.09) (95% of random 3-token and 100% of 4-token corpus windows qualify) and predicted inactive only for short prompts where every token lies outside that window: any one-token prompt (position 0 has z ~ +0.7, so even this scan's own trigger tokens ' Edwards', ' Rak' and ' screens' measure 0.00 alone) or a two- to three-token prompt built entirely from the deep-negative words above (e.g. ' world first', ' computer million first'); it is retrospective, with no promoted-token set (Jacobian kurtosis 3.3, lens overlap 0).

Retrospective lexical detector at layer 1: the pole fires on the current token when that token is a nominal of the 'listed item / reported quantity' family - plural count nouns and -tion/-ment/-er/-ity/-ship nominalizations such as ' bodies', ' names', ' sources', ' factors', ' documents', ' folders', ' statements', ' agencies', ' countries', ' cases' or ' results' (peak 0.2-1.4), and more weakly on singular abstract nouns such as ' health', ' life', ' case', ' proof' or ' world'. It sits at the GELU floor (about -0.17) on function words, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, punctuation, animal names and occupational-role nouns, and its membership is lexical rather than purely semantic, so near-synonyms split (' names' much greater than ' tags', ' factors' greater than ' reasons', ' bodies' greater than ' corpses'); strength is graded and dips in a text's first few positions (at position 0 it is active on every token, hence the first-token floor).

Lexical layer-1 detector on the current (non-first) token: it fires at about 0.4-1.0 of max on a small word set, strongest ' apt', ' ancestry', ' Preferred' (capitalised, space-led), ' attribute', ' favor'/' favour', ' Primary', ' heritage', ' prefer', then ~0.35-0.55 on ' demographic', ' households', ' supporters', ' fans', ' voters', ' necessarily', ' carriers', ' wish', ' endorse', ' choose' (choice/preference/support and group-lineage words), with activation growing somewhat with preceding context. Close synonyms stay below ~0.2 of max (fitting, accurate, suitable, roots, lineage, population, residents, citizens, members, opponents, like, want, hope, lowercase-split 'Preferred' inside an identifier), and ordinary prose or code containing none of the listed words peaks below ~0.25 of max.

This pole fires retrospectively on the completing token of a conventionalized multi-word chunk in expository/news-style text: the attribution verb after its source ('Investigators said'), the head noun after its modifier ('rookie season', 'back of the year'), or the second half of a fixed name or word ('John Matthew', 'Re+formation'), with weaker activation on the chunk's earlier tokens. The same word outside its chunk stays low (verb 'to season the soup' is silent, bare 'Matthew' is silent), swapping the completing word out of the chunk collapses firing, and tokens after the peak do not matter.

Fires on the determiner (a/the/an) or head adjective of a predicative nominal complement of a be-verb: at 'is/are/was/were/be/been + a/the/an + (adjective) + noun' where the phrase ascribes a role, property, or evaluation to the subject (e.g. 'was a significant contributor', 'are the norm', 'may be a good thing', 'has been a cause'). The copular construction, not the specific adjective or noun, drives it: replacing the be-verb with a lexical verb collapses activation while swapping the adjective leaves it unchanged. Retrospective: activation peaks on the determiner/adjective itself and falls on the following noun, integrates distant subject context (mean attribution distance 12.4 tokens), and the Jacobian lens shows only a diffuse role-noun direction (kurtosis 3.3), so it reacts to the already-read ascriptive construction rather than preparing a specific upcoming token.

Fires retrospectively at the linker that predicates a characterizing, currently-holding state of a topic established earlier in the passage, typically a present-tense copula or stative verb (is/are/remains), a persistence marker (still/now), a small-clause object pronoun (keeping me/us), a methods participle or preposition (stored/cultured/on/at), or a coordinator joining kind descriptors (and/or). It stays quiet when the same token appears without such an upstream topic-plus-state predication, as in imperatives, fragments, metalinguistic mentions, or semantically implausible complements.

N1331+ fires on the leading piece of a stock, memorised multi-token unit inside formal prose: the first or middle piece of a common complex word (' aff' in 'affirms', ' rem' in 'remands', 'Cal'/'cul' in 'Calculate', 'ef' in 'indefinite', 'Rel' in 'Relational', ' here'/'ina' in 'hereinafter'), or a small function word that opens a fixed collocation ('rule of', 'Court of Appeals', 'have to', 'need to', 'will not', "don't", 'per cent', 'at all'); the closing piece of the same word fires much less (' aff' 2.0 vs 'irms' -0.2, 'Cal' 1.9/'cul' 1.8/'ate' 0.1). The pole is gated by the surrounding passage, not just the local token: it is loud in legal opinions, contract clauses, patents and arithmetic templates and near-zero in chat, personal narrative, recipes and marketing copy, so the same tokens are predicted active when their left context makes the rest of a formulaic word or phrase predictable inside formal/technical prose, and predicted inactive for those same tokens in conversational prose (' court' 2.3 after a contract clause vs -0.1 after a chat message; ' of' 2.6 after 'rule' vs 0.35 after 'point'; the same sentence 'The trial court did not deny the motion.' scores 2.3 on ' court' after legal prose and 0.0 after casual prose of equal length).

Retrospective detector for a locally highly predictable continuation: it fires most when the peak token completes a frequent bigram/trigram collocation or fixed frame (on the, from X to, at sea level, Hello world, email FROM, j + ') or a canonical subject-verb / verb-argument pairing (river-flooded, orchestra-tuned, watched-sunrise, by Friday) given the preceding 1-4 tokens; the same peak token in an atypical local context activates weakly.

The pole fires on a specifier or prenominal modifier inside a noun phrase: a determiner or possessive (a, the, his, notre), a quantifier or number (few, fewer, any, six, three), an attributive adjective (better, good, consecutive, direct, proper), or a quantity/unit-linking preposition (of, per) that specifies or links the head noun. The same word used predicatively, adverbially, or outside a determiner/nominal frame does not activate it, and the head noun's identity does not matter.

This pole detects scalar level/grade morphemes from the high/low/mid/middle family (any case, including compound-internal uses) that mark intensity, quality tier, elevation, temporal midpoint, age bracket, or centrality. It fires whether the morpheme is an attributive modifier (high school/performance/res, Middle Kingdom, middle aged), a compound part (midseason, low-ball), or a standalone nominalized or predicative state (emotional high, high on drugs); near-synonym degree words without that morpheme (tall, sick, fast, early, Outer, old) do not drive it.

Fires on the head noun (or the modal/auxiliary right after it) of the SUBJECT of an object-extracted relative clause or wh-question in abstract expository, technical, business or patent prose, i.e. at the point where a subject has been read and the verb whose object is the already-mentioned filler is due ("the advantages that renewable energy [[sources]] offer", "the effects that environmental [[conditions]] have", "calm that only nature [[can]] provide", "what does this [[all]] mean", "the trust Sentosa [[Care]] has in us"); it is strongest when both the extracted head noun and the subject are abstract (benefits/impact/role + policies/conditions/sources), weak (<0.3 of max) for the same nouns in an 'of'-phrase, and near zero in concrete everyday narrative ("the toys that my little brother left", "the book that my sister wrote") and on ordinary simple sentences; there is no first-token or positional floor. Secondary leftovers: 'not' in 'which/what it does not', the 't' of "doesn't" before a main verb, the stock phrase "The present invention", and end-of-identifier tokens of class/type names in code ("InputMethodSettings[[Interface]] {", "VpnSites[[Client]] struct").

Fires on the function word, directive adverb, or subword fragment that continues a formal institutional, regulatory, or administrative passage (government agency, court, school, corporate-compliance, licensing, or public-industry report) established over the preceding ~10 tokens; the identical continuation in a casual personal or conversational context does not fire.

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes or sharpens a multi-token reference to a specific person, place, count, spatial measure or score, menu/filesystem path, titled apposition, antecedent-linked possession, or code signature (surnames and place-name parts, numerals with count/space units, path slashes, appositive commas and role nouns, possessives like 'their', signature closers like '):'), with strength boosted by a longer preamble establishing the referent. It stays near zero on time-duration complements of waiting/lasting verbs, isolated quality adjectives on common nouns, and unlinked definite descriptions; the previously failing probes (code '):', UI-path '/', prose 'their') are predicted active under this account, not inactive.

Fires on the light middle element of a fixed multi-token construction once its constraining left half has been read: the ':' separator inside clock times and the 'T' inside ISO datetimes, a temporal/locative preposition or approximator joining its head to a predictable complement (just after/before, in/at/about plus a time, place or round), the perfect auxiliary 'been' after have/n't/'d, or the first fragment of a word or name whose completion is then fixed (im->am, sl->urring, Ahn->Qiraj, Jim->surname, sitting->on, time->I). The same surface token outside such a construction (a prose colon, dashes in digit strings, or nonsense in the slot) drives little activity, while swapping one valid slot-filler for another (after->before, Qiraj->ville) leaves it active.

This pole fires retrospectively when the preceding context establishes an agentive attainment or contest outcome (an award, election, record chase, poll lead, game result, credential, verdict, or completed traversal by a person or team), at the token that begins specifying its measure, scope, endpoint, or consequence. It stays quiet on the same trigger tokens (numbers, 'fell', 'crossed', 'a') in mundane frames with inanimate subjects or no competitive, honorific, or decisional stakes.

Fires throughout running text in Continental West/North Germanic languages (German strongest, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian; also German place names such as Innsbruck or St. Gallen inside English), on word-start or mid-word subword pieces like ' w'(urden), ' g'(eleden), ' b'(ij), 'gg'(es), typically 0.4-1.0 of max per sentence; secondarily, in English scientific-abstract prose it fires (~0.5-0.7) on the ' to' introducing the purpose after 'The aim/purpose of this study/survey was' or 'were used'. Ordinary English text (including everyday 'to' infinitives), Spanish and Italian stay near 0, so there is no activation floor on English prompts.

The pole fires on closed-class 'slot-opening' tokens: the articles and possessive determiners (the, a, an, my, your, his, its, our, their, whose) and the in-line separators (comma, colon, semicolon, en/em dash, '=', ':=', '|', '{') that introduce the next item or the head of the next phrase. It is essentially silent on open-class words (nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs measure 0.00 in prose) and markedly weaker - at or below a quarter of the pole's scale - on demonstratives (this/that/these/those), quantifiers (every, each, any, no, both, all), prepositions, conjunctions and clause-final punctuation (period, newline, closing bracket); its write at a firing token strips the modifier/determiner vocabulary and pushes the lexical head that fills the slot (at 'the' after 'Calculate' it promotes ' value', ' number', ' cost' and removes ' following', ' actual', ' final').

The pole fires on the abstract, relational word that anchors a 'how / in what respect / to what degree / by what means / on what ground' phrase — terms, regard, means, basis, extent, degree, advantage, insight, access, ability, scope, relevance, significance, implication, proportion, proximity (and relational adjectives such as able, possible, capable, proportional) — peaking on that word just before the preposition or infinitive it selects ('in terms of', 'with regard to', 'by means of', 'on the basis of', 'at the expense of', 'the advantage of', 'give insight into', 'be able to'), with manner/degree adverbials ('directly', 'slowly', 'badly') firing the same way. It stays near zero on concrete object nouns (table, car, bottle, shelf), on non-relational abstract entities (happiness, justice, music, money), and on the same relational words used as plain one-place noun-phrase heads ('the expense report', 'the access was denied', 'his insight was valuable', 'the terms were clear').

The positive pole is a retrospective lexical detector: it fires when the current token is one of a learned set of common English predicate words, above all everyday verb word-forms of the take/get/give/keep/help/make/find/save/protect/provide/create/turn/go/come/run/look/try/think family (and every inflection of them: take/takes/taking/took/taken, become/became/becomes, help/helps/helped, find/finds/found), plus a few degree-and-time adverbs ('more', 'less', 'longer', 'easily', 'fully', 'eventually', 'later', 'finally', 'quickly'). The syntactic frame and the described situation do not decide it: other verbs with nearly the same meaning stay at the pole's floor in an identical frame ('obtain', 'purchase', 'receive', 'deliver', 'repair', 'cook', 'eat', 'pay', 'teach', 'buy', 'win', 'lose', 'increase', 'reduce', 'know', 'learn', 'study', 'arrive', 'leave', 'stop' all measure 0.00-0.49), so label a token active iff it is in this lexical set (a lemma family counts as one entry), with the one positional modifier that these words fire ~6-14x more often when they sit in a predicate right after an auxiliary ('has/have/will/can/been') or an infinitival 'to'.

The pole fires at a phrase-final joint: the last content word of a phrase whose head selects a light connector that follows it ('due/owing to', 'able to', 'subject to', 'such as', 'based on', 'depends on', 'corresponds to', 'attributed to'), and at the comma, semicolon or markup/code delimiter that marks the same kind of joint (a comma setting off a parenthetical adverb, '... , therefore, ...', or separators such as 'align="', '', '=>', '_'). It stays inactive on list commas, on ordinary content-word continuations and on sentence-final periods; its own output direction promotes a comma.

The pole fires on the vocabulary of quantitative comparison: degree/comparative operators that relate two magnitudes ('more/less/fewer/greater/higher/lower/smaller ... than', 'equal/equivalent/close to', 'almost', 'nearly', 'roughly', 'just over'), the pivot words 'than'/'to' that introduce the second value, 'or' reformulating a quantity, paired alternatives ('the former ... the latter'), and measure words in quantitative statements ('rate', 'ratio', 'percent', 'length', 'size', 'century', 'year', 'night'). Non-comparative uses of the same words ('other than', 'rather than', 'due to', 'according to', a destination 'to', 'or' between two ordinary nouns) and non-measure nouns in the identical frame stay at the ~0.75 floor.

Fires on the function and connective tokens (a, -, can, be, its, more, and, or, is, you) inside formal institutional, legal or corporate prose, strongest in software-license and copyright boilerplate ("governed by a BSD-style license that can be", "Inc. or its affiliates", "one or more contributor", "permissions and limitations") and in corporate or industry subjects ("the software industry is", "board of directors that can be"); it also gives moderate responses on degree qualifiers after a negation or article ("not entirely", "equally", "vastly", "very"). It is near zero on casual, domestic or narrative text with the same syntax ("my mom or her friends", "the puppy is chased by a"), and the first token of a prompt is always ~0, so there is no floor.

This pole is GPT-2's GELU dip - gelu_new bottoms out at -0.17004 near pre-activation -0.75 - so it reads at or near its 0.170 maximum on almost all prose; its one semantic structure is animacy: strength falls to zero on tokens naming a sentient being (personal, possessive and object pronouns I/you/he/she/we/they/me/him/her/them/my/your/his, personal names like Tom/Mary/John, and person or animal nouns such as man, woman, boy, girl, friend, brother, mother, teacher, nurse, child, dog, cat) and at the first token of the prompt whatever it is, while determiners, prepositions, punctuation, verbs, inanimate nouns (stone, table, car, wind, engine, team) and abstract nouns (theory, idea, market, government) sit at the maximum (only pre-activations far below the dip, roughly -2 or lower, fall back toward zero). A short copular sentence whose predicate names a person leaves the pole at zero ('He is my brother.', 'You and I are friends.'), and swapping that one word for an inanimate noun restores the maximum ('He is my table.', 'You and it are friends.').

Retrospective detector that fires on the token completing the core complement of an episodic action clause: the determiner, numeral, quantifier, head noun, or negated verb that pins down which entity, how many, when, or what was done (e.g. 'the' before a descriptive noun, 'three' before 'days', 'next' before 'year', 'answer' after 'did not'), gated by an agentive subject plus action verb upstream. It stays weak or silent on the same tokens in copular/definitional sentences, with non-agentive proper-name subjects, and on repeated determiners in later adjuncts or clauses.

Retrospective detector firing at the function-word juncture where characterizing or specifying content is delivered or projected: a degree modifier before a gradable predicate (very/extremely/so/most plus adjective), a copula joining its subject to a predicative complement (the idea was to..., the task was difficult), a precise quantity or time specification (3:01, at nine), or an elaborating connective continuing a characterization (passion and this..., But the more...), with magnitude amplified by surrounding descriptive context; the identical tokens stay near baseline in eventive, locative, quotative, or concrete uses (was at home, said: hello, milk and eggs).
