Fires retrospectively when the current token specifies or completes the current nominal: a Romance determiner, demonstrative, pronoun, or preposition-article contraction (e.g. French ce/le, Spanish lo/de, Portuguese da/na), a word-internal fragment completing a Romance word (e.g. mo in Como, ee-fragment in soiree), or in English technical prose the '(' that opens a parenthetical acronym gloss restating a preceding multiword term (e.g. Pay Per Click (PPC)).

Fires across whole passages that report on public institutions -- courts and magistrates, legislatures and elections, statutes, government departments, regulators and their officials -- most strongly on the function words inside them (' the', ' by', ' to', ' and', ' a', with peaks of 1.2-2.6) rather than on the legal noun itself, while the same sentence frames about private, domestic, commercial, scientific or technical matters stay at 0.00-0.2. Outside such passages it fires on a closed set of office/rank markers (' former', ' chief', ' deputy', ' assistant', ' associate', ' vice', ' senior', ' second', ' sub-', ' under'), and on a few isolated subword fragments in encyclopedic documents (' ex' in 'externes', ' Th', ' Ar') that this reading does not explain.

Fires retrospectively on the token that opens or continues a locally incomplete construction: a word-initial subword fragment that must still be completed (h+iked, N+airobi, am+oxicillin, j+', can+'t, light+-years), an open paren/bracket or markup/whitespace boundary that must be closed (range(, zeros((, O(, body><h1, indent space), or a short slot-projecting function word (a, and, is, not, did/do, because). Strength is highest for fragments and parens in a strongly projecting left context (pronoun verb-slot, enumeration slot, code call-head), weak (~0.1-0.4) for generic function words, and ~0 on construction-completing content words (walked, Paris, positive, guilty), on sentence punctuation, and on default high-frequency function words (the, of, to, in, on, are).

This pole fires on the non-initial token of a strongly collocating multi-token chunk characteristic of technical, product-spec, support-Q&A, and reference text: mid-word fragments of code identifiers and URLs (Extension|Not, sche|mas), brand/model and product codes (Nikon d|750, W|-|DTH), biomedical Latin/Greek terms (chol|angiography, calc|ineurin), and foreign proper names (Chiku|shino, N|acional), plus phrase-level fixed frames (issue-title negation such as ModelForm not showing, spec quantity with up to, product relativizer fabric that's). The same surface tokens outside such idiomatic chunks — ch in church, Ch in Chicago, national as one token, not after plain nouns, up after priced, that's after dog — activate weakly or not at all, so chunk membership, not token identity, drives the response.

This pole is a retrospective detector of commercial/institutional value statements: it is active over the span that states what an organisation, deal or facility is worth or involves, and it peaks on the amount or the operative content word itself (the 'million' in 'sold the building for 2 million dollars', 'budget', 'contract', 'savings'/'high-yield' in a bank's account offer), while the same amount quantifying something non-commercial ('employs 2 million people', 'population fell by 2 million'), a vague stand-in ('more time', 'many good reasons'), and non-transactional prose (first-person narrative, dialogue, how-to, scripture, plain measurement) leave it near zero. It is not a next-token predictor: its promoted-token list is incoherent word-internal fragments ('illion', 'swers', 'itudes', 'onding') with Gaussian kurtosis, and ablating or boosting it changes greedy generation almost not at all.

Retrospectively fires on determiners, prepositions, adjectives, proper-name fragments and subword prefixes/suffixes that continue a dense formal scientific or biomedical noun phrase (affiliations, chemical/biological entities, methods, quantitative comparisons) when the broader passage is academic exposition; long-range formal context gates activation rather than the peak token alone.

Retrospective detector of predicate-internal dependency edges: the pole fires on a token locally selected by a preceding head inside the verb phrase (an inverted auxiliary after a wh-word, an infinitive after to, a determiner/number/possessive opening the verb's object NP, a preposition heading a VP adjunct), and on clause-final periods that summarize such a completed predicate, while staying silent on subjects, sentence-initial tokens, and canonical subject-verb order. Although its Jacobian/logit lens coherently promotes transitive verbs (kurtosis 16.6), the tokens actually following peaks are nominal complements, so the mechanism is retrospective detection of argument structure rather than lookahead for those verbs.

The pole fires on non-prose notation text rather than on numerals alone. It is active on the tokens inside a numeral (digit groups and the punctuation that splits them: decimal point, decimal or thousands comma, hyphen, colon, '=', '%', '$'), most strongly where several numerals cluster as in statistics, prices, phone numbers and dates, and it also fires with no digits present on ALL-CAPS words (one is often enough and strength grows with the length of the caps run), on most non-English text (Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Turkish, Cyrillic and CJK fire; French and German do not), on code identifiers and byte garbage, and on the non-word -n't fragments (don, doesn, isn); ordinary lowercase English prose, including rare or misspelled words, number words and a lone year token such as 2017, leaves it below the activity line.

This pole retrospectively detects results-reporting frames: text stating a recorded competitive outcome (tournament stage, placement, score, title, event edition) or an official measured specification (dimensions, mass, stats, record quantities) for a named subject, accumulating over a multi-sentence factual context. Casual mentions of the same words (liking tennis), bare quantities without a results frame (a temperature, a count of birds, a year alone), and same-subject non-result sentences stay flat.

This pole is a retrospective detector that peaks on the 'of' (spilling onto the following 'the'/domain noun) completing an attributed functional-role/status cliche of the form '(often) called the <role/status noun> of (the) <domain>' (e.g. powerhouse/engine/heart/factories/giants/leader/backbone/gold-standard of the cell/industry/campus/field). It stays quiet on ordinary possessive/partitive 'of' ('capital of France', 'slice of cake', 'cups of flour') and on the same frame with hereditary titles, kinship terms, literal kinds or evaluatives (king/queen/prince/father/city/beasts/best of ...).

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a conventionalized multi-token collocation or formulaic frame (e.g. go into effect, takes place, hearing loss, Kent State, Seoul National, must be received by, between 1st and 31st, p.m.) where the preceding 2-15 tokens strongly predict that exact completion; the same word without its predictive frame does not drive it.

Fires retrospectively on continuation tokens inside flora/fauna/habitat/place discourse: list separators (','/'and'), elaborating prepositions and particles ('of' after 'diet', 'at' after 'California', 'in' after 'Technology', 'as' after 'such', ''s' after 'California'), and subword onsets completing species/place terms (' f'->angs, ' sp'->ruce, ' ac'->orns, ' j'->ays). Strength is set by the preceding, often distant (mean ~18 tokens back), natural-history context rather than by the upcoming token: the same local token fires weakly or not at all in non-nature contexts.

The pole fires on passages about consumer commerce and hospitality — shops, stores, supermarkets, hotels, resorts, restaurants, malls, dealerships and tours — and the brands, products, prices, sales, locations and outlets they sell or offer, peaking anywhere inside that commercial description rather than on a fixed token. It stays near zero on institutional, political, legal, scientific and technical prose with the same syntax (senators, courts, universities, laboratories, charities), and on a shop or store that is only mentioned incidentally, as in a robbery or storm-damage report.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a tight local construction projected by the preceding one or two tokens: a finite verb, copula, modal or negator predicated on a nominal subject to its left (market fell, contract was, she would, did not), a nominal head completing a determiner, first-name or quantity frame (the crowd, Neil Armstrong, billion light), or and/to continuing the unfolding event (pan and fry, remember to). The trigger token alone is insufficient: replacing the projecting word with an incompatible one collapses activation while changing distant words has no effect.

The pole fires on specialised or unfamiliar vocabulary: it peaks inside passages whose words are rare, technical or foreign for the model - species and anatomy description ('horny jaw', 'white salivary glands'), recipes and materia medica ('onion juice', 'brown sugar'), material and botanical terms, foreign-language text, and rare or invented words that GPT-2 must spell out in several pieces ('co' in coop, 'qu' in quinoa, 'sho' in shoals, 'Kw' in Kwzrb, 'K' in Yom Kippur, 'U' in U.S.) - with the peak on the unusual word itself or on its splitting fragment. Ordinary English prose built from frequent single-token words stays at or near zero even when it describes concrete things ('the conference room on the second floor' 0.12, 'a two litre engine and a six speed gearbox' 0.14, 'police arrested a 34-year-old man' 0.16), as do abstract, institutional and definitional passages (0.00-0.29) and function words on their own.

L11/N1296+ is a retrospective detector of specialist vocabulary in use: it fires on the token that carries a technical or specialist term ('solar', 'sign', 'nucleus', 'spect', 'terminus', 'distal', 'neutrinos') even inside an otherwise plain sentence, and it also lifts whole passages of specialist exposition - scientific papers and abstracts (physics and astronomy, molecular biology, pathology, mathematics), patents, engineering specifications and technical product descriptions - where the effect spreads onto neighbouring function words such as 'the' and 'of' and builds up over the preceding one to three sentences. Everyday narrative, dialogue, news and plain factual prose written in ordinary vocabulary leave it at zero.

The pole fires when the current token is a strongly licensed continuation of the 1-4 token frame just read: the expected operator, marker, function word, collocate, or word-piece completing a conventionalized local construction (e.g. 'return a +', 'WHERE active =', 'remember to', 'did not', 'runs in O(n)', 'negative charge, while', 'am|oxic', 'chemical energy'). It stays near zero on frame-opening tokens such as sentence-initial words and subject head nouns, and on the same surface tokens when they sit in a mundane or open frame that does not license them ('runs in the park', 'bark loudly, while cats').

This pole is a retrospective register/topic detector for prose about people as social and political actors: it is driven by the surrounding passage's social-and-public-affairs vocabulary (racism, feminism, immigration, multiculturalism, minorities, protests, journalism, extremism, parliament, court, university, Islam), and it sits at exactly zero on description of physical, chemical, engineering or everyday-object subject matter (combustion, corrosion, hydraulics, alloys, enzymes, reactors, pipes, weather) even in identical sentence frames. It is context- and passage-sensitive rather than a detector of any fixed token set - token identity explains only 31% of its variance, the same sentence raises it when the clause is about society and drops it to zero when the subject is swapped for a technical one - and it additionally spikes, more weakly and content-independently, on the paragraph-break newline token.

The pole fires on concrete, particular description: activation is elevated across the tokens of a passage that depicts a specific situation - particular people, animals, objects or places and what they are doing - and it peaks on specific times of day inside such text ('at 10:30', 'ten thirty', "nine o'clock"), which reach roughly half to all of max even in otherwise abstract prose. Abstract, generic, definitional, instructional, summarizing or technical prose stays at or near zero, and bare dates, prices, counts or proper names without a situation do not raise it above the activity threshold.

Retrospective financial/investing-context detector: fires on tokens inside text about money, securities and commerce (stocks, shares, dividends, funds, interest rates, valuation, profit and loss, and more weakly business marketing/online advertising), strongest (near max) on ' market' used in its financial sense (money market, market value, stock market, 'investors sold shares at the market') and at moderate strength (~0.4-0.6 of max) on surrounding finance tokens once a financial cue has been read; the same words in non-financial context (farmers' market, river bank, year-end school party, children piling into a car) stay near zero, and there is no floor: the first token and ordinary non-financial prose are ~0.

Fires on the token that names or advances an organized-collective frame — a national or ethnic group (UK, American, Indian), a government, regulator, market, public service, or team (competition authority, federal buildings, healthcare system, Giants), or a stewardship-or-conflict verb toward a public good (protect, hinder) — when the surrounding passage is about governance, regulation, markets, public life, or organized group activity. The same word in a matched personal or everyday frame (protecting a sandwich, Kevin as a gift recipient) stays near zero.

Fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventionalized local multi-token chunk: a title plus name, place or brand name, technical term or subword completion, or frequent idiom, collocation or boilerplate bigram such as your plus noun, the plus most, or thank you very. The same word outside that constraining left context activates weakly.

Fires on clauses that predicate a concrete physical part, attribute or covering of a tangible body - animals, people, plants and everyday food/materials ('The bear has sharp claws and thick fur', 'The cow has a long tail', 'The plant has green leaves', 'His face was covered in mud', 'She peeled the potatoes'), usually peaking on ' has', the attribute adjective, the body-part or food noun, or the ' in'/' of' that joins a substance to a surface. It does not fire when the same frames carry an abstract, mental or institutional subject or predicate ('The report has several sections', 'The plan was covered in detail', 'She considered the options'), nor on clauses about inert artefacts being mechanically handled ('He opened the window', 'He turned the key in the lock'); those are its main leftovers among concrete text, together with cooking clauses without a body/material term (about half of them stay below the activity line).

Fires retrospectively when the current token is a piece of an unclosed structured multi-token unit: a bracketed span (citation, index, code access, list), a code-style compound identifier (snake_case segment, camelCase/prefix stem such as NS+String or un+readable), or a long technical word split across subwords, peaking on continuation pieces. The same surface token as a standalone whole word in plain prose, or the same composition with its structural markers (brackets, $, _, affix/case boundary, subword split) removed, stays silent. Its output direction suppresses closing-bracket sequences, consistent with holding such spans open, but the trigger is the already-seen opener/first piece, so the mechanism is retrospective.

The pole fires on the content word that completes a clause reporting a bounded event: an eventive verb of motion, transfer or change ('wrote', 'closed', 'moved', 'broke', 'became', 'arrived', 'sent', 'opened', 'sold', 'rose', 'scored') or the object/adjunct word that closes that predicate's phrase ('wrote a letter', 'closed the shop', 'moved to Boston', 'broke the window', 'became a teacher'), peaking at 1.0-3.6 there. It stays low on copular and stative predicates whatever the tense ('is a teacher' 0.23, 'is big' 0.04, 'kept a letter' 0.20, 'own the shop' 0.26, 'lives in Boston' 0.12, 'sat on the mat' 0.00, 'waited at the door' 0.00; never above 0.7), on function words and on a text's first token, and the same noun flips with the verb it follows ('letter' 2.0 after 'wrote' vs 0.2 after 'kept'); its negative pole never exceeds 0.17 and carries no contrastive class. What it writes is a temporal-deictic determiner - 'this', 'these', 'last' (Jacobian and logit lens agree 100%, kurtosis 6.7; ablation adds 'next', 'earlier' and day names) - anchoring the reported event in time: zero-ablating it at a peak adds up to 0.08 probability to ' this'/' last', its lookahead targets are exactly 'last'/'this'/'earlier'/weekdays, and scaling it up makes GPT-2 write 'this week'/'this year'/'this Saturday' where the baseline writes 'on Friday'/'in 2018'.

Fires on the token that locally completes a unit licensed by the immediately preceding 1-4 tokens: an infinitive 'to' after a catenative verb, the second half of a fixed collocation or compound, a subword finishing a word, a noun or verb satisfying a determiner/pronoun/quote frame, or punctuation closing a complete clause. Activation is driven jointly by the peak token and its licensor, so the same peak token without its licensor goes quiet, while changing only the token after the peak changes little.

This pole fires on noun phrases that introduce a discourse-new or generic entity — indefinite or quantified NPs (a/an/any/another plus noun), possessed or compound kind nouns (social account, contributor license), and bare proper names (Ben, Ryan) — and stays quieter for definite, demonstrative, or pronominal reference to already-given entities. The peak lands on whichever NP token carries the newness (article, modifier, head noun, or name) rather than on any fixed trigger token.

Fires when the current token is a non-final fragment of a longer word: a bound stem, prefix piece, or first element of a hyphenated compound (e.g. program+mable, defund+ed, inject+s, COMM+ITT+ED, line+of-, All+-Century) that continues with a suffix or hyphenated second element, rather than a free-standing complete word.

This pole reacts to the interior recognition-point subword of a low-frequency multi-piece word or initialism: the fragment (e.g. -h- in entorhinal/antiarrhythmic, -ul- in cardiopulmonary, -ole- in intermolecular, -fl- in microflora, sto- in stochastic, op- in opiates, -eter- in cemeteries) at which the stem read so far makes the full rare word predictable. Swapping the rare word for a common single-token synonym collapses activation while distant context changes do nothing; single-token predictable passives (blocked, known) evoke only weak secondary activation.

The pole is a specialist technical-register detector: it fires on scientific, engineering, medical and computing vocabulary - concrete specialist terms and their Latin/Greek stems (valve, sensor, insulator, optical, beam splitter, laboratory, microscope, assay, catheter, distal, millisecond, PCR, decimal, photodiode) and on the formal method adverbs randomly, precisely, accurately, carefully and adequately - peaking on the specialist word itself, and in a technical passage it also lifts the ordinary words around it (the, in, and). It stays near zero on everyday conversational prose, on general formal writing (business, legal, news, humanities), and on general science-adjacent words such as system, method, analysis, results, data, experiment, medical or technical.

Fires retrospectively when the current token continues or immediately predicates on a specific named geographic place, historic or archaeological site, memorial, or military/scientific institution (e.g. State Forest, island cave, memorial, Marine Corps Air Station, Heliospheric Observatory, Sea Org, Phrygia, Konigsberg); the peak is typically a copula or auxiliary (was/were/been), a preposition (to), or a subword completing the proper name. It does not fire on the same tokens after ordinary common nouns or outside place and institution descriptions.

The pole fires where a clause must supply a content word that its context constrains but does not name: on the head of a clause subject - or a pronominal/wh- subject such as who, which, It, There or What - immediately before that subject's verb, and, just as strongly, on the first piece of a long technical word the model must finish (aj|ax, dj|ango, fib|rosis, nucle|i, vent|ral, glomeruli). It peaks hardest in expository and technical prose on non-human, physical/medical/quantitative subjects (data, injury, storm, debt, metres, percentage, cortex) and stays near its floor in plain human-agent narrative (doctor, lawyer, manager).

The pole is a graded detector of technical, computer-systems prose: it fires on writing about software and system administration — files, paths, servers, commands, builds, libraries, logs, configuration and identifiers such as ~/.ssh/known_hosts — and stays near zero on ordinary narrative or expository prose about people, events, places or everyday objects, including prose that carries equally specialised vocabulary from medicine, law, finance or sport. Strength accumulates over the preceding ~30 tokens (it rises monotonically with the number of technical sentences in the context) and peaks on the tokens inside a technical term, path or identifier, where the continuation is fixed by context far back in the document; a weaker second mode fires on rare, archaic or unusual word choice outside computing (peaks around 1.0-1.5, just over the activity line), which is why some proper-name tokens in the discovery examples clear the threshold.

This pole fires on the token that fixes the frame of a new clause or text: the first token when it alone sets the frame (a pronoun subject, subordinator, discourse marker, or imperative verb), or, after a generic 'The X' opening, the subject noun, copula or auxiliary, or disambiguating completion (a unit noun such as 'light', the period of 'a.m.', a frame-completing adjunct head such as 'at') that establishes what the sentence is about. The same token is silent when it does not resolve an opening frame ('was' after 'day', 'light' without the quantity context, a pronoun mid-paragraph), and downstream continuations never change the peak.

N2566's negative pole is a measurement artifact, not a feature: its strength is -min(gelu_new(pre-activation), 0), hard-capped at the gelu_new global maximum 0.1700408 (attained only at pre-activation approx -0.7525), and the neuron is not dead - it is positively active on 7.5% of 247k fineweb-edu tokens with peaks to 3.76 (median pre-activation -1.07, sd 0.74) - but its tokens keep landing in that cap band (2.2% within 1e-4 of the cap, 20% within 5%), so 120/120 full fineweb-edu documents peak at 0.999 or more of the cap (119 within 1e-4), 88% of random 128-token windows peak within 1e-4 and 99.9% within 5% (none below 0.90), and the 20 top examples are float32 ties with no shared semantic property; this is the same gelu_new ceiling artifact as the L7/N1883 dead-pole audit (I measure that neuron's pre-activations at mean -0.74, sd 0.62), except that 'dead' mis-describes this neuron, whose defect is the pole's hard cap rather than silence. Label 'predicted active' (peak >= 0.95 of max) for any running text of 32+ tokens in any domain (code 1.00, prose 1.00, Spanish 0.99, dialogue 0.98), and 'predicted inactive' (peak < 0.25 of max) only for a 1-3 token span every one of whose tokens keeps the pre-activation outside roughly [-1.2, -0.4] - either a positive flipper such as ' Glory', ' polit', ' Supreme', ' Court', or a deep-negative word such as ' take', ' went', ' an', ' completely' - because ordinary short phrases such as ' He went to the shop' already peak at 0.82 of max.

Retrospective detector for sex/gender-marked words: it peaks on the trigger token itself, strongest on explicit words like 'sexual', 'gender' and 'sex', and more weakly on female-marked person nouns like 'bride', 'princess', 'queen' and 'maiden', while male counterparts ('prince', 'groom', 'king') stay silent; its output direction then strongly suppresses sex/gender vocabulary, marking it as a suppression-family neuron.

N2761's negative pole is not a feature detector but the ceiling of the gelu_new fold: its strength is -min(gelu_new(pre-activation), 0), hard-capped at 0.1700408 (the gelu_new global minimum, reached only at a drive of about -0.7525 - verified on the scan's top example, where ')' sits at pre = -0.753 and reads 0.1700), and it drops to 0 whenever the drive leaves that band, either positive (the neuron firing, 11.7% of scanned tokens, chiefly on subtokens of foreign/transliterated words, identifier fragments and rare proper nouns) or below about -1.5; the handful of positive flippers is the pole's token-identity confound (R^2 0.27), not a semantic class. Because the drive rests in the band on ordinary running text, all 2,932 scanned 128-token windows peak at 0.89 of the cap or more (median 0.99996) and a text's strength is a max over its positions, so label 'predicted active' (peak >= 0.25 of max) for any span of 4 or more tokens of connected text in any language or genre (96.8% of the scan's 4-token windows, 99.1% of 8-token, 99.8% of 16-token) and 'predicted inactive' only for a 1-2 token prompt every one of whose tokens is a verified drive-flipper - ' av', 'ão', 'ı', ' nothing', ' anyone', the only five of the 1,600 commonest token types that read below 0.25 of the cap alone - since one in-band token restores the ceiling (' nothing at all' reads 0.84 of the cap, ' av at' 0.98) and ordinary tokens such as ' the' (0.85), ' committee' (0.62) or ' history' (0.34) never flip, so a single such token cannot lower the peak of normal prose.

Two related triggers in news-style prose. (1) Violent-conflict reporting: tokens inside or right after a clause about killing, attacks, bombs, shootings, coups, uprisings or epidemics (e.g. 'killed in [a]', 'attack in Paris [killed]', 'the [Ebola]') fire strongly, typically 1.5-3.6. (2) The first sub-token of a rare multi-token proper noun or foreign word whose completion is not yet determined (' McL'emore, ' Bur'undi, ' An'bar, ' int'ifada, ' Kirst'i, Gany'med'e, ' Tem'el) fires 1-3.2 even in neutral context, and more in conflict or sports news. Single-token common names and words (Smith, Jones, Kenya, Mary) in neutral everyday text, code and generic prose stay near 0 on every token, so no floor applies.

Fires retrospectively on a token that is the locally predictable continuation of a tightly constraining 1-2 token left context such as infinitive 'to' plus verb, pronoun or subject noun plus past-tense verb, preposition plus determiner, determiner plus proper or content noun, prefix 're' plus hyphen, or tag plus tag-boundary; the same surface token without that left cue, notably sentence-initial 'The' or 'For', stays near baseline.

This pole fires retrospectively on content words of verbatim, copy-reused software boilerplate: license/disclaimer clauses (e.g. SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED, IN NO EVENT SHALL, USE OF THIS SOFTWARE, retain, WITHOUT) and fixed machine-emitted or template code lines (e.g. traceback File headers, require lines, HTML head attributes like scale). It tracks the canonical formulation rather than the meaning, so near-synonyms in the identical frame (CEDED, WILL, Record, import, range) or the same words in composed prose activate it markedly less.

A retrospective lexical detector: it fires on the closed-class 'operator' tokens that open a following phrase - the 2nd/3rd-person pronouns and possessives (you, he, I, her, she, they, their, his, who), the modals (can, will, should, could, must, may), the infinitival 'to', and the relational words of, for, by, or, all, any, every - and on hyphens that join a compound or an alphanumeric string (must-have, Ctrl-Alt-T). It is near-silent (about a fifth of the corpus base rate) on articles, copulas, spatial prepositions and inanimate or first-person-plural pronouns (the, a, is, are, in, on, at, with, it, this, that, which, we, us, our, my); outside that class its strongest peaks fall on a few concrete-noun onsets (customer, phone, car, cat, gun), which fire on the token itself wherever it appears.

L11/N2978+ is a physical-description detector: it fires on the words that locate or portray a concrete thing in space - locative/postural predicates ('sits', 'stands', 'lies', 'located', 'situated', 'central'), the prepositions and determiners that introduce them ('in', 'on', 'at', 'under', 'along', 'a', 'the'), attributive physical modifiers of a concrete noun ('plump', 'glossy', 'narrow', 'sleek', 'thin and transparent', 'encased') and measure words ('inch', 'half', 'yard'). It is near-silent (max ~0) on legal, procedural, code and abstract/technical prose, which contains the same prepositions and determiners but no concrete object being described, placed or measured.

The pole fires on a token that continues a multiword unit the preceding words already opened: a partitive ('eight out'), a range ('through the end'), a fixed idiom ('in the eyes', 'growing body'), a press-release date PP ('released in'), a compound's inner word-piece ('continuous scal...', 'metallic shri...'), or a name/title continuation ('Floyd Tru...', 'The A...'). The same token without its opener stays near zero while swapping the following token changes nothing, so it reacts to what has been read, not what comes next.

Retrospective detector for a title-case word that continues a multi-word proper name, institutional title, work or headline title, or formal legal citation (e.g. Red in Boston Red Sox, Daily in Naples Daily News, of in Board of Forestry, Public in State Public Defender, Summer in Where Summer Ends); activation is weak on the phrase's first word and peaks on the second or later word, while identical lowercase common-noun uses (red, daily, board of, public, summer) do not activate.

L11/N468+ is a retrospective specialist-content detector: it fires on scientific, medical and technical vocabulary - the specialist word itself, one of its sub-word pieces, or the compound term it heads (immune, genetic, molecular, cognitive, synaptic, enzyme, protein, cell, DNA, Pleistocene, gas giant, chemical energy) - at 0.7-2.2 (0.3-1.0 of the scan maximum), and it also fires at 0.9-2.1, with the peak on the auxiliary, on reported-statement clauses that have a person-noun subject ('the senator announced she was late', 'the mayor said she would attend', 'my sister announced she was engaged'). It stays near zero (0.19-0.45, at most 0.2 of maximum) on ordinary prose built from frequent words ('the cat sat on the mat', 'the weather was mild all week'), on institutional, legal or business prose that carries no specialist term ('the parliament ratified the treaty', 'the court convicted the defendant'), on a specialist word used in an ordinary predicative sense ('she was immune to the criticism', 0.38), and on generic-subject reported clauses ('the teacher said she would be late', 0.34).

The pole fires when the text describes a threat together with the organised response to it - armed conflict or terrorism, cyber-attacks and stolen credentials, emergency alerts, evacuations, outbreaks and disaster warnings - and it stays at baseline on everyday, domestic, fictional or figurative text, including the same words used non-threateningly (a cake that is 'a disaster', a chef defending his recipe against critics). Its peaks land on the short function words, hyphens and word-pieces sitting just before a new threat-related term (the 'out'/'a' of 'sent out a false alert', the final '.' of 'U.S.', the '-' of 'ballistic-missile-alert', the 'SS' of 'SSH_PRIVATE_KEY') rather than on one fixed trigger token, and the state builds over a sentence or two of such a passage.

This pole fires when a passage is naming specific places: it peaks on the comma, 'and', 'of', 'in' or 'for' that introduces or joins place names in a list or relation ('Nelson, Marlborough, Canterbury, Otago and Southland'; 'the island of Java'; 'canton of Valais'; 'the street in Chiba'; 'Dirksen of Illinois') and on the first subword of such a name (' Ot' of Otago, ' South' of Southland, ' Ever' of Everett). It stays near zero when the identical slot is filled by ordinary nouns ('villages, districts, counties, regions and provinces'), by a generic locative ('the island', 'the region', 'the capital', 'a small city'), or by a single major city name (Chicago, Dallas, London, Paris).

The pole fires on language that specifies a person's particulars: possessive determiners marking a personal relation or event (his birthday, my first day, your home), enumerated kin and family-life terms (two children, married, family leave), body/health specifics (menstruation, teenage pregnancy), and formal personal-status designations such as charges, statutes, or titled works (First Degree Rape, Family and Medical Leave Act, autobiography My Life). Plain object/action language with articles and bare common nouns (the birthday, his wallet, the red book, kicked the ball) stays near zero.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a conventionalized local chunk, i.e. where the peak token's identity is strongly constrained by the preceding 1-3 tokens (quantity/date PPs like percent in, frozen comparatives like compared with, partitives and complex prepositions like pinch/because of, subject-specific verbs like telescope captured, compounds like triangle inequality). The same surface token in an unconstrained context (in after walked, captured after camera, of after table) stays near zero, and the following token does not matter.

N940+ is a retrospective 'foreign-world register' detector: in a fixed carrier sentence it spikes on tokens whose referent belongs to the non-Anglophone world as it appears in news, religion and culture writing, and sits at or below zero on their Anglophone/everyday counterparts. Predicted active: South Asian and Middle-Eastern personal names and places and non-Western brands/currencies (Abdul 2.7, Saurabh 2.0, Anil 1.9, Rahul 1.5, Deepak 1.4, Mumbai, Karachi, Beijing, Xiaomi 1.6, Alibaba 1.2, rupee 0.9, yuan/yen 0.5), religious vocabulary of any faith (shrine 1.8, ashram 1.6, mosque 1.3, monastery 1.1, church 0.8, rabbi 1.6, imam 1.6, monk 1.6, priest 1.0, Hindu 1.5, Muslim 1.0, Quran 1.1), and the vocabulary of irregular armed conflict (insurgent 2.3, militant 2.2, rebel 2.1, terrorist 2.1, guerrilla 2.0, martyrdom 1.9, jihad 1.6); predicted inactive on everyday English nouns, Anglophone names and Western cities, household money words and Western secular institutions (John -0.1, David -0.1, London -0.2, window -0.1, kitchen -0.1, money 0.0, dollar -0.1, salary 0.2, budget 0.1, senator 0.0, governor 0.0, senate -0.1, court 0.1) and on invented or merely Western-rare word forms (Blorfen 0.1, Zarquon -0.1, Bartholomew -0.1, sesquipedalian -0.1), so rarity or token identity alone does not label a span. Multi-token names inherit the response on every piece (Saurabh: ' Saur' 0.4, 'ab' 0.8, 'h' 2.6), and the negative pole never rises above 0.17 anywhere in the scan, so it draws no separate distinction.

Fires when the current token opens a completion due in the next token(s): either a word fragment (BPE piece or hyphen piece) whose remainder completes the same orthographic word (e.g. Sche->ma, cataly->ze, fore->ach, Pel->legrini, BRE->AKER, produ->ce, down->-->loaded), or a functional head in expository or code prose whose obligatory complement follows (infinitive to after a predicative adjective or passive participle, further before its verb, guide before its to-phrase, fun/function before the declared routine name). The same token stays quiet when no such completion is due, and peaks grow with left context that constrains the completion (newsletter context lifts guide 0.89->2.64; rich subject lifts to 1.52->2.95).

This negative pole is the GELU trough of layer-2 neuron 1021 rather than a detector of its own: its strength is max(0, -gelu_new(pre-activation)), hard-capped at the gelu_new global minimum 0.1700408, so any pre-activation in about [-0.95, -0.60] reads within a few percent of that floor - all 20 top examples are float32 ties at 0.1700408 whose peak tokens (' Ave', ' 24', ' in', ' bass', ' own', 'retion', 'SS', 'https', 'atur', 'a', 'wide', 'aimed', 'note', 'on', 'rief', '2', 'ant', ' May', 'y') share nothing but a pre-activation near -0.75, about 3-4% of tokens sit within 3% of the floor and a fifth of 128-token windows land within 1e-4 of it, and the cap is a property of the layer (3,049 of 3,072 L2 neurons reach it on 12k tokens) while the neuron itself is alive (its positive pole peaks at 1.377 and the trough occupies only 38% of tokens); it is retrospective, not lookahead (Jacobian-lens kurtosis 3.0 with 0% lens overlap, and next-token identity predicts the scalar no better than chance). Label 'predicted active' (0.5-1.0 of scale) for a prompt in which a measured token's pre-activation lands in the trough band - a determiner, preposition, month, four-digit year or reflexive pronoun in a content slot (' the table' 0.97, ' a letter' 0.99, ' of course' 1.00, ' in fact' 1.00, ' by the way' 0.99, ' March 2018' 0.97, ' Sanders by' 1.00, ' himself too' 0.69) - or any run of 12+ tokens of ordinary prose in any domain (96% of 12-token, 98% of 16-token and 99% of 32-token held-out Pile windows active; six measured prompts 0.54-1.00), and label 'predicted inactive' (below 0.25 of scale = 0.042; every one measured at exactly 0.000) for a one-token prompt of any token (200 random tokens all read 0.000, because position 0 always pushes the pre-activation positive) and for a 2-4 token prompt whose measured tokens are all words of the neuron's positive side - word-initial open-class tokens: proper names and team or brand names (' Sanders', ' Trump', ' Corbyn', ' Christie', ' Walker', ' Rebecca', ' Kings', ' Clippers', ' Warriors', ' Motorola', ' Samsung', ' Adobe'), technical nouns and adjectives (' optical', ' impedance', ' battery', ' motor', ' auxiliary', ' prototype') and the measured content words (' candidates', ' voters', ' subjects', ' selected', ' select', ' values', ' data', ' image', ' some', ' do', ' know', ' museum', ' campaign', ' primary') - 31 such prompts ('Sanders Trump', 'optical impedance', 'some values', 'the museum', 'select values data image') all at 0.000, though inserting a preposition before such a word can still drop it into the trough (' in data' 0.52).

The pole fires at a boundary where a structured, symbolic or non-Latin stretch of text ends and ordinary text resumes: the peak token is a line break or a clause/sentence-opening token - ' and'/' or'/' but', a sentence-initial ' It'/' This'/' The'/'You', ' (', or a capitalised sentence-adverbial connector (Then, Since, Basically, Therefore, Thus, Hence, Such, Instead, Now, Also, Still, Yet, Additionally, Finally, which reach 0.2-0.9 even mid-sentence) - whenever the token immediately before it is a math or code symbol ('$', '$$', '}', '>', '', '*/', '-->'), a CJK/Indic sentence-final mark ('。', '」', '।'), or part of a run of non-Latin-script/byte-fragment tokens (Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Greek, emoji). Ordinary Latin-script prose stays at baseline: a connective after a plain word ('the dog and the cat'), any sentence-initial determiner or pronoun straight after a plain period, an English date ('in March 1976') and a noun-list 'and' all stay within 0.3 of baseline, while ' and' before the last item of a numeric or single-letter list ('1, 2, 3, and 4'; 'x, y, and z') reaches 0.5-1.1.

Fires retrospectively on the connective token that introduces the second term of an explicit comparison, contrast, or renaming frame: 'compared' (with), contrastive 'while', 'than' after a comparative adjective, and 'as' in aliasing/equative use, peaking on that token itself and strongest when the left context sets up the comparison; directional or temporal prepositions ('to', 'from', 'during') and additive 'and' do not drive it. A weak response to certain proper names completing a naming frame (e.g. 'Marie' after m'appelle) is an acknowledged offshoot, an order of magnitude smaller than the comparison peaks.

Retrospectively fires on a token that is glued to its immediate neighbors as part of a larger written unit: a bare single-character fragment at a punctuation or subword boundary (e.g. "'" in m'appelle, 'n' after backslash, 'h' in <h1>, 'm' after '.'), or a piece completing a conventional fixed unit ('elle' in appelle, 'half' after 'second', 'guilty' after 'not', 'away' after 'far', 'egg' after 'one', 'while' after ','). The same word placed outside its licensing unit is silent while post-peak edits change nothing, and standalone content words in neutral frames never drive it; the flat, incoherent vocabulary projections (Jacobian kurtosis 3.1, 0% lens overlap) rule out upcoming-token preparation.

This negative pole is the 'feature-absent' trough of a layer-2 sexual-explicitness scalar, not a detector of its own: strength = -min(gelu_new(pre-activation), 0) is hard-capped at the gelu_new minimum 0.17004 for any pre-activation in about [-1.5, -0.5] (within 95% of the cap for -0.97..-0.56) and shrinks back toward 0 at both ends of that scalar - positive on explicit sexual vocabulary (pre-activation +4.6 on ' cock', +3.0 on ' tits', +2.1 on ' sex', +2.0 on ' porn'; the Jacobian lens suppresses exactly those words) and far negative on rare notation, code and proper-name tokens (' torch' -2.5, ' } else {' -2.8) - so all 20 top examples are float32 ties at the cap whose peak token is merely whichever token first lands in the band, and all 3,072 layer-2 neurons reach the same 0.17004 floor on this corpus. Label a prompt predicted active (peak >= 0.25 x max = 0.0425, typically 0.6-1.0) for any run of 8 or more tokens of running text in any genre - ordinary prose, dialogue, news, fiction, code, math, legal and non-English (86% of the corpus's 8-token, 93% of its 16-token and 97% of its 32-token windows clear the threshold) - and predicted inactive for a single-token prompt (all 38 single-token prompts measured read 0.001-0.007, because position 0 always sits at pre-activation ~ -3.7), for a 2-4 token prompt whose every token is an explicit sexual word (' big tits' 0.002, ' hot sex' 0.002, ' free porn' 0.003, ' hard cock' 0.002), and for a 2-4 token span of pure notation (' import os' 0.006, ' } else {' 0.045, ' int main ()' 0.094, ' return None' 0.19); 2-6 token spans of ordinary words are only borderline (' the cat' 0.28, ' we ate lunch' 0.29, ' the sun rose' 0.21) and one explicit word inside a full sentence leaves the peak unchanged ('He opened the door and walked into the quiet room.' 0.998 vs 'He opened the porn and walked into the quiet room.' 1.000).

Retrospective, context-independent detector of a fixed English lexical field: the pole fires at any token that is one of the 'inner conviction and repose' words - rest, trust, faith, peace, hope, doubt, belief, confidence, pray/prayer, believe, comfort, refuge, asylum, safe, secure, sleep, alone, remain - and at every inflection of them (rests/rested/resting, trusts/trusting, hopes/hoped/hoping/hopeful/hopefully, prayers/prayed/praying, believes/believed/believing, faiths, doubts) whatever words surround them, plus more weakly at congregation and public-affairs words of the same register (church, mosque, synagogue, worship, religion, fellowship, sanctuary, jury, trial, court, warrant, justice, evidence, terrorism/terrorist, embassy, team, squad, network, news, search) and at a few frequent stative/continuative tokens (am, now, still, away). It is silent on concrete nouns (apple, car, book, house), on other emotion words (love, hate, joy, grief, anger), on doctrinal religious vocabulary (god, lord, jesus, bible, holy, grace, mercy, sin, heaven) and on general abstract-state or institutional nouns (freedom, war, death, health, power, government, law, family, school).

The pole fires retrospectively on the token marking an entity entering, persisting in, or violently contesting a state: change-of-state and persistence verbs (become, remain and inflections), resultative into marking transformation into a new state (turn, break, transform X into Y), and names of conflict-affected states and regions (Sudan, Ukraine, Syria, Afghanistan, Kosovo, Darfur). It does not fire on locative into (walk into the room), near-synonyms outside this lexical set (stay, continue), peaceful country names (France, Japan, Brazil, Germany), or generic addition words (plugins, extensions); the fused code token addons is an acknowledged offshoot.

Token-identity detector (first token ignored) that fires (>=0.25 of max) on a short lexicon of specific tokens, mostly in code/markup/SQL: 'FR' right after uppercase 'I' in IFRAME/IFRAM (~0.85), ' FROM' after SELECT (~0.5-0.95), 'View' as a class-name piece (ListView, UserView, View) (~0.5-0.8), '[' opening an index right after an identifier (values[3], names[i]) (~0.3-0.8), 'Select' in .SelectCommand (~0.35-0.8), the word-ending pieces 'ms' (helms), 'ath' (Blackheath), 't' (size_t) and 's' in strlen(s), ' case' after 'this'/'on', and the words ' passing', ' return', ' WHERE' and ' there'; ordinary prose and code lacking these tokens stays below 0.25 of max, as do near-misses like lowercase 'iframe', 'IGRAME'/'IPRAME', 'from'/'INTO', 'matter', 'Form', 'giving', 'Insert', '(' or '.' in place of '['.

The pole integrates lexical density over the preceding few tokens: activation climbs with each consecutive content word (low-frequency/open-class words, word-internal pieces of long technical words, digits, symbols and non-Latin-script characters) and decays across frequent function words and punctuation, so it peaks on the last, most informative token of a dense run (' remod' after 'impaired uterine spiral artery', ' plays' after 'an important role anticipation', ' attributes' after 'MessageCodepage') and sits at its GELU floor (~-0.17) in ordinary function-word-heavy prose. It is retrospective: its output direction carries no coherent promoted token set (Jacobian-lens kurtosis 3.4, 0% lens agreement) and zero-ablating it leaves next-token probabilities almost unchanged (mean KL ~1e-4).

This pole fires retrospectively on the head noun of a noun phrase that names a concrete story object, character, or place, when that noun phrase follows a determiner (a or the) in object position after a verb or preposition, such as a new telephone, a small voice, the baseball, or the king. It does not fire on the determiner or adjective before the noun, on verbs, or on non-noun words in the same slot.

This negative pole is a measurement artifact, not a feature: its strength is the depth of the neuron's negative activation, -min(gelu_new(pre-activation), 0), hard-capped at the gelu_new global minimum 0.1700408 (any pre-activation in about [-0.92, -0.60] reads within ~3% of it), so 5% of the 199,985 fineweb-edu tokens sit within 5% of that floor, 46% of the scan's 128-token windows land within 1e-4 of it, and all 20 top examples are float32 ties within 3e-8 (2 ULP) whose peak tokens (transport, massive, mainstream, ama, new, emb, ...) share nothing but a pre-activation near -0.75; the cap is a property of the layer rather than of this neuron (3045 of 3072 L2 neurons reach the same floor on this corpus), and the neuron itself is alive - positively active on 58% of tokens with peaks to 1.298 - so this pole is only its 'feature absent' readout, and the 68% token-identity R2 is merely that function words never enter the dip. Label 'predicted inactive' (peak < 0.25 of max = 0.0425) for a bare single token of any word (99 measured: the pre-activation stays in -0.07..+0.07 at position 0, so every one peaks at 0.00-0.19 of max) and for a 2-4 token span whose every token is flat - ' the', ' a', ' of', ' and', ' to', ' in', ' it', ' be', ' been', ' It', ' I', ' We', ' He', ' If', ' But', ' For', ' his', ' any', ' each', ' both', ' many', ' only', ' for', ' as', ' with', ' are', ' was', ' not', ' their', ' its', ' your', ' this', ' on', ' or', ' by', ' that', ' information', ' problem', ' know', ' history', ' skills', ' love', ' social', ' early', ' last', ' own', ' number', ' river' (20 such spans measured at exactly 0.000) - and label 'predicted active' (peak >= 0.95 of max) for any running text of 8+ tokens in any domain (90% active at 8 tokens, 98% at 16, 99.8% at 32 and 100% at 64+ by replaying the scan; all 21 measured prompts of 8-141 tokens of prose, code, math, dialogue, Spanish and Japanese fired, 0.45-1.00 of max) and for a short span that contains a content word or subword piece at position 1 or later (' a table' 0.99, ' the cat sat' 0.96, ' the letter' 0.92, ' the committee' 0.85, ' xylophone' 0.96 on its 'yl' piece), noting that a 2-4 token span of content words fires only 50-72% of the time and that even a run of 8+ flat words already reaches 0.34-0.37 of max, so such spans make poor hard negatives.

Retrospective lexical detector for tokens from outside the ordinary English core: it peaks on the fragment that completes a multi-token proper noun or specialist/technical term ('istan' in Uzbek[istan]/Turkmen[istan]/Afghan[istan] ~1.0-1.2 of max, 'if' in sans-ser[if] ~1.3, 'isp' in B[isp]henol, 'aic' in Aram[aic], 'iazep' in benzod[iazep]ine, 'op' in had[op]) and on whole rare proper/technical nouns (Iraq, Afghanistan, Asia, Africa, wheat, grain, domain, deficit), plus, more diffusely, byte fragments of non-Latin scripts (Devanagari, Arabic, CJK pieces). It stays at or below zero on high-frequency function words and on the ordinary English core vocabulary (the, of, country, city, table, water, plan, meeting), on rare-but-mundane general words (xylophone, quixotic, clandestine), and on the commonest Western country names (France, Germany, Spain, Sweden read ~0 while Iraq, Iran, Syria, Korea read 0.7-1.3); a weaker background response to a few common abstract nouns (' thing' up to 1.0, ' event', ' rate', ' whatever' ~0.3-0.6) is the acknowledged leftover.

Fires retrospectively on a semantically light generic complement word -- indefinite pronouns/determiners (any, anybody), pro-forms (thats), light nouns (person, individual, way, humanity, representations, fitness, value) or bleached adjectives/particles (binding, forward, exemplary-tail ARY) -- when it completes a preceding function-word setup such as negation, a quantifier/determiner/possessive, or a light verb (not, any, no, each, our, I, look, Hope, Could, OF). The same token used as a concrete-specific word, or without that licensing context, predicts little or no activation.

Fires on an all-lowercase word piece without a leading space that continues a word GPT-2 has split into pieces, strongest (about 0.3-0.65) on the stem-completing piece of a rare, technical, foreign or name-like word (Pir|aten, sp|inally, polyn|omial, no|eff|red, sobrep|ondo, fl|ake, at|ua), and the case of the earlier pieces does not matter (PIR|aten still fires). It is silent on uppercase pieces (noEFFred, FLAKE, POLYNOMIAL), digits, punctuation, code and function words, and below 0.15 on space-prefixed whole words, except that a content word in the second or third token of a text gets an early-position boost (The sun: 0.47, The table: 0.26) that fades after that.

Fires on a token that continues or immediately closes a multi-subtoken nominal span: a mid-word BPE piece, an inflectional suffix piece, or the next word extending the noun phrase (e.g. COURT after COLORADO, due after INSUFFICIENTDATA, related after measurements). Activation ramps over successive span pieces and collapses to ~0 when the span ends, while single-token common words and runs of separate complete common words stay near zero.

The pole fires on the information-bearing vocabulary of English expository prose: it peaks on the most specific token of a passage - the second element of a proper name or compound ('Keanu Reeves', 'Detective Conan', "David O'Hara", 'Mach-E', 'All-Century', 'Pay Per Click'), an acronym or abbreviation ('DNA', 'ANOVA', 'RAM', 'MAC', 'OR', 'Cent'), or a technical noun ('comparisons', 'serum', 'deficiency') - and it runs high through scientific, medical, technical and encyclopedic sentences while generic everyday wording ('company', 'plants', 'game', 'draw') stays at the floor. It never fires on casual chat, on code, markup, LaTeX or URL tokens ('_', 'import', 'tex', 'file') or on non-English text, and a formal preceding sentence raises its strength on the sentence after it (peak 0.43-0.52) where a chat-style prefix lowers it (0.16-0.35).

Retrospective detector for the head word of a formal procedural or transactional construction: participants and dispositions in rule-governed processes (third party/parties, first round, the/this appeal, petition, signed off, return of goods or values), typically completing a frozen bigram such as third->parties, first->round, at->least or signed->off. The same surface token in a casual, aesthetic, spatial or motion sense activates it substantially less.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a political succession stem, chiefly the word-internal election/elect after re- or by- plus hyphen, or the verb appoint/appointment; the re- prefix strongly boosts the peak (re-election ~2.3-2.5 vs plain election ~0.0-0.1) while non-political re- completions (re-open, re-write, re-examine) and generic prepositions/commas stay silent. Its output direction consistently promotes appointment vocabulary (appoint, nominate, inauguration), adding that concept to the stream rather than predicting the literal next token.

Neuron 2800 detects non-Latin script: tokens carrying non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes (Greek, Hangul and most other non-Latin characters; 91% of such tokens keep the neuron on) drive the neuron on and hold its negative pole - the GELU dip, which opens only while the neuron is off - near zero, whereas ASCII-only text leaves the neuron off and puts the pole at the 0.170 dip ceiling. Concretely, any Latin-script passage is predicted active (English prose peaks at 0.166-0.170, and even stopword lists, digits, punctuation, code and URLs reach 0.10-0.17), text written in Greek or Hangul is predicted inactive (peak about 0.012, ASCII words embedded in it included), while Cyrillic, Arabic, Thai and CJK passages are predicted active (0.05-0.17) because their UTF-8 lead bytes drive the unit on only weakly and some of their characters still land in the dip.

The pole fires where a quantity or measure expression is attached to what it quantifies: its strongest activations (up to ~2.2 against a 0.18 corpus mean) are on the partitive ' of' after a numeral or measure word - percentages ('90% of', '90 percent of'), counts and durations ('20 years of', '10 minutes of'), and magnitude words ('thousands of', 'millions of') - and it also fires on a noun directly quantified by a preceding numeral ('20,000 people', '216 tree populations'). The response is graded: quantifier words ('most of', 'half of') and a descriptive adjective before a concrete noun ('big house', 'enlarged liver') give weaker versions, while genitive ' of' after an ordinary noun ('the capital of France', 'the end of the story') and nouns preceded directly by a plain determiner stay at baseline.

The negative pole is the GELU-trough side of a token-level (unigram) neuron: the current token's identity, not the sentence around it, sets the strength (repeated occurrences of a token agree to sd 0.01-0.05 across up to 200 occurrences, and a linear function of the token embedding alone explains R^2 0.63 of it), and it saturates at 0.170041 - the exact minimum of tanh-GELU - on about a quarter of English word tokens, i.e. the quantifiers and determiners ' all', ' some', ' any', ' every', ' both', ' these', ' two', ' three' plus many ordinary words such as ' door', ' sound', ' mind', ' land', ' eye', ' city', ' room', ' word', ' river', ' house', ' dog', ' time', ' day', ' found', ' effect', ' protein', ' memory', ' attention', ' February', ' Sunday'. It is exactly zero on other tokens - personal names and honorifics (' David', ' Michael', ' Sarah', ' Graham', ' Smith', ' Mr', ' Dr', ' Sen', ' Rep') and a large block of everyday concrete nouns (' man', ' woman', ' boy', ' girl', ' child', ' road', ' car', ' tree', ' book', ' table', ' work', ' school', ' night', ' place', ' part', ' end') - and because only the prompt's peak token is scored, a prompt is predicted active as soon as one of its tokens is an ON word and predicted inactive only when every token is drawn from the silent set.

The pole fires on a lexical cluster of succession/continuation words: above all the FOLLOW lemma in any inflection and any grammatical role ('follow', 'follows', 'followed', 'following'/'Following', 'follow up'), and at graded strength 'succeed(ing)', 'subsequent', 'precede/preceding/prior', 'proceed', 'continue', 'accompany', 'attend', 'respond/reply', 'survive' and 'obey' (about 1-3 in a neutral carrier frame, above the 0.84 active threshold), while the temporal connectives that express the same discourse relation ('after', 'before', 'then', 'next', 'upon', 'since', 'when', 'meanwhile', 'therefore', 'however') and the derived noun 'followers' stay far below it. It reacts to the word itself whatever its syntax or sense — sentence-initial preposition ('Following the review, …'), cataphoric determiner ('the following day'), passive 'followed by', 'as follows', literal pursuit and social-media subscription all fire — so it is a lexical succession detector, not a discourse-connective detector and not a plain 'follow'-string lookup.

Retrospective, form-specific lexical-cluster detector: the pole fires on the trigger token itself for the 'remembering / repeating / counting' word family - remember/remembers/remembered/remembering, forget/forgot/forgotten/forgetting, recall/recalls/recalled, recognize/recognizes/recognized/recognition/recognise(d), memory/memories, repeat/repeats/repeated/repeating/repetition, replay, double/doubles/doubled/doubling and count/counts/counted/counting - in any grammatical role and any sense (peak strengths 0.5-3.1 against a 2.80 max, usually above 1.0), provided at least one token precedes it (a text's first token is always silent). A weaker, context-dependent fringe (roughly 0.3-1.5) covers ' switch', ' loop', cash/dollar/coin, 'digits'/'numbers' in phone-number contexts and the bare (no-leading-space) digit token '19' inside four-digit years; differently spelled near-synonyms outside the set stay at baseline (remind/reminder, memoir, reminisce, commemorate, anniversary, echo, twin, pair, twice, twofold, tally, sum, amount, account, price, cost, payment, button, toggle), and isolated mid-strength fires in dense patent-style prose (circuit, player, method, variable, state, code) are unexplained leftovers.

The pole is a sharp retrospective detector (99.6% of the scan's tokens sit below 0.1 of max) that fires first on the token piece 'under'/'Under' wherever that piece stands on its own - the preposition 'under' in every sense and register, and the 'under' of a compound the tokenizer splits (under|weight, under|lie, under|way), 1.4-3.5 of max and still about 0.4 in legal boilerplate, but not when it is the first token - and more weakly and more context-dependently on behind > through > over > underneath > beneath, while below, above, around, across, past, into, against and without stay at or below 0.13. It also fires, without the piece 'under', on the core American-football play vocabulary when the sentence is a football play or stat line (yards, carries, passes, catches, rushing, running, touchdowns, quarterback, receiver, tackle, fumble, football, Chargers/Giants/Patriots), whereas generic sports words (team, game, coach, score, stadium, referee), non-football settings (a tackle box, a waiter who passes something) and single tokens that bury the string (understand, undergo, underground, overweight) stay near zero; its output direction promotes NFL/quarterback/touchdown continuations and ablating it removes football-continuation support (blitz, rush, pass, route, sacked, TD).

This pole fires on the content-word head of an object or complement phrase: the direct object or predicate nominal (asked the public, was the jury), the object of a preposition (on the Board, throughout the ventricles), an appositive name (businessman Julio), or the complementizer launching a reported or clausal complement (said "...", ruled that) — while the same words as clause subjects, or a that-clause as subject, stay near baseline. Within object position it is lexically selective, preferring people, social groups and institutions, and body parts (queen, jury, soul, mouth, verdict, ventricles) over generic, inanimate or abstract nouns (child, table, blood, idea), which stay quiet even as objects.

Fires on a no-space word-continuation subword (e.g. 'omer', 'go', 'able', 'ling', 'sh', 'fully', 'ably', '_', '-') that is glued directly onto a preceding space-initial token which is itself a complete common English word (' is', ' for', ' reach', ' how', ' after', ' meaning', ' suit', ' get', ' like'), i.e. where a standalone word turns out to be the first piece of a longer word or identifier; the stem alone, the continuation written as a separate word (with a space), or a synonym single-token word do not fire, and continuations after non-word fragments (' suc'+'rose') or very frequent compounds (' download'+'able') stay weak. Ordinary prose otherwise stays near zero, except that sentence-final periods and some code tokens can reach about 0.25 of max.

L2/N595's negative pole is a word-level (unigram) detector, not a context detector: the word the current token belongs to decides the firing and the same word fires the same way wherever it appears (' still' 0.13-0.17 on all 37 occurrences across 35 documents, ' whether' 0.15-0.17 on all 19 across 18, ' space' 0.10-0.17 on all 31 across 22, against ' method' and ' machine' at exactly 0 on every occurrence in 8 documents each and ' who' at exactly 0 in 88), while grammatical role, position, passage topic, word frequency and word length have no measurable effect (word identity 64-71% of the variance, position ~1%, next-token entropy r=0.05); the words that silence the negative pole are largely the ones that drive the positive pole (' yesterday' +0.43, ' production' +0.28, ' example' +0.27), so the unit is one lexical axis with two sides rather than a detector of any syntactic or semantic property. Predict activity from the word alone: ON covers most common English words (everyday concrete and place vocabulary such as space, station, nation, color, sea, lake, island, mountain; hedging and quantity words such as whether, still, various, generally, approximately, potential, million; and verbs such as help, try, continue, share, treat), OFF covers closed-class words, punctuation, personal names and many abstract, institutional or inflected words (method, system, law, machine, tradition, production, evidence, require, determine, establish), so a prompt whose words are ON reaches the 0.170 GELU-dip saturation while one built from OFF words stays at zero, and ordinary prose clears the 0.25-scale activity line on about a quarter of its tokens and hits the dip on about 2.5%.

Fires on the first token of a continuation that extends the current clause, list, code block or discourse unit past a point where it could have ended: the newline starting the next line after a line ending in an opening or continuing mark ({ [ ( , ; : |), or the word following a continuing 'and'/'And' (list conjuncts, ', and X', sentence-initial 'And X', 'a while ... and still'). It stays quiet on newlines after plain words and on 'and' joining ordinary noun pairs or mid-clause without a preceding boundary.

Fires on space/tab tokens that are part of a run of two or more consecutive whitespace characters, whether line-initial indentation after a newline or mid-line alignment padding, with strength ramping higher as the run lengthens; isolated single spaces between words produce no activation.

This pole fires retrospectively on the current word when it is a mid-frequency agentive verb of providing, presenting, transferring, assigning, arranging, performing, directing, or contesting (offer, spread, assign, lend, deliver, issue, share, provide, submit, present, perform, execute, render, demand, invite, trade, exchange, lead, break, beat, win, fail, pass), including deverbal nouns, participles, and split-token completions (offers, performing, issuing, fakes, board in freeboard/cupboard, throughout). It stays near-silent on ultra-common light verbs (give, take, put, set, go), on rare narrow verbs (tender, impart, allot, vow, nominate), and on pure saying/thinking/perceiving verbs (tell, publish, announce, think, see).

The pole is a word-form detector for one family of common English relation words: the placement verbs lay/laid/laying/lays, lie/lies/lying, sit/sits/sitting/sat and put/puts/putting; the consequence adverbs thus, therefore and hence; the Latin conjunction et (chiefly in 'et al.'); the restatement adverbs merely, simply, basically, literally, namely and respectively; and, more weakly, the quantity/composition words sum, measure(s), consist(s), comprise(s) and discrete. It is form-specific rather than a semantic field: differently spelled near-synonyms (place, stand, rest, remain, set; however, moreover, clearly, obviously, generally, really, only) leave the pole at baseline in every context, so a text is predicted active iff it contains one of the listed word forms (or the tokenizer piece of one, e.g. ' lay' in 'layering', ' sit' in 'sitagliptin', 'ence' in 'Hence', ' pe' in 'pea'), with a line-initial occurrence attenuated.

The pole fires retrospectively when the current token marks that a person, item, value, or setting has been assigned, chosen, named, or recorded — past participles of assigned status (listed, designated, declared, named, selected, scheduled, chosen, slated) or the bare or nominal stems of the same verbs (select, list, setting, saving, names). It stays quiet on other past-tense verbs, adjectives, and unrelated nouns in the same frames.

Fires on the operative word, word-piece, or citation symbol of a conventional legal-procedural collocation (appellate dispositions and standards of review such as erred, denial, affirm, wrongfully, hereinafter, Honorable, and opinion/citation formatting such as §, star pagination, blank reporter cites) when the preceding 1-4 tokens supply the expected legal collocate; the same subword in a non-legal collocation fires weakly.

Fires on a no-leading-space continuation token that glues onto the token just before it to complete a short code or split word: strongest (about 0.5-1.0 of max) for a digit right after a short capital-letter code (T1, MP3, K2, PKD1, C3) and for short pieces like 'id' in sk|id, 'box' in gear|box, 'up' in y|up, 'he' in cat|he|ters, 'ove' in Cl|ove|lly, plus a LaTeX closing '}}'. Ordinary prose of whole space-led words, numbers that follow a space, the same piece written as a separate word (gear box, sk id), and long or common suffixes (-ysis, -fish, -apper, -ly) stay below about 0.3 of max (the text's first token is not counted).

This pole is a retrospective detector for the distal demonstrative 'that'/'those' used to pick out a specific thing, set of things or proposition that the context has made available — as a pronoun ('I want that', 'with that', 'and that mattered', 'what is that?') or as a determiner ('that study', 'those findings', "That's why", sentence-initial 'That …' after a full stop or a newline) — and it is silent on the proximal 'this'/'these' and on 'that' where the preceding word already selects a complementizer or relative clause ('the fact that', 'suggests that', 'it is clear that', 'the one that I wanted'); firing is graded by how well the prefix supports that referring reading (strongest after a full stop or newline, a conjunction, a preposition or a transitive verb, weakest after nouns and clause-selecting verbs, and never at a text's very first token). It also fires more weakly and only in some contexts (roughly a tenth to a third of the demonstrative peak) on scattered specific, technical or quantitative content words — 'revenue' after 'quarterly', 'charges' after 'faced', and 'test', 'system', 'computer', 'monitor', 'processor', 'measurement', 'metric', 'unit', 'model', 'number', 'input', 'output', 'component' after a determiner — which I read as an offshoot of the same 'specific, already-identifiable referent' direction rather than a second job.

Fires on the predicate token that sets up a stance or evidential frame toward a coming proposition or infinitive: attitude/epistemic verbs and adjectives (' believed', ' hoped', ' suspect', ' sure', ' willing', ' convinced'), evidential verbs only when the subject is a result/evidence noun ('Analysis/The results showed', 'The study found', 'The evidence suggests', but not 'The man showed'), the copula after abstract framing subjects ('The result was', 'There was'), and modal clitics ('It'd', 'It'll'); it also fires on the final suffix piece of tokenizer-split adverbs ('doub|ly', 'defin|et|ly', 'hop|efully', 'eas|ily'). Ordinary content words, concrete-subject verbs ('He bought', 'The man showed'), whole-word adverbs (' quickly', ' very') and the first token of a prompt stay near zero (<0.1 of max), so there is no floor on plain text.

This pole retrospectively detects tokens from a small family of marker/indicator words — debug, log(s), tag(s), flag(s), point(ed/s/ing), port(s), prod — plus the number token 21 in coded identifiers, peaking on the token itself. For family members usable as both noun and verb, verb-position use drives substantially higher activation than noun-position use (e.g. 'Please point' ~2.2 versus 'The point' ~0.5; 'I will log' ~1.4 versus 'ship log' ~0.25), while synonyms or neighbors with other stems (dance, paint, product, poster, label-as-noun) stay silent or weak.

This pole is a software-documentation detector: it fires on code keywords and identifier/file fragments ('.py', ' import', 'def', ' pass', ' while', 'json', 'html', 'js', 'bash', 'docker', 'config', 'python') and on the plain verbs that technical instructions and explanations use (' pass', 'print', 'save', 'run', 'need', 'see', 'check', 'set', 'load', 'read', 'write'), and its strength also scales with how technical the preceding 15-50 tokens are: the identical clause 'You can pass the fields in the URL' peaks at 2.2 after a technical sentence but 0.7 after a fictional one. It stays near zero on ordinary English nouns that merely name technical things ('server', 'file', 'code', 'data', 'error'), on UI verbs (' edit', 'send', 'update', 'submit'), and on the same documentation words inside narrative or conversational prose, with one leftover: the particle triggers ' across' and ' through' also fire after ordinary motion verbs ('walked across the field'), so they should not be counted against the claim.

A sparse, largely token-keyed detector (zero on whitespace, almost always zero on punctuation and function words, and zero at position 0, so plain text built from common words usually stays below 0.25 x max) that fires on the content token that completes a short unit. That token is either the second piece of a word whose first piece is a short prefix-like fragment (under|weight, unc|orrect, r|ags, Un|ions, un|ify, U|pps, super|visor, C|OS) or the head noun, participle or superlative right after a possessive, determiner or intensifier (your premiums, our minds, Your best, the greatest, highly decorated, newly diagnosed, more experienced). The token itself sets most of the strength, and a tight modifier or prefix just before it boosts it (highly > very > and before 'decorated'); the neuron is silent on the modifier or prefix itself and on the next token.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a contextually licensed noun phrase: anaphoric 'one' standing in for a just-named category (a positive/cold one), a kind label predicated of listed items (are all/both capital cities), a possessed noun whose owner fits it (orchestra tuning their instruments), or a fitting object of a characterizing or desire verb (called the powerhouse, wanted a drink). The same noun with a mismatched or missing licensor, numeral 'one', subject-position 'capital', 'They tuned their instruments', 'drove a drink', 'courtroom of the cell', stays silent, so firing tracks contextual fit rather than the noun alone.

N1782+ fires on a token that belongs to a fixed, non-compositional technical or commercial string rather than to running English prose: a piece of a language or brand name (the '#' of C#, the '&' of A&W), a code/query/notation fragment (YOUR_PARAM_NAME, this.refs, $_POST, wrap_content, x509, SQL backticks, LaTeX '\sum' and '^', the '.' of a property access or version number), an established domain term (Pay Per Click, cron job, checksum, line-of-business), a numeral inside a larger number (the '600' of 1,600) or a non-English/technical word (Pour, chakra, coenestopathic); the bare tokens 'return', 'null', 'JSON', 'POST', 'click' and 'curl' also fire wherever they appear. Ordinary narrative, literary and legal prose stays at the floor, and rewriting the same content as plain English ('C sharp', 'A and W', 'a timed job', 'ordinary', 'cheques') drops the peak by 0.28-0.58 of the 2.26 scale.

The pole tracks stated measurements: it is active on a number with a unit of physical measure (feet, metres, inches, cm, kilograms, tonnes, kilometres, degrees, litres, dollars, gigabytes), and it peaks at the opening parenthesis ' (' placed right after such a unit, or after the single word that completes the measurement, where the text restates the quantity as a unit conversion or a unit symbol ('6.5 cm (2.6 in)', '324 metres (1,063 ft)', '110 million kilowatt-hours (kWh)'). It sits near baseline on prose that states no measurement and on parentheses attached to ordinary non-quantity nouns ('the novel (a thriller)', 'the report (which is long)').

The pole marks discourse-level clause openings: it fires on the sentence adverbs and connective adverbs that frame a proposition instead of naming anything (certainly, obviously, probably, maybe, indeed, actually, never, always, usually, now, again, although, though, while, whereas, however, moreover, furthermore, therefore, instead), on the deictic/wh-words that open a clause (there, here, what, why, when, where, who), and on the head of a fixed sentence adverbial after its preposition (of course, in fact, in truth, in reality, for sure, no doubt, on the contrary, on the other hand, in addition, not only). It is near zero on those same words when they follow a verb or a determiner, and near zero on referential content - concrete nouns, adjectives, pronouns, determiners, modal auxiliaries - and on degree intensifiers such as very, quite, almost and exactly.

A retrospective lexical detector, not a predictor: the pole's strength is set by the current token, and it peaks when that token is an institutional, organisational or occupational content word of written expository English - collective bodies and agencies (' jury' 1.03, ' council' 0.71, ' parliament' 0.60, ' agency' 0.53, ' committee' 0.39, plus board/court/police/management), functional roles (' mechanic' 0.76, ' curator' 0.70, ' architect' 0.47, ' engineer' 0.35, ' manager' 0.38), and the process/role nouns of that same register (' purpose' 0.65, ' role' 0.51, ' construction' 0.44, ' regulation' 0.41). It sits at the ~0.11 baseline (the position-0/'The' floor, identical for every first token, which is what the confound table's 'The' row measures) on concrete physical nouns (bottle, bucket, ladder, water, door, tree), personal and family terms (mother, friend, teacher, nurse, president, king), function words, source code and non-English text.

This pole is the GELU trough of neuron N1963's own pre-activation z rather than a feature of its own: strength is -min(gelu_new(z), 0) capped at the gelu_new minimum 0.17004 (any z in about [-0.92, -0.60] reads within 3% of the cap), so it is exactly 0 wherever z >= 0 (35% of the scanned tokens: most content nouns, e.g. ' committee', ' proposal', ' cinnamon', and ' this'), it is ~0 again wherever z <= -2 (' in' z=-3.5, ' of' -3.1, ' and' -2.6, ',' -2.6; all under 1% active), and it fires only where z passes through roughly [-1.9, -0.06]: sentence-final and bracketing punctuation ('.' active on 100% of its 5668 occurrences, '?' 1.00, ':' 0.99, '*' 0.99, ')' 0.92, '#' 0.91, '/' 0.83), the determiner ' the' (59% of occurrences active, mean 0.060), and scattered words whose z happens to land in the band (' gave' and ' both' 1.00 active, ' includes' 0.167, ' simultaneously' 0.167). Label a prompt PREDICTED ACTIVE when any token sits in that band - any running text of 8+ BPE tokens nearly always does (95% of 8-token, 99.3% of 16-token, 99.9% of 32-token and 100% of 64-token windows of this scan; 0.15-0.17 measured on English, Spanish, Chinese and Japanese prose and on code), as does any span holding a sentence-final '.'/'?' or a preposition before a determiner (' in the' 0.108, 'She walked in the garden' 0.139, 'The meeting ended at noon.' 0.140) - and label it PREDICTED INACTIVE for a one-BPE-token prompt (the 340 document-initial tokens read mean 0.018, max 0.045, 339/340 under the 0.0425 line; only capitalized 'During'/'At' reach it) and for 2-4 token spans of frequent whole words with no such punctuation or preposition+determiner (' the cat' 0.024, ' the committee' 0.024, ' of the' 0.037, ' it was not' 0.017, ' the problem of' 0.024, ' result in the' 0.019, ' many of their own' 0.019). The mechanism is retrospective: holding ' the' fixed and changing the following noun across 12 nouns leaves z at exactly -0.53, while changing the preposition in front of it moves z from 0.00 after 'that'/'as'/'between' to -0.59 after 'over', and zero-ablating the pole on these prompts is not lookahead-like (KL 3.9e-6).

The pole fires on the preposition that closes a predication of what a thing holds, is supplied with, or is separated from: 'with' after a verb of filling, loading, arming, equipping, supplying, covering or infecting ('was armed/loaded/filled/equipped/supplied/covered/stuffed/infected with X'), 'of' in the removal and origin phrases 'out of', 'rid of', 'stripped/robbed/deprived/emptied of X' and 'the source/cause/result of X', and 'from' in 'released/freed/fled/arising/resulting/came from X'. It stays near zero on 'with' of accompaniment, agreement or bare attribution ('walked with', 'agree with', 'the man with a red hat'), on 'of' of part-whole or classification ('the roof/top/window/history/price/president of X'), on 'made of' and 'consists of', and on 'in'/'into' + place; a separate, unmodelled family of abstract nouns (charge, control, command, responsibility, burden, victory) and closing LaTeX math delimiters are acknowledged leftovers rather than predictions.
