Fires when the current token heads a post-nominal modifier of the noun phrase immediately to its left, typically a present or past participle forming a reduced relative clause ('villages belonging to', 'data obtained from', 'changes associated with') or a comparative particle in the same slot ('terms like', 'protocols such as'). It does not fire when the identical word occurs as a finite main verb, gerund subject/object, or prenominal modifier.

This pole fires on the token that completes a familiar multi-token chunk: the predictable second half of a lexicalized collocation, hyphenated compound, or subword-split word (e.g. 'screen' after giant/large/black, 'handed' after short-/right-, 'world' after real-, 'ball' after long, 'solo' after second, 'order' after In, 'ound' after conf-, 'aves' after after+sh-). The same token without its usual preceding cue activates it markedly less.

Retrospective two-token-unit detector: the pole fires on the token that completes a unit begun by the immediately preceding token, and its largest responses are sub-word - when a capitalised or rare word is split into several BPE pieces (Glob|ally, Ter|med, al|ready, cy|st, Mamm|als, epit|hel, BOO|ST) the piece that completes the stem fires at 1.2-1.8, while the first piece of the same word, and the same word written as a single token (' already', ' termed', ' globally'), stay at or below 0.4. It also fires more weakly (0.4-1.4) on the second word of frequent collocations when that word is bound to the first ('the end', 'father of', 'The results', 'anyone else', 'find out'), and it is not a general word-final or continuation-fragment, suffix-class, part-whole-semantic, or multi-word-expression feature: isolated continuation pieces, word-final pieces of ordinary words, the part words 'part'/'portion'/'fraction'/'share', and unseen phrases such as 'on behalf of' and 'by means of' do not fire.

Fires on the current token when it is a word from one 'affinity / nearness / attempt' lexical family: spatial or social proximity adjectives (near, close as an adjective, closer, closest, nearest), affection verbs and relationship nouns (like as a verb, love, miss, friend(s), girlfriend), and attempt verbs (try, tried, trying). It is strongest after a first-person subject ('I tried', 'I like', 'I miss'; about 2-3x weaker after 'he'/'they'), weaker for verb 'close' and courtroom 'tried', silent for prepositional 'like' ('looks like') and synonyms ('by', 'attempt', 'test', 'need', 'careful'), and silent on the first token of a text.

The pole fires on the token that completes a partitive or portion expression: the ' of' after a word naming a part, remainder or boundary of a whole ('the rest of', 'a part of', 'a portion of', 'the remainder of', 'a member of', 'the majority of', 'half of', 'all of', 'each of', 'the end/beginning/start of'), a temporal noun after a distributor ('every day', 'each time', 'first season'), and the bound continuation of those same stems inside a word or a hyphenated compound (rest|er, rest|lessly, all|ay, maintain|er, full-|time, part-|time, All-|Time). It stays near zero on ' of' after an ordinary relational noun or numeral ('the name of', 'the title of', 'the size of', 'the coach of', 'the director of', 'one of', 'most of') and on a non-temporal noun after 'every'/'each' ('every person', 'each room').

The pole detects the English partitive construction: it fires when the preposition 'of' is directly governed by a quantity, fraction, portion or superlative expression - the quantifiers most, some, many, all, much, more, less, few, several, any, one/two/three, half, a third, a quarter, percent/%, majority, bulk, whole, rest, total - or by a superlative adjective (oldest, tallest, highest, richest, fastest, best), and on the first word of the set being quantified over (the, these, those, them, it, us, this, my, his, their, our, its), peaking highest when that word is a relative pronoun: 'of which', 'of whom' and 'of whose' fire at full strength even when the preceding noun is ordinary ('the book, of which I have three copies', 'the people of whom we spoke'), and 'following' in the fixed phrase 'the following X' also fires. It stays at zero on 'of' governed by an ordinary content noun (the colour of the sky, the level of the water, the weight of the package), on measure nouns (a cup of coffee, a piece of cake), on verb or adjective 'of' (because of, made of, full of, spoke of), on quantifiers with no 'of' (most students, all the delegates, much has been written) and on other prepositions before a relative pronoun (in which, to whom, from which); with a weak head (each, both, none, part, number, amount, lots) it clears the activity line only when the complement begins with these/those/them/it, and a bare superlative with no following 'of' gives only a partial, usually sub-threshold response.

The pole reads a content noun that names a bounded region or span of a larger whole: an extended physical area - an anatomical region or its covering (pelvis, abdomen, belly, gut, chest, torso, skull, spine, neck, back, waist, flank, jaw, forehead, shin, knee, skin, shell, lining), an area or surface of a building (lobby, hallway, porch, attic, basement, balcony, garage, deck, ceiling, floor, roof), or a stretch of land or water or geographic place (interior, coast, shoreline, harbour, port, pier, dock, prairie, tundra, foothills, canyon, outskirts, capital, Nairobi, the Moon) - or, by the same bounded-span generalisation, an interval of time (half, quarter, period, inning, minute, hour, week, month, year, afternoon, morning, night, noon); it peaks on the noun itself, strongest on the word-final sub-token of multi-token words (pel'vis', footh'ills', Nairo'bi'). It stays at zero on discrete objects, fixtures and their parts (chair, table, box, cup, window, door, handle, page), on distal body parts (hand, finger, foot, eye, ear, hair), on establishments treated as functional entities (office, hotel, museum, school, hospital, market) and on the abstract labels for parts (area, region, zone, district, space, part, section, portion); its negative pole is a diffuse near-zero offset that carries no contrastive class.

Retrospective detector for a small token cluster (little, too, ticket/tickets, similar, bit, glimpse/view, idea, fellas) firing on the trigger token itself, strongest directly after a/A or a scalar adjective (a little, a ticket, average/lower ticket, a similar, too plus gradable adjective) and weaker but still positive in attributive, additive and traffic uses (the little boy, apples too, speeding/parking ticket, have similar); near zero on form-similar neighbors (very, so, lot, much, fine, dog, young) and on capital Little.

Retrospectively fires at the head token completing a time, place/direction, or partitive-membership phrase licensed by an immediately preceding preposition, determiner/quantifier, or number/adjective scaffold (e.g. at any time, this weekend, in two days, at the start/expense of, in the West, in front of, some of, somewhere else); the same head without that left scaffold, or the same scaffold with a non-temporal/spatial/partitive head, activates weakly.

N2683+ is a retrospective, token-keyed lexical detector: it fires on content words of written informational/attributional English - the vocabulary of producing, recording, sourcing and analysing text and data (according, ask/asked, write/wrote/written, read, said, author, question, word, text, sentence, record, figure, data, analysis, method, study, document, article, publish, editor, label, survey, interview, program) and the expository connectives (also, additionally, during, within, among, moreover, furthermore, based) - and on the non-initial BPE pieces of long Graeco-Latin words (versely in in|versely, stract in ab|stract, ivariate in bi|variate, izontal in hor|izontal, ologies, ologically, ophysical, opathy, otype, atively, ively, uments). It stays near its floor on function words and on narrative, emotional and generic abstract vocabulary (happiness, love, fear, dream, desire, prosperity, death, truth, freedom, time, people, world, life, work, way, thing, cat): context moves a given trigger token by at most about a third of the scale and never turns a lexical non-member into a peak.

Fires on the token that completes a strongly associated two-part chunk: the second subword of a split word (Bo+il, P+our, pa+ired), the second word of a fixed collocation or multiword term (Book of Mormon, Dietary Guidelines, Keeping up, political commitment, 95% confidence), or a comparator/equals sign completing a statistical, measurement or arithmetic comparison (P <, Q <, F =, 45 =, mean < median). The same surface token without its predicting left neighbor activates weakly or not at all.

Fires retrospectively on the word that states the unit, scale, or measured dimension of a quantity: unit nouns (degree(s), percent, cents, times), amount nouns (rate, number), dimension/mode/level nouns (direction, manner, gear), or magnitude adverbs (exponentially), when used in a measuring construction after a number, quantifier, or measure-introducing frame (at/in/by a, specific, grown). The same surface token in a non-measuring sense (college degree, phone number, rate as a verb) drives little or no activation.

This pole fires on the content word that completes a frozen discourse-functional frame: a verb, passive participle, phrasal particle, copula, sentence adverb, or relational noun directly following a pronoun, auxiliary/be-verb, wh-word, the preposition 'In', or a markup/quote bracket (e.g. 'you return', 'be returned', 'it back/down', 'What/How + be', 'was initially', 'In response/reply/contrast (to)', 'Enter' after Please/Press/not/quote, '<head', 'It consists (of)'). The same words used as arguments or in open compositional frames ('the return', 'his back', 'came back', 'her response', 'you know', 'mixture contains'), and content words in referential compounds or plain imperatives ('peanut butter', 'New York', 'click here', 'fill it out'), stay near baseline (weak edge activations on e.g. Senate/versus/as-a are acknowledged leftovers, not core predictions).

The positive pole fires retrospectively on the non-narrative apparatus of a written or web document: the piece that names or completes an administrative, technical or catalogue unit, and almost never on the same words inside narrative prose. Concretely it peaks on the continuation half of a compound or label ('out' in printout / readout / handout, 'in' in built-in, ' Site' in 'Download Site', 'com'/'org' in Amazon.com / apache.org, ' on' in 'posted on', ' by' in 'published by', ' from' in 'available from', 'adem' in 'Category:Academics') and on whole words of that vocabulary (guide, cover, archive, appendix, template, page, document, database, newsletter, thumbnails, ratings, submit, login, permalink, captcha, json, upload, copyright); on ordinary narrative prose and news body text, even with the same surface words present, it stays at its floor (peak under 0.1: 'He went out to the garden' 0.20, 'the site of the battle' 0.10).

The pole fires where a text pins down what something is - its name, its kind or class, the content of a claim, or a measured value - and peaks on the linker that carries that content: ' of' after a quantifier or a kind/representation/measure noun ('one of', 'a couple of', 'the name/type/kind/sort/form/example/instance/case/pattern/image/description/definition/concept/idea/sense/sound/species/category/incidence/prevalence/frequency/proportion/number/presence/evidence of X') and ' that' after an assertion or evidence noun or verb ('the news/evidence/idea that', 'found/indicate that'), with the same job on the separators inside a written value ('3 x 3', 'n=123', '2,900'); it also fires, more weakly, on the verbs that perform that move (identified, named, known as, classified as, attributed, diagnosed, detected, found, seen, recorded, listed). It stays at baseline when the same linker follows a first-order noun - an object, part, possessor or event ('the leg/roof/head/owner/cost/price/value/result/purpose/rule/loss/weight of X') - and on ordinary narrative prose, so it tracks the specification construction, not the bare token ' of' and not the trigger-token list.

Retrospective chunk-continuation detector: the pole fires when the current token, together with the preceding 1-3 tokens, completes a memorized multi-token unit — a subword fragment finishing a word or name (ville, valor, voor, Epps, 13th, examen), a short noun finishing a fixed modifier-plus-noun collocation (south/northern tip), or a label opened by punctuation (?(Bob attribution, (MLS, #sel). The same short token without its licensing opener, or a longer non-formulaic token in the same slot, drives it weakly or not at all.

The pole detects feminine gender on the token it has just read: it peaks on feminine kinship/role nouns (wife, mother, sister, daughter, woman, girl, lady, queen, actress, goddess), feminine titles and the feminine -ess/-ress suffix (Mrs, Ms, Miss, Princess, baroness, hostess, actress), female given names (Elizabeth, Mary, Lois) and the pronouns she/her/herself, and sits at baseline (~0) on the masculine or gender-neutral token in the same slot (he, him, his, father, brother, son, man, boy, king, actor, host). The trigger is the feminine form itself rather than animacy (it fires on 'She' whose referent is a ship) and strength is graded: frequent kinship nouns, titles and pronouns peak hardest (2.0-3.2), rarer feminine nouns (goddess, waitress, Madam) fire weakly.

The positive pole fires on a word-internal joiner token - the short token that welds a MODIFIER to the rest of a written unit - and stays at the floor when the same token follows a noun. It peaks on the hyphen of a modifier+head compound (full-time 2.7-3.0, single-photon 2.5-2.7, small-for 2.7, long-term 2.2-2.5, all-day 2.5, four-wheel 2.1-2.4, multi-year 2.0-2.3, two-year 2.1-2.4, wide-ranging 2.5, open-source 2.0, high-risk 1.6-2.0, short-term 1.9-2.0, real-life 2.3-2.5, long-lost 2.2, 100-metre 2.0), on the ordinal or unit suffix after a numeral (3rd 1.8-2.5, 10th 2.0, 500th 2.6-2.8, 3D 2.1-2.5, 4G 1.4), on a decimal point, date slash or time colon between digits (2.5 1.1-1.2, 10/12/1999 2.4, 3/4 2.1, 3:30 1.2), and on the 'and' that coordinates two scalar adjectives (single and multiple 2.8, small and medium 2.2, fast and slow 2.0, third and final 1.8, tall and thin 1.0). The first element decides it: a hyphen after a noun stays at the floor (mother-in-law 0.00, fish-based 0.00, user-friendly 0.00, battery-powered 0.00, brick-built 0.00, government-run 0.00, gas-powered 0.29, part-time 0.31, state-owned 0.05-0.23), 'and' between nouns, verbs or two colours stays at the floor (cat and dog 0.00, men and women 0.00, sang and danced 0.00, red and white 0.20), replacing the joiner with a space or deleting it collapses the peak (full time 0.04, long term 0.00, two year 0.00, 3 rd 0.31, 3 D 0.19, fulltime 0.91 on the word 'time'), and the compound's second element is irrelevant (full-time/full-scale/full-size/full-year all 2.74); ordinary possessives ('a dog's bone' 0.00) and ordinary sentence punctuation never fire. Leftovers outside the claim: the pole also fires at some internal morpheme boundaries of long technical words (tri|peptide 2.3-2.6, auto|stereoscopic 2.3, intra|pulmonary 2.1, nano|structures 2.1-2.2, readt|hedocs 2.1, poly|peptide 1.4-1.5, top|ographic 1.8-2.0) but not others (heter|ogeneity 0.00, path|ological 0.00, under|standing 0.00, organ|ization 0.00), and I have no rule separating the two sets. The mechanism is retrospective: the peak sits on the joiner itself rather than before a predictable token, the Jacobian lens promotes no coherent token set (kurtosis 3.1, 10% agreement with the logit lens), and zero-ablating the pole moves next-token KL by only 8e-4.

Fires on the modifier or keyword that opens a declaration or clause in source code. It is strongest (~0.9-1.0 of max) on ' private', ' protected' and ' final' in a 'private/public static final' chain at the start of a class-member line, and weaker on ' public' (~0.5-0.6), ' static', 'const' in a parameter list, and VB ' then'. Any code with braces or statements also sets a floor of ~0.5-0.7 of max on ' {' and ';' tokens, but plain English prose stays near 0 even with 'private' or 'public' in it (e.g. 'the private sector'). The leftovers are a few prose tokens that reach ~0.3-0.5: ' than', ' Jersey', ' Pennsylvania'.

Fires on a phrase-internal continuation token that is directly selected by the preceding one or two content words: a relational or measure noun before of or a unit (capital of, cups of, 100 degrees), a change-of-state or perception verb before its preposition or number (fell to 3, stared at), or a modal, auxiliary, or subject before its negation or verb form (would not, you going). The same surface token with a preceding word that does not select it, or at a phrase boundary, is predicted inactive.

Not a feature detector: this pole is the GELU-dip readout of unit 587, whose strength is exactly max(0, -gelu_new(g)) of the layer-3 pre-activation g, hence capped at |GELU min| = 0.17004, attained only at g = -0.7525 - all 20 scan peaks sit at g = -0.7525 +/- 0.0004, 204 of 199,964 corpus tokens (0.1%) sit within 1e-6 of the cap and 36.4% exceed 0.25x max, so the top examples are ties at the ceiling with no content signal (the same unit is a normal sparse detector on its positive pole: 99.5% of tokens at 0, max 3.79). Predict active (above the 0.25x max line) on any prompt of two or more ordinary tokens, and inactive (peak 0.01-0.06) only on single tokens or short symbol/function-word runs where every pre-activation falls outside the band g in [-2.03, -0.09]; the token-identity R2 = 0.59 is a consequence of tokens differing in pre-activation, not a feature, and semantic edits leave the peak within |delta| <= 0.03 of max.

The positive pole is a sharp, form-based retrospective detector of the Greek/Latin 'learned-name' word shape: it fires on the token that completes a word ending in a classical nominal suffix (-us, -a, -um, -is, -es, -os, -ia, -ium, -ius, -eus, -acus/-icus, -anus, -ensis, -ides, -ula, -acter, -illus), so it responds to ancient Greek/Roman names and places, to Latin biological names (Streptococcus, Bacillus, Candida, succinalis) and to invented words with the same endings, while the same stem with a vernacular ending (-am, -itz, -son, -ley, -stein, -ov, -ski) stays at zero. It is near zero for ordinary English words (including common Greek-derived vocabulary such as philosophy or democracy), for rare English words without that shape (flabbergasted, perspicacious), and for English/European family surnames and Anglo first names (Smith, Garcia, Schmidt, Rossi, Clinton, Kevin), while its output direction promotes further classical/foreign proper names (Herod, Hannibal, Hades, Assy, Philipp, Hussein, Saddam, Tayyip).

N830+ detects the release event of a product, media work, service or venue - the moment it is brought into public availability or circulation by a producer, retailer or presenter - firing hardest on the event word itself ('ship' 3.37, 'opening' 3.05, 'launched' 2.92, 'launch' 2.81, 'released' 2.79, 'available' 2.72, 'release' 2.69, 'opened' 2.34) and secondarily on the availability-timing words that state or anticipate it ('not yet' 1.8-2.3, 'due for release' 1.78, 'slated', 'soon', 'coming', 'ready'). It is retrospective rather than lookahead (58% of input attribution is on the event token, replacement effect there 0.98-1.00, and zero-ablating the pole leaves next-token predictions diffuse, not concentrated on any upcoming token), and it is context-gated, not token-gated: the same token stays near zero when the preceding subject is not a producer/venue committing the act ('the door opened' 0.00 vs 'the store opened' 1.81; 'the police released the hostage' 0.00 vs 'the studio will release' 2.41; 'NASA will launch the rocket' 0.12; 'began/started/finished/published/issued' all <0.4), while consumer-product nouns and trade vocabulary ('new phone' 1.74, 'crossover SUV' 1.19, 'cost' 1.20, 'popular' 1.03, 'box office' 2.5-3.0) give a weaker secondary rise and generic 'not yet'/'due' temporals a weaker leftover (~1.0-1.4).

Retrospective bigram detector: the pole fires on the second element of a two-token unit that the model has already bound into a single chunk, and its strength follows how tight that binding is. It peaks on the completing piece of a word GPT-2 splits ('Supp|ose', 'B|MP', 'low|ball', 'free|-use'), on a fixed collocation or phrasal unit ('would like', 'would prefer', 'cut back', '95% CI', 'on the other hand', 'for each'), and on ' for' when the preceding noun names a means, method, requirement or reason ('technique for', 'method for', 'algorithm for', 'analysis for', 'need for'). It stays at or below the floor when the same second token is joined to a different partner ('cut down', 'the side of', 'search for', 'plan for') and when ' for' follows a noun naming an emotion or a goal ('love for', 'hatred for', 'aim for', 'purpose for', 'hope for').

Retrospective detector for spatial meaning: the pole peaks on the content word that places something in a spatial frame of reference, i.e. an axis/direction word or morpheme ('forward', 'backward', 'downward', 'upward', 'outwards', 'westward', 'top-down', 'north', 'east', 'northeast') or a distance/dimension/spatial-motion term ('radius', 'coordinates', 'distance', 'dimensions', 'width', 'height', 'gravity', 'travels', 'descended', 'accelerated'), including conventional spatial metaphors such as 'top-down approach' and 'fast forward a few years'. It stays at its floor when the same surface string is grammaticalised or idiomatic rather than a spatial content word (the verb particle 'down' in write/shut/calm down, 'around' as an approximation in 'costs around five dollars', 'forward' meaning 'send' or 'look forward to', and the '-ward' of Edward/reward/awkward/coward), the one noted exception being that the token ' along' fires on most of its occurrences even in idioms, so firing tracks spatial meaning rather than token identity.

This pole fires when the current token repeats or continues a parallel structure already established earlier in the passage: a second-or-later mention of a name or content noun (Gray, height, players), or a structural delimiter (=, ":, period, comma, newline) inside repetitive formatted text such as code assignments, JSON pairs, legal captions, or Wikipedia category blocks. It stays near zero on the first occurrence of the same token with no earlier parallel to echo.

The pole fires on the token that completes a short conventionalized construction set up by the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens: a verb's complementizer, preposition or particle (ruled-that, follows-from, went-by, runs-in), a fixed keyword or compound pair (ORDER-BY, sea-level), a determiner, quantifier or preposition's noun (the-sunrise, at-noon, all-charges), existential there after a scene-setting clause (away,-there), or a comma closing a fronted adjunct (report,) — with strength graded by how conventional the completion is, so the same surface token in an unconventional left context does not activate it. Subword and code-punctuation completions (N-airo, backslash-n, 10-):) and the ramp on preface tokens (court, ruled, year) are weak limiting cases of the same local-completion response.

Sparse retrospective detector for the completing piece of a few specific multi-token units: the second sub-word of words split by GPT-2 as hyp|ox(-ia/-emic), ext|race(-llular), comm|otion, neph|ron, catast|rop(-hes), fib|ro(-blast), Rub|icon, Deep|ost(-av), and abstract salience or magnitude nouns that complete a collocation: ' attention' as the object of drawn/gained/attracted/received (not 'pay attention'), ' concern' or ' interest' after great/growing/of, ' scale' in 'the scale (of)', ' years' in 'in recent years', ' recently' after More/Until, ' of' in '(in the) light of', and ' up' in 'looking up'. Other sub-word continuations (intr|ace, cardi|omyopathy, demo|cratic) and the same words in other frames stay near zero. The first token of any prompt reads about 0.40-0.43 (about 0.16 of max), below the active threshold, so prompts with none of these units are predicted inactive.

Retrospective detector for a locally completing grammatical dependency: the pole fires on the token that completes a short licensing relation with the preceding 1-3 tokens, such as subject noun plus finite verb (cat sat), existential there plus verb (there lived), copula plus predicative adjective or participle (is open), auxiliary plus adverb plus participle (are often called), relativizer which plus verb (which sits), or preposition/conjunction plus determiner, numeral, or negation (to the, after three, pleaded not). Activation requires both the right peak word-class and the licensing predecessor, so changing either reduces it while swapping a distant uninvolved word does not.

Fires retrospectively when the current token completes an explicit signal that adjacent material is supporting detail for the preceding claim: either an example/specification flag (for example, for instance, e.g., i.e., including/INCLUDING, specifically, most prominently, etc.), or the typographic (curly) closing quotation mark ending a directly quoted supporting statement. It does not fire on the same content words in other roles (noun 'an example of', manner 'displayed prominently', ASCII quotes, or unattributed speech verbs like 'Riley said').

Opening-quotation-mark detector: a '"', "'" or curly quote immediately before the current token adds a roughly constant +1.4 to +2.6 to this neuron's pre-activation (measured on the same token with and without the quote: 'the' +2.58, 'missing' +2.57, 'Closed' +2.05, 'Porsche' +1.36) and the effect decays to nothing by the third or fourth token, so the positive pole fires on the first one to three lowercase tokens inside a quotation and stays at or below zero when that token is capitalised, a proper name or a code identifier, while its output row promotes the tokens that close a quotation ('";', '".', '",', '"?', '"]' head w_out.W_U; the context-averaged Jacobian lens is uninformative at this layer). The negative pole is the complement, and its ceiling is GELU's: strength = -GELU(z) cannot exceed 0.170 (the GELU minimum) and is non-monotone in z, maximal at z around -0.75, so it reads high (0.10-0.17) over ordinary lowercase running text and collapses to about 0 at exactly two kinds of token - the one to three tokens just inside an opening quotation mark (z above 0) and capitalised, proper-name, camelCase-identifier or rare subword tokens (z below about -1.5, where GELU returns to zero); six of the 32 scanned tokens with z > 0.25 ('…', ' continue' after an ellipsis, a document-initial ' is', ' ought', ' every', ' terrifying') are leftovers this does not cover.

Fires retrospectively at the token that completes a stereotyped multi-token chunk — a calendar date (month + day-number + ordinal suffix or comma), an approximator/degree phrase ('or so', 'ever so'), or another fixed collocation ('Due to', 'long before', 'brings on', 'occasion of', 'was announced') — with most drive from the preceding 1-2 tokens; the same surface token outside such a chunk activates weakly.

L4/N147+ fires on relational vocabulary that places one thing against a reference: comparison/identity words (different, similar, other, various, separate, same), extent-or-degree words on the 'more' side of a scale (large, big, great, wide, long, greater, larger, longer, more, most, much, many, all, additional, increase), position/order words in time or space (further, later, next, following, continue, beyond, behind, throughout, close, top, end, rest, then, still), and the relational predicates that link a cause, a part or a result to its relatum (lead/leads/led/leading, part of, followed by, as a result, related, consistent). It stays near zero on intrinsic physical properties (red, blue, wooden, cold, old, nice, simple), on the decreasing side of a scale (small, short, narrow, low, few, less, least) and on nominalisations of the same notions (difference, similarity, variety, size, degree, leader).

Fires on a generic organizational, collective, or relational noun (e.g. brand, colleague(s), embassy, ministry, division, campaign, newsletter, cabinet) when it directly completes a preceding proper name, group/demonym adjective, or possessive determiner that names its owner or affiliation (e.g. 'Saint Laurent brand', 'his colleague', 'U.S. Embassy'). The same head noun without such an attributive/possessive specifier, or the same specifier followed by a non-collective concrete noun, activates it much less.

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a compound noun: the head noun of a noun-noun compound such as box in toy box, ticket in train ticket, driver in car driver, pile in sand pile, square in town square, tree in apple tree, car in model car, time in dinner time, loop in pancake loop, or trains in toy trains, or the final subword fragment of a compound word such as he in bookshelf, ber in barber, or keeper in shopkeeper. A lone noun with no compound partner, or the first element of a compound, fires weakly.

N2467+ fires on the token that continues a unit the preceding tokens left open, not on the token by itself: (i) the second or later BPE piece of a multi-piece word, especially names, jargon and code identifiers ('enter|ic' 1.88, 'Stonehen|ge' 1.72, 'Pen|ang' 1.83, 'colon|ic' 1.01, 'con|str|aint', 'wrap|_content', 'Lin|ear', 'ital|ic', 'Strepto|coccus'), which is 65% of its peaks at or above 1.0 (0.47 x max, versus 40% of all tokens), and (ii) the complement slot immediately after a noun naming a part, portion or position of a whole ('the end|of' 1.81, 'inside|of' 1.34, 'middle|of' 0.83, 'close|of' 0.58, and the same for beginning/start/part/piece/half/rest/side/back/front/outside/bottom/spine/preface/copy/text/author/editor/founder, 0.35-1.9). It stays at the floor (0.00-0.25 of the 2.15 max) on the very same token ' of' when the preceding noun is self-sufficient ('the table/title/cover/index/center/corner/size/color of X') and on the trailing piece of a common word the model already resolved from its first piece ('microbi|ology', 'dermat|ology', 'gast|ric', 'Chel|ten|ham', 'Ave|bury'), so what predicts it is whether the current token is bound into a larger unit rather than which token it is.

L4/N2533- has no key of its own: it is the off-state half of neuron N2533, its strength being -GELU(z) of that neuron's pre-activation, so it is exactly 0 on the ~49% of tokens where N2533 fires (z > 0), it saturates at GELU's floor 0.1700 - the scan maximum, which is why all 20 scan peaks are tied at 0.169-0.170 and the listed 'highest-mean tokens' are only the tokens that most often land near z = -0.75, not a trigger set, and why WordNet's 'whole' group is an artefact of that tie - and it is a graded dial in between rather than a detector of any concept. Predict ACTIVE (peak >= 0.0425 of the 0.170 scale) for any prompt of eight or more measured tokens of running text, since English prose, code and non-English all measured 0.10-0.17 there, and predict INACTIVE only for short prompts of at most four measured tokens that are complete high-frequency English fragments staying wholly inside N2533's positive regime ('I think so.' 0.000, 'She said so.' 0.000, 'He did it.' 0.000, 'We saw them.' 0.000, 'We did that.' 0.000, 'The door was open.' 0.000, 'She reads books.' 0.000); that short-prompt region is the dial's weak side, where about half of such probes still stay below the line, and five to seven measured tokens cannot be called from surface form.

Fires retrospectively on a token that is specifically licensed as the continuation of the immediately preceding syntactic frame -- the predicate, argument, modifier, operand, or clause-closing punctuation selected for by the preceding 1-3 tokens -- and stays near zero on the same token when the preceding words do not select for it or the clause is incomplete. Uniform ~0.26 first-token readings are a position floor, not detections.

Retrospective detector for the completion of a frequent, locally stereotyped multi-token collocation: the pole fires on the token that completes a fixed compound ('light-years'), a canonical measurement ('100 degrees'), a fixed binomial ('golden brown', 'far away'), a stereotyped verb construction ('market fell', 'rushed into'), a constrained factual completion ('France is Paris'), or a subword completion ('prot-ons'), with most of its drive coming from the one or two preceding tokens; keeping the peak token while breaking its left-hand phrase sharply reduces activation.

N2682+ is a retrospective detector of unfamiliar word spellings: it fires on the subword piece that spells out the unusual part of a rare, technical or foreign word that GPT-2's tokenizer splits into several tokens (e.g. 'uss' in 'truss/trusses', 'ST' in 'CONSTANT(S)', 'uh' in 'Muhlenberg', 'un' in 'Scunthorpe', 'wh' in 'narwhal', 'gh' in 'sorghum', 'inn' in 'cinnabar'), wherever it sits in the sentence. Predicted inactive when the same word arrives as one token ('constant', 'canceled', 'canopy') or when an ordinary word fills the slot ('trust', 'beams', 'sugar', 'Allentown'); a weaker secondary response also appears on the word right after a modal or possessive ('can even', 'its conclusion', "the program's goals").

This pole is a retrospective context-depth (positional) detector: it fires on tokens sitting roughly 8 or more tokens into the context regardless of their lexical content, and is silent on the same tokens presented early in a short prompt. Token identity only modulates amplitude (e.g. subword pieces and frequent tokens peak higher), so any fixed word list underpredicts late random words and overpredicts the same words early.

This pole fires when the current token completes a short conventionalized chunk: the second word of a fixed idiom or collocation (Once upon, times a day, light-years), the joiner of an enumerative or coordinated list (A, B and C), or punctuation or a closing bracket that terminates a complete clause or statement. It stays low on the same tokens when the preceding words do not form such a completed unit.

This pole retrospectively detects the token that completes a locally highly-constrained multi-token collocation (tag-closer after a tag name, unit noun after a numeral, preposition after verb-plus-adverb, participle after be-plus-adverb), firing on the completing token in proportion to how strongly the preceding 1-3 tokens constrain it; with no preceding context it sits at a weak ~0.1 position-zero baseline.

The pole fires at the onset of the second element of an English coordination: it is ~0 on the conjunction itself and jumps on the token immediately after 'and'/'And' (also 'but', 'or', 'nor') whatever that token is (determiner, pronoun, adverb, preposition, content word, even '42' or an unknown letter string), decaying over the next one or two tokens of the second conjunct. It stays silent when the same material is joined only by punctuation (comma, semicolon, full stop) or a non-coordinating connective ('so', 'yet', 'plus', 'because'), for non-English conjunctions ('et', 'und', 'y'), and for the numeral 'and' of 'one hundred and five'.

Fires on the completion piece of a strongly constrained multi-token chunk: the second half of a fixed whole-word collocation or idiom (started well, stopped short, points ahead, sounds like, track back, with respect, No. 1 in) or the second subword piece of a longer word (K-IND, track-back, dou-c, bialle-lic), where the preceding 1-2 tokens strongly predict the peak token. The same surface token in an unconstrained context (sounds after The, total after points) does not activate it.

Fires on the second word of a two-token scalar-degree construction: a quantifier or measure head (few, some, little, hundred, two), a degree adverb (quite, definitely), or an evaluative head (worth, want, good, away, to) when the immediately preceding one or two tokens supply its degree licensor (a, few, quite, well, far, sure, a modal such as may/should/could, or a light be/have/verb). The same head word without that licensor, or a non-scalar word in the same frame, drives it weakly or not at all.

This pole fires on specialised technical vocabulary: long, Latin/Greek-derived scientific, medical and engineering terms and the word-internal pieces of such words (bronchial, epithelium, magnetometer, carcinoma, dynamometry, actinomycetemcomitans), and likewise on long unbroken code identifiers and path strings (BOOST_MPL_LIMIT_UNROLLING, fontloader-basics-nod.lua, __init__.py). It is near zero on short, everyday English words, function words and plain conversational prose; separately, and for non-semantic reasons, it is also broadly on at the second token of any input.

The pole is a curly-apostrophe contraction detector: GPT-2's byte-level tokenizer splits U+2019 into the two byte tokens [âĢ][Ļ] and leaves the following clitic as a bare continuation token, so we’ve/I’ve/you’ve tokenizes as [we][âĢ][Ļ][ve] and we’ll as [we][âĢ][Ļ][ll], and the pole peaks on the clitic token 've' (token 303: 2.3–3.3 in running prose, 1.3–2.5 in short probes) and on 'll' (token 297: 1.2–2.3), with the two apostrophe byte tokens just behind. It sits at 0.0 for the same auxiliaries written with a straight apostrophe ('ve and 'll as single tokens) and for uncontracted have/will, sits at 0.0 for ordinary words that contain the letters ve (government, vegan) and at about 0.5 for the word-initial ' ve' token (id 1569), is weak on the other curly clitics ’s, ’m, ’d, ’t and ’re (0.2–0.6 in a short sentence, up to about 1.1 after a full preceding clause, versus 1.3–3.3 for ’ve/’ll), and only a few standalone words (happen, meant, capable, truly) reach 1.0–1.8 in some sentences.

Fires on hard-news wire-report prose (violence, crime, conflict, government/official actors, weekday datelines, 'officials/spokesman/police said' attribution), with activation building through the news sentence and peaking at the end of an attributed news sentence: on 'said'/the attribution phrase, the closing period, and above all the newline token that ends that paragraph (about 0.6-1.0 of max). Casual, personal, code or math text stays near 0; a mundane sentence ending in '..., X said.' followed by a newline gets only a weak floor (~0.2-0.3), and removing the trailing newline or ending with ':' instead of '.' drops the peak by about 0.2.

The pole fires, retrospectively, on the noun that names the manner or mode of an action - 'how something is done': predicted active for the token ' manner' in essentially every occurrence (1.10-1.65 across its six scan occurrences and 0.55-1.78 across my constructed probes), and for ' way', ' style' or ' fashion' when a descriptive adjective characterises them ('a very strange way/style/fashion'), which I measured at 0.75/0.74/0.66 against 1.22 for ' manner' in the same carrier. Predicted inactive for that same slot filled by a kind, instance or attribute noun (kind, sort, case, form, place, mood, tone, character, means, technique) or by a concrete content noun, and for demonstrative-only forms ('in this way/style/fashion'), which all sit at the pole's floor (0.19 there against 1.22 for 'manner' in the identical frame).

Retrospective detector for the token that completes a frequent two-piece chunk: a particle after go/went/going (over, ahead, with, through, by, about), 'like' after would/'d/look, the title word after Going (Public), or a subword piece finishing a word (og after go in googling/googled, ic after webcom, ink after Br). The same peak token without its anchor piece does not activate it.

This pole fires on the token that completes a frequent local collocation: it peaks when the one or two tokens immediately before it strongly predict it (fixed phrases like 'second half' and 'golden brown', or strongly associated subject-verb pairs like 'market fell', 'protons carry', 'wind rushed'). Replacing the predictive preceding words with unpredictive ones while keeping the peak token identical sharply reduces firing, while changing distant tokens that leave the local pairing intact does not.

The pole fires on a verb in predicate position that belongs to a construal-and-arrangement family, i.e. verbs saying how something is seen, framed, or put in order (interpret, construe, view, regard, frame, characterize, portray, structure, balance, summarize, stack, end), and on the 'to'/'of'/'at' that completes a cognition or communication verb whose target is non-spatial (look to, look at, think of, speak of, point to, refer to, allude to, listen to, drawn to). It stays near zero when the same word is a noun ('the structure of', 'the interpretation of'), on motion or grammaticalised 'to' (walk/drive/move to, due to, according to), and on ordinary physical or reporting verbs (carry, push, throw, build, walk, say, state, report, explain, describe, document, consider, treat, order, compare).

Retrospective detector for short, high-frequency qualifier tokens: degree/epistemic adverbs (quite, exactly, actually, truly, really, rather, certainly), evaluative or comparison adjectives (perfect, good, bad, great, different, similar, same, better, less), contrast connectives (However, but, though, instead) and verb particles (off, out, away, into). It peaks (1.0-1.5 of max) only when such a token sits at a junction: right after a comma, colon or full stop, right after an opening brace in code (the newline that opens an indented block), or right after the verb or stem it completes ('shave off', 'missing out', 'dr|ab'); ordinary nouns, main verbs, names, physical adjectives (red, big, cold) and pure determiners/pronouns (the, a, we, it) leave it at zero.

This pole fires on the token that completes a locally licensed two-part routine: the head of a second conjunct after a coordinator (watched/walked/stared/cried after and/or/but; the subject 'hall' of an and-linked second clause) or the fixed second half of a boilerplate pair (upon after Once, zeros/ones after 'np.', body after '</', active after WHERE). The same peak token is silent without its licensing cue one to three tokens back (upon after camped, stared after then, hall after as, div after '</'), though not every coordinator plus verb qualifies (e.g. pushed after 'turned the key and' stays silent).

N1137+ fires retrospectively on the head of a completed, past-time predicate: the finite past-tense verb of a clause reporting an act of inquiry, search, contact, perception or movement into/out of a place or state (asked, examined, searched, contacted, saw, declared, decided, entered, left, departed), the same verb inside a purpose 'to'-infinitive (stopped to examine, came to see, was designed to evaluate), and the relational head of the matching nominal ('invasion of', 'conversion into', and the addressee frames 'To the Editor:' / 'To the Court:'). The identical clause in the present, future, modal, passive or 'want/hope/need to' form, and generic light verbs (read, clean, thank, ignore, change, walk, measure, print), stay near zero, while changing the token after the peak never moves the activation.

The pole fires when the current token is a strongly licensed local continuation of the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens, completing a conventional collocation (capital to of, museum to is, fell to sharply, heavy to the rain slot, guilty to to, far to away, re to hyphen); strength is graded by how constraining the left context is, so the same token after an incongruous head (of after table: 0.17 vs after capital: 1.32) or an incongruous token in the same slot (green for heavy, apple for is) stays near zero, while words after the peak leave activation exactly unchanged.

The pole fires on the word that classifies a referent by its general type rather than by its own properties: typicality/kind adjectives (typical, ordinary, everyday, usual, common, normal, standard, average, classic, quintessential, conventional, traditional) and essence/rank adjectives (primary, main, fundamental, basic, essential, key, real, ultimate, best, top), plus the indefinite/quantified determiner that makes the phrase non-specific (a, an, another, some, every, all, most, one, two). It peaks in predicative position after a copula ('it is typical' 1.80, 'this mistake is classic' 1.86) or between an indefinite article and its noun ('a typical example' 1.26, 'a primary source' 1.88). It stays near zero on concrete descriptive modifiers (blue, wooden, heavy, sad, clumsy, bitter) and on particularizers (specific, unique, individual, single, distinct), roughly halves when the same classifier takes a definite article ('a typical mistake' 1.43 vs 'the typical mistake' 0.46), and has only a weak secondary response on the day number of a date ('December 23' 1.51 vs 'on 23' 0.50).

This pole fires retrospectively on the second piece of a conventionalized two-piece lexical chunk, where the immediately preceding token strongly predicts the peak: phrasal-verb particles (made/set/coming up, come forward/upon), fused discourse formulae (here+after, as+follows, the+latter), passive/participial collocations (organization+created, Code+generated), or stem+suffix completions (lav+age, ball+sy, C+#, AK+P, ARIS+ING). The same peak token in isolation or after a non-partner token (up without made/set/coming, after without here, follows without as, age without lav/et) does not activate it.

Retrospective detector for the word 'of' (peaking on 'of' itself or on its complement word) that fires only when the head-noun + complement pairing forms a conventionalized 'X of Y' unit: fixed collocations ('thing of beauty', 'drug of choice', 'powerhouse of the cell', 'book of poems', 'land of the free'), evaluative predicative 'be of ADJ N' ('of great concern', 'of little value', 'of paramount significance'), and quantifier/superlative idioms ('of all kinds', 'of the century', 'Pick of the Week', partitive-relative 'of which'). It stays at baseline for other prepositions in identical frames and for productive measure/substance pairings ('cups of sugar', 'bowls of rice', 'fossils of sugar'), with only weak activation for loosely licensed frequent pairings ('capital of France').

Retrospective fragment-continuation detector: the pole fires on a non-initial BPE piece that continues a rare, fragmented word (foreign loanwords, transliterated proper names, non-English fragments such as m+ung, ta+ek, The+ss, A+berg), marking piece-by-piece spelling of an unfamiliar word. It stays silent on continuations of familiar words (soy+bean, sw+imming, x+ylophone, Her+bert) and on common whole-word tokens, and responds only moderately to a noun completing an article-A phrase head (A Tribe > A Band > A dog).

Fires on the onset of the first branch of an explicit two-part coordination introduced by 'between', 'both', or 'either' (e.g. the '1994' in 'between 1994 and 2010', the 'practical' in 'both practical and symbolic') — the first endpoint or conjunct token where a matching 'and'/'or' completion is expected.

Retrospective detector that peaks on the head content word (classificatory noun like kind/variety/order/meaning/idea, defining participle or adjective like proposed/required/included/used/termed/abbreviated/valid, or the complement introducer of/in/as/to/with/for/from itself) of a phrase taking an overt complement that names, quantifies, or specifies it (termed/known/referred/abbreviated as X, kind/variety/order/meaning of X, included/used/proposed in X, go with X), firing strongest on appositive naming and kind/variety/order-of quantifying frames and weaker-to-moderately on the same head words in eventive, purposive, exemplifying (such as), or duration-for positions rather than switching off. It stays near zero only when no specifying head or complement introducer is present, on bare episodic verbs (stirred, painted, opened), non-specifying modifiers (blue, expected, seen, pointed, near, form, collection, described), and subject nouns.

Fires retrospectively when the current token is the conventional, highly constrained completion of a formal multi-token chunk opened in the previous 1-3 tokens: the final letter(s) of a parenthesized acronym abbreviating the preceding term, the second half of a conventional proper name, or the head noun, relativizer, preposition, or participle that closes a formal noun phrase or clause. Mismatched continuations in the same slot activate weakly or not at all, and common colloquial collocations (peanut butter, red dress) do not drive it.

Fires on clauses that describe concrete, physically situated situations — tangible objects, places and bodily actions (a letter falling onto a table, a man walking into a room, a card pressed into a slot, a man chained to a crane) — and stays near zero on abstract, institutional or definitional prose (company profits, funding decisions, approved policies, 'X is a Y' definitions, marketing copy), whatever the tense, definiteness or register. It is retrospective, tracking content already read rather than preparing an upcoming token; isolated spikes on math delimiters ($$) and code keywords (if) are leftovers it does not explain.

The positive pole is a segment-boundary detector: it fires on the token that closes a long, self-contained non-prose block embedded in running text - a citation list (' ]]' or '].'), display math ('$$'), a code block ('});', '}'), a comment ('*/'), a closing quote (' »') or a parenthetical of roughly 15+ tokens - and on the first token of the prose that resumes when such a block ends (a sentence-initial 'However', 'But', 'So' or 'On the other hand', or a pronoun such as 'He' after a list-like boilerplate block). Strength is graded by the length of the segment being closed (about 0.1 for a 4-token span versus 1.0-1.2 for a 30-token citation list), while the same delimiter characters inside ordinary running prose, opening delimiters, short parentheticals and plain sentence ends in a single paragraph do not fire.

Fires strongest on the second token of a frozen, highly predictable two-token collocation that completes a conventional unit (e.g. far/year-cue plus away, capital/powerhouse plus of, sea plus level, market plus fell, digit plus decimal point), requiring both the specific preceding cue and the completion token. It also shows a weak baseline of about 0.3 (roughly 20% of max) on any sequence-initial token regardless of identity.

Fires on the preposition ' about' (much more weakly on ' on'/' regarding'/' of' in the same slot) when it attaches to a preceding quantity or information noun to introduce a topic of knowledge, as in 'find out more about', 'learn/know/see more about', 'more information/details about', 'something/nothing/a lot about' (peak ~0.8-1.1 of max); it stays near zero for approximate 'about' ('costs about ten'), for verb + about ('talked/cares/thinking about'), and for 'What/How about', and is only moderate for bare 'know about' (~0.4). A weaker secondary job (~0.5-0.9 of max) is a mid-word subword piece inside long biomedical/chemical compounds ('ul' in isomaltulose/cardiopulmonary, 'em' in sociodemographics, 'ologically' in histopathologically); ordinary text including the first token stays near 0, so there is no floor.

The pole is a word-level detector for a piece of correspondence or a dispatch and for the act of sending one: it fires at 0.8-2.5 of max (above the 0.71 active threshold) on the token that is, or completes, a message/paperwork noun - letter(s), note(s), memo, message, email, text, telegram, dispatch, correspondence, notice, notification, reminder, reply, document(s), report, file, page, sheet, sentence, statement, log, dossier, briefing, mail, envelope, stamp, epistle, missive (with information/data/orders/instructions/warning weaker at 0.9-1.1) - and on send-to-a-recipient verbs (send/sent/sends/sending, mailed, forwarded, returned, brought, shipped, dispatched, delivered, relayed, wrote, showed); the response is carried by the word itself rather than the sentence sense, so 'letter' fires equally in 'the letter of the law' and 'the letter B', 'telegram' peaks on its completing piece 'legram', and the token ' Sent' fires inside 'Sentimental'. The target word itself stays at or below 0.2 of max for authored or published works (book, novel, poem, essay, article, paper, manuscript, draft, proposal, journal, magazine, newspaper, story, news, paragraph, advertisement, diary), functional slips (ticket, menu, schedule, form, label, receipt, invoice, bill, contract, licence, permit, petition, application, postcard), undirected information nouns (facts, content, question, answer, account, description, announcement, advice, insight) and goods or handling verbs (parcel, box, opened, kept, sold, carried, moved, received, weighed, told, announced, mentioned), so it is neither 'anything document-like' nor 'anything about information'; a small leftover it does not explain is firing on word-internal pieces of some rare loanwords ('en' in Hellenistic and millennia, 'etz' in chametz, 1.6-2.2).

Fires when the current token is the hinge that completes a conventionalized multi-word formula: discourse-temporal 'Today/today' opening a sentence, 'of' inside a stock 'X of Y' idiom/title/template (rule of thumb, point of no return, Queen of, Place of birth, warranty of), ')' closing an enumerator such as '(1)', '1)' or 'a)', or boilerplate hinges such as 'Note:', 'already' in 'You already have', and 'on' in 'point on it'. Activity requires both the hinge token and its formula-predicting predecessor and list/boilerplate context, not the hinge token alone.

The pole fires on the token that opens a newly introduced word or phrase: the first token after an opening or separating boundary ((, {, [, :, ;, an em dash, or a line break inside a code block) or after a phrase-introducing word that takes a following complement (use/using/used, by, with, through, like, including, because, but, according, rely, employ), and on a mid-sentence capitalized proper name that names a new entity. It is predicted near zero for tokens that merely continue an already-open phrase (after the/a and after in, of, to, on, for, and), for a lowercased copy of a name, and inside non-Latin-script text.

L5/N2154+ marks the opening of the noun phrase introduced by a possession, containment, availability or existential predicate - a main-verb have/has/had/having, with/without, there is/are/was/exists, contain/include/house/feature/carry/bear/sport/boast, provide/offer/give/show/present/display/exhibit, or lack/possess/retain - firing on the determiner or quantifier that starts that NP (2.5-3.0, plus a smaller bump on a gradable modifier inside it) and decaying back to baseline within three tokens. The same determiner is silent after locative prepositions (in/at/on/of/from/by/for: mean -0.09 for ' a' there versus +1.63 after a possession predicate, a 40.9x enrichment of strong activation in the possession frame), after eventive verbs (make/build/buy/take/occupy), on perfect or modal have (has built, have to), and on non-possessive statives (be, resemble, remain, become, seem); the one near-synonym that only half-fits is 'owns' (0.1-0.9 depending on the object).

Fires on the completion token of rigid news/website boilerplate when its long-range template opener is present: the year closing a byline or tweet dateline, the credit noun or colon closing a caption (Source:, Photo:, In Photos:), the anchor closing a recirculation instruction (tap here...), or punctuation closing a headline or section header. The same token without its template opener stays near silent.

This pole retrospectively detects a learned subset of common content-word tokens: singular nouns and bound stems that commonly head partitive, unit or measure expressions or begin multi-token technical terms (e.g. period, couple, lot, number, amount, ton, pair, portion, fraction, slice, item, factor, area, motif, degree, ratio, and stems hal-, menstru-, agon-, cataly-, comb-, wavelength). It peaks on the head/stem token itself and fires identically no matter how the word or phrase actually continues. Its amplitude is boosted by quantitative or technical wider context (adult versus trial period, medical prose), while matched precise-unit nouns (dozen, percent, minute), generic nouns (water, system, problem, result) and unrelated stems (electr-, archae-) stay near zero; its output direction shows no specific-token prediction (Jacobian kurtosis ~3.4, 0% lens agreement), so it prepares no particular upcoming token.

This pole fires when the current token is one of a memorized set of short (1-4 character) strings: first- and third-person pronouns and reflexives (me, my, I, him, her, his, em, myself), cardinal direction and position words (left, right, back, fore), a few frequent monosyllables (went, gone, hard, wish, ha, ho, o), and consonant-led subword fragments (bl, ru, lim, ble, bre, bru, gru, hol, hau, lem, lau), whether standalone or as a piece of a longer word. It peaks most strongly on the fragment 'bl' after ' Le' (Leblanc, ~3.2) and is silent on matched neighbors differing by one letter or tokenization (be, by, them, for, bin, rest, write, lack, meet, blue, limit, internal 'ble').

Fires in source code on the delimiter that introduces a type, package or namespace name in a declaration/qualified-name context: each '.' inside a dotted package/module path (import/package lines, reverse-domain names like org.apache.commons., com.android.), ' extends'/' implements' after a class name, '<' opening generic/template arguments (List<, apply<), '::' in a namespace qualifier (facebook::), and ':' before a parameter type (tableView: UITableView); declaration keywords ' class'/' struct' fire moderately (~0.45-0.6 of max). It stays near zero on '.' in ordinary member access or method calls (user.getName()), on '<' as a comparison, ':' in dict literals, and on all punctuation in English prose (no floor: prose prompts stay ~0).

This pole fires retrospectively at the initial token or piece of a predictable multi-token lexical unit: the first subword of a morphologically complex word (isomer, ischaemic, isomaltulose, doxorubicin, inelastic, bloodless, cardiomyopathy), the first half of a hyphenated compound (to-do, on-chip, boy-scout), or the first word of a fixed collocation (credit card, run feature, not for profit, and electronic). The same starter token stays quiet when its bound continuation is missing (bloody vs bloodless, elastic vs inelastic) or when the left context does not license that specific unit (danger vs safety of isomaltulose), while changes that preserve the stem-plus-continuation structure or touch only distant tokens leave it unchanged.

Fires on a sector-, discipline-, or scope-specifying word (commercial sector, institutional domain, academic discipline, sport, or geographic scope, e.g. business, Retail, Science, dairy, law, Insurance, Rugby, Middle, Worldwide) when it names or attributively modifies a multi-token institutional, publication, geographic, or URL-domain name, including the identifying segment or dot separator inside such a domain; it stays low on the same word used as a plain common noun and on generic non-sector modifiers or dots outside names and URLs.

Retrospective detector for the token that completes a locally highly predictable 2-3 token collocation or construction (e.g. court-ruled, fell-silent, raised-interest, guilty-to, number-billion, FROM-table-WHERE, subword completion, or formulaic comma/period); the same token without its constraining 1-2 predecessors stays weak.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a familiar fixed phrase or collocation that is strongly constrained by the immediately preceding tokens (e.g. light-years + away, stared + at, For i + in, Se + ine, upon a + time); the same token outside its collocational left context, or a different token in the same context, activates weakly or not at all. A ~0.28 activation on the first token of any text is a positional baseline, not signal.

Fires on the token that completes a locally licensed collocation frame: the current token is strongly selected for by the immediately preceding word or two, such as a question or attitude verb taking a wh-word or complementizer (wondering where, surprising that), a noun or adjective taking its characteristic preposition (distant from, information on, glimpse into), a verb taking to plus its complement (looking to, wait to hear), or a fixed phrase (no doubt, newly signed). The same word in the same position without its licensing trigger is predicted to stay near-inactive.

Retrospective detector of the thing a sentence is attending to: it fires on the noun phrase that a verb of looking, reading, watching, checking, asking, describing, discussing, mentioning, considering, imagining or remembering takes as its object ('the video', 'a question', 'the article', 'the blue dress'), together with the determiner or pronoun that opens that phrase ('the', 'a', 'it', 'them', 'this') and any complement particle that continues it ('about', 'of', 'to', 'from'). It stays at the GELU floor when the same words are the grammatical subject ('The video was watched by many people') or the object of a physical-manipulation or possession verb ('moved/pushed/carried/lifted/painted the chair'), and colour terms are its one purely lexical trigger ('bright blue', 'a green scarf', 'a red coat').

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a locally licensed two-piece phrase: the current token is the strongly cued continuation of the preceding one or two tokens (a motion or change verb's preposition or particle, a verb's expected complement, a numeral or determiner's noun, a known function name's open-paren, or a tag stem's closing bracket). The same trigger token fires much less when its licensor is swapped for one that does not cue it, and a distant-word swap leaves it unchanged.

Fires retrospectively when the current word names the measured outcome, aggregate variable, or overall appraisal under investigation in research, survey, or evaluation discourse (e.g., mass index, performance, satisfaction, impact, intake, value, or verdict words like look, handle, think, perceive), especially after investigative, comparative, or interrogative framing such as examined, compared, satisfaction with, or How/what questions; the same word in casual non-evaluative use does not drive it.

This pole fires on the token that completes a strongly constrained local collocation: a token highly predictable from the preceding 1-3 tokens, including fixed phrases ('all the time', 'top right'), verb+particle or verb+preposition frames ('made up of', 'handed down', 'published in', 'write to'), and conventional frames ('start at $5', 'voted 7'). Breaking the preceding trigger collapses activation even when the sentence frame is kept; distant-context changes or swaps between equally unpredictable words leave it unchanged.

This negative pole is not a feature but GPT-2's GELU dip read on neuron N4's pre-activation: the MLP computes gelu_new, so the pole strength is -min(gelu_new(z), 0), capped at the gelu_new global minimum 0.1700408 (a pre-activation in about [-0.91, -0.61] reads within 3% of the cap, z >= 0 reads exactly 0 and z below about -2 relaxes back toward 0), so the 20 top examples are float32 ties within 3e-8 (3 ULP) of that constant on semantically unrelated peak tokens (' and', '|', ',', ' soil', ' frequency', ' May', "'s", ' in', ' continues'), 8.2% of the 199,985 scanned tokens sit in the top bin 0.1644-0.17004 and 23.4% below 0.006 (mean token 0.071, 42% of scale), and both vocabulary lenses are flat (Jacobian kurtosis 2.93, top-10 overlap 0%). Label a prompt ACTIVE (peak at or within 10% of the cap; all 20 scanned 128-token windows peak within 3 ULP of it, and the marginal token rate makes the 0.25-of-scale activity line near-certain from 8 tokens on) for any running text of 16 or more BPE tokens in any domain, and INACTIVE (peak exactly 0.000) only for a prompt of exactly one BPE token, whatever that token is - position 0 is the attention sink and puts z at a fixed positive value there, so every first token measured reads 0.000000 (all 408 scanned first tokens and all 25 top-example first tokens, including tokens that reach the cap later in their own window: ' and', ' in', ' the', '|', ',') - while a 2-7 token span is not decided by this hypothesis (the same word reads 0 or the cap with context: ' and' reads 0 in 14 of 54 instances, ',' in 27 of 87, ' the' in 40 of 84) and makes a poor probe; within running text the zeros are the tokens on which the neuron's own feature fires (its positive pole is an adverb detector, max 2.12, ' suddenly'), which is out of scope for this record.

Retrospective detector for local chunk completion: the pole fires on a token that completes a strongly associated, immediately adjacent multi-token unit — a split word (zer+os, prot+ons, Bon+j+our), a frozen collocation or idiom (golden+brown, powerhouse+of, three+times), or a canonical functional sequence (conditional-comma+then, quote+attribution pronoun, subject+characteristic verb). The same surface token without its collocating predecessor goes silent (e.g. ' brown' 0.82 after ' golden' vs 0.0 after ' very' or predicatively; ' of' 0.69 after ' powerhouse' vs 0.0 after ' table'), and ~80% of causal dependence lies on the peak plus the single preceding token (mean distance 1.1), beating the unigram-trigger baseline. The Jacobian/logit lenses are incoherent (kurtosis ~3.1), so it detects a completed past chunk rather than preparing any specific upcoming token.

Fires retrospectively on the token that continues or completes an already-started construction when the preceding 1-2 tokens form a complete phrase it can attach to: list commas after an item, coordinators and subordinators (and, before, from, FROM/WHERE) after a complete clause or VP/NP, temporal or nominal completions (Friday after by, times after three, year after the, next after a noun), the second word of fixed bigrams (upon after Once, to after According), and sentence-final period after a complete clause. The same surface token stays quiet without such a completable prefix, e.g. a bare weekday without by, infinitive to, abbreviation period, or a non-continuing punctuation mark.

Retrospective lexical detector for a content word that begins a new phrase, firing mainly on (a) the first subword piece of a rare technical or proper multi-token word (' cere|bellar', ' strat|ification', ' sil|viculture', ' Tuls|i', ' Ther|maled', ' compens|atory', ' Tru|jillo') and (b) clinical or remedial vocabulary (' pulmonary', ' mental', ' cerebral', ' peripheral', ' therapeutic', ' treatment', ' improve', ' boost', ' protect', ' help'), plus the purpose ' to'/' for' after attempt or evaluation words ('trying to', 'what does it mean to', 'important for'). It stays below 0.25 x max on articles, prepositions, conjunctions, punctuation and everyday common nouns and adjectives (' water', ' house', ' public', ' severe', ' new'), and the first token of any prompt sits at only about 0.07 x max, so prompts made only of such words are predicted inactive.

The pole fires when text reports or attributes a statement — it is a reported-speech/reported-writing detector. It is active on a reporting verb or noun (said, says, told, wrote, writes, remarked, noted, stated, explained, declared, added, replied, announced, confirmed, reported, 'according to', statement, letter, report) and peaks on the token that carries the attribution: the comma, colon or full stop that closes the reporting clause, the connector that opens the reported content ('that', 'how', 'whether', 'on', 'about', 'of', 'for', 'regarding', 'to'), a source or date inside the attribution ('said on Sunday', 'told The Washington Post Friday'), or the first words of the reported clause. The same punctuation, dates and connectors outside an attribution stay inactive: a plain date ('We went to the beach on Sunday'), 'that' after a non-reporting predicate ('the fact that', 'she noticed that', 'the analyst believed that', 'the court ruled that'), or a comma in an ordinary clause.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a frozen two-token function-word collocation whose first half makes it highly predictable (The more, the rest/sort, this way, kind of, his or, Whether or, and familiar subword completions such as HOW+EVER or A+FFIRMED); the same word without that left context (more, rest, way after other words) stays weak.

Fires when the current token is the highly predictable medial connector or continuation that completes a fixed multiword collocation given the immediately preceding token(s): a conjunction, preposition or particle (and, or, of, to, by, out), a joining symbol (/, &, .) or a word-internal piece (fl in cloud-fl-are, am in Ros-am-ond), as in Securities-and, margin-of, rags-to, blocks-out, Harris-/, cloud-fl.

The pole fires retrospectively at the token that completes a specifying or delimiting elaboration of an already-introduced referent, action, or claim, stating or asking which one it is, what kind it is, what it is for, or under what condition it holds. Covered completions include relative and embedded-interrogative pronouns (which, who), restrictive modifiers and compounds (only, built-in, international), function/purpose for, deontic condition words (Valid, Required), and the lexical verb resolving a modal or wh-frame (can follow, did get); the same surface token without the specifying antecedent, beneficiary for, local for international, repeated which, an anomalous verb, stays near zero.

The pole fires on the marker that opens a later entry of a run of parallel, list-like lines: the number or bullet of a list item together with the '.' or ')' that closes it (or the first word-piece of that entry), and in code the first word-piece of the next line in a block of same-shaped lines such as import statements, field declarations, or dict/object-literal entries. It stays near zero on the same digits, words and punctuation inside ordinary prose and on a lone entry with little text before it, while its strength grows both with the number of entries already in the run and with the amount of text that precedes the run.

Fires retrospectively on the current token when it is the highly predictable completion of the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens (closing paren/bracket, tag digit, indentation, subword piece, or second half of a fixed collocation/phrasal verb), with strength scaling with how forced the completion is; the same surface token without that constraining prefix does not activate it.

This pole fires on the possessor-anchored noun phrase that names the entity a dynamic, change-of-state predicate acts on: it peaks on the possessive determiner (my/our/their/your/her/his) that heads the object of an aspectual or causative verb ('ended her career', 'started my machine', 'closed my account', 'finished their project'), is weaker with 'the' and near zero with an indefinite 'a', and stays near zero when the same object follows a stative, perceptual or communicative predicate ('liked her career', 'described my machine', 'mentioned their project', 'knew my brother'). The same detector fires on the bare goal locative 'home' after a motion verb ('came/gone/drove home') and on completion/phase adverbs that mark where a situation stands ('already', 'yet', 'shortly') - the locative and temporal instances of the same 'specific entity or situation undergoing a change' feature.

The pole fires on the function word that heads a phrase specifying an extent - how long, how far, how much, how often, or compared with what: interval, rate, range, bound, approximation and comparison markers ("for" + duration, "in"/"during"/"since"/"throughout"/"past"/"over"/"across"/"within" + a time or place span, "per" + unit, "a day", "between X and Y", "X to Y", "at least", "about"/"around"/"approximately"/"nearly" + a measurement, "as ... as", "than", "like", "even"), including the same words when they front such an adjunct at a clause start ("In ...," "During ...," "For example, ..."). It stays at the neuron's floor when the same word is a complement selected by the preceding verb, noun or adjective ("waited for", "resulted in", "talked about", "used as", "walked to"), on point, contact, direction, possession and accompaniment prepositions ("at", "on", "to", "of", "with", "by", "into"), and on determiners, conjunctions and content words; activations climb with preceding context, so one-clause probes read well below running text.

Fires on the head word of a verb-phrase-internal complement that linearly follows its verb — prototypically a direct, indirect, or prepositional object noun or pronoun ('bought [[it]]', 'told [[him]]', 'opened the [[door]]', 'on the [[mat]]'), and more weakly on verb particles, resultative adjectives, and progressive participles ('stormed [[out]]', 'creaked [[open]]', 'was [[raining]]'). The same word stays near zero as a grammatical subject, as a fronted or topicalized object before its verb, as expletive 'It', or on the verb itself; within object position strength is token-modulated, so object pronouns and content nouns ('it', 'them', 'him', 'door', 'report') clear threshold while weak mass nouns ('salt', 'rice', 'cake') stay low even as objects.

This pole fires, on a mid-clause token, when that token delivers the clause's decisive new specification: flipping polarity (not/never/n't after an auxiliary), pinning an explicit quantity, referent or standard (one/1/five/12/eight, anaphoric one), naming a change-of-state or forceful motion (fell/rose/ran/rushed/broke/slipped), evaluating how it holds (gladly), or anchoring it in time, cause or comparison (after/because/in/than/to-infinitive/least). It stays near zero on sentence-initial words, in stative, existential or labeling frames (sat/costs/there are/Level/number is), on vague quantifiers (some/much/a lot/many), and on weaker or concessive alternatives (before/although/during/green/zero/two).

The pole fires on the operator that opens a modal or infinitival verb phrase: the modal auxiliaries (would, could, should, will, can, might, must, may, shall, 'll, 'd) and the infinitival 'to' together with the bare verb it governs, peaking on the operator itself or, when the 'to' is flat, on that bare verb ('to open', 'to pick'). The same sentence position filled by a copula, perfect or do-support auxiliary (is, was, were, has, had, be, been, do, did, does), or by 'to' introducing a noun phrase, stays at baseline.

L6/N1635- is the neuron's 'off' readout through GELU's dip rather than a detector of its own: strength is -min(gelu_new(z), 0) of the neuron's pre-activation z, so it reads its ceiling (the GELU global minimum, 0.1700408; within 3% of it for any z in about [-0.91, -0.61]) wherever the input sits in that trough band, and exactly 0 wherever z >= 0, which is where the enabling/improving vocabulary its positive pole encodes sits (help/helps/helped/helping, allow/let/enable/encourage/guide, support/promote/build/create/develop/improve/enhance/gain/benefit, positive/healthy/natural/social/awareness/opportunity/focus). Label 'predicted inactive' (peak below 0.0425) only for a one-token prompt (all 58 single-BPE-token words measured peak at 0.000, because a prompt's first token drives z above zero) and for a 2-4 token span whose every token stays in that field ('help', 'help develop', 'We help students', 'We can help', 'build healthy habits', 'develop positive social skills', 'positive social change', all 0.000), and label 'predicted active' at 0.9-1.0 of the ceiling for any running text of 8 or more tokens in any register (99.4% of the 8-token and 99.97% of the 16-token windows of a 247k-token pass over the scan corpus clear the 0.0425 line) and for any 2-4 token phrase with an ordinary word after position 0 (' the cat' 0.98, 'in the' 0.99, 'the committee' 0.89, 'help students' 0.73); at token level the pole is exactly 0 across that enablement field and 0.03-0.14 wherever the input is driven well below the trough (dates, rare capitalised word-initial tokens, restriction vocabulary such as 'compatible'/'patents'/'banned').

The pole is a retrospective clause-boundary detector: it fires on the linking token itself - a comma, or a clause-joining connective such as ' and', ' but', ' while', ' although', ' yet', ' as' or ' so' - when the tokens before it already form a complete subject-predicate clause and the prefix leaves the model expecting a new clause rather than more of the same noun phrase ('She opened the door and' 0.97, 'in a kingdom far away,' 1.07), and it stays at zero where the same tokens join sub-clausal material ('the cat and the dog', 'two cups of flour, one egg, and', 'I like cats and', 'The man, who was tall,', ' or', and sentence-final '.'). The peak is bit-identical whatever follows the boundary (1.063 for 'and stared', 'and on the floor' and 'and the dog barked'), so it encodes 'a finished clause is being linked to a continuation', not any particular upcoming token, with a small unexplained offshoot on high-frequency 'can't + verb' stems ('can't believe' 0.70, 'can't wait' 1.17, 'can't help' 0.67).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a research-reporting construction in which an epistemic agent (a study, poll, paper, results, reporter, or 'we') discloses, probes, or summarizes findings, peaking on the disclosure verb (investigate, explore, reveal, answer, suggest, examine) or on the complement marker introducing its object (into, on, at, that, how, or nouns like insight and evidence). The same verb or preposition without that agent-plus-findings framing activates weakly.

Fires on the verb (or stranded preposition/particle) that completes an object-gap relative or wh-clause: the head noun is the understood direct or prepositional object of that word, with an overt subject intervening between the head noun and the verb (e.g. the song she sang, the food you eat, the cases they are working on).

This pole fires retrospectively on descriptor/modifier stems: attributive adjectives (private, blind, quiet, custom, fast, serial, randomized), self-/hand- prefixes, and the onset pieces of coordinated or morphologically split verbs (rep-, refurb-, sequ-, instant-), plus the joiners (and, comma, hyphen) linking morphologically parallel items. The identical joiner tokens are silent when joining clauses or mismatched items, and head nouns and main verbs in the same frames stay near zero.

Fires on the word that links an outcome already stated to its cause, source or determining condition: 'of'/'from' after an effect, consequence, benefit, gain or damage noun ('the effects of X', 'the impact of X', 'the gains from trade', 'damage from the storm'), the causal connectives 'because (of)', 'due to', 'thanks to', 'as a result of', 'caused by', 'results from', 'attributed to', 'depends on', and a postposed 'if'/'had' clause that makes a good-or-bad outcome (fail, succeed, die, survive, be ruined, go bankrupt) depend on a condition. It stays inactive when the same words mark a non-causal relation (partitive 'of', locative 'from', agentive 'by', manner 'with', dative 'to', interrogative 'if'), when the causal arrow runs cause-to-effect ('X causes / leads to / results in Y'), and on fronted conditionals or fronted cause phrases ('If X, Y', 'Because of X, Y').
