The pole fires where the text pins down a quantity of a concrete, material or human entity: it peaks on the head noun of a cardinal/quantity phrase ('34 patients', '6,364 patients', 'hundreds of patients', '16-year-old girl') and on the ' of' that follows a concrete container, measure or person name ('a box of', 'the river of', 'eight tracts of', 'That chain of', 'John Smith of', 'Jenny L. McLeroy of'). It drops to the GELU floor in the same slots when the noun is abstract or taxonomic ('a kind of', 'the nature of', 'the number of', 'a type of', '34 ideas'), when an article replaces the quantity word ('the patients' instead of '34 patients'), or when a non-' of' word follows the concrete noun ('the river was').

This pole fires retrospectively on the first token of a subordinate or complement clause that follows an emotional or evaluative main clause, such as was happy that, was glad he, was sad that, or no matter how, where the clause elaborates what the character feels, knows, or accepts. It does not fire on the emotion or evaluation word itself, on a plain main-clause token, or on a clause with no preceding evaluative or concessive frame.

This pole tracks an asserted adverse consequence: the fallout, consequences, repercussions, ramifications, impacts, effects, implications, risk, danger or hazard that some event did or could have (and, at about half strength, the positive counterpart 'benefits'). It peaks on the word naming that consequence and on the preposition or complementiser through which a warning, fear, worry or criticism introduces one ('warned of', 'feared that', 'worried about', 'concerns about', 'raised over', 'directed at'), and it is near zero on neutral topic nouns with identical syntax ('results', 'outcomes', 'details', 'goals', 'causes', 'advantages', 'merits') and on bare descriptions of an adverse event (a crash, a spill, a fire, an injury, a disease, a layoff); its only strong non-semantic offshoots are the word-form responses to the piece 'el' in 'abelian' and to the period in 'U.S.'/'U.K.'.

The positive pole is a retrospective word detector for the vocabulary of specialized professional, technical and institutional domains: it fires on field, sector and discipline nouns (finance, education, healthcare, engineering, chemistry, linguistics, history, law, medicine, retail, marketing, agriculture, industry, sports) and on the relational adjectives and technical nouns of those domains (medical, clinical, financial, economic, environmental, cognitive, behavioral, molecular, immune, actuarial, photovoltaic, fiscal, systolic; health, market, credit, tax, insurance, employment, cancer, diabetes, security), peaking on that word at roughly 0.2-3.8 against the scan's 0.49 maximum and most strongly inside multi-word technical or institutional terms ('Financial Surveillance Section', 'cognitive neuroscience', 'mental health problems'). It is not a next-token predictor (Jacobian-lens kurtosis 3.1, zero lens overlap, and ablating the pole moves the next-token distribution by KL 6e-5 with no concentrated target), and it stays at exactly zero on everyday narrative vocabulary (table, cup, kitchen, cat, bread, kettle, lantern, bicycle, umbrella), generic abstract nouns (idea, question, reason, time, world), generic adjectives (important, various) and person/role nouns (professor, consultant, surgeon, cardiologist, lawyer, engineer), even when those name the same field; strength is context-modulated, so a domain word in an ordinary frame can fall toward the 0.12 active threshold while the same word in a technical term reaches several times the scan maximum.

Fires retrospectively when the text establishes someone's childhood or youth life-stage (a young age number, young/teenage/unborn/baby/virgin/embryo descriptors) or a kinship, reproductive, or romantic bond (father/mother/son/daughter/baby, birth, marriage, falling in love, childhood abuse), with the peak often landing on the word completing the relation (old, born, with/to/as). Adult-age numbers, non-kin uses of the same prepositions, and non-family nouns in the same frame do not sustain it.

Fires retrospectively on the clause-advancing word -- a verb, temporal/predicative adverb or adjective (already/still/now/early), or comparative/completive particle (than/to/OK) -- that continues a predicate set up by a modal, auxiliary, subject pronoun, negation, or comparative/connective frame (you/can/will/had/not/more-...-than/and/then/from-...-to). The setup word plus the advancing word are jointly required; wording of the downstream complement is irrelevant.

The neuron fires retrospectively on the token that refers to a story character or animate being: a personal name or the final subword of a multi-token name (Sam, Sue, Lily, John, and the fragments ue in Sue, ie in Rosie, my in Timmy), a pronoun or animate common noun referring to an established character (it, people, bird, ant, owl, someone), most strongly when that referent has already been introduced earlier in the story. It also fires, more weakly, on the indefinite article a/an when it introduces a new sound or percept after a perception verb (heard a voice, heard an angry sound, heard a loud noise). It does not fire on verbs, adjectives, or determiners in other roles, and only weakly on inanimate nouns such as tomatoes or cars.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a locally highly predictable multi-token chunk: a hyphen, en dash, slash or colon joining a compound word, name, numeric range, fraction or time, a non-initial subword piece continuing a longer word or name, or the final word of a fixed collocation such as 'a little bit' or 'slowly and carefully'. The same surface token in an unpredictable or non-chunk context stays quiet.

Fires on the token that completes a lexicalized two-part unit: the second subword of a split word (res-olutions, cons-ignment, v-ials) or the second word of a conventionalized compound, collocation, or fixed phrase (stock price, bus driver, Application form, Operating System, barbecue area, margin of, weigh-in, built into). The same word in a compositional context -- 'of' after 'thought' versus after 'margin', an adverb after 'bus'/'barbecue' versus the compound noun, or 'cons' without 'ignment' -- stays near zero.

Fires retrospectively on the specifier token — a numeral or quantifier, ordinal, polarity or negation marker, degree adjective, or endpoint preposition or operator — that fixes the quantity, order, polarity, or destination of the phrase headed by the next token (e.g. the final->note, the second->half, to 3->.9, by 12->percent, a positive->one, to->the-summit, would not->seek). It needs the 1-2 token preamble that opens the slot (the/to/a/by/at/than/for, a verb like prescribed, or a numeral like 13) and goes quiet when the same slot holds a purely descriptive word.

The positive pole fires on a numeral (arabic or spelled out, any magnitude) that is lower than a numeral seen earlier in the same passage - a descending step in a numeric listing such as a countdown, a reverse-chronological year list, a ranked score or delegate-count table, a discount price column, or a decrementing counter; the earlier, larger number does not have to be the immediately preceding one. Ascending and repeated numerals stay near zero, as does an isolated number in ordinary prose, activation is strongest for runs that step down one at a time, and descending letters (d, c, b, a) give a weak version of the same response.

The positive pole fires on words that name a person's physical body and how it looks: body shape and build (physique, figure, curvy, waist, stocky, slim, muscular, 'build'), body size and weight (weight, weigh-in, pounds, underweight, overweight, 'body' in 'upper body'), fitness and athletic condition (fit, fitness, gym, workout, muscle, strength, athlete, wrestler, boxer), and the grooming-and-display words that present a body (makeup, mascara, glamour, fashion, runway, pageant, bikini, nude, beautiful or attractive said of a person). It is sense-specific and local: the same surface forms in abstract, object or non-human senses - 'the body of the text', 'the figure in the report', an airport runway, 'an early stage', 'a financially attractive offer', a curvy road, the beauty of a painting, sport results and politics - stay near zero, as do neutral prose and long-range topic carry-over.

Retrospective genericity/definition detector for expository prose: the pole fires on the linking token that opens the predicate of a kind-level statement, i.e. the ' to' of 'X refers to / is specific to / is relative to / is tied to Y', the ' a' or opening quote of 'X is / describes / is called a Y' and 'what is called a ...', and the 'between' of 'X distinguishes between A and B', with the peak strength set by the subject and predicate that precede it. A bare-plural or indefinite 'a/an' subject keeps it high (peak 1.5-2.5), while the same sentence with a definite or demonstrative subject ('the', 'this') falls to 0.5-1.0, and ordinary event narrative and lexical verbs and conjunctions leave it at the ~0.54 floor; peak height does not depend on the words that follow the peak. Leftover examples are name/identifier introductions in code ('import Kiss', 'name: "Sides"', 'get_where'), which fit a naming offshoot of the same 'introduce a specific term' job.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that continues or completes a conventionalized multi-word chunk cued by the preceding 1-3 tokens: the second hyphen of hyphenated compound modifiers (up-to-date, N-year-old, one-to-X), 'of' after chunk heads (a lot of, devoid of), 'from' after away, 'and' joining paired adjectives (different and unique), 'bounds' after leaps and, 'yet' after not. Breaking the cue words to the left of the peak lowers activation, while changing words after the peak leaves it unchanged, so the pole detects chunk completion from left context rather than predicting what comes next.

The pole fires on a single token that names or performs a warm social or emotional expression: a positive emotion or moral-good noun such as happiness, fairness, love, excitement or surprise, a greeting such as hello, a thank-you such as thanks, or a social-repair word such as sorry. The peak is on that token itself, with nearby friendly or feeling words (friendly before hello, feel before love, give before thanks) supporting it.

Fires retrospectively on a token whose identity is strongly determined by the preceding context, that is, the predictable completion of a unit already established in the passage or by convention: the final token of a repeated proper name (Abigail, Susie, Timmy) or repeated story entity (dragon, rabbit), the completion of a fixed phrase such as time in Once upon a time, or a common descriptive adjective in an indefinite noun phrase such as red in a red car. First mentions of a name, the same adjective after the, and uncommon completions such as wooden in a wooden chair fire weakly.

Fires on the token that opens a parenthetical interruption inserted mid-sentence in running prose, strongest (often >0.6 of max) on a spaced dash ' –'/' —' or an open paren ' (' placed right after a noun phrase or subject before its clause is finished, and moderately (0.4-0.8) on the comma or the first word ('for' in ', for example', 'as', 'however', 'which' after an em-dash) of a comma-delimited aside; it is near zero on plain prose with no inserted aside, on the first token of any prompt, on hyphens/ranges/minus signs in compounds, numbers or code, on function-call parentheses like f(x), and on a parenthesis that starts a new sentence.

The pole fires on words that carry an appraisal or a conferred status rather than describing the situation: evaluative/attitudinal adjectives and participles (controversial, important, welcome, appreciated, delighted, amazing, risky, notorious, foolish, valuable, tedious), designation/attribution verbs and participles (considered, regarded, deemed, termed, dubbed, labeled, called, viewed), evaluative comment adverbs and approximating hedges (surprisingly, importantly, unfortunately, essentially, basically, nearly, almost, virtually, widely, largely), and the particle that closes such a predicate ('viewed as', 'taken as', 'filed under', 'close to'). It stays near zero on objective property words (red, tall, wooden, rectangular, secure), plain event verbs (made, said, used, given), and exact intensifiers (very, completely, exactly, clearly, certainly); the same evaluative word fires far more weakly as a bare attributive modifier ('the controversial decision', 0.09) than in predicate/appositive position ('the decision was controversial', 1.84), and the peak is the stance word itself rather than the following token, so the unit is retrospective (Jacobian lens kurtosis 3.05, 0% agreement with the logit lens, no coherent promoted token set).

The pole fires on the word that joins a phrase to the complement or clause it introduces - the connector itself, never the content that follows: a wh-word after a preposition ('in which', 'by which', 'with which'), 'where' after a noun ('the place where', 'the laboratory where'), purposive 'so (that)', a question word plus inverted auxiliary ('how do', 'what is'), a purpose 'for' that complements a preceding noun or 'in order' ('a charity for', 'in order for'), the dot or slash that opens a new label inside a URL or file path ('github.com', 'http://', 'libcds/'), and the high-frequency complement-taking verbs bring, help, provide, supply, give and link when they introduce an object. It stays inactive on the same words in phrase-internal or filler uses - 'the', 'is', 'and', bare subject/object relatives ('which', 'who', 'whom'), degree 'so', 'how many', 'how to', verb-adjunct 'for' ('used for', 'paid for') and an ordinary sentence full stop - and its strength does not change when only the following content changes.

Fires retrospectively on the relational head word (a preposition, loop separator, or examination/selection verb such as FROM, among, in, across, atop, au/des, :, grade, analyzing, surveyed) at the point where an already-read selection, ranking, iteration, examination, or spanning operation attaches to the collection, population, source table, or span it operates over; strength is gated by that operator frame (SELECT enables FROM, foreach-headers enable in, spanning verbs enable across), not by the head token alone.

N809+ fires on predications of an ongoing or currently-obtaining situation rather than a completed event or a generic property: it peaks on the present participle of a be ... -ing progressive or a participial modifier (is walking, was cooking, you are doing, sat reading, stalking through), on while/as when one event is framed as running on while another happens, and on a locative or definite time complement of be (is outside, are upstairs, is here, is winter, is Monday); the same clause in simple past/perfect (fished, the children all laughed, has already finished), a passive past participle (was broken, was written), a nominal -ing (building, feelings) or a generic property predicate (is pleasant, is red, is a doctor, are animals) stays near zero. This is not chunk-completion or local predictability: the trigger is imperfective aspect plus referential anchorage, so highly predictable simple-tense collocations stay dead ('the kettle boiled' 0.00, 'central bank raised rates' 0.55 on a non-imperfective token) while low-probability progressives fire maximally ('is rumbling' 2.01, 'were laughing' 1.17), and a single aspectual edit flips the same lexical frame ('she is walking' 1.83 vs 'she is late' 0.62; 'was breaking' 0.97 vs 'was broken' 0.21). The pole sometimes lights on the auxiliary one token before the participle (are at 2.92 before doing), but it peaks on the participle already read, and zero-ablating it mostly removes probability from -ing and path words (umbling, playing, being, through), so the mechanism is retrospective.

Fires retrospectively on linker tokens that attach a qualifying specification to the preceding clause or noun: causal/occasion subordinators (since, because, once) opening a reason-or-occasion clause, and the joiner pieces of compound adjectival modifiers — the adverb well directly premodifying a participle/adjective and the hyphen joining a modifier compound (long-term, avant-garde, well-defined). The same surface tokens stay quiet in other roles (concessive though/although, manner-adverb or noun well, scoreline hyphen), and the content of the specification itself does not matter.

Fires on the word right after a definite article 'the' (the head noun, or a pre-nominal evaluative/degree adjective such as good/high/great/low) when that 'the'-phrase is the object of a verb or preposition and names an abstract, non-referential notion that waits for a defining postmodifier: manner, situation, stage, role, kind, range, point, mistake, effects, approach, fortune, or the 'high/low/good' of an attained quantity (earn the high, achieve the low, have the good). It is near silent when the article is 'a', 'this' or 'his' instead of 'the', when the noun is concrete (box, kitchen, table, piano, hammer, car, bus), and on sentence-initial subject phrases such as 'The way ...'; a weaker offshoot fires on 'that' or 'it' starting a relative clause right after an abstract noun (toughness that, attitude that).

This pole fires at the boundary of a labelled entry in enumerative or definitional text, i.e. at the position where a specific name is about to be spelled out or where the next listed item begins: the token ' for' of 'stand(s)/standing/stood for' and 'short for' (all 12 such ' for' occurrences in the scan fire, 0.92-4.25), the ' (' that follows an all-caps initialism ( CEC, SPF, USGS, PII, DTD, MESSENGER: 0.7-2.5), and the separator that closes one entry of a list, directory, table or citation run (newline, comma, semicolon, '|', middle dot, bullet dash: 0.5-2.8, with the scan maximum 5.60 on a newline closing an organisation entry), strength building over successive entries. Running prose, a lone newline before an isolated name that is not part of a list, sentence-initial articles or imperative verbs after a newline, and enumerations of numbers stay at or near zero.

Fires retrospectively when the current phrase describes contestants vying for, winning, losing, retaking or holding a contested position, prize, territory or lead (race/struggle/competition for office, won/wins/win/victory/winning, secured/regained/reclaimed/seized/clinched/claimed a title). The same peak tokens in non-contest frames (a desire/care for X, left office, discussed rank) do not activate it.

The pole fires on a narrow set of speaker-stance tokens rather than on descriptive content: the hedges and degree words quite, rather and too, the evaluative adverb unfortunately, interjection token forms (ah, uh, eh, ok) and negated auxiliaries (doesn't, isn't). Its highest peaks (2.0-2.5, above any ordinary word) fall on short interjection-like BPE pieces ('ah', 'uh', 'ok', 'ess', 'ih') that sit inside rare, foreign or code-like words (e.g. 'ah' in 'Takahata', 'uh' in 'Kuhn', 'ess' in 'Sessao'); ordinary content words and precise degree adverbs (bad, problem, the, of, highly, slightly, nearly) stay near zero.

Fires on the bare single-letter BPE token ' b' (or 'b' after a hyphen/joiner), i.e. a word-initial 'b' that the tokenizer split off as its own token because the word (bode, bisher, bij, biliary, bivalent, bachelors, bought in a URL) is not one vocabulary item, at roughly 0.5-1.0 of max in any context (weakest, ~0.3, for an isolated list label like 'b)'); weaker (~0.3-0.55) on other short word-initial prefix fragments such as ' mult', ' bl', ' ant', ' ob', ' cl', ' single'. Whole-word tokens starting with b (' bought', ' bear', ' bachelor', ' blue') and all other tokens, including the first token of a prompt, stay near zero, so prompts without such a fragment token are predicted inactive.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes or continues a formulaic identification of a person or attributed source: the closer of a birth date/place frame, or the pronoun, copula, relative pronoun, conjunction, title noun, or stance/source marker that states or adds role, kinship, affiliation, or evaluative standing (He is, she serves, who works, actress and singer, Policy Expert, Ambassador of, Source, Arguably). The same tokens stay near baseline in ordinary event narrative or when the description concerns non-persons; mid-word all-caps headline fragments (MOROCCO, ALMANYA) are an acknowledged unexplained offshoot.

The pole fires on the constituent that follows a copula or auxiliary in a clause where the element the verb governs has been displaced to that slot: the associate NP after existential 'there is/are/was/were' (peaking on the quantifier/determiner that opens it and on its head noun — no, some, more, much, many, any), the postponed subject of a root wh-/yes-no question ('Is the president correct?', 'What is cloud computing?'), and the last word or closing comma of an adverbial inserted between an auxiliary and its complement ('were, in the end, published'). The same words stay near zero when nothing is displaced: NPs in pre-verbal subject position ('Much doubt about the plan remains'), a plain article+noun complement of a non-existential copula ('It is a question of time'), and ordinary declaratives ('The results were published').

Fires when the current token completes a familiar, highly constrained two-part chunk: the second half of a year or number (16+20, 17+25), a surname, demonym or compound (Jerome+Powell, Port+man, Californ+ians), a fixed collocation (year-old, half a dozen, no patience, some light, Parents are), or the comma closing an age or circumstance clause (was six, / years old, / without her,). The preceding token or tokens strongly predict the peak token.

Fires retrospectively on the operative word of a clause reporting an authoritative disposition or carried-out action — a court, police, government, employer, or God-like authority granting, denying, ordering, imposing, appointing, or effecting something (sentenced, granted/denied a motion, declared a mistrial, directed a verdict, froze an account, appointed officers, employs people, enabling/helping); the peak is usually that verb or participle, or the complementizer, preposition, or determiner continuing its clause (that, for, after, a, first).

This pole fires retrospectively on separator punctuation that joins segments of a structured technical reference: prototypically the '.' in a domain (bag.com), a filename with extension (min.js), or a dotted library/method path (system.getInfo), with '/' in path-like references (e.g. /r/LEGO) as an offshoot. It is gated by technical context: the identical sentence-final '.' ending an ordinary non-technical sentence leaves it silent.

Fires on a restricted set of unit-opening stems and word-initial fragments (fire, Wind, Sand, Fen, Thunder, Ded, opens, integ, due, up, come, Red, Boston, Chris, G, and the hyphen inside such units) exactly when the prefix up to and including the token forms the still-incomplete left half of a stereotyped multi-token unit: a tokenizer-split word (Sand|well, Fen|way, Thunder|bolt, Ded|ication, opens|ource) or a frozen collocation (due|to, up|to, come|from, fire|extinguisher, Red|Sox, Boston|Red, first-name|surname, G|damn, up|front, Wind|turbines in power-grid context). The identical token stays weak or silent when its phrase is already complete (camp fire burned, was due yesterday, friend Chris arrived, topic-less sentence-initial Wind), and the pole never fires on compound openers outside this trigger set (chicken broth, Manchester United, coast road, Schedule B, water/dam/boats passages) or on the completion pieces themselves (well, way, bolt, ication, Sox).

This pole fires retrospectively on the linking word of a concrete descriptive predication: the copula ('is'/'was'/'were'), an attributive preposition ('of'), or the clause-final stop after a clause that pins a physical state, magnitude, composition, location or concrete quantity onto a specific entity ('The museum is open', 'The powerhouse of the cell is small', 'The boulder at the trailhead was enormous'), and on scalar state/magnitude predicates themselves ('open', 'enormous'). The linking word's strength is set entirely by its left context, the subject entity plus the richness of the preceding descriptive buildup, so it is blind to the predicate that follows and grows with multi-clause concrete description; it stays near zero on colour, material, taste and shape adjectives in isolation and on abstract institutional, legal, modal or code-register predications ('material breach', 'unlikely', 'critical timeout', 'void and moot'), even in identical copular frames.

This pole fires retrospectively on a non-initial token of a conventionalized multi-token unit whose left context strongly constrains it: the hyphen joining a familiar compound (risk-free, dose-dependent, cost-effective), a non-initial subword piece of a long word (enz-ym-atic, centrif-ug-ation, spont-ane-ity), or a preposition opening an adjunct right after a coordinator or comma (and at least, But at least). The same surface token with a neutral left context stays quiet (table-free, thymatic, walked at, cost/effective), and changing only the continuation after the peak leaves activation unchanged.

N1883's negative pole is not a feature detector but the silence readout of a rarely-firing neuron: its strength is -min(gelu_new(pre-activation), 0), hard-capped at the gelu_new global minimum 0.1700408 (reached by 3,071 of the 3,072 L7 neurons on this corpus), and the neuron is silent on 88% of tokens, so 97% of the scan's 128-token snippets peak within 1e-4 of that ceiling, no snippet in 200k tokens peaks below 0.1696, and the 20 top examples are float32 ties 1 ULP apart. Label 'predicted active' (peak >= 0.95 of max) for any running text of >= 8 tokens in any domain, and 'predicted inactive' (peak < 0.25 of max) only for a short span every one of whose tokens flips the pre-activation positive - ' In', ' appear/appears/appeared', ' inside', ' within', ' known', ' name/names', ' seems/looks', ' easily/easier', ' isn/doesn/aren/wasn/won', ' ran', ' past', ' could', ' might' - which is also the entire 33% token-identity confound; a single such token cannot lower the peak of normal prose, because the peak is a max over positions.

Fires when the text is identifying, describing or credentialing people (or the institutions they belong to) in social or professional terms - an occupation or role (lawyer, banker, professor, director, specialists, princess), who leads, founds, hires, staffs or partners with whom, or the standing and credentials ascribed to them (renowned, eminent, reputable, respected, prestigious, top, leading, experienced, wealthy, talented). Event narration, inanimate scenes, technical or abstract explanation and bare quantities leave it at zero, and the negative pole is only GPT-2's GELU floor (~0.17 on every token) carrying no separate feature.

L7/N2069+ detects a bounded part, portion or component of a larger whole. It peaks on a noun that names a component or subdivision of a structured object (body parts: chest, shoulder, neck, finger, muscle, tissue; subdivisions: line, page, row, string, set, piece, byte, scene), and on the ' of' of a partitive or measure construction where a portion/measure/collection noun is tied to the substance it portions out ('a bottle of water' 1.03, 'a kilogram of sugar' 1.27, 'two cups of flour' 0.76, '500 mg of amoxicillin' 1.58); a measure or unit noun also peaks when directly preceded by an expressed number ('5 meters' 1.56 vs 'meters' 0.16). It stays at its floor when the same head noun heads a genitive or property relation ('the colour of water' 0.02, 'the price of sugar' 0.00, 'the glass of the window' 0.04, 'the crust of bread' 0.11) and when a unit noun has no expressed number ('distances in meters' 0.18); a plain counted object after a number does not fire ('5 apples' 0.00).

The pole detects legislative and electoral politics in the text read so far: it fires on political office-holders and bodies (senator, congressman, Congress, Senate, House, parliament, lawmaker, governor, councilman, incumbent, secretary of state), on legislation and votes on it (bill, legislation, amendment, measure, appropriations, filibuster, veto, repeal, and vote-report phrases such as 'the motion passed by a narrow margin'), and on office-seeking phrases ('run(s)/ran/running for X', 'seek a second ...', 'seek another term', 'seek re-election', 'candidacy'), often peaking on the token that completes the political phrase ('would not seek re-election', 'running for president') rather than on the political noun alone. It stays inactive on ordinary prose and on non-political domains (courts and judges, government agencies, company results, sports, science, recipes), and on 'run for' with a non-human subject such as 'the dog ran for the ball'.

Fires retrospectively when the current token is a past-tense cognition, belief, perception, or affect predicate (knew, thought, believed, felt, realized, suggested) or the complement introducer or continuation of its clausal complement (that, like, it/I, or clause-final punctuation), registering a remembered belief, impression, or assessment. Present-tense counterparts and non-mental past-tense verbs in the same frame drive it weakly or not at all.

This pole fires retrospectively on sentence-continuation junctures: subordinating or conditional frame-setters (given, before, while, since, By plus gerund), coordinators joining two contentful phrases (and, or), boundary commas marking apposition, lists or adjuncts, complement-taking speech verbs such as asked before a wh-complement, and prepositions that extend a phrase (to, by, from) — tokens whose structural role is to continue or embed the current clause with new material rather than terminate it. It stays near zero on superficially identical tokens that do not continue structure, such as the comma inside '1,000', 'and' inside the frozen binomial 'rock and roll', or an uncoordinated proper name.

The pole fires retrospectively on a token whose immediately preceding cue licenses it: fixed two-token chunks (ORDER/GROUP to BY, golden/dark to brown, pleaded/did to not, degrees to Celsius/Fahrenheit, 5 to p) and a small memorized set of broad licenser cues (death, late, capital, murder) that elevate many following nouns; the identical head token after a non-licensing cue, including near-synonyms (dead, big, twin, killing, was, pretty), stays near zero.

This pole fires on tokens at the second and later positions of a conventionalized multi-token chunk: fixed collocations and reduplications (question after question, from time to time, speak truth to power, year upon year), name coordinations (News & World, Securities and Exchange, Q&A), and standard number, date, time and rate formats (18-49, 40 events per minute, five days a week, August 14, 13 June, 4:30 p.m., 4,000 years). Firing is driven by the preceding chunk context, not token identity: the same token outside such a frame (to after 'money', after after 'long', '-' after 'numbers 18', '13' after 'bought') activates weakly, while changing only the following word leaves the connector unchanged.

Fires on a negator token when the negation bears on an evaluative adjective, a gerund or obligation, or a past-tense contraction: ' not' before an adjective or gerund ('not nice/mean/shiny', 'not listening', 'asked not to tell'), "'t" in 'couldn't/didn't/wasn't' + verb, ' no' in 'no one', and ' hardly'/' barely'. It is strongest (about 0.7-1.0 of max) on ' not' before an evaluative adjective or gerund and on ' no' in 'no one'. It stays weak (below about 0.25 of max) on 'do/does not' + an ordinary verb ('know/like/want/believe'), 'is not a' + noun, quantifier negation ('not every/only'), existential 'no' ('no milk/time/water'), 'cannot', 'never', and 'doesn't/wouldn't/isn't' contractions. Two token-specific offshoots from the prior record still fire strongly: the 'im' piece of 'Narasimha' (about 1.0 of max) and ' of' in 'Section <number> of the ... Act' (about 0.8 of max).

Fires retrospectively on a deictic anchor token — the demonstrative determiner (this/that) or the authorial first-person plural (we/We) — when it occupies its slot in a conventionalized formal-exposition formula stating the work's aim, method, or institutional holding (e.g. 'The aim of this investigation', 'In this study, we examined', 'this Court determined').

Fires on the token itself, mainly on the desire verb " wish" (strongest when it follows a subject in a relative or conditional clause: "products that they wish to", "if you wish to", "I wish I") and on the royal titles " Queen"/" King" used as a capitalised title or the start of a name ("Queen Mary", "King's Cross", "King's College"), each about 0.65-0.9 of max. Near-synonyms (want, like, hope, plan), "Kings"/"Kingston" and ship-style names stay at or below about 0.35. The relative/interrogative " who" (0.35-0.55), "Prince", "Thank you"/"Thanks in advance" and "Copyright (" in long license headers fire more weakly. Ordinary prose stays near 0.1, but sentence-final '.' or ',' after a clause often reaches 0.2-0.35 of max, so even short prompts without a trigger can sit near the 0.25 threshold.

Peaks on dependent-linking tokens that attach the current phrase to an already-read head: relative pronouns and complementizers (that, which, whatever), prepositional linkers (by, of, with, as), conditional if, and the bound pronoun or gapped verb continuing the dependent clause (I, sich, posed). Strength tracks how specifically the linker refers back to that head, so anaphoric that beats proximal this and argument-linking by beats locative near/at, while the same upcoming word with a different linker fires differently.

Fires retrospectively on the marker introducing the second branch of a two-part parallel construction -- ordinals like 'second', repeat adverbs like 'again', sequence adverbs like 'then', a second quantity or name, or a contrastive 'and'/'but'/comma -- only when earlier context established a matching first branch (a first time, first quantity, first alternative, or first step). The same trigger tokens without a parallel antecedent evoke little or no activity.

Retrospective locative/situating detector: fires on words that say where or by what something is situated or serviced -- strongest on passive ' served' (also ' run', ' held', ' covered', ' operated' weaker) right after 'is/was', on the comma right after a street address or room number ('Avenue,' 'Street,' 'Room 108,'), on spatial ' on'/' in' after a posture, occurrence or copular verb ('standing on', 'is on', 'shot in', 'go on', 'running on'; it fires there whatever follows), and on the place noun that closes such a phrase ('hallway', 'hall', 'floor', 'kitchen', 'room'). It is silent or weak on argument/idiomatic prepositions ('depends on', 'relies on', 'interested in', 'fond of', 'born in', 'based in'), predicate adjectives/nouns, and plain text without a placement phrase; there is no floor (the first token is ~0.08 of max).

This pole fires on the second token of a locally highly constrained continuation: the completion of a fixed collocation such as a verb plus particle (slow down, speed up, open out), a complex preposition (out of), boilerplate (IN NO EVENT SHALL), a question or conditional onset (How would, will/would/does after a comma or preamble), a predictable subword (outstripped, Rawalpindi) or an identifier plus '(' in code, and it stays low on the same surface token when the preceding word or two do not strongly predict it.

This pole fires on the token that completes a locally predictable continuation: a frequent collocation or idiom (the second, can't, upon a time), a morphological completion (re-election), or a function word, quantifier, numeral, or subordinator grammatically licensed by the preceding words (are after Where/There, to after remember, three after after). The identical token evokes little or no activation when the preceding one or two tokens neither lexically predict nor grammatically license it (three after table, time after green), while a few ultra-frequent completions ('t, all, election after any hyphenated prefix, after) fire near their token-driven level regardless.

Fires at the pivot of an explicit comparison or likening, where the comparative, similarity or repetition particle introduces its second term: 'than' and 'as ... as', 'like', 'to'/'from' after identical/similar/different/comparable/superior, and the second 'after' of 'X after X', together with the determiner or substitute that opens that term ('more effective than the treatment', 'identical to those of the first study', 'as clear as the earlier findings', 'question after question'). It stays inactive on non-comparative uses of the same words - temporal 'after', spatial 'to', the conjunction 'and', and degree comparisons against a bare quantity ('more than a hundred') - and on comparisons of simple concrete physical objects ('the box was heavier than the bag').

Fires retrospectively when the current token is the digit 1 (forms '1' and ' 1'), with strength graded by left context: strongest when the 1 heads a structured enumeration or announced quantity (lone math answer, address '1 London', crowd '1,600', ratio '1:1', list '1.'), weaker when bare or hedged ('Only 1%'). It also fires moderately on a narrow non-numeric trigger set — the 'common' family ('common', 'uncommon', 'commonly'), 'convention'/'Convention', and the word 'one' — but not on other digits in the same slots ('7 London', '2.', '$5') nor on near-synonyms ('shared', 'company', 'first', 'many'). Weaker partial responses on a few other content tokens (e.g. 'spread', 'polymorph', 'Patriot') are acknowledged leftovers this claim does not cover.

Fires retrospectively on the function/purpose marker of a fitness-or-utility construction: the current token (for, in, to, help, serve, assist) introduces the use, benefit, role, or effect-domain of a capability, instrument, requirement, or causal factor described just before (e.g. 'required for', 'used in', 'risk factor for', 'solution to', 'powers help'). The same preposition or verb after a locative, motion, or neutral context (played in, taken for, small object for) activates it weakly or not at all.

The pole fires retrospectively on tokens at within-word positions: non-initial pieces that continue or complete a split multi-token word (cat+he+ters, d+ural, f+ruct, hal+ve, end+ear), and whole-word tokens from a specific learned set (burn, cut, fatal, human, lend, hal, double, spinal, wound, death, fracture, ending). It responds to the word itself across left-contexts while matched same-rime controls (turn, gut, final, woman, send, tal, trouble, mural, scar, cancer) stay near-silent.

Fires on a coordinating token ('and', 'or', 'nor', 'vs', 'versus') that links two items as alternatives or values under one frame: the correlative 'both X and Y', the comparison 'X versus Y', and the 'and' that closes a numeric or graded series ('10, 20, and 30 minutes', 'pre and post measurements'); in code the same junction shows up on the operator or separator between two operands ('? :', '+', '>'). It stays near the floor when the coordinator instead merely groups two independent referents, names, fixed binomials or whole clauses ('Barnes and Noble', 'drinks and snacks', 'the nurses and the doctors', 'nice and warm', 'opened the door and walked in').

Fires retrospectively on a token that marks a temporal transition in a story: most strongly ' until', which ends an ongoing state at a boundary point ('kept weighing the deaf people until the church was happy', 'keep it safe until later', 'stayed at the top of the tower until the sun was setting'), ' soon', which marks an imminent change of state ('soon felt better', 'soon fell asleep', 'soon talking'), and ' upon' in the story-opening formula 'Once upon a time'; more weakly ' fast' and ' quickly' (pace of change), ' When' and 'when' (a temporal clause that shifts the scene), ' then' and 'Then', ' later', ' After' and 'after', ' before', ' finally', and ' Suddenly' (sequencing of events). It does not fire on the same words when they do not mark a narrative time transition, and its output direction promotes tokens about departure, arrival and ending (' retire', ' demise', ' departure', ' return', ' arrival').

Fires retrospectively on the content word that completes a conventionalized two-to-three-word collocation frame (ordinals first/second/following or contrastive other after in/the/on, and idiomatic completions such as looks-like, top-end, in-that-case, on-the-other-hand/side, cut-in-half, space-over, a-good/fine-job); the same word in free composition without the preceding function-word or fixed-head frame activates weakly or not at all.

L7/N499+ is a lexical detector for the English verb DO: it fires hardest on the token that carries DO's stem in any full surface form (' do'/'Do', ' does'/'Does', ' did'/'Did', ' doing', and 'done' when it is a verbal participle), no matter what role DO plays - auxiliary of negation ('they do not change', 3.9), emphatic verb ('They did experience', 3.6), inverted support in a wh-question whose subject precedes it ('subjects do you have', 3.6), imperative ('Do this', 3.8) or the main verb ('the filter does a good job', 3.9; 'were doing research', 3.8) - and it is indifferent to negation and to what follows ('does not' = 'does often' = 'does mention', all 3.5-3.6). It is not a general auxiliary, tense or negation detector: be/have/can/will/would/could/should/must sit at -0.12 mean over thousands of occurrences (max 0.52), ordinary verbs (mention, require, use, say) at about 0, and activation is graded down within the DO paradigm - to 0.2-0.3 when the same form is clause-initial/inverted rather than in its post-subject slot ('Why does this happen?' 0.26, 'and so does the assistant' 0.18, 'she wondered why does the manager...' 0.82 vs 2.79 in situ; across the scan mean 0.82 vs 2.36), to roughly half on the contraction stems don't/doesn't/didn't (mean 0.92-1.38 vs 2.1), and to ~0.3 on adjectival 'done' ('the job is done') though verbal 'has done' still reaches 3.1; the only fringe outside DO is the modal 'may' (mean 0.66, max 1.9), while the 'Am' entry in this pole's confound profile is a subword fragment of names ('Amstrong', 'Amish', 'Amro', 'Amazin') - the copula ' am' is flat at 0.11.

The pole fires where an abstract frame - a dimension of a situation rather than a thing - is named, or handed over to the phrase that specifies it: on the frame noun itself ('the aim', 'the purpose', 'the goal', 'the way', 'the extent', 'the case', 'the mechanism', 'the format', 'the manner') and on the wh-word or relativizer that opens the embedded, relative or complement clause supplying that frame's content ('depends on when/where/how he arrives', 'the manner in which he spoke', 'the reason why he left', 'the fact that he never called'). It stays near zero when the same word carries no such frame: a wh-word opening a root question ('Where does he park the car?', 'When does he arrive?'), the verbal complementizer 'that' ('I think that he is right'), or the noun in a verbal or fixed idiomatic use ('we aim to compare', 'took aim at the target', 'on my way home').

The pole fires on a token that sits inside an already-open multi-token unit rather than starting one: (a) a non-initial subword piece of an uncommon word - 'yl' in Wylie/amyloid/xylophone, 'z' in Menzies, 'en' in Gyllenhaal, 'ipl' in whiplash, 'and' in quandary, 'me' in nonheme, 'ik' in Nishikado/Tchaikovsky, '1' in H1N1, 'isen' in Meisenbach; and (b) an enumeration/continuation marker that extends a list already under way ('and'/'or'/list comma, 'etc', 'and so on'/'and so forth'). It stays near its floor on a multi-token word's first piece, on 'and' joining two adjectives or two clauses, and on ordinary prose; the interior-piece half is a learned set (24 uncommon multi-piece words tested, about 6 fired), so an unfamiliar interior piece is more likely inactive than active.

This pole fires retrospectively on a single-character token, a lone letter or digit with or without a leading space, that is not itself a common standalone word such as a or I: typically the opening fragment of a longer word, such as the first letter of a proper name (Lily, Tandy, Sue), of a vivid descriptive word (yummy, yucky, elderly), or of a compound (x-ray), or a short numeral (3). It does not fire on ordinary multi-letter word tokens, or on single letters that form a complete common word.

Fires on a coordinating conjunction or comma (' and', ' or', ' but', ',') that extends a clause's SUBJECT noun phrase before its main verb has appeared (e.g. 'The CEO of the FRC[[ and]] the CEO of PwC have...', 'The morality of this work[[,]] like...', 'Age and disease duration at surgery[[,]] gender...'), strongest after a long, modified subject NP at the start of a sentence or embedded clause; the same ' and'/',' after a verb (inside an object NP) or joining two clauses is near zero.

The pole's dominant and generalisable trigger is orthographic: it fires when GPT-2's tokenizer emits a bare lowercase 'v' as its own word-internal piece ('Spor|v|ognsdrift', 'ne|v|ada', 'nonsur|v|ival', 'tri|um|v|iral', 'sol|v|ability'), across unrelated words and languages (82% of 34 dictionary words with such a piece scored above 0.4, versus medians at or below 0.07 for bare m, n, c, t, l, k, s, d, r, b and f), and it drops to the prompt baseline when that 'v' is edited to 'b' or when the v sits inside a larger token ('gave', 'love', 'never', 'village' are all about 0). A weaker second job runs on the vocabulary of bonds, agreements and opposition between parties - married, marriage, engaged, joining, comply, obey, consent, agree, agreement, mutual, couples, spouse, quit, stay, avoid, confront, oppose, resist, defend - which reads 0.4-1.5, while concrete nouns, abstract non-relational nouns and physical or transactional verbs (house, method, give, build, take, love, choose) sit between 0 and -0.15.

The pole fires at the onset of an anchoring attachment to an already-complete head: a parenthetical elaboration on a descriptive nominal ('(RWA)', '(see fig. 3)'), an exception phrase on a quantified domain ('except Madison'), a time/place/means/extent PP or goal particle completing a bounded event ('in 2014', 'on Monday', 'by the lake' after 'ends', 'with a pocketknife', 'through the second paragraph', 'home' after 'went'), a gerundial elaboration after an aspectual begin/end verb ('began by reading'), or the copula predicating of an established topic noun ('The focus ... is ...'). It is graded by boundedness: strongest with specific anchors on bounded heads ('by reading' 2.3, acronyms 1.4-1.7), moderate on partial anchors ('with a pocketknife' 0.7, 'went home' 0.6, 'by Friday' 1.2, 'at the end' 1.6), and weak-to-floor on core arguments rather than adjuncts (operand/passive 'by'), routine modification inside unbounded or procedural frames ('waited by the window', 'for an hour', 'at the store', 'of the lens', 'Multiply ... by 3 (...)'), bare 'to'-infinitives ('began to read'), generic kind-definitions ('A cataract is ...' 0.08), bare NP-list coordination, square-bracketed elaborations (weaker than round parens), and headless sentence-initial material ('(All prices ...)', 'As').

This pole fires on a definite determiner, 'the' or a possessive pronoun (her/his/your/my), that is the immediate complement of the preposition 'on' (with 'at/upon' as near-equivalents and weaker 'to/off/through/by' variants given supporting left context). It stays quiet when the slot holds an indefinite article or no determiner, when the determiner is not governed by such a preposition, or after other prepositions such as under, near, beside, in, or from; the head noun that follows is irrelevant.

This pole fires retrospectively when the preceding context names a specific person, occupational role, or collective human group or organization linked to an affiliation, gathering, or communicative action (e.g. consultant at the firm, professor of biology told, advocacy group cited, volunteers at the shelter, talk with a group of students), peaking on the role/group noun itself or on the adjacent linking word (of/at/with/and) or reporting verb; replacing just the human/collective referent with an inanimate noun while keeping the trigger word collapses the peak.

Fires on the head noun of a quantity phrase (numeral or 'few/many/just' + noun, e.g. 'two months', '12 miles', 'five points', 'just days') when the phrase sits where no object is expected, after a copula, an intransitive verb, a comma or a complete clause, so that it can only be an adverbial measure of distance, time or margin for a following relation word (from, after, before, ahead, west, tall, late). The noun's identity barely matters ('300 bricks tall' fires like '300 feet tall'), the same quantity as a direct object ('took/spent/wasted two hours') stays near zero, and a weaker secondary peak falls on a comma that closes a complete clause before a trailing participial or appositive modifier (', killing', ', followed by', ', opening'); there is no per-prompt floor, since sentence-initial and ordinary tokens are ~0.

Fires retrospectively on non-initial elements of a parallel multi-element series: comma-separated enumerations of 3+ items, paired quantity or range constructions (eight characters and one number; 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.), and repeated structural tokens such as closing markup tags or a reused code identifier. Strength rises along the series, while the same tokens (of, and, one, city/food nouns) are inactive outside such series or in plain two-word conjunctions.

Retrospective detector that fires when the current token completes or sits inside a conventional expression specifying an amount, fraction, date, or degree: decimals and numerals (3.9, three), fractions (half; cf. thirds/dozen promoted by the lens), small-measure nouns taking 'of' (pinch of), ordinal/comparative markers (second, last, least inside 'at least', final), and time/date anchors (year, days, Friday), with strength accumulating over the preceding 2-4 quantity words; as a memorized offshoot it also fires on the greeting formula '[Hello/Goodbye], world!'. The same surface token is silent outside such constructions (pinch-as-verb-subject, 'the least work', 'a year and ...', '3x9').

Fires on the function words and time modifiers that open a phrase stating where something or someone came from: its origin, birth, creation, lineage, upbringing or founding date (e.g. 'daughter of [a]', 'born [in the]', 'grew up [in]', 'founded/built [in the] 9th century', 'dates back [to]', 'began [in the mid]-1960s' for a tradition, 'when I [was] a boy', 'How did you get into X? I [was]'); it also fires lexically on ' through' after search verbs (rummaging/searching/dug through) and on ' late/mid/early' before dates. Comparable prepositional phrases about ordinary present-day events or non-origin relations ('the meeting began in the room', 'friend of a', 'cleaned in the 1300s', 'these days I spend') stay below 0.25 of max; there is no floor (sentence-initial tokens sit near 0.08 of max).

N1439+ fires retrospectively on the boundary/connective token that stands between the two members of a construction: the comma, 'and'/'or', colon or line break that separates the items of an enumeration or two co-ordinated clauses, the preposition ('of', 'from', 'against') that links a head to its further member, the quantifier that opens a further member of an already-open set (' other' in its additive use after ' and'/' any'/' many', ' several', ' various'), and the markup delimiters that bind an attribute name to its value ('=', '="', '>'). Strength is graded: a later separator of a 3+ item list fires while a plain two-part coordination stays near zero ('red and white', 'John and Mary'), a repeated preposition or repeated attribute fires harder than the first, and a compositional 'X of Y' ('the destruction of the army') fires while a lexicalised one ('the head/end/Department of the army') does not.

Fires retrospectively on the word that pins down the size, scope or count of a set under discussion -- restrictive/exclusive (only, just, even, lone/alone, no/nobody/none/empty), totalizing (all, whole, entire, total, each/both), exact count/frequency (twice, second-item 'and a/an' in enumerations, partitive 'of' in 'all of the') -- peaking on the scope word itself or on the glue word right after it ('of' in 'all of', 'and' before a second 'a'); strength scales with preceding entity-rich context, so it is strong mid-passage (2.0-3.1) but weak (<=0.5) in short generic sentences. A weaker secondary sensitivity fires on mid-word fragments ending in 'a'/'A' inside split rare, foreign or code words (sh|a|256, SL|A|VE, AZER|BA|YCAN, #d|a|4939, is|cha, line-initial La after a list label). Plain prose with no scope word and no such fragment stays near 0.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that names the resolved outcome or resultant state of a preceding episode, such as a return, repetition, departure, recovery, reconciliation, or lesson learned after an earlier action or event. It does not fire on an ordinary ongoing action token, on a plain description of an object, or on a token that merely continues an episode without resolving it.

Fires on low-information structural continuations (sentence- or paragraph-boundary punctuation, code brackets/dots, operators like * = -, or function words like of/to/after) when they are the highly predictable continuation of a long-range repetitive or boilerplate template such as an enumerated list, code idiom, legal/license formula, math derivation, or fixed symmetric phrase like 'face to face' / 'question after question'; the same punctuation or function word without the establishing template does not activate it.

Retrospective word-form detector: the pole fires on a token whose meaning is a relation between two or more things, or a graded evaluation of a thing, rather than a concrete entity - relational/joining nouns and adjectives (combination, connection, contact, link, association, interaction, interface, composite, joint, separate, dependent, related, combined, different) and difficulty/severity/level adjectives (difficult, hard, easy, simple, bad, poor, terrible, severe, weak, low, high), plus the quantity prefixes micro-/multi-/macro-. It sits at its floor (~-0.17) on concrete entity nouns (table, chair, window, dog, capsule), on non-relational abstract nouns (concept, idea, condition, factor, procedure, composition) and on plain verbs, and the response follows the word form rather than the use ('the link' fires ~0.85 both in 'the link between the two events' and in 'the link in the chain'); its very largest peaks (~2.1-2.5) instead land on inner pieces of low-frequency names and loanwords (Piliocol[ob]us, Stellen[bos]ch, Bor[gh]uis, Kl[ob]uchar), which this class does not cover.

This pole fires on the current token when it is a standalone single-character F/f subword fragment, i.e. the isolated 'F'/'f' piece of a multi-token rare word, identifier, acronym or code constant (bFGF, t.Fatal, FETCH_ASSOC, FSE, FULL, FTPClient, fichier, fructo-, for), with strength boosted by surrounding technical context; it stays near zero on ordinary English words even when they contain the letter f (of, for, off, Frog, affluent, efficient). A small set of short F-adjacent pieces (FF, GF, AB, eff, failed) drives it moderately as offshoots.

Fires on the universal-quantifier determiners 'all'/'All' and 'both' when they head a noun phrase ('all the X', 'all these X', 'all my X', 'all of X', 'all X', 'all day', 'both X'), with a graded, much weaker response to other set quantifiers in the same determiner slot ('every' ~ 'most' ~ 'many' > 'each' ~ 'several' > 'half' > 'some' ~ 'the' ~ 'the whole/entire', the last three at zero). It is near-silent when the same words are non-determinative (floating 'the members all agreed', 'at all'), and has a second, weaker cluster on abstract rank/part modifiers of a definite noun phrase ('main', 'central', 'key', 'major', 'upper', 'front') that does not extend to concrete classifiers ('red', 'biological', 'same' all give 0); the level is set by the preceding clause alone, and 13 different continuations after 'all' left it bit-identical.

This pole fires on the token that completes a tight local head-dependent pair at the core of a clause or phrase: a finite verb or copula given its subject noun phrase (telescope captured, violinist played, Lima are), or the preposition, particle, affix, or continuation punctuation selected by the immediately preceding head (increased by, calls for, sits on, at least, np., print(). Replacing the selecting head with a syntactically incompatible word of the same token length collapses the peak even though the peak token itself is unchanged, while swapping a distant word leaves it intact.

Pole 2396+ is a voice detector for consumer-facing web prose: the chatty, opinionated, present-tense 'blog voice' of blog posts, live blogs, product reviews and announcements, and brand / about-us copy. Across such a passage it runs at mean activation 0.2-0.5 with peaks of 1.2-2.2, while the same content written as specification, method, encyclopedia, essay, legal, recipe or code text stays at mean 0.0-0.1 (peaks <= 0.5), as do dialogue and unedited forum fragments and third-person narrative fiction; within the active voice it peaks on that voice's stock frames - sentence-initial 'As' opening a reported clause, 'as expected', 'as quick as', 'at least', 'finally here', 'kick off', 'check out', 'excited to', 'stay updated with the latest'.

Fires retrospectively when the current token completes an evidential grounding of a claim: either the speech, thought, or analytic act itself (stated, explained, declared, puts, makes, piece, imagined, feared, analyzes) or the epistemic marker (fact), or a precise checkable locator (clock minutes like 24/45, dates, citation and page numbers, equation results) appearing inside such an attributional frame; the same tokens without a claim-grounding frame stay quiet.

N2851+ is a retrospective, word-level detector of the English formal-institutional register rather than of spelling: it fires on the vocabulary through which institutions state obligations, permissions, provisions and transfers to a reader - liable/liability, responsible, required, provided, necessary, consent, comply, permission, provisions, limitations, obligations, contribute/donated, submit, transfer, please, thank (with 'mechanism(s)' its strongest single trigger, 0.8-1.6 in any carrier) - and it also peaks on the identifying piece of some unfamiliar proper names and place names that GPT-2 spells in several pieces (Guadagnini, Cirencester, Bournemouth, Carlucci, Arias-de-Reyna, Corte), while ordinary concrete nouns, plain Anglo-Saxon re-wordings of the same sentences (has to fix, gave, bring) and narrative prose stay at or below zero. The old mid-word/BPE-piece claim named the wrong trigger and must be corrected: mid-word position lifts the active rate only 1.1x over its own base rate (0.010 vs 0.009), the productive suffixes -ing/-ed/-er/-al/-ent/-ion fire at most once in 60-110 occurrences each, ordinary compound hyphens such as last-minute and cross-country reach only 0.44, and most rare multi-piece names (Machiavelli, Tchaikovsky, Aberystwyth, Kidderminster, Marchetti) are silent - so it over-predicted plain narrative holdouts that are in fact silent and never predicted the register words that carry the real activation.

The pole fires at the pivot of an alternation or range over quantities: the token ('or', 'to', the hyphen in 'one-to-four', or the 'and' of 'between one and three') that follows a quantity expression (a number word or quantifier such as one, two, zero, 5, several, some, all, half, few, possibly heading a noun phrase: 'one phone', 'one micrometer') and introduces a second quantity or alternative. It stays silent when the same connectives join non-quantities ('red or blue', 'from here to there') and when a quantity takes a plain coordinator ('one and two', 'one plus two'), and its output direction promotes quantity words (two, three, four, five, many, multiple, several) even though the protocol's lookahead concentration gate stays below 0.5.

This pole retrospectively detects the situating vocabulary of report-style prose: it fires on modal/epistemic operators and hedges (will, could, can, may, might, would, should, probably, likely), on time expressions (now, still, soon, later, ago, today, years/months/weeks/days, weekday and day-part names such as Tuesday or morning) and on the concrete place and property nouns of local reporting (county, village, town, farm, hospital, house, land, beach, office, place), firing on 20-40% of tokens in those classes against a 2.4% base rate over the scan. It sits at the floor on abstract and technical content words (method, result, data, issue, problem, format, segment, parse), on plain copulas and auxiliaries (is, was, does, did, has), on determiners, prepositions and pronouns, and throughout scientific, patent and code passages - the same trigger words go silent in that register ('Voters in the county will decide on the measure Tuesday' peaks at 0.76, while 'The results were published in the journal last year', 'The algorithm sorts the array in quadratic time' and 'The method will be explained below' peak at 0.00 to 0.06).

This pole fires retrospectively on a word inside a verb phrase whose predicate carries elaboration beyond a bare minimal clause, an auxiliary, modal, negation or adverb on the verb, or an additional complement or adjunct such as a prepositional phrase, conjoined noun phrase, predicate nominal or adjective, or measure expression, peaking on the elaborating nominal itself (of, the, to, at, into, 12, chemical, positive) or on the modified verb (called, seek). It stays near-silent on the same nominals in verbless fragments ('A pinch of salt'), in bare light-verb subject-verb-object clauses ('She added salt'), and in unelaborated clauses ('The algorithm runs', 'Our revenue increased yesterday'); the negative pole shows only weak unstructured activity, and the HTML-tag peak is an unrelated leftover offshoot.

Fires on the slot-marking token of formulaic 'specification' templates: CSS/HTML property separators after a property name (the ':' or '-' in 'color:', 'background-color', 'frameborder=', 'col-sm'), digits and hyphens inside phone/ZIP numbers ('(212) 299-2380'), the availability boilerplate 'at any time/point' and 'as they become available', a degree sign after a temperature, and 'Category' starting a Wikipedia footer line after a blank line; ordinary narrative prose stays below 0.25 x max (no floor: the first token and plain sentences read ~0-0.6).

Fires retrospectively when the current token is a highly constrained continuation completing a conventional multi-token construction set up by the preceding 1-4 tokens, e.g. adjective or nominalization plus preposition/determiner (rich in, concentration/priority/Forum of, across the, on our), modal or plural noun phrase plus auxiliary (can be, were selected/constructed), result predicate plus significantly (significantly affected/associated), or subword/unit/syntax completion (lic+enses, mg+/+g, 65.+1, lib+/+python, weight+=, categories+:). The same function words, digits, units, or punctuation do not drive it when they initiate a phrase or lack the local licensing trigger.

Fires on the token that completes a conventional subject-predicate or verb-complement pairing stating a declarative clause's central event or state (the verb after its subject, or the object noun or preposition after its verb), with strength graded by how well the preceding word predicts it; the same token after an incongruent word, or the same content word outside that clausal frame, evokes little activity.

Fires retrospectively when the current token continues or completes a fixed, highly predictable multi-token chunk: an idiomatic binomial or collocation (quickly and easily, early and late, Fast and Furious), a degree/quantity/time formula (for quite some, little if any, at any time, at least, somewhat or not), a contraction stem (don/doesn toward n't), a hyphenated compound (moderate-intensity, early-stage), or a mid-word subword continuation inside a long complex word (Ther|ape|utic, neutrop|en|ia, Multifl|or|i). The same surface tokens in novel compositional combinations (John and Mary, quite good, walked in the park, harmful treatment) evoke little or no response, and output-lens projection is incoherent (Jacobian kurtosis ~3.1), so the pole detects chunk continuity in what was just read rather than preparing any specific upcoming token.

N751+ tracks informal, personal, expressive English - the voice of product reviews, food and experience write-ups, blog posts, forum comments and personal asides - firing on everyday slang, sensory and casual-evaluative words (weird, nasty, crappy, shitty, disgusting, amazing, tasty, yikes, wow, honestly, kinda, totally, dude, damn) and running hot across chatty first- or second-person narration. It stays near zero through formal, impersonal or technical prose (specifications, papers, news reports, reference documentation) even when that prose states a judgement, so the scan's global peak is the aside 'don't laugh' lodged in an otherwise technical explanation of hexadecimal numbers, and the strongest everyday frame is 'Damn, that is weird.' (peak 2.10) against 'That result is anomalous.' (0.00).

The pole marks an indefinite quantity/extent phrase: it fires on 'a'/'an' where the model expects such a phrase's degree or amount word next ('a lot of', 'a few', 'a number of', 'a variety of', 'a wide range', 'a high standard', 'a good deal'), and on the degree modifier itself when it follows (wide, vast, broad, high, long, good, great, very, significant); its output direction promotes exactly those quantity heads (variety, array, range, multitude, slew, plethora, host, lot), and zero-ablating it changes the next-token distribution only weakly (KL ~1e-5), so the claim is retrospective. It is near zero on 'the'/'some'/'his', on 'a' in copular predicate nominatives ('she is a doctor'), on quantifier heads (few, number, lot, variety), and on degree words outside an indefinite phrase ('the range is very wide' is silent, 'the wide range' about half as strong).

Fires retrospectively on the token that continues an already-established clause frame: the predicate head (modal, auxiliary, or lexical verb) immediately after an overt nominal or pronominal subject, or a function word (determiner, preposition or temporal subordinator, infinitive 'to', open paren, SQL 'BY') immediately after the transitive verb, noun, or clause header it complements. Strength is set jointly by the peak token and the 1-2 preceding frame tokens, so the same peak token without a selecting subject or verb frame is predicted inactive.

Fires retrospectively when the current token completes a restrictive/exclusive modifier that singles out a limited, sole, smallest, earliest, or prior instance — superlative selectors (The nearest/earliest), exclusives (only/just + determiner or number), or temporal restrictors (prior/previous + noun).

This pole fires retrospectively on contexts of formal judgment, legal entitlement, or civic authority — courts, juries, verdicts, lawsuits, violated rights, claims to office or seats of power — peaking on the authority noun itself or on a nearby verb or copula that carries the ruling forward, and its output direction upweights the evaluative vocabulary right, Right, rights, and wrong. The same noun or copula in a neutral frame (court versus garden, seek versus eat, verdict versus weather) goes quiet, so it detects the judgment frame rather than a trigger token; a weaker offshoot firing on the French first-person clitic in 'je m'appelle' falls outside this frame and is left over.

L9/N1018+ detects the causative/resultative frame of 'make': it fires on the verb 'make' in any inflection ('makes', 'make', 'made', 'making') when that verb takes a (pro)noun object plus a predicative complement that states the object's resulting property, state or experience - an adjective ('makes it convenient', 'makes the Avenues unique', 'makes it mandatory', 'make it all the more interesting'), a mental-state or perception verb ('made me wonder', 'make you feel', 'makes it seem so far away', 'make your food taste sweet'), or 'to be' - or, with no separate complement, in the two degree idioms 'make (a lot of / little / no) sense' and 'make (little / no / big) difference'. It is the frame, not the word form and not the word: all four inflections reach near the pole's maximum of 2.69 in this frame (the 20 top peaks contain 7 ' makes', 6 ' make' and 1 ' made', and ' make' has more firing instances in absolute terms than ' makes' despite its lower mean), whereas the same token stays near zero in physical creation ('make a cake', 'made him dinner', 'makes cars in three factories'), in light-verb action nouns ('make a decision', 'make a call', 'make a mistake'), and in fixed, phrasal or commercial uses ('make money', 'make it to the party', 'make up', 'the make and model'), and near-synonymous causatives do not fire ('render it mandatory', 'deem X Y', 'regard X as Y' sit at 0.24-0.40 mean, 9-15% of max). The peak sits on 'make' itself and spills onto the object and degree words (' little', ' a', ' it', ' you'), 29% of input attribution lies more than 16 tokens back (the frame's subject), and with Jacobian kurtosis 3.12 and 40% lens overlap the output promotes no coherent next-token set, so this is retrospective frame detection rather than lookahead. Known residue this claim does not cover: about 30% of the top peaks (both ' El' peaks are 'Elmore', both ' j' peaks are 'jpg'/'jellies', plus ' of' in 'Idylls of the King' and ' to' in 'device to enhance') look like a separate weak sensitivity to BPE word-onset fragments in name, URL and formatting contexts (the confound list's '@', ' www', 'EL', ' u'), and should be probed separately.

Fires retrospectively when left context invokes an accumulated track record or experience via a perfect construction (have/has/had plus past participle, including negatives, never/before experientials, and equivalent cumulative phrases like winning streak or for X years) presented as grounds for a present evaluation; it peaks on the scope or continuation token (this, and, over, a) rather than the auxiliary. Rewriting the perfect as simple past or present with the topic fixed lowers the peak, while swaps inside the same perfect frame do not.

L9/N1026+ fires on a token the preceding context has already determined: a distinctive completion of a chunk the text has committed to - the head word of a compound identifier or technical term (Confirm|Dialog, Text|View, Jni|Method, Job|Context), the closing tag '</' after element content, or the completing word of a stock collocation ('at least', 'what it', 'the Senate Commerce Committee', 'the lower body'). Activation tracks how strongly the context forces that token: the same token rises from about 0.2 to 2.0 when its surrounding text makes it the expected continuation, collapses when swapped for an equally well-formed but unpredictable word, and is unchanged when swapped for an equally predictable alternative.

Fires on words that give a physical orientation or direction of aim, such as 'pointed/points', 'aimed', 'facing', 'straight', 'upward/down', 'along', 'angle/degrees', 'threw right'. It peaks on the verb or adverb that says which way something points, and stays high on the directional words right after it (e.g. 'needle pointed straight down', 'arrow points directly at', 'sign points north'). The first token always reads 0 and plain narrative without an orientation phrase stays below 0.25 of max, except for a secondary offshoot on ' and'/' &' inside fixed paired names ('Fast and Furious', 'Hall of Fame and Museum'), which can also make a prompt active.

The pole fires retrospectively on a token that belongs to a conventional, prefabricated stretch of written institutional English rather than on the word itself: its strongest response is the fixed formulae of copyright, licence and permission text ('All rights reserved', 'licensed under the ... License', 'the non-exclusive, non-transferable right', 'you may not reproduce, distribute, or transmit'), and it also fires on stock institutional or product names, spelled-out specifications and set temporal or epithet frames ('Cornell Medical College', '16GB of RAM', 'four years later', 'the much loved ...'). Freely composed narrative, dialogue, description and argument - and the same words outside such a frame ('All animals reserved', 'four cats later', 'The tall woman walked ...', 'The company gave the other company the right ...') - stay near zero, and changing a formula's free continuation (reserved -> observed, years -> days) leaves the peak unchanged, so it reacts to wording already read rather than to a particular next word.

The pole fires on the token that carries a stretch of time, or a stretch of accumulated prior work, rather than a point in time or a concrete thing: the plural time-unit noun heading a definite temporal phrase ('the years/months/decades/weeks that followed', 'the days and weeks following', 'the years after the war'), the attributive relative-time modifier or bound of such a stretch ('early' morning/1990s, 'recent' years/work, the bound prefixes 'pre-' and 'post-', 'from that day on', 'until then', 'between 2001 and 2005'), and a continuative or perfect predicate that extends an action or a body of work over time ('walked and walked', 'continued', 'kept on', 'few studies have', 'recent work has'). It stays inactive on deictic point-in-time words ('yesterday', 'last week', 'on Tuesday'), on bare durational measure phrases ('for many years'), and on the same strings used without temporal reference ('the postman', 'anti-inflammatory', 'I have a car', 'the colour of the door').

Retrospective detector for the token that closes a structurally complete segment in formatted expository text: the '.'/'\n' closing a repeated figure or caption label (FIG. 2.) or list enumerator (3.), the relational word ('of'/'from'/'to') or salient content word completing a title/heading noun phrase, or the '.', '?' or '\n' terminating a full sentence or paragraph before a new block. It integrates long-range formatting context (prior labels, enumerators, heading layout) and stays quiet on the same tokens mid-sentence, in abbreviations, or in unstructured prose.

The pole fires on the token that carries the spelling of an uncommon, not-yet-resolved word - the opening fragment of a proper name, a genus/species name, or a rare technical or foreign term that BPE splits across several pieces ('An' in Anastasia 2.11, 'As' in Asio 2.73, 'a' in aldosterone 1.40, 'me' in meandering 1.99) - and stays partly raised over that word's later pieces. The driver is the word's unresolved identity, not the token or its capitalisation: the same token sits at the floor when it is a common word ('As' 0.15 in 'As if he knew', 'me' -0.07 as a pronoun, 'An' 0.15 as the article, 'a' 0.08 in 'It was a problem'), and frequent multi-piece words do not fire (penicillin -0.01, testosterone -0.12, Thomas 0.00). Residue this claim does not cover, measured but not explained: the indefinite article of an extent or measure phrase also fires strongly ('less than a year later' 2.75, 'they overlap a little' 2.41, 'a few months later' 2.62), and it tracks the clause's subject rather than the following noun ('The bird was a sparrow/problem/thing' 1.46 each vs 'It was a problem' 0.08).

At each position this pole reports how much the current token plus its short left context ascribes socially-evaluated worth or self-possession: identity, character, reputation, status, credibility, confidence, competence (skill, talent, leadership), appearance and bearing (beauty, style, charm, walk, smile, voice), moral standing (honor, faith, integrity), and their yardsticks (judge, mark, rank, rating); it generalizes across spelling variants (honor/honour, color/colour), fires on the neutral word 'the' only after report/witness left-contexts (told, handed, of, on), and fires on bare single-letter initials (i, j, J). It stays silent on neutral concrete nouns, tender/affiliative and divine terms (love, mercy, charity, god, holy, sacred), brute force and mere fame (power, force, celebrity, superstar, winner, success), near-synonyms outside the cluster (renown, standing, regard, admiration), and on 'the' after neutral verbs/prepositions (saw, opened, before, in).

This pole fires when the current token completes a conventionalized local chunk, a fixed idiom, collocation, phrasal verb, or otherwise strongly cued word pair (e.g. par+for, born+and, run+out, in+full, do+it, is+losing+control), with activation peaking on the completing token and requiring both the cue word and the specific completion; replacing either side of the pair with an equally grammatical but unconventional alternative sharply reduces activation.

Fires on the token of a specialised, technical content word, mostly molecular/biochemical vocabulary and word pieces (' molecular', ' cataly-', 'ococ' in Streptococcus, 'cy' in polycystic, '-ational' in conformational, ' cellular'/' genetic' more weakly) and the formal ' Armed' (Armed Occupation Act, Armed Services); scientific-abstract framing ('the precise', 'a first glimpse into the') boosts it, and it also fires on two set phrases: ' hard' in 'the hard way' and ' is'/' was' in 'wonder what is/was the point'. There is no floor: plain everyday narrative prose ('The cat sat on the mat.') stays near 0, although an ordinary ' the' or noun after a technical or abstract-framing phrase can reach about 0.3-0.4 of max.

This pole fires on the content word that felicitously completes an open complement slot — the object or complement licensed by a preceding verb, preposition, or fixed phrase (opened→door, of→France, far→away) — and stays near zero when the same word appears as a subject/topic or when the slot holds a semantically infelicitous filler.

This pole fires when the clause under way predicates something about a person: activation climbs through the first few tokens of the predicate (the copula or auxiliary - is, was, are, am, have, can - a predicate adverb such as 'also', 'not', 'mainly', or a possessive/relative pronoun that refers back to the person: his, who, or its for an organisation) whenever the clause's subject denotes a human being (a name, he/she/I/you, a human noun phrase) or a body of people (an organisation, committee, institution, family). It falls to near zero when the identical predicate is applied to an inanimate or abstract subject ('the building', 'the machine', 'the protein', 'it') - the same surface token ('also', 'very', 'was') is typically 2-4x weaker, so the personhood of the subject, not the token identity, sets the strength.
