The pole marks specific, identifying particulars inside a noun phrase: it is most active on the leading token of an attributive quantity or ordinal ('a 500 MW plant', 'the 80,000-seater stadium', 'the 28th annual meeting', '3.34 million pounds building', '70.9 degrees of inclination') and on a name or demonym that names a specific entity ('the United States', 'the German team', 'the Yuzhnoye Design Bureau'), with a weaker response on the determiner that opens such a phrase ('the', 'its', usually right after a preposition). It is near zero on generic or vague description - vague quantifiers ('a very large plant', 'much capacity'), plain common-noun phrases ('in the country', 'the factory') and numerals used as a bare post-verbal count ('seats 80,000') - and on abstract, non-factual prose.

Fires on the token that continues or completes a frozen, formulaic multi-word chunk of published written language: license and legal boilerplate (WITHOUT WARRANT to IES, THEORY OF LIABILITY to WHETHER, wholly without merit), statute and title citations (Title VII of to the, Copyright to 2016, Public to License), and fixed slogans, idioms and dialogue exclamations (MORE to THAN, What to on, shouted to Whoo). It reacts to the distinctive chunk onset already read; swapping the tail word for nonsense (Mars, garden wall) leaves the peak unchanged.

In encyclopedic and historical prose this pole fires on the token that records an institution's, place's or event's origin and formal history - a passive predicate such as 'was founded', 'established', 'built', 'completed', 'formed', 'created', 'launched', 'signed', 'passed', 'nationalized' (also as a fronted participle, 'Founded in 1789, ...') - and on a place name that such a statement locates the entity in ('founded in Detroit', 'established in Los Angeles'). The same words in ordinary or stative sentences ('Japan is an island country', 'the train stopped in Detroit', 'she has lived in Japan', 'the company specializes in software', 'the meal was eaten') stay at zero or a small fraction of peak, while the pole's write adds ' in' - its top promoted token under both vocabulary lenses and in the ablation - the preposition these statements normally continue with.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token continues or completes a familiar conventional chunk: day and month names fire on token identity alone (baseline ~0.35-0.85, e.g. ' March' with no date frame) and peak (~0.75-1.0) inside date/list frames, while function tokens, code keywords, measurement adjuncts and predictable word-pieces (' at' after 'Celsius', 'For i', 'ORDER BY name', 'am|oxicillin', 'hab|ite', 'zer|os') fire only when the constraining left template is present, and clause-final periods fire weakly as closers. The same tokens outside any formulaic template stay near zero (' at' is 0.0 in 'cat sat at sea level', periods 0.0 after random words), and the flat Jacobian/logit lenses (kurtosis ~3.2, only suffix-fragment agreement) promote no coherent upcoming-token set.

N1721- is not a content feature but GPT-2's GELU dip read through this neuron, so it fires on a resting state rather than on a topic: the MLP computes gelu_new(c_fc(x)), the pole strength is max(-gelu_new(pre), 0), and it is hard-capped at the gelu_new global minimum 0.1700408 (pre about -0.75), exactly 0 whenever pre >= 0, with this scan's maximum exactly that constant and all 20 top peaks float32 ties at it (it is active, at or above 0.25 of scale, on about half the scan's 199,964 tokens). Two facts decide a label. (1) A text's first position is always cold: at position 0 the pole reads exactly 0.000 for all 50,256 GPT-2 vocabulary tokens (measured in one batch, maximum 0.000), whatever the token, script or rarity, so a prompt that tokenizes to ONE token - 'cat', ' math', ' location' - is INACTIVE with peak 0.000, as is a whitespace-only prompt. (2) After the first token the pole sits at the cap (0.10-0.17, 0.6-1.0 of scale) on lexical tokens - nouns, verbs, adjectives, names, numbers, subword pieces, code identifiers, non-Latin script - and also on ' is/was/are/were/be/been/have/has/can/will/it/you/I/we/they/that/this/not' and bare letter or digit pieces, while it reads 0 on whitespace and, most of the time, on punctuation and on the commonest space-prefixed phrase-structure words (' the/a/an/of/in/for/with/by/from/as/or/but/and/The/In/A/its/his/their/my/your/than/said'). Hence label a prompt ACTIVE (peak 0.6-1.0 of scale) when it has two or more tokens and any token after the first is a lexical word: 32-token windows of the scan's running text are active 98.9% of the time (1,123 windows), 10-token spans 90.6% (3,458), and 18 of 18 hand-written sentences - and label it INACTIVE (peak exactly 0.000) only when it is a single tokenizer token. Strings of 2-9 closed-class tokens are NOT decidable from text and are not valid hard negatives: ' the of and to a in' and ' the the the' read 0.000, but ' of the' reads 0.100, ' in the of' 0.134, ' is is is is' 0.164 and ' at the' 0.170, because attention copies earlier tokens into the current residual. The pole's output direction prepares no upcoming token (Jacobian lens kurtosis 3.1, an incoherent promoted list, and no correlation with the next token's surprisal, rho +0.01), so it is retrospective.

Fires retrospectively on the word that completes an event description with its endpoint, outcome, or measure: the sensory result predicate after until or a copula/perfect (golden brown, creamy, hot, smooth, thick, hardened), a dimension, unit, or quantified nominal (long, cm, 15 percent, population, richer/small), or the article introducing such a post-verbal nominal (gives the pancakes a ..., had a ...). Activation is strongest for concrete physical and culinary result states and falls for temporal or abstract substitutes in the same slot.

In encyclopedic prose the pole fires on the token that closes a bibliographic reference, most strongly the 'in' of '<work> was published / will appear [on <date>] in <venue>' ('was published on the 24th July in the journal Science', 'will appear in the Journal of Positive Psychology', 'in its 16 July 1945 issue'), and it stays raised across the following venue/title tokens; a dated record that is not a publication ('...University of Manchester and in 1981 director of...') raises it about two-thirds as much. It is not driven by 'in', dates or names as such: 'published in' (1.6-2.1) far exceeds 'discussed in' (0.7) and 'mentioned in' (0.4), a plain birth date ('born on 16 July 1945 in a small town') or narrative 'the cat sat on the mat in' scores ~0, and proper names without a reference frame ('University of Notre Dame') score 0.

The pole fires when the current token is a strongly licensed local continuation of the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens, completing a conventional collocation, multi-token name, subword stem, or grammatical slot (j' to hab, wrote to Hamlet, kingdom to far, contract to was, seek to re, in to the); strength is graded by local congruity, so the same peak token after an incongruous licensor (banana to was, eat to re, at to the, under to mat) or a different peak token in the same slot (Trumpet for Hamlet) stays near zero, while words after the peak leave activation exactly unchanged.

N2000- is not a feature but GPT-2's GELU dip read on the neuron's pre-activation z: the MLP computes gelu_new(c_fc(x)), so the negative pole is max(-gelu_new(z), 0), capped at the gelu_new minimum 0.1700408 (at z about -0.75), and this scan's maximum is exactly that constant (0.170040756), with 17.6% of its 199,985 tokens in the top bin (0.1644-0.17004) and the top-20 peaks being float32 ties among cap tokens; the 200 highest-mean tokens are the semantically unrelated ' forefront', ' harder', 'ibility', ' compiler' (means 0.162-0.170), the Jacobian lens promotes nothing (kurtosis 3.15, 20% overlap with the logit lens), integrated gradients spread over a mean 16 tokens back (replacement agreement rho = -0.03), and the neuron is alive only in the other direction (positive pole 90% exact zeros, sparse tail to 3.215), so this pole reads the current token's pre-activation and no content feature. Label a prompt ACTIVE (peak 0.87-1.00 of scale) when it has ten or more running-text tokens - only 1 of 2,246 sliding ten-token spans in the top windows peaks below the 0.25 activity line, and one-word edits inside such a span leave the peak at the cap (delta about 0) - and label it INACTIVE (peak about 0.13-0.15 of scale) only for a one-token prompt, because sequence position 0 reads 0.0220-0.0248 for every first token in all 20 top windows and 0.0233 over all 408 scanned windows, whatever the word; spans of 2-9 tokens are not decidable from text (17/20 position-1 and 15/20 position-2 tokens already clear the line), so a bare single token is the inactive probe and ten or more tokens of running text the active one. Apart from position 0 a token stays below the cap only when its pre-activation leaves the dip - z of 0 or more gives exactly 0 (the positive pole's support, 10.0% of tokens) and z below about -2 relaxes toward 0, together 22.5% of tokens - and that set is not decidable from meaning (token identity 27% of variance, position 0.4%), the flat tokens at this layer not being a clean function-word list (' are' 0.045, ' as' 0.048, ' be' 0.043 mean, all at the 0.0425 activity line).

Fires retrospectively when the current token states or completes an explicit scalar bound or quantity: a cardinal count with a unit ('88 centres', 'thirty patients', 'over 7000 families'), a temporal bound ('until'/'Until', 'yet been', 'awhile', 'never', 'Before' with dates), or a scalar/quantificational operator ('anybody' in questions, 'even' under negation, degree 'slow to'). The same function words in non-quantificational prose, and vague non-numerical descriptions in the same frames, stay low.

This pole fires on words and short spans that carry strong affective or evaluative force: a speaker's or writer's feeling about, or strongly felt appraisal of, what is being described, in either polarity (praise or condemnation, pleasure or distress, e.g. wonderful, dreadful, grim, awful, cruel, bitterly, boos, boorish, keen, fond, comforting, a warm voice). It stays at its near-zero baseline on neutral, factual, technical or administrative description and on mild or purely epistemic appraisal (accurate, correct, typical, important, interesting, licensed, specified).

The pole fires at the separator or prefix token that immediately precedes the next numeral of a running enumeration of numerals: the comma, 'and' or 'or' before the next item of a consecutive count (1, 2, 3, 4 ...), the slash or hyphen of a numeric range (2018/19, 1947–48, 1674–1682), the semicolon, newline or spaces before the next numbered or lettered list item, and the bracket prefix inside a run of reference numbers ([@B1][@B2]..., [17, 18]). Isolated numbers, numbers carrying a unit or a date, and ordinary prose leave it at its floor, so it tracks the running count rather than numerals as such.

Peaks on the token that completes a cause, condition, or situation description (often the final noun of the subject phrase, or a modal/adverb such as may, can, also, would, which, or so) when the next one to two tokens state its effect, preparing an upcoming causal or consequence verb such as cause, lead, allow, enable, make, mean, or give. Predicts active on cause-then-effect sentences and inactive when the same antecedent is followed by a non-consequence verb.

N2409+ is a local Romance-language detector: reading the orthography of the current token plus the two or three tokens before it, it fires at 3-6 across Spanish, Portuguese, Catalan or Galician prose (prompt peak 4.5-7) and at 2-4 across French or Italian prose, while staying at 0.0 on English (even Latinate English such as "organization's constitution ... administration"), German, Polish, Turkish, code and mathematics, so a prompt is predicted active only when its text is Romance or when it contains a Romance word or name. It is retrospective, not lookahead: inside English prose it rises to 1.5-5.5 on a single Romance token (Diego 4.2, Francesco 5.5, Moreno 2.3, casa 3.1) but reads 0.0 on Germanic or Slavic names (Smith, Schmidt, Hansen, Kowalski), and its output adds probability to Spanish function words (de, que, un, la, en, con) rather than preparing one specific next token.

Fires retrospectively on the head word of a topic construction — a communication, inquiry, or attitude noun, verb, adjective, or quantifier (information, details, discussion, debate, knowledge, advice, talked, care, passionate, concerned, more) that licenses an about-style topic complement — peaking on that head word itself whether or not about/on follows; its output direction then boosts about-family prepositions (about, around, concerning, regarding).

The pole fires where the text is about to name a person: it peaks on the last token before a personal name begins - the '.' of an author-style initial ('M. Lindström', 'C. Benítez', 'R. Alison Adcock'), the 'and' that follows one person and introduces a second ('Kathy and I', 'my brother and', 'Barney and Robin'), and the 'said' of a dialogue tag before a speaker's name - and on the first token of a name that opens a sentence. It stays low where that same slot is filled by a place, an organisation or a thing ('Paris and', 'the bread and', 'by Lindström', 'at Google'), and its output promotes personal names (Lena, Sheila, Nikki, Sylvia) and personal/possessive pronouns (mine, hers, my, I, me).

Fires when the just-read token selects, narrows, or confirms one alternative out of an implicit contrast set in the immediate phrase — prototypically an exactness marker (right, just, direct, straight, only) scoping over a time, place, direction or outcome anchor (right now/here/away/after/under, just before, direct result), and the same selective function in directional choice (right side/click/wing), tag confirmation (right?), and fixed selective frames (Q&A, speak up, one thing, of all places).

Fires retrospectively when preceding text establishes a dyadic reciprocal, comparative, or joint relation between two entities — a pair, rivalry, joint action, or mutual interaction — peaking on the second pair member, the joint-action verb, or the relation noun itself; the same word in a one-sided or non-relational use does not activate it.

The pole fires on the singular linking word that carries a clause's predication: a singular be-form (is, was, be, been, 's, 'm, am, being, and the "'t" of isn't/wasn't), any form of become (become, becomes, became, becoming), or the role-marking prepositions as and into where the phrase they head gives a capacity, role or resulting state ('used it as their main design tool', 'grew into a major supplier'). It fires strongest when the clause predicates something of a person (a personal pronoun, person noun or personal name - 'He was...', 'John Smith was the mayor...', 'Gerda Gilboe (1914-2009) was a Danish actress'), where auxiliary and passive be fire too, and stays below the active line for inanimate or abstract subjects, for plural are/were, for non-predicative as (comparative 'as good as', 'such as', 'as if', 'as soon as') and for directional or idiomatic into ('walked into the room', 'burst into tears', 'paid into an account').

This pole fires at the token that carries an ascending, forward-running numeric progression to its next element: the separator between the two ends of an increasing span or range ('70-80', '38-50% and 67-100%', '0.4-0.9', '1.10-1.63', '6 to 8 feet', '1970 through 1974', '741 F.3d 1367, 1378', 'from 67 to 100'), and the comma or repeated label just before the next, larger value of a run ('1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8', '0, 30, 60, 90, 120', '963-967', 'October 2nd, October 4th, October 6th, October 10th', 'group 3), (group 6), (group 24)', '(2006) (2008) (2010)', and forward ordinal series such as January to August, Monday to Friday, a to h or the primes). Reversed or scrambled versions of the same spans and runs ('100-67', 'Prices fell from 100 to 67', '8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1', April back to January, shuffled dates), unordered lists of words or numbers ('January, duck, purple, seven', '4, 9, 2, 17, 5, 8'), lone numbers or dates, and a single two-number span in a plain sentence ('It was 5-9') stay near zero or at most about a quarter as strong as the forward version.

Retrospective detector for word-initial subword fragments: it fires when the current token begins but does not complete a multi-token word (e.g. ' Op'+'io', ' Fac'+'ilit', ' op'+'ulent', ' Advis'+'ors', ' lig'+'ament') and on byte-level fragments of multi-byte non-Latin characters, with peak strength tuned to specific fragment identities (strong for Op/Fac/Advis/lig, weak for cart/Medic/organ) rather than firing on every split piece or on complete single-token words.

Retrospective: fires when the current token extends or adds to what precedes it - additive connectors (as well as, along with), inclusive verbs (include), intensifier plus gradable-phrase extensions (very healthy, as long/simple as), and plural or collective nouns/subwords naming the enlarged set (conditions, Things, outsoles). The same surface forms also drive it morphologically or word-internally (the 'as' in asbestosis, 'uns' in unsweetened), while non-extending uses of 'as' (such as) stay quiet.

Fires on runs of ALL-CAPS English text (headlines, section headings, names and case captions in capitals), peaking at 0.55-1.0 of max on capitalised function words and word pieces inside a multi-word caps run (' THROUGH'/'OUGH', ' THE', ' FOR', ' TO', ' ON', 'ING', 'ENT', 'ARD', the '-' in 'ANNE-MARIE'), from the second caps word onward; Title Case headlines reach only about 0.4-0.65 (e.g. 'Gobbles Up', 'Puts Us') and the same words in lowercase stay low. Floor: the first token of any prompt sits at about 0.20 of max, short plain lowercase sentences with concrete nouns and verbs peak at 0.20-0.25, but longer ordinary prose often reaches 0.25-0.35 on pronouns, auxiliaries and 'that'/'to' (weakly active), so a negative must be short plain prose, code, or lowercase text.

The pole fires on the singular quantificational determiner that opens a non-referential noun phrase - an NP denoting an unspecified member of a set rather than a particular, already-identified individual: ' a' (strongest, active on 24% of its 3163 scan occurrences), ' every', ' each', ' another', ' any', ' one', ' no' and the ordinals ' first'/' last'/' next', with ' an' a much weaker member. It is essentially silent on determiners that pick out an identified individual or a plural/mass quantity (' the' fires on only 14 of 7893 scan occurrences; ' this', ' that', ' these', ' some', ' my', ' your', ' his', ' its', ' their', ' two', ' all', ' both' at zero), the same token ' a' falls to zero when its NP is a predicate nominal ('she is a doctor', 'she married a doctor') rather than a new referent ('ten dollars a day', 'take a look', 'she wanted a doctor'), and the capitalised fragments high in the confound list (' Qu', ' Bre', ' Ba', ' fe', ' pe') are only GPT-2 BPE word onsets whose response is token-bound - ' qu' fires about 2.3 whatever word it begins ('a quandary', 'a quiche', 'a quilt') and under 1.3 after 'of' or a numeral - a ~15% residue that carries no extra semantics.

This pole fires retrospectively at the token that states an amount, measure or degree inside a predicate: a numeral plus its measure noun in a change or threshold phrase ('by two goals', 'by twenty percent', 'five dollars', 'at least eight characters'), a comparative or degree modifier ('greater', 'more', 'less', 'best', 'very'), a verb of increase, improvement or reduction whose object is such a magnitude ('improve your score', 'reduces the risk', 'its costs'), or the predicate of an abstract quantity noun ('the cost / the risk is ...'). Locative, identity, naming, possession and plain-description frames ('walked to the park', 'the cat sat on the mat', 'the capital of France is Paris', 'the company describes the risk') leave it near zero even though they contain the same function words, so it detects the amount/degree claim rather than the tokens 'at', 'in', 'by', 'a', 'is' or ','.

The positive pole fires at the point where a clause commits to a goal: the finite copula (was/is/be/been/were/remains) of a subject that is a goal/purpose/intention noun - 'the aim/goal/objective/purpose/intention/point of X was', 'our goal is' - and, as the same goal-directedness offshoot, on the verb 'look', strongest in the progressive 'looking' ('we are looking for/at'). It is not a generic copula or perception detector: 'the color of the car was' (0.00), 'the method/design/result of the study was' (0.9-1.5) and the literal 'I see the cat' (0.00) stay near zero, and the peak is identical (3.47) whether the copula is followed by a purpose clause ('to compare') or by 'unclear'.

L9/N613+ fires on a token that lies inside a repeat of a multi-token span that already appeared earlier in the same context: it tracks the model's copy/repeat (induction) signal, not the token's identity, peaking a few tokens into the second or later copy of a repeated URL/version string, import path, IP address, timestamp, table row, error or boilerplate line, or repeated sentence. The first occurrence of the same material, a paraphrase of it, and any non-repeated text stay at the token's own baseline (usually 0-0.5, at most ~1.5 for IP-like digit strings), while each additional copy raises the peak (a repeated import line: 0.06 at one copy, 1.73 at two, 2.90 at three, ~3.05 at four or more, saturating) at almost any copy-to-copy distance (0-80 tokens tested); plain narrative prose repeated only twice sits at the weak end of the same scale (0.3-0.5), so the copy signal is graded by how distinctive the repeated string is.

This pole fires retrospectively when the preceding context frames an electoral or sporting contest between rival sides (vote, primary, candidate, party, lead, points, record) or an explicit comparison between alternatives (which/any/each/whatever, right/wrong), peaking on the determiner, evaluative adjective, faction noun, or score word that picks out the alternative. Trial verdicts, plain negation without alternatives, and the same trigger words in non-competitive narration stay near baseline.

Fires on a closed-class token that is still inside an unfinished fixed noun-phrase frame: chiefly ' and'/' or' right after an ordinal or identity/quantity adjective that has no head noun yet ("the third and final", "first and only", "same or similar", "second or third"), and the possessive after 'on'/'in' ("on its/her/our way", "on its own"); a secondary offshoot is a capitalised word-start fragment of a tokenizer-split word, most strongly the 'L' after 'licenses/' or '.org/' in a URL path (LICENSE) and CamelCase pieces like Just|D|ied. Coordination of descriptive adjectives or nouns ("big and beautiful", "salt and pepper", "a car and a house"), ordinary determiners, and the first token of a prompt stay below 25% of max, so there is no floor on ordinary text.

This pole fires on the final token of a news-report framing clause (an attribution or release verb such as said/released, a date-anchor preposition such as on/until/for, or a relative-time marker such as last/earlier/next) once it completes an extended news or event-report passage, i.e. at the position where a date/time anchor, canonically a weekday name, is due next; its output direction promotes weekday tokens (Jacobian kurtosis 5.2, 90% logit-lens agreement, ablation top-shifted tokens include Wednesday through Saturday).

Fires on the token that completes a frequent, highly constrained local multi-token formula or boilerplate chunk (e.g. have-been raised, when-it comes to, hit back at, whether-or-not, demonstrate the benefits/reductions of, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, Alter-Amend-or Vacate, Calculate the greatest common, mass-surveillance, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS) or the next subword piece of such a predictable word, driven by the preceding 1-4 tokens; the same surface token in an unpredictable context should activate weakly or not at all.

Retrospective, not lookahead: the activation at a token is fixed by the text before it and does not change when only the next token changes (it is identical on 'which ones are fake', 'which ones to buy' and 'which ones on the table'). The pole fires on the subject slot of a subordinate clause -- the relative pronoun (that/which/who) that heads a relative clause, and the final word of an embedded clause's subject phrase, usually a plural or generic noun phrase ('the animals that were rescued', 'that the equipment is', 'the discs will not be damaged') -- and it drops to background on the clause's finite auxiliary, modal or lexical verb itself, on non-relative uses of that/which ('that sort', 'that time', 'which one'), on the same nouns followed by a preposition instead of a clause, and on short sentence-opening main-clause subjects ('The people are coming').

The pole fires on the sub-word token that carries the distinctive spelling of an uncommon, technical word - 'yl' in amyloid, 'oph' in Haemophilus, 'rob' in Agrobacterium, 'l' in angioplasty, 'ob' in trilobite, 'Cl' in Clostridium, 'micro' in microflora - and is about twice as strong when the sentence is about a technical subject (a bacterial list, a measurement of a substance) as when the same word is merely mentioned in a flat report frame. It stays near zero on technical vocabulary the model knows as frequent words (meningitis, cholesterol, Salmonella, Streptococcus, Escherichia, diabetes, bacteria) and on everyday nouns; its only common-word responses are extent/degree words used descriptively ('so severe', 'too little', 'a thin coat', 'far higher'), which reach 1.3-2.5 against the 2.2-3.6 technical peaks.
